News.title: Car ‘repeatedly driven into group of people after fight’ in village – as cops launch probe into ‘disturbing’ incident
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

'CRASH' PROBE Car ‘repeatedly driven into group of people after fight’ in village – as cops launch probe into ‘disturbing’ incident







Next

COPS have launched an urgent probe after a car was allegedly driven into a group of people multiple times following a “fight” in a village.

Police and emergency services scrambled to Beddau in Wales, at 9.05pm on Saturday following a report that a car had collided with two members of the public.

The force could not confirm any arrests or what the injuries were.

A South Wales Police spokesperson said: “Minor injuries were reported and investigations are ongoing.”





However, footage circulating locally appears to show a group of people involved in a fight before a car drives into members of the group.

The vehicle then appears to pull away before returning and driving towards the group again, at relatively low speed.

Cllr Karl Johnson praised police’s swift response to the incident in a post on Facebook.

The Conservative councillor for Llantwit Fardre and Efail Isaf on Rhondda Cynon Taf Council wrote: “Disturbing scenes in Beddau last night.

“I hope everyone involved is safe and well, and thank South Wales Police for responding so quickly.

“Anti-social driving puts lives at risk and causes real concern for residents.

“We need swift action to identify those responsible for last night’s incident, alongside sustained work to tackle the wider problem locally.

“We will continue to push for measures to make our roads safer and keep our community safe.”



Later he said that from his understanding of Saturday’s incident a car drove into a crowd opposite the Welfare Hall on Tynant Road near the Post Office.

News.title: Gherkin-class Burnham is in a bit of a pickle – will he risk snap election to stop the walls closing in?
News.content:
Next

HAVE we all been too quick to mock the humble gherkin?

Chancellor John Healey’s promise of cheaper pickles prompted such a snort of ­derision it could have knocked over a jar of the stuff.



Sneer all you like, a Treasury official texted me in the days after the Budget, but polling shows the public really rather liked it.

In fact, according to YouGov, the mild tariff cuts to imported foods including gherkins was the fourth most popular policy in the speech.



It only ranked below ­decisions to remove standing charges from gas bills, freeze fuel duty and extend the zero per cent VAT rate on electricity costs.

And it ranked just above policies to extend business rates relief, raise the minimum wage and give a £100 one-off energy bills bump to 20million families.



Are we meant to be ­surprised that these policies have been given the thumbs-up by voters?

Or is it, in fact, the ­obvious outcome if you further bribe a country that’s become completely addicted to state- sanctioned ­handouts.

Who wouldn’t want a bit of HMG dosh dropping into their bank accounts this winter?

So the saying goes that a Budget is like a pint of milk — what smells fine in the evening can turn rancid overnight.



Within moments of the Chancellor delivering his final flourish, legions of boffins and bean-counters start tearing through the plans like a pack of hungry hyenas.

They comb over the smallprint into the early hours and have usually stumbled upon a few landmines by breakfast.

But last week they instead found something even worse: an essentially bare cupboard when it comes to tackling the tough stuff.

It was such an inoffensive Budget that it was actually offensively inoffensive.

Don’t mind our eye-bleeding debts, blossoming welfare state, creaking tax burden, clapped-out defences and sliding living standards.



PM Andy Burnham wasn’t kidding when he admitted it wasn’t a terribly radical Budget — a comment that I hear more than rankled with his next door neighbour at No11.

What ARE we to make of a man who promised to upend 40 years of neoliberalism but instead cut 4p off gherkins?

The answer for many in Westminster is easy — he is planning an early General Election.



The theory goes something like this: A load of crunch points are hurtling down the track that will force our people-pleaser PM to make unpalatable decisions.

Even if he acts, the parlous state of the UK’s finances means things are likely to get worse before they get better.

So he agrees a first Budget stuffed with a load of giveaways to boost his popularity while leaving the thorny bits for another day.

Then, bam! Call a snap ­election and bag a full five years, where he can then start to give the country its ­tough medicine.

With the Tories and Reform still split, and the Greens and Lib Dems stuck in the ­doldrums, striking while the iron is hot gives Burnham the mandate he craves.



Reopening debates around Brexit and electoral reform could even re-unite the left-wingers who deserted the party under Sir Keir Starmer.

Of course Burnham will deny he is plotting a snap poll.

The moment he so much as hints at an election, he will be left with no choice but to follow through or forever be branded a bottler.

Better therefore to wait until the most opportune moment to pounce.

All those repeated denials will quickly be forgotten in the white heat of a campaign, especially if it is unveiled around Christmas time.



That is the theory currently grinding through the Westminster speculation mill.

Whether it will become ­reality is a whole other matter.

There are reasons to give Burnham pause for thought. The most obvious spanner is that victory is far from ­guaranteed.



While Labour are currently polling six points clear of the Conservatives and Reform, such gaps tend to close during an election campaign.

The PM will be forced to retreat from his TikTok ­comfort blanket and partake in televised debates against ­formidable opponents.

Nigel Farage is a veteran orator and Kemi Badenoch has wiped the floor with him in several Commons clashes.

In more than 100 days, ­Burnham’s media handlers have allowed him to do just two televised press ­conferences.

And what would the PM even have to sell on the ­doorstep? Getting his own mandate largely means breaking out of the tax straitjacket he inherited from Starmer.



“Vote for me and I’ll hike your taxes” is far from a ­winning message, and is unlikely even to be stomached alongside promises to fund social care or defence.

But even if he survives the campaign stump, Burnham is still all but certain to lose MPs.

Nobody expects him to better Starmer’s 2024 landslide, and at least one recent poll showed he would sacrifice his majority altogether, forcing him into some sort of chaotic ­coalition with the Lib Dems, Greens and Nats.

It’d be one hell of a gamble for a PM who has devoted the best part of two decades to grasping for the top job — and one which I suspect will prove too much of a risk.

The next few months before Christmas will see Burnham’s thinking become clearer.



The strength of immigration reforms this week will be a good indication of how much control he exercises over his party.

And his response to two ­welfare reports due this month will also reveal if he is serious about tackling the benefits ­crisis, and how quickly.

A much-vaunted ten-year plan will map a blueprint for Burnham’s Britain.

How much of it requires a fresh mandate will be telling.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Try as he might, our ­gherkin-class hero is struggling to put a lid on all this election chatter.



I suspect in truth, he’s in a bit of a pickle.

News.title: Urgent warning after toxic pufferfish with poison 1,000 times deadlier than cyanide washes up on popular UK beach
News.content:
BEACH SHOCK Urgent warning after toxic pufferfish with poison 1,000 times deadlier than cyanide washes up on popular UK beach







Next

A DEADLY pufferfish – with poison 1,000 times deadlier than cyanide – has washed up on a British coastline after apparently being blown hundreds of miles off course.

The highly poisonous exotic fish was discovered by a stunned diver on Knoll Beach, in Studland, Dorset.



Owen Booty initially mistook the strange-looking creature for a small marker buoy before realising it was a fully inflated pufferfish measuring around 17 inches long.

Although dead, the fish remains extremely dangerous, with toxins in its skin and organs capable of causing fatal poisoning.



The natural poison found in pufferfish is up to 1,000 times more lethal than cyanide.

They are usually found in the tropical and subtropical waters of the Indian, Pacific and Atlantic Oceans, making the discovery on a Dorset beach particularly unusual.



It is thought the fish may have been swept hundreds of miles off course by recent storms Austen and Boalo.

Pufferfish get their name from their bizarre defence mechanism, inflating their bodies into a balloon-like shape to make themselves harder for predators to swallow.



But their toxins can also pose a deadly threat to humans.

Poisoning can occur if the fish’s sharp, hidden spines pierce the skin, allowing toxins to enter the bloodstream.

Another risk comes from eating pufferfish that has not been prepared properly.

Their organs contain powerful toxins which can contaminate the edible flesh if accidentally cut during preparation.

Owen, from the company Freedive Life, said he had been walking along the beach when he spotted the unusual object.



He said: “I was out walking along Knoll Beach as the sea was a little too rough to get in the water, when I spotted what initially looked like a buoy or plastic bag washed up on the shore.

“I walked over to investigate and realised it was actually a dead fish.

“Having encountered pufferfish while diving abroad, I had a good idea what it was, but sent the photographs to Dorset Wildlife Trust and a friend who’s a marine biologist for confirmation.

“I spend a lot of time in the water exploring Dorset’s coastline.

“We’re fortunate to have some fantastic marine life right on our doorstep.



“But despite all the time I’ve spent diving locally, I certainly wasn’t expecting to find a pufferfish washed up on the beach.”

A spokesperson for Dorset Wildlife Trust said the fish was a rare sight in British waters.

They said: “Usually found in open water in the warmer parts of the Atlantic as well as the Indian and Pacific oceans, these fish are a rare sight in the UK, but they do turn up occasionally.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The charity has warned people not to touch any pufferfish they find and urged anyone who spots one to report it.

The National Trust, which owns Studland Beach, said the discovery had not been reported to them.

News.title: Germans divided over future of Hitler’s ‘Eagle’s Nest’ after lair gutted by fire – amid fears it could attract neo-Nazis
News.content:
Next

THERE is much confusion in Germany as to whether Adolf Hitler’s Alpine guest house will – or should – be rebuilt after a fire that gutted it.

The Kehlsteinhaus, also known as Eagle’s Nest, has been a thorn in the side of authorities for the better part of 60 years after surviving World War Two unscathed.



The debate over whether it should be preserved has now resurfaced after the Nazi relic – turned dark tourist hotspot, particularly for visitors from the US and Israel – was destroyed in an inferno over a week ago.

Now the site has been cordoned off until a decision is eventually reached.



There are major concerns over the possibility of squatting or pilgrimages by neo-Nazis.

Barriers and further scaffolding will be transported by helicopter to the top of the mountain to guard the remains.



“We can hardly leave the ruin standing there,” said Joachim Herrmann, the conservative Bavarian interior minister, who advocated reconstruction.

But Sven Keller, the director of the Obersalzberg Documentation Centre, argued that a perfect reconstruction was “out of the question”, owing to the extent of the damage.

Jens-Christian Wagner, director of the Buchenwald concentration camp, described Eagle’s Nest and other architectural relics from the Nazi era as “pieces of evidence”.

“They lose their evidential value if they are not preserved in their original form but are instead replicated,” he told The Telegraph.



“For this reason, no replicas should be built, as these would, in a sense, constitute ‘fake history’.”

Wagner wants to see the site repurposed in a historically responsible manner.

Meanwhile, Mary Fulbrook, a professor of German History at UCL, said the project was fraught with the risk of attracting right-wing Nazi sympathisers.

She said: “Reconstruction of a site so closely associated with Hitler risks creating a focus attractive to Right-wing sympathisers with Nazi ideology and recreating the impact of the grandiose architecture of the dictator in this impressive setting.



“On the other hand, preservation of the ruin in some way to provide historical contextualisation, and still draw tourists, could be a very useful adjunct to Germany’s extensive memorial landscape.”

Earlier this year, The Sun travelled to Vienna, where a similar debate has been simmering over the terrace of the Hofburg Palace, where Hitler announced the annexation of Austria to the Third Reich.

People were invited to cast their vote on whether it should be reopened – but there were fears that Neo-Nazis would flock to it to perform Hitler’s salute.

Peter Hohenhaus – a world authority on the industry, who has visited over 900 “dark” destinations – is concerned about the “wrong kind” of pilgrims, those who treat tragedy less as history and more as a shrine.

“I have difficulty with Nazi sites, for example, Eagle’s Nest [built in 1938 as a Nazi party conference and social venue] in Germany,” he told The Sun.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

“I went on an organised tour once. Interestingly, they only exist in English and are mostly taken up by Brits and Americans. I was the only non-native English speaker.

“I had a very uncomfortable feeling as there is always the risk of glorifying Nazism.”

News.title: Girl, 6, left with ‘devastating’ burns after being engulfed by flames when she was struck by faulty firework
News.content:
FIREWORK HORROR Girl, 6, left with ‘devastating’ burns after being engulfed by flames when she was struck by faulty firework







Next

A SIX-YEAR-OLD girl has been left scarred for life with “devastating” burns after a faulty firework struck her in the neck and set her clothes alight.

The youngster had gathered with her family for a backyard display at the end of October last year when the horrific accident occurred.



Despite the family strictly following all safety guidance, a rogue firework shot sideways, ricocheted off a swing set and hit the child in the neck and shoulder.

Her mother, who wishes to remain anonymous, said her daughter was engulfed in flames within seconds and was rushed to hospital for harrowing skin grafts.



The heartbroken parent explained that they had specifically purchased quieter, low-noise fireworks to protect their pets and had set everything up at the recommended safe distance.

She said the family genuinely believed they had taken every possible precaution for a quiet evening of food and celebration.



But tragedy still struck when the device failed to launch skywards.

“Instead of travelling straight up into the air, it fired sideways,” the mother said.



“It hit a swing set that had been moved out of the way and bounced back towards the other side of the garden, where our family was standing.”

The mum said the family “panicked” before ripping off the girl’s dress and getting her in the shower to begin cooling the burns.

They then wrapped her burns in cling film and sped to A&E, completely unaware of how drastically the freak accident would alter their lives.

Her mum added: “The burns were so severe that, later in November, our daughter had to undergo surgery for a skin graft.

“She then had to endure dressing changes every two days, which were incredibly difficult for her.



“For a six-year-old child, having to repeatedly go through painful and frightening treatment is something no parent ever wants to see.”

The mother is now speaking out to warn other parents that fireworks can inflict devastating injuries in the blink of an eye, even when all instructions are followed to the letter.

She stressed that they were not careless and had done exactly what they were supposed to do, making the nightmare even harder for the family to accept.

“Our daughter will unfortunately carry the physical and emotional effects of that night with her for the rest of her life,” she said.

The family hopes their traumatic ordeal will urge the public to seriously consider the severe risks associated with home displays, warning that the consequences can be far more serious than anyone imagines.



She said: “Before that night, we never imagined that a firework would hit our daughter.

“We certainly never imagined that one evening would leave physical and emotional scars that our daughter may carry for the rest of her life.”

The warning comes after the Children’s Burns Trust charity said firework injuries have surged 63 per cent in the last year.

Ken Dunn, consultant burns and retired plastic surgeon who is vice chair of Children’s Burns Trust, said: “We are deeply concerned by the sharp rise in firework injuries to children.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“A single spark can cause life-changing burns, scarring and long-term rehabilitation and the recent 63 per cent increase in child injuries is a stark reminder that fireworks are not harmless toys.



“Please attend organised public displays, keep children well away from fireworks and sparklers, and know how to respond quickly if a burn occurs, early action can make a real difference.”

News.title: Moment King asks ‘where’s the umbrella’ as he’s caught in downpour in Antigua… while Camilla walks off with brolly
News.content:
Next

THIS is the hilarious moment King Charles is left standing in a downpour asking his entourage “where’s the umbrella” – as Queen Camilla scuttles off with the brolly.

The Monarch was seen waving his arms and repeatedly calling out for cover after the heavens opened during an independence day parade in Antigua.



Meanwhile, Camilla had already made her way to a covered stand.

In the clip she is seen clutching her see-through umbrella before sitting down with a cheeky wry smile.



Charles was left out in the pouring rain as others scrambled for shelter.

He was eventually handed a brolly but stoically carried on with his duties.

The sodden damp King remained and continued duties, meeting members of the Antigua and Barbuda Defence Force and Royal Police Force.

The King was rewarded with a huge cheer from the crowd as he braved the storm.



The royal couple had arrived at Sir Vivian Richards Stadium to attend the parade.

The event marked the 45th anniversary of Antigua and Barbuda’s independence.

The royal couple were greeted with cheers as they stepped out of their car and onto the dais.

But the weather took a turn for the worse during the national anthem, with torrential rain soon soaking the parade ground.

As the anthem finished, Camilla turned and headed for the covered stand with her umbrella.



Charles also stepped off the dais, gesturing and repeatedly asking: “Where’s the umbrella?”

Despite the downpour, the King continued with the inspection as the ceremony went on around him.

A brolly was eventually found and handed to the King.

The visit also gave Charles the chance to meet four cricketing legends who have all been knighted.

They included Sir Viv Richards, Sir Richie Richardson, Sir Andy Roberts and Sir Curtly Ambrose.

News.title: Fresh Brexit betrayal as Labour prepares to let 80,000 young Europeans a year live and work in Britain
News.content:
Next

LABOUR is preparing to let up to 80,000 young Europeans live and work in Britain every year in a fresh Brexit concession to Brussels.`

Ministers have raised their proposed cap from 50,000 in a bid to secure a deal ahead of Andy Burnham’s EU summit on November 20.



Under the plans, EU citizens aged 18 to 30 could live, work and study in Britain for up to three years.

But Brussels is pushing for an even higher cap of 100,000 places, according to The Sunday Times.



Shadow Home Secretary Chris Philp blasted: “At a time when young Brits are struggling to find jobs, afford housing and get on the property ladder, Labour is putting the interests of the EU ahead of our own people.

“This is not a reset; it is a retreat.



“Meanwhile thousands continue to cross the Channel illegally and Labour look set to water down reforms to ILR.

The Conservatives are the only party that will secure our borders and put our national interest first.”

EU negotiators are also demanding cheaper university fees for European students, despite warnings the move could cost cash-strapped British universities millions.

The Government hopes to strike agreements on youth mobility, cutting border checks on food exports and linking emissions trading schemes at the summit.



But major sticking points remain, raising doubts over whether a deal can be struck in time.

It comes as Mr Burnham is also preparing to unveil options for Britain’s future relationship with the EU later this month – having admitted he wants to rejoin the bloc in his lifetime.

News.title: Haunting details emerge after jogger, 28, knifed in neck minutes before meeting parents – as she remains on life support
News.content:
Next

A JOGGER who was stabbed in the neck while running in New York was on the phone to her family just minutes before the attack, said police.

Katie Suarez, 28, was discovered by her own dad on a waterfront path in Brooklyn with two knife wounds on either side of her neck.



Her stricken father begged a passer-by to call 911 and Katie was raced to hospital and hooked onto life support – where she remains in a coma.

Now, chilling new details have emerged about the horrifying moments before the bank teller was attacked.



The jogger had been due to meet her parents at 6.30pm outside her workplace at TD Bank – a family tradition after Katie finished for the day.

She met her mum outside at the scheduled time – but her dad was running late, according to a police statement given to the New York Post.

READ MORE CREEP SNARED Chucky mask-wearing suspect who terrorised city and chased jogger is unmasked



Katie then headed off for a solo run along the Belt Parkway – a scenic path stretching along the river which she had jogged many times before.

Eventually the dad joins his wife and at around 8pm the pair call their daughter to discuss where to meet up.

She reassured them that she was just half a mile away – a distance the marathon-trainer could cover in about five minutes.

This phone call was the last time Katie’s parents spoke to their daughter.



She never arrived at the agreed meeting spot – and when her parents called again she did not pick up the phone.

Her parents immediately launched a desperate hunt for their child, splitting up to cover more ground.

It was her dad who found his girl lying on a blood-soaked path near Bay 17th Street stabbed twice in the neck – on both her left and her right side,



Police revealed she had run roughly 100ft after being knifed before collapsing to the ground.

Disturbing photos captured blood soaked into the concrete path and splattered on a nearby railing.

The attack has been described as “random” with no evidence of sex-crime motives or robbery, according to police.

She was found still with her pink phone and jewelry – but with no sign of the suspect.

Police have launched a major manhunt for the attacker and deployed scuba divers, K9s and drones in the search operation.



Katie has been described as a “very kind” woman who has a “very good character”.

One neighbour said: “I mean, nobody is supposed to have [their] life taken, you know, being bad or good, but she was kind of exceptional to me.”

She had reportedly been training for Sunday’s New York City Marathon.

The event organiser told Fox News: “We were sad to hear of this horrible attack—our hearts are with her family and the running community.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The bike path where Katie had been running offers beautiful views across the river of Staten Island and is often bustling with walkers, runners, bikers and fishermen.



Police are asking the public for help as the investigation continues.

News.title: Woman, 28, on jog in Brooklyn ‘stabbed in neck’ moments after speaking to dad
News.content:
Woman, 28, on jog in Brooklyn ‘stabbed in neck’ moments after speaking to dad

Bank cashier Katie Suarez is on life support after being brually attacked on a run - her injured body discovered by her father to have been stabbed in the neck twice as he waited to meet up with her

View 4 Images Bank teller Katie Suarez is on life support after being slashed in the neck while on a run Friday night (Image: Katie Suarez / Linkedin)

A 28-year-old woman was stabbed in the neck in a vicious attack while she was out jogging on in New York. The horrific attack in the United States came just moments after she was speaking to her dad on the phone, according to reports.

‌



‌



Bank cashier Katie Suarez has been declared brain dead and is on life support, the New York Post reports, after the apparent random assault on a promenade in Brooklyn, New York City.

‌



Katie had met up with her mum shortly after leaving work at around 6.30pm, police sources have shared with the New York Post. The mother and daughter met up near the TD Bank where Katie worked in a shopping plaza - a family tradition after Katie clocked off.

‌



Katie's dad would typically join them but was running late on Friday evening, reports continue. Katie had already changed out of her work clothes and into her running gear, handing over the clothes to her mum before heading off on a run by herself.

Katie ran along the Belt Parkway westbound toward the Verrazano-Narrows Bridge, with reports adding that she may have been training for Sunday's New York City marathon.

View 4 Images The jogger was stabbed in neck was planning to meet parents when attacked, sources say (Image: Katie Suarez / Linkedin)

‌



Katie's dad eventually caught up with her mum. At around 8pm, he phoned their daughter - a graduate of Brooklyn College Kingborough Community College and a native of El Salvador, according to her LinkedIn - to talk about where they could meet up, reports add.

The father told his daughter that he and her mum were still close to the bank and asked where she was, with Katie replying she was about half-a-mile away - around a five-minute jog for her. The New York Post reports that nothing concerning came up during the phone call.

‌



A short time later, when Katie didn’t appear at the meeting point, her dad called her again. This time, she didn’t pick up, reports say. The parents split up to look for their daughter, who was discovered by her dad.

View 4 Images Crime scene investigators work at the scene where Katie was stabbed (Image: Kyle Mazza/Shutterstock)

‌



Katie was found stabbed twice in the neck, on both her right and left side near Bay 17th Street and Shore Parkway, before her dad frantically pleaded with a passer-by to call the emergency services, the New York Post wrote.

Investigators believe the attack was random with no indication of a sexual or theft motive, as her pink cell phone and jewellery were still with her, sources have said. It is believed that Katie ran another 100 feet after being attacked, before collapsing.

‌



Images from the gory scene showed blood splattered on a nearby guardrail. Katie is now being treated at New York University Langone Hospital.

“It’s going to come to light whoever truly did it,” said the victim’s cousin, Gianluca Frances, 19, to The Post on Sunday, speaking outside the hospital.

‌



View 4 Images Blood at the scene of the brutal stabbing (Image: Kyle Mazza/Shutterstock)

He suggested Katie may have been training for the marathon while calling the situation “truly an awful, awful time” and urging “the worst” to happen to the person who attacked his cousin.

‌



The following day, Saturday, a neighbour said: “It’s very sad. I’m sad for everybody, but this is close. It’s too much right now. It’s a mad world.”

Katie had worked as a teller at the bank branch for more than five years, according to her LinkedIn. The reports add that Katie often jogged along the path, which features breathtaking views of the Verrazzano-Narrows Bridge and Staten Island.

Article continues below

It is also popular with walkers, joggers, bikers and fishermen.

News.title: Energy Secretary says there's 'one way' Britain can bring down bills for good
News.content:
Energy Secretary says there's 'one way' Britain can bring down bills for good

Miatta Fahnbulleh insists Budget measures provide breathing space as report finds incomes have fallen faster than households can cut back spending

View 4 Images Research found nearly three in five people are now making more effort to cut spending than they were a year ago (Image: Getty Images/iStockphoto)

Energy Secretary Miatta Fahnbulleh has acknowledged Budget measures to tackle soaring gas and electricity bills aren't the "silver bullet".

‌



‌



Writing in the Mirror, Ms Fahnbulleh listed the package announced by Chancellor John Healey last week to try to take the pressure off families. Those include £100 for 20 million households, extending a VAT cut on electricity bills until next July, and removing standing charges from the gas element from later on next year.

‌



"These steps will give people some breathing space in the short term, and take the sting out of high energy bills," she wrote. "But I want to be straight with readers. I know this isn't a silver bullet.

‌



To see more of the stories you love from The Mirror and to find them easily in Google then make us your preferred source. Free and easy-to-do, just click on the link here to find more from The Mirror at the top of your feed.

View 4 Images Energy Secretary Miatta Fahnbulleh says Budget help with bills 'will give people some breathing space in the short term' (Image: Maja Smiejkowska/PA Wire)

John Healey says young workers might not get minimum wage boost before next election READ MORE :

"The only way Britain can take control of its bills and bring them down for good, is to reform our system so we are less exposed to global energy shocks. And the only way to do that is to get more clean, homegrown power online, and reduce our reliance on expensive, volatile fossil fuels.

‌



"That means building projects in the right places, with the grid to carry it, so that new energy projects lower bills for households across the country."

Her comments around reducing reliance on fossil fuels comes amid reports of a cabinet split over a decision on the Rosebank North Sea oilfield, with Ms Fahnbulleh said to be minded to refuse the project on environmental grounds but Mr Healey in favour.

‌



Mr Healey said on Saturday that ministers would veto new clean energy projects if they add to Britain's multibillion-pound wasted wind bill and push up electricity costs for consumers.

Last month saw the government give the go-ahead to the controversial Jackdaw gas field in Scotland. The project, off the coast of Aberdeen, has been in limbo for two years after the High Court ruled a previous approval was invalid.

‌



Critics say measures announced in last week's Budget do not go far enough given predictions that Ofgem's price cap will surge by average 27% - nearly £470 a year - in January.

It comes as the wider cost of living pressure facing families was hammered home by research suggesting the average Brit has £175 a month less to spend after shelling out for essential bills than they did a year ago.

‌



The report by the website Moneysupermarket claims the average person spent £1,477.85 last month across 31 household bills and everyday outgoings. That was actually down from a figure of £1,657.67 a year ago and although the research doesn't fully explain why, it appears to be partly due to people cutting back where they can. Some of the biggest year-on-year falls came from insurance, with households able to save an average 18% on their home cover and 15% on car policies.

View 4 Images More people are looking are ways to trim their outgoings in the face of rising bills (Image: Getty Images/EyeEm)

‌



Yet offsetting those savings has been an even bigger drop in how much money households have coming in. The research puts the average person's income after tax at just over £2,200 this October, down from £2,558 a year ago, but without giving a reason for the fall. The end result is that average disposable incomes have declined year-on-year from just under £901.91 to £725.15 - a drop of £175.76 a month.

Put another way, bills and outgoings now account for 67% of a typical person's income, up slightly from 65% a year ago, but with large variations across the country. The research suggests Norwich is where essential bills eat up the biggest chunk, at 77%, and leaving a typical person in the Norfolk city with £428.23 a month, or £107 a week. Next was Plymouth, where bills account for 72% of someone has coming in, followed by Bristol (71%).

‌



London, perhaps not surprisingly, had the highest outgoings, at an average £1,703.60 last month. But those in the capital also tended to have higher incomes, meaning those costs take up around 65%, leaving Londoners with an average £898.90 a month, Moneysupermarket's annual Household Money Index claimed.

View 4 Images Norwich was found to top the cities where people have the lowest disposable incomes (Image: Getty)

‌



The research also points to the fact, while some costs have fallen year-on-year, they have risen in recent months. Since July, the average spent on energy has gone up 2% to £98.40 a month per person, while water bills have increased 3% to £42.50.

According to the report, average monthly outgoings overall increased by £23.31 between July and October this year, while reported monthly income after tax rose by just £2.50 in the same period. That means the average person had £20.81 less left over after bills and outgoings than they had three months ago.

‌



It came as economists warned families are in the grip of the worst decade of income growth since at least the 1950s. The Institute for Fiscal Studies said households' disposable incomes are set to rise by just 2% during the 2020s. The go-slow has been caused by a combination of factors, including high inflation, weak wage growth and tax increases.

Moneysupermarket's report also found how nearly three in five of those surveyed said they were making more effort to cut spending than they were a year ago, while just over two in five are looking for ways to increase their income. For some, that means making simple trade-offs. More than two in five have skipped a purchase they wanted to make, while two in five have chosen a cheaper alternative and put the difference aside.

‌



The research found nearly one in three people are cutting back on non-essential spending to help cover energy bills, while 29% are spending less on meals out and the same proportion on clothes. More than one in five are reducing spending on holidays or travel, while 19% are cutting back on subscriptions.

Those concerns are also shaping Christmas spending plans. More than a quarter of people plan to spend less on Christmas presents to help cover their energy bills, while 26% are cutting back on festive socialising and 24% on Christmas food.

‌



Kara Gammell, personal finance expert at Moneysupermarket, said: "Compared with a year ago, people report spending less on a range of household bills and everyday costs. But reported incomes have fallen even faster.

"The regional picture tells a similar story. The places with the highest household costs aren't always the places where people feel the greatest squeeze. What matters is not just what people spend, but how much income they have left afterwards.

Article continues below

"We're also starting to see signs that some everyday costs are edging upwards again as we head towards winter. At a time when household budgets remain under pressure, regularly reviewing your outgoings, understanding what you're paying for and comparing your options can help create some much-needed room in your monthly budget."

Lis Barton, chief customer officer of MONY Group, parent company of Moneysupermarket, said: "This year’s index shows just how resourceful people are when it comes to looking after their future finances. We’re calling them the ‘Future Me Funders’. Our research reveals that more than half of people across the UK are finding creative ways to free up money and put it towards their future."

News.title: Girl, 6, left with severe burns after being hit in neck by firework
News.content:
Girl, 6, left with severe burns after being hit in neck by firework

The girl had been enjoying a fireworks display with family members when one firework shot sideways and struck a swing before changing direction and hitting the child

View 5 Images The girl needed surgery following her injury (Image: Getty Images/iStockphoto)

A six-year-old girl was left with severe burns after she was hit in the neck before her clothes were set on fire.

‌



‌



The youngster had gathered with family members to enjoy a firework display in her back garden when disaster struck at the end of October last year. Her mum said despite following all the safety instructions, one of the fireworks shot sideways and hit a swing set before changing direction and striking her daughter in the neck and shoulder.

‌



Seconds later, her clothes were engulfed in flames and she was rushed to hospital where she had to undergo skin grafts. The mum, who wishes to remain anonymous, says her little girl has been left with lasting physical and mental injuries and is now warning of the dangers of fireworks.

‌



View 5 Images The girl was with family when a firework struck her in the neck (Image: Children's Burns Trust / SWNS)

Nine killed after business jet crashes into mobile home park and bursts into flames in Florida READ MORE :

She said they had deliberately bought low-noise fireworks to be mindful of their pets and followed all the safety guidance. But when one of the fireworks failed to launch properly, instead of travelling skyward, it shot sideways across the garden.

The mum said: "It was supposed to be a lovely evening where we could spend time together, enjoy some food and have a few fireworks. Because we have animals, we were particularly conscious about the noise.

‌



"We chose low-noise, quieter fireworks because we wanted to enjoy the evening while minimising the distress and fear that fireworks can cause animals. We also took the safety instructions seriously.

"We followed all of the instructions on the firework packaging, made sure the fireworks were set up correctly and kept to the recommended safe distance. We genuinely believed we had taken every precaution we could to keep our family safe.

‌



"Sadly, that wasn't enough. When one of the fireworks was lit, it was faulty it did not go up as it should have. Instead of travelling straight up into the air, it fired sideways.

View 5 Images The girl was left with severe burns (Image: Children's Burns Trust / SWNS)

‌



"It hit a swing set that had been moved out of the way and bounced back towards the other side of the garden, where our family was standing. It hit our six-year-old daughter in the neck and shoulder.

"Within seconds, her clothes had caught fire." The mum said the family "panicked" before ripping off the girl's dress and getting her in the shower to begin cooling the burns.

‌



She added: "We then wrapped the affected area in cling film and rushed her to A&E. At that point, we had no idea just how much this accident was going to change our lives.

"The burns were so severe that, later in November, our daughter had to undergo surgery for a skin graft. She then had to endure dressing changes every two days, which were incredibly difficult for her.

‌



"For a six-year-old child, having to repeatedly go through painful and frightening treatment is something no parent ever wants to see their child experience. And the effects haven't simply been physical.

"Our daughter will unfortunately carry the physical and emotional effects of that night with her for the rest of her life. As a family, we will also carry what happened with us forever.

‌



"What makes this particularly difficult for us is that we never thought this could happen. We weren't being careless. We weren't ignoring the safety instructions. We had deliberately chosen quieter fireworks because of our animals.

View 5 Images The burns were so severe she had to undergo surgery for a skin graft (Image: Children's Burns Trust / SWNS)

‌



"We followed the instructions on the box, set the fireworks up correctly and kept to the recommended safe distance. We did what we believed we were supposed to do.

"And yet, a faulty firework still ended up hitting a six-year-old child. We want people to understand that fireworks can cause devastating burns and life-changing injuries in seconds.

‌



"Even when people take precautions and follow the instructions, something can still go wrong. We hope that by sharing what happened to our daughter, people will think very carefully about the risks involved with fireworks and understand that the consequences of an accident can be far more serious than they ever imagine.

"Before that night, we never imagined that a firework would hit our daughter. We never imagined that something intended to be part of a family celebration could result in our daughter needing surgery, a skin graft and repeated painful dressing changes.

‌



"We certainly never imagined that one evening would leave physical and emotional scars that our daughter may carry for the rest of her life. As a family, this is something we will never forget, and something we will always wish had never happened."

View 5 Images The warning was shared after a surge in fireworks-related injuries last year (Image: Children's Burns Trust / SWNS)

‌



The warning comes after the Children’s Burns Trust charity said firework injuries have surged 63 per cent in the last year. Ken Dunn, consultant burns and retired plastic surgeon who is vice chair of Children’s Burns Trust, said: “We are deeply concerned by the sharp rise in firework injuries to children.

"A single spark can cause life‑changing burns, scarring and long‑term rehabilitation and the recent 63 per cent increase in child injuries is a stark reminder that fireworks are not harmless toys. Please attend organised public displays, keep children well away from fireworks and sparklers, and know how to respond quickly if a burn occurs, early action can make a real difference.”

‌



Becky Guy, senior policy manager at the Royal Society for the Prevention of Accidents (RoSPA), said: “RoSPA encourages families to attend organised firework displays wherever possible, as these are the safest way to enjoy the celebrations.

"If you're planning to use fireworks at home, it's important to buy them from a reputable retailer, follow the instructions carefully, and ensure children are supervised and kept well away from fireworks.

Article continues below

"Sensible precautions can help prevent serious injuries and ensure everyone enjoys Bonfire Night safely.”

News.title: Bedrooms stay warm and cosy without central heating if you do 1 simple task
News.content:
Bedrooms stay warm and cosy without central heating if you do 1 simple task

With energy bills rising and millions of households reportedly avoiding central heating, keeping warm at home doesn't have to cost a penny.

How to keep bedroom warm with no heating

As the winter months creep closer, keeping warmth at home becomes a major concern. Cranking up the heating can provide welcome relief, but with energy bills skyrocketing for countless households, any money-saving tips are worth knowing about.

‌



‌



A shocking 1.7 million households reportedly said in 2024 that they wouldn't be turning on their central heating because of spiralling energy costs. Yet cold temperatures can cause health issues and interfere with quality sleep. But you don't necessarily need to rely on the heating to stay warm.

‌



Lisa Davis, product advisor at Opera Beds, has shared several budget-friendly suggestions to keep your bedroom warm this winter without adjusting the thermostat. One of these tips doesn't require spending a single penny — it's as simple as rearranging your room furniture.

‌



View 2 Images If you don't want to turn up the heating, consider some more cost-effective hacks instead (Image: Getty)

Positioning your bed against interior walls is typically best, as these walls are less affected by temperature fluctuations, helping you remain consistently warm through the night. It's also advisable to keep the bed away from windows, as even the best-insulated ones can leak heat and allow cold draughts in.

Ensure our latest lifestyle stories always appear at the top of your Google Search by making us a Preferred Source. Click here to activate or add us as Preferred Source in your Google search settings

‌



Don't block radiators with furniture, which can reduce their effectiveness, and consider placing a rug on hard flooring to add insulation and reduce heat loss.

Another free method to keep your home warm is to draw your curtains at a particular time. With the clocks now turned back, it's essential to close your curtains as soon as dusk falls to keep the warmth inside.

‌



View 2 Images Cranking up the heating during winter can be expensive (Image: Getty)

Curtains featuring thermal lining are particularly effective at preventing cold air from seeping through windows.

‌



The best curtain fabrics for retaining heat are thick, weighty materials such as wool, velvet or fleece. If money is tight, try placing a shower curtain behind your existing curtains to create an extra barrier against the cold.

Finally, ensure all draughts around windows and doors are blocked using weather stripping and window film, as this can have a far greater impact than you might expect.

Article continues below

To identify any draughts in your home, check for air movement around doors, windows, floorboards, beams, skirting boards, and air conditioning units. You can also use the straightforward trick of holding a lit match near suspected leaks to see whether it flickers.

Keep doors to rooms you're not using closed to concentrate heat where it's most needed, and use a draught excluder to prevent cold air from sneaking in beneath doors.

News.title: 'Henry Nowak never came home - his family deserve answers and justice for their boy'
News.content:
'Henry Nowak never came home - his family deserve answers and justice for their boy'

Henry Nowak's family deserve answers, accountability and the absolute assurance that lessons will be learned. Above all, they deserve justice for Henry.

View Image Voice of the Mirror has its say...

Lessons to be learned

The anguish of Henry Nowak’s family is almost too painful to comprehend.

‌



‌



A mother recalling the knock on the door that brought news of her son’s murder. A father collapsing in grief. A sister clinging to her brother’s clothes as they still carry his scent.

‌



These are the heartbreaking memories of a family whose lives were destroyed by an act of senseless violence.

‌



And his family’s suffering was deepened by his appalling treatment in his final moments.

As he lay bleeding, desperately pleading for help, police handcuffed him. His cries that he had been stabbed were dismissed.

Eight agonising minutes passed and 18-year-old Henry never came home.

‌



His family deserve answers, accountability and the assurance that lessons will be learned.

Above all, they deserve justice. No family should ever have to endure such suffering.

‌



Dignity vital

Britain cannot change the horrors of its involvement in slavery, but it has a duty to confront that shameful chapter with honesty, humility and compassion.

Andy Burnham’s willingness to discuss a formal apology is a welcome recognition that the wounds of slavery still run deep.

‌



Chancellor John Healey is right to acknowledge the tough questions about financial reparations, particularly the responsibility of today’s taxpayers for atrocities centuries ago.

At the Commonwealth summit, the Prime Minister has an opportunity to demonstrate Britain’s willingness to listen.

Article continues below

A meaningful dialogue, conducted with dignity and goodwill, could help build a stronger, more united Commonwealth.

Hull of a trek

After 28 years, 30,000 miles and countless adventures, Karl Bushby has finally made it home to Hull. What an incredible feat of courage, determination and endurance. His mum’s first question? “What time do you call this?” Some things never change.

News.title: Zelensky says Putin is 'losing the war' as Russian oil refinery burns in huge strike
News.content:
Zelensky says Putin is 'losing the war' as Russian oil refinery burns in huge strike

The Ukrainian military claimed Russia suffered its worst battlefield losses in October - more than any other month since the Vladimir Putin launched the full-scale invasion in 2022

View 3 Images Ukraine launched drone strikes against Russia (Image: X)

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky says Vladimir Putin was 'losing the war' as a huge oil refinery burned after a "massive" overnight drone strike on key infrastructure inside Russia.

‌



‌



Zelensky confirmed today a barrage had struck the Kamensky missile manufacturing plant in the Rostov region, along the border with Ukraine. He added overnight attacks by Russian forces left hundreds of thousands of Ukrainians without power.

‌



Dramatic pictures appeared to show multiple fires at the huge Kstovo facility in the Nizhny Novgorod region. Gleb Nikitin, governor of Nizhny Novgorod, confirmed a "massive drone attack" involving more than 100 unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs).

‌



"The intensity of the strikes is very high, and the Russians are seeking to maximally exploit the deficit of ballistic missile interceptors," he said in a message shared on Telegram. Russian officials said it had shot down 235 drones launched from Ukraine.

Zelenskyy said: "Russia is losing. We are holding our positions, liberating territory, and ensuring that every day of the war costs the aggressor as much as possible."

It comes as Russia suffered more casualties last month than at any time since the invasion of Ukraine began began in February, 2022, with Russia 54,400 soldiers killed.

‌



View 3 Images Putin is hoping for a breakthrough in Ukraine (Image: Getty Images)

Meanwhile, Ukraine's air force claimed to have shot down 371 of 433 long-range drones that were launched by Russia since Saturday. There has been no let up in fighting ahead of the winter, even as a six-day ceasefire held in the town of Oleshky, currently under Russian control.

‌



Russia continues to pay a high price for every metre of territory it seizes, while Ukraine is making gains. In October, Ukraine liberated 96.2 square kilometres of land, according to Zelenskyy. This is 10.4 square kilometres more than Russia managed to capture during the same period.

Zelenskyy added: "To stop these insane losses, Russia only needs to choose a ceasefire and diplomacy.

‌



"We are justly defending ourselves against Russian aggression and doing everything to reduce Russia's capability to continue it,"

Russia this week accused Ukraine of continuing to strike its oil refineries and ignoring a request from US President Donald Trump, who signed a controversial deal with Vladimir Putin to purchase hundreds of thousands of Russian diesel to temporarily ease US sanctions.

‌



Trump lashed out at Zelensky following previous attacks on Russia who claimed he has been "negotiating peace" between the two warring countries. But Zelensky has shown little signs of easing pressure on Russia after the US military aid to Ukraine effectively collapsed.

A humanitarian ceasefire, brokered by US First Lady Melania Trump, allowed hundreds of residents to flee the city of Oleshky which is occupied by Russian forces. Up to 6,000 people, including 200 children, were believed to still be living in the city and its surrounding areas, with 1,700 in the city itself. Residents had a four-hour window to leave; a convoy of 25 buses brought in for up to 750 evacuees, along with ambulances for people with limited mobility.

‌



View 3 Images Ukraine struck oil refineries in Rostov overnight (Image: X)

After travelling through Russian-occupied territory to southern Russia, then flying to Belarus, evacuees arrived on buses to a military facility in Chernihiv on Saturday. On the tarmac, some elderly residents were so weak they had to be carried on stretchers.

‌



For many, there were emotional reunions once they returned to Ukraine.

The ceasefire was due to end last night. Mykhailo Palii had an emotional reunion with his daughters Dasha and Anya. He told them about life under military occupation.

‌



"A hole was blown into the bathroom," he told the BBC. "There were drone attacks and missile strikes. I didn't tell them about it because I knew they would worry."

News.title: Man, 18, dead and boy, 16, injured in moped crash in Kent after being approached by police patrol
News.content:
Man, 18, dead and boy, 16, injured in moped crash in Kent after being approached by police patrol

A moped crashed in Sheerness, Kent, on Saturday evening, killing an 18-year-old man and seriously injuring a 16-year-old boy

View Image Officers approached the moped while carrying out a foot patrol in the area around Sheppey Leisure Complex (file image) (Image: Google Maps)

An 18-year-old man has died and a 16-year-old boy has been critically injured after a moped crash in Kent.

‌



‌



Kent Police said officers approached two people riding a moped in Sheerness shortly before 7.50pm on Saturday while carrying out a foot patrol in the area around Sheppey Leisure Complex.

‌



The moped then left the scene via a nearby alleyway before crashing. Kent Police has referred itself to the Independent Office for Police Conduct (IOPC), and an investigation is under way.

‌



Didcot rapist who contacted funeral director in front of victim to arrange her funeral is jailed READ MORE :

Toddler injured after firework explodes near her in Northern Ireland READ MORE :

Officers at the scene provided first aid to both people. The rider, an 18-year-old man from Sheppey, was pronounced dead at the scene. The passenger, a 16-year-old boy from Sheppey, was taken to a London hospital, where he remains in a critical condition.

Police are appealing for anyone who witnessed the incident or the events immediately beforehand to come forward.

Article continues below

Anyone with information is asked to contact Kent Police on 01622 798538 or email sciu.td@kent.police.uk, quoting reference RY/JM/088/26.

CCTV or dashcam footage can be submitted through the force's online reporting portal.

News.title: Five teenagers stabbed at Halloween party
News.content:
Five teenagers have been seriously injured after being stabbed at a Halloween party, police have said.

Officers were called to Park Road in Chandler's Ford, near Eastleigh, shortly after 22:30 GMT on Saturday.

The injured teens - three boys aged 16 and two aged 17 - were taken to hospital.

Hampshire Police said it believes an unknown group gained entry to a party at an address on Park Road before the stabbings.

The force has appealed for witnesses and anyone with information to come forward.

A police cordon remained in place on Sunday while officers continue their investigation.

Senior investigating officer Det Ch Insp Elizabeth Pirie acknowledged the impact on local residents and thanked the community for its patience.

Earlier, an eyewitness told the BBC ambulances and an air ambulance had attended.

Another eyewitness said they saw someone running out of the house involved, shouting that he had been stabbed and that he was being chased by two people.

News.title: 'Like a missile coming down' - Nine killed in fiery Florida jet crash
News.content:
US media reports and flight analysis indicate that the jet was plummeting hundreds of feet per second before crashing.

In air traffic control audio recorded moments before the crash, the pilot of the aircraft can be heard saying the plane was descending 10,000 feet per minute, according to the BBC's US partner CBS News.

Then the pilot declared an emergency, yelling, "We are in an overspeed condition descending 20,000 feet per minute," CBS reported.

"We're gonna crash ... We're out of time," the pilot told the tower.

Unverified footage posted on social media shows what appears to be a dash-camera recording of the moment of the crash. It shows vehicles driving on a residential suburban street, when suddenly an aircraft nosedives into the ground almost vertically, and explodes into a large fireball.

"When you see that video, it's a jarring thing," Florida Governor Ron DeSantis told reporters at a news conference after the crash. "It's like a missile coming down, and a massive explosion, debris going everywhere."

It is not yet clear who was aboard the jet when it crashed. DeSantis said "as of now, we don't have any reports of anyone who was on the ground...who was killed or injured".

Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy described the crash as a "horrific tragedy", and said the FAA was sending a team to the scene to help an investigation by the National Transportation Safety Board.

"Please join me in praying for the families and loved ones of those we lost," Duffy added.

Palm Beach County Fire Rescue has declared a "mass casualty incident".

News.title: Thousands of jobs at Virgin Media O2 to be cut
News.content:
Thousands of Virgin Media O2 staff face redundancy risk as the telecoms firm looks to save money in the face of billions of pounds of debt and tougher competition.

The broadband provider has not finalised the number of roles to be cut but it is likely be a sizeable chunk of its 16,000 workforce, the BBC understands.

VMO2 has billions of debt on its balance sheet and is tackling competition from both smaller providers as well as giants like BT, which has agreed a deal to acquire rival TalkTalk, a move which VMO2 has firmly opposed.

VMO2 declined to comment. The Prospect union, which represents VMO2 staff, said the cuts were "disappointing and very unsettling".

Deputy general secretary Noel McClean said it was "committed to supporting our members through what is a difficult time, as well as also working with employers to explore ways to mitigate the number of redundancies and ensure retraining and redeployment of staff affected".

The majority of the affected staff will be in non-customer facing roles and a number of senior leadership changes are already under way, the BBC has been told.

VMO2 is also expected to review its use of contractors and suppliers in conjunction with the job cuts that were first reported by Sky News.

As of 30 June, VMO2's total debt stands at Â£27.2bn while it holds assets worth Â£45.9bn, according to the firm's latest accounts.

Meanwhile, the company is dealing with fierce competition from cheaper "altnets" like Hyperoptic, Community Fibre, Gigaclear and YouFibre.

VMO2 had attempted to respond to this growing threat by buying altnet competitor Netomnia for Â£2bn via nexfibre, a joint venture owned by VMO2's owners.

However, the Competition Markets Authority (CMA) has provisionally found competition concerns in the deal, external, with a final decision to come in December, sparking anger from VMO2.

News.title: Democrats have high hopes for midterms, but polls have let them down before
News.content:
The Democratic Party has high expectations as it heads into these pivotal US midterm elections.

A historically unpopular Republican president, an American public unhappy with the rising costs of food and bills, and months of favourable polls point to a good night for them on Tuesday.

Democratic candidates lead in well over the 218 seats needed to flip control of the lower chamber of Congress, the House of Representatives, the polls suggest. And they are tied or narrowly ahead in the key Senate races.

A recent New York Times poll had the Senate race in South Carolina, a state Donald Trump won by 18 percentage points in 2024, as a tie. Recent CNN surveys put the Democrats ahead in Texas, Kansas and Maine.

But are the polls accurate?

Recent US political history is littered with examples where public opinion polls, even ones just days before an election, were off the mark. Trump outperformed predictions on his way to White House victories in 2016 and 2024. His narrow defeat in 2020 came after most surveys indicated a more comfortable win for Democrat Joe Biden.

Earlier this year, polls suggested Democrat Abdul El-Sayed was poised for a double-digit win in Michigan's Democratic Senate primary. Instead it was 1%. In Wisconsin's Democratic primary for governor, the candidate that had a polling lead that approached 20 points lost by a fraction of a percent.

News.title: Antonelli becomes world champion as Verstappen wins in Mexico
News.content:
Kimi Antonelli clinched his first world title and became the youngest champion in Formula 1 history by finishing third at the Mexico City Grand Prix.

Antonelli - 20 years and 68 days old - finished the race in third, behind Red Bull's Max Verstappen and Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton.

His moment of glory came on a day when tensions at Ferrari between seven-time champion Hamilton and team-mate Charles Leclerc came close to boiling over.

Antonelli drove a composed race amid some hectic action involving the other front-runners in a grand prix interrupted by a red flag that led to a 25-lap sprint to the finish.

The Italian, a teenager until late August, spent the closing laps watching Hamilton try to get close enough to pass Verstappen after the two had made contact at the first chicane at the restart.

But Hamilton found it impossible to get his Ferrari close enough to Verstappen to try to pass and ended the day frustrated and feeling a win had slipped through his fingers as a consequence of Leclerc's aggression on the first lap.

That was a secondary story on the day Antonelli made history, smashing Sebastian Vettel's previous record for being the youngest champion by three years and 66 days.

Antonelli also becomes the first Italian to win the F1 title since Alberto Ascari in 1953.

Antonelli had tears mixed with laughter over the radio on the slowing down lap as he proved initially incapable of talking when his team told him he was world champion.

After he half-composed himself, he said: "Thank you so much. We did it. We did it."
