News.title: A&E warning system to flag sick children deteriorating quickly
News.content:
A similar "early warning" system to identify acutely ill adults, including those with sepsis, is already in use in emergency and general NHS hospital wards.

More than 90 hospitals across England have been using the alert system in children's wards, with different age-appropriate assessments available for babies through to teenagers.

The NHS has already said it will expand Martha's Rule to all hospital emergency departments in England. The rule gives patients, families and carers the right to request a rapid review if they are worried that a patient's condition is getting worse and their concerns are not being responded to.

The initiative is named after Martha Mills, who died aged 13 in 2021 after developing blood poisoning, or sepsis, in hospital following a bike accident.

A coroner ruled that her family's concerns about her worsening condition were not listened to and she would probably have survived had she been moved to intensive care earlier.

Martha's parents Merope and Paul came up with the idea of the rule in a bid to change the culture that contributed to her death.

A&E units will have a dedicated phone number that can be called to trigger an urgent review of a patient's care.

News.title: King to address slavery in Antigua as PM says he is open to possible UK apology
News.content:
King Charles III is to speak with "unflinching honesty" and "sincere sorrow" on the lasting pain of the transatlantic slave trade, during the final leg of his Caribbean tour in Antigua, Buckingham Palace has said.

The King will address Commonwealth leaders on Tuesday in a speech which will touch on the issue.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham said earlier he was "open" to the possibility of the UK formally apologising for its role in slavery - a change in the government's stance.

It is understood the Palace was told in advance of Burnham's comments in an opinion piece on Friday night, and the King has not made any changes to his speech in light of them.

The British government has never formally apologised for slavery or offered to pay reparations.

Burnham has previously stuck with the policy of his predecessors, and stopped short of offering any consideration of reparation payments.

In an address to the nation to mark Antigua and Barbuda's independence day, Prime Minister Gaston Browne said the history of slavery was painful and "its consequences have not disappeared with the passage of time".

He said the country's pursuit of reparatory justice deserved "seriousness, sensitivity and sustained international engagement".

Browne went on to say his government was having these conversations in bilateral discussions with the UK and other Commonwealth countries at the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting (CHOGM).

Conservative Party leader Kemi Badenoch described "endless talk about apologies" as a "distraction" from solving current problems.

She told BBC Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg: "The transatlantic slave trade happened centuries ago. It is time for the Commonwealth to start looking forwards, not endlessly backwards."

The King will make his speech at the CHOGM.

He "will not shy away from confronting the most shameful aspects of the past during this visit", a Palace spokesperson said.

"You may therefore expect him to address them in his speech with unflinching honesty, sincere sorrow, and respect for the wider discussions that will be taking place between relevant governments on this issue at CHOGM and beyond."

When asked about the King's reaction to the prime minister's comments, the spokesperson said it would "not be appropriate" for the King to address matters of policy relating to "the UK government's position".

The Caribbean tour has again thrust King Charles into the difficult debates over the UK's colonial legacy in the region.

On his first stop in the Bahamas, the King delivered a speech where he spoke of the "suffering of the past".

In Guyana, he visited the site of a Slave Rebellion where hundreds of enslaved people were killed.

Buckingham Palace said it was a moment for the King to learn more about the history of slavery and resistance. His engagements have also covered the environment, opportunities for young people and trade relationships with the UK.

News.title: Tributes to 'inspirational' Olympian Ciara Mageean after death at 34
News.content:
Tributes have been paid to former European champion and two-time Olympic runner Ciara Mageean, who has died at the age of 34.

Mageean, from Portaferry in County Down, was diagnosed with stage four bowel cancer in May 2025.

She died on Sunday morning, surrounded by her loved ones, a statement posted on her social media accounts said.

"A beloved daughter, sister, wife, friend and inspiration to so many, she will be deeply missed," it said.

Mageean's death comes less than three weeks after her marriage to her long-term partner Thomas Moran.

The athlete represented Ireland at the 2016 and 2020 Olympics and won gold in the 1500m at the European Athletics Championships in Rome in 2024.

She also represented Northern Ireland at the Commonwealth Games, winning silver in Birmingham in 2022.

News.title: Henry Nowak's family tell of trauma of seeing son handcuffed as he lay dying
News.content:
Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood has announced an independent review into the murder, led by former lord chancellor Alex Chalk, which will look at "any missed opportunities to intervene".

Henry, 18, from Chafford Hundred in Essex, was a first-year accountancy and finance student at the University of Southampton when he was murdered.

He was stabbed five times as he walked home from a night out with friends from his football team in Southampton on 3 December 2025.

Digwa, 23, was jailed for life with a minimum term of 21 years.

It took officers another 24 hours to identify Henry's body and tell his family.

"I jumped out of bed and I saw the police car on our driveway," said Katie.

"One of the police officers was holding his hat in his hand, and I just knew straight away that something horrific had happened."

She said Mark fell to his knees when he heard the news.

"He let out a cry that I'll never forget," she said.

"I just remember saying 'it's Henry' and breaking down in tears," Mark said. "It's just unbelievable pain."

News.title: Watch: King Charles III caught in torrential downpour at Antigua and Barbuda parade
News.content: King Charles III was left drenched and without an umbrella when a torrential downpour interrupted celebrations of Antigua and Barbuda's independence day on Sunday. Queen Camilla was swiftly given an umbrella when the rain started, while the King was seen gesturing to be given one of his own.

News.title: Reeves says UK's future should be inside the EU
News.content:
Former Chancellor Rachel Reeves has argued the UK's future should be inside the EU, and that Brexit has made the country "poorer, weaker and less secure".

In her first major intervention since leaving the Treasury, Reeves said she welcomed debate around the UK's relationship with Europe.

At the last election, Labour's manifesto said a Labour government would stay outside the EU and make Brexit work.

But Prime Minister Andy Burnham has said there needs to be an honest discussion about what the future relationship looks like.

The Conservatives have said there is no desire to rerun the Brexit debate and Reform UK's Nigel Farage has said there is no mandate to pursue closer EU ties.

Labour's 2024 election manifesto ruled out a return of free movement, single market membership or a customs union.

Burnham has said that any changes would require a mandate at a general election, which is next due by 2029.

In the Sunday Times, external, Reeves wrote: "No-one in the Treasury ever doubted where my instincts were. I do believe Britain's future lies in the European Union."

She said supporters of rejoining the EU had to "make the argument, demonstrate tangible benefits and to get the next steps right".

Reeves added that at the forthcoming UK-EU summit, she hoped for confirmation of the youth mobility scheme she has been pushing for since she was in office.

She also said she was hoping for "progress towards entry" into the Security Action for Europe (SAFE) scheme.

Announced last March, SAFE is part of an EU-wide effort to rearm after Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine.

A defence pact agreed with the EU last May paved the way for UK-based defence companies to be part of projects funded by SAFE.

In her piece for the Sunday Times, Reeves also sought to defend her record in office.

She wrote about the need for governments to be "braver" in building big infrastructure projects and "clear eyed" about the risks and benefits AI would drive in advanced economies.

Conservative Party leader Kemi Badenoch said she "can't even believe we are reopening" the Brexit debate.

She told BBC One's Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg: "This is not something that is needed in order to cut welfare, in order to spend money on defence.

"We are having yet another Westminster bubble argument about the EU when it is time for us to actually start using the opportunities, fix mistakes that have been made and go into the future."

Badenoch added: "I do not want to indulge Andy Burnham's fantasies about redoing the referendum because he doesn't have a plan for what to do today."

Burnham told Badenoch during the most recent session of Prime Minister's Questions that he was focused on "getting a better deal for Britain, that is my responsibility".

The next UK-EU summit will take place in Brussels on 20 November.

News.title: Karl Bushby 'overwhelmed' at Humber Bridge welcome
News.content:
British adventurer Karl Bushby crossed the Humber Bridge through thick mist on the final leg of his 31,000-mile (49,890 km), 28-year trek from South America to Hull.

Bushby left Chile in 1998 to head home to the UK without breaking two self-imposed rules: not to return to the UK until he had completed his journey, and not to use transport to advance.

The adventurer said he was "absolutely overwhelmed" by the crowds who lined the bridge.

Bushby, a former paratrooper, is due to complete the challenge on Monday and will be met by his mother, his son and granddaughter when he arrives in Hull.

News.title: More than 300 arrests at Palestine Action support protest outside US embassy
News.content:
More than 300 people have been arrested during a protest supporting the banned Palestine Action group outside the US embassy, police have said.

Hundreds of people gathered at Nine Elms in London on Saturday, with many holding signs reading phrases such as: "I oppose genocide, I support Palestine Action."

The Metropolitan Police said on Sunday that 325 arrests were made. The force added on social media that 320 of them were for "expressing support for a proscribed organisation under the Terrorism Act".

At least 4,000 arrests have been made in relation to the group, which was proscribed in July 2025.

The UK Supreme Court is due to review Palestine Action's ban under terrorism legislation, after the group's co-founder was granted permission to appeal it.

The Home Office has said that it will robustly defend against the appeal.

Officers on Saturday made arrests into the evening, taking people to police vans for transfer, to the applause of many protesters, some of whom chanted: "Free, free Palestine."

In some instances, officers had to carry demonstrators who refused to walk.

Retired lawyer Charles Allison - who was taken by police in the afternoon - had travelled from Cumbria to participate. He said he feared for people's civil liberties, which he said were "being devalued and watered down".

"I hope the Supreme Court justices - they won't necessarily be influenced by it [the protest] - but I hope that they will take a long-term view of what is happening in this country and decide that the proscription was unlawful, as I believe it was," the 75-year-old said.

David Bolden, another protester awaiting arrest called the ban an "absurd law".

Defend Our Juries, which has been co-ordinating a series of protests over the ban, said the number of people detained this weekend took the total over 4,000 arrests since the group was proscribed, calling it "truly dystopian".

According to Home Office figures seen by the BBC, 3,630 arrests were made in the year ending June 2026. Along with the 134 people arrested outside Westminster Magistrates Court earlier this year and those on Saturday brings the total up to 4,089.

The BBC has contacted the Met to confirm any figures it might hold.

Amnesty International UK has criticised the arrests and called for the government to drop the proscription of Palestine Action.

Defend Our Juries called the arrests "unjust" and an assault on free speech.

News.title: Healey risks breaking minimum wage promise for younger workers
News.content:
The Chancellor, John Healey, has suggested that younger workers might not receive the same minimum wage as others before the next election, potentially breaking a Labour manifesto promise.

In 2024, Labour said it would remove "discriminatory age bands", vowing to end the gap between the adult minimum wage and pay for 18 to 20-year-olds.

But in last week's Budget, Healey said that younger workers would see the same increase as older workers, leaving a gap between the two rates this year.

Pay for 18 to 20-year-olds in 2026 will rise to Â£11.27, while over-20s will be paid a minimum of Â£13.21 an hour.

In a BBC interview broadcast on Sunday, Healey was asked if younger workers would be paid the same as older workers, when it comes to the minimum wage, by the time of the next election?

"We'll take one step at a time," he said, suggesting that Labour might abandon its plan to close the gap before the next election.

It is a change that is likely to anger the unions and some on the left of the party.

Healey added that Labour was still committed to the ambition, but hinted the plan to equalise wages might be delayed, partly to encourage businesses to employ younger workers.

"There is no question about whether or if, it's a question of when - it's a question of how fast," he said.

"I want to make sure we can look hard at those trade-offs that are there between jobs and wages."

"I want to take business, I want to take trade unions with me, and with the government, because together we have to get into what at the moment is a moral shame on this nation. A million youngsters - written off without any prospect of being helped into work and making contributions to this country for the future."

News.title: Seven arrested after city centre firework disorder
News.content:
Seven people have been arrested after disorder, involving fireworks being set off, in a city centre.

Footage posted on social media showed crowds gathered on Corporation Street in Birmingham, with fireworks being set off close to police officers and vehicles.

West Midlands Police had warned firm action would be taken against anyone involved in fireworks-related disorder, following serious incidents in the city during Bonfire Night last year.

Those arrested, aged between 15 and 26, were held on suspicion of offences including assault, possession of fireworks and possession of an offensive weapon.

They all remain in custody for questioning, the force said.

Officers used Section 60 stop-and-search powers, which allow searches without the need to have reasonable grounds to do so.

The arrests were made in and around Stephenson Street and Corporation Street, after officers responded to "pockets of disorder," involving fireworks being set off in a dangerous manner, said the force.

Ch Supt Tom Boyce said: "Misusing fireworks is not only dangerous: it's illegal and can lead to fines, arrest and criminal charges."

The force said extra officers had been deployed at key locations to prevent a repeat of last year's violence.

On 6 November 2025, 21 people were arrested after officers were attacked with fireworks on Dale End and Staniforth Street.

News.title: Police probe video of officer hitting youth with handcuffs
News.content:
A police force has said it is reviewing a video which shows one of its officers punching a boy.

The footage circulated on social media shows a Merseyside Police officer punching what appears to be teenage boy three times while holding a pair of metal handcuffs in the hand he is striking him with.

The force said officers had been responding on Friday to reports of about 20 youths in the Alder Wood Avenue area of Speke, Liverpool, blocking roads with wheelie bins and "aiming fireworks at anyone who tried to remove them".

"We would like to stress that a short clip doesn't always show the full context," a Merseyside Police spokesman said.

The footage being circulated on social media - which has been viewed more than 40,000 times - begins moments before the officer strikes the boy.

It does not show anything that happened in the run-up to the incident.

Merseyside Police said youths had reportedly "smashed windows of nearby flats, tried to start fires and threatened members of the public".

News.title: Nobody Wants This star shuts down rumors about on-set tension
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Nobody Wants This actor Tovah Feldshuh is shutting down speculation about tension on the show over Adam Brody’s statement that he supports “a free Palestine.”

Rumors about bad blood on the set of the hit Netflix rom-com series have swirled since Brody, 46, voiced support for Palestine and called Israel’s actions in Gaza a genocide, which show creator Erin Foster later disagreed with publicly.

However, 77-year-old Feldshuh — who plays Brody’s mother, Bina Roklov, on the show — denied claims of a behind-the-scenes feud in a recent post on Threads.

“Tensions are NOT RISING,” the actor wrote. “Profound differences of opinion are. Please do not conflate the two — And none of it will be brought to the set.”

She added: “I deeply enjoy filming [Nobody Wants This] and hope we are chosen to go on for a fourth season.”

open image in gallery 'Nobody Wants This' actor Tovah Feldshuh is denying rumors about tension on set ( AFP/Getty )

In the Netflix series, which first premiered in September 2024, Brody plays a rabbi who falls in love with a non-Jewish woman played by Kristen Bell. The show is loosely based on creator Erin Foster’s experiences of converting to Judaism after meeting her husband.

While promoting the show’s third season, Brody told GQ in September: “Put me down as thinking it’s a genocide. Put me down as wanting a free Palestine.”

“It’s awful that it’s taken so much death and misery, but it does feel like it’s reaching a breaking point that it should have a while ago. I’m hopeful that another administration can really do some good and correct some of these policies that are helping that situation be as awful as it is,” he said.

open image in gallery Kristen Bell and Adam Brody star in the Netflix series ( Netflix )

The comments sparked pushback from some of his colleagues, including Feldshuh. She told the New York Post at the time, “To accuse the Jewish people of genocide is wild. It’s right out of Hitler’s playbook. You take the victim and you make the victim the perpetrator.”

Last month, Foster finally spoke out on Brody’s remarks and said that while she disagrees with his view, “everyone is entitled to a different opinion.”

“You know, it’s complicated. I think our work environment, our set, is very similar to dinner tables around the world, where people are having debate and discussion and disagreeing,” she said on the Not Skinny But Not Fat podcast. “And while I love Adam, I also disagree with him, and that’s okay.”

She went on to describe her show as a “love letter to Judaism.”

“That is why I made this show. It’s because of how beautiful of an experience I’ve had becoming Jewish and being a Jewish person, and sitting here right now at this time in the world where there is almost zero positive representation of Jewish people,” she said. “I think it’s so important to have that, and that is what this show is intended to be.”

She added: “Everyone is entitled to a different opinion than me. I can just tell you what I created this show for and what the intention of the show is.”

News.title: ‘I let it all out’ – Emotional Kimi Antonelli makes F1 history in Mexico
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Kimi Antonelli admitted he had tears in his eyes on the final lap in Mexico City as he made history by becoming Formula One’s youngest world champion.

The 20-year-old clinched the title by finishing third on Sunday, completing an extraordinary march to the crown in just his second season in the sport – with four rounds remaining.

He needed to finish only ninth but showed composure beyond his years to navigate a chaotic race and become the first Italian champion since 1953.

Antonelli parked his Mercedes in the middle of the raucous Foro Sol Stadium, jumping out of the car and into the arms of his jubilant parents and younger sister Maggie.

Kimi Antonelli has clinched the 2026 Formula One title to secure his place in history as the sport’s youngest world champion.

“I think I lost probably two seconds because I was already crying,” Antonelli said, when asked what was going through his mind.

“I couldn’t see clearly ahead – and I could see two Ferraris somehow with the tears!

“A lot of memories went through my mind in that moment. All the memories since karting. So, it was a very special final lap and definitely, when I crossed the line, I let it all out because achieving one of my biggest dreams is very special.

“To be able to share this moment, to witness this moment with my whole family, with my team, and for my friends as well, it’s a moment that will be always remembered.”

The race was won by Max Verstappen, with Lewis Hamilton second, meaning Antonelli shared the podium with two men who have 11 world championships between them.

open image in gallery

There was a fitting moment as F1’s newest champion found himself on the shoulders of giants, Hamilton and Verstappen holding the young Italian aloft on the podium.

“I will definitely frame that picture and put it in my house, because it’s just an incredible moment. It’s great to see so much respect from two incredible drivers,” Antonelli added.

During his world champion’s press conference, Antonelli became emotional when asked about Italian opera song Nessun Dorma playing as he celebrated in the stadium.

“It was very emotional for me because it was a song that my grandfather used to listen to always, so it was very special to hear that,” he said, before breaking down in tears.

“So I think that he would be very proud. Oh, my word. I cried too much today!

“I just felt very emotional because of my grandfather, so I was very happy also for him.”

Father Marco, himself a former racing driver, has been by Kimi’s side throughout.

Antonelli was signed by Mercedes at the age of 12, the karting superstar rising through the ranks before being chosen as Hamilton’s replacement in 2024.

He credits his family for helping him remain grounded on his path to F1 glory, adding: “My dad, you know, has come to basically all the races this year… it has been crucial to have such a leader.

“And, my mum and my sister, when they could come, but especially my dad during the whole season, was very important because he was the one keeping me grounded, especially after very hard moments.

open image in gallery Antonelli was embraced by his parents (Bradley Collyer/PA) ( PA Wire )

“He was the one that was always there when I was facing a difficult situation or I wasn’t feeling the best.”

Antonelli has won nine races in a dominant season, with his third place in Mexico extending his title lead to a whopping 119 points over Verstappen – who rose to second place.

The world champion has the right to put the number one on their car for the following season but Antonelli intends to stick to 12 – the number associated with racing hero Ayrton Senna.

“I’ll stay with number 12 because obviously it’s a very special number for me, but also it’s a way for me to stay grounded, to stay humble,” he said.

“I feel like by keeping number 12, it allows me to have a new point where to start and build on everything again and try to improve.”

open image in gallery

Antonelli will have little time to celebrate his crowning moment, saying he will spend the evening with his family, as F1 heads to Senna’s home of Brazil next weekend.

The Bologna-born star does not drink alcohol but intends to toast his special moment in style after that race and before Las Vegas.

“Definitely when I will go back home, I will take time and I will organise something big,” Antonelli said.

“I’ve got to enjoy the moment. And then, of course, we’re going to try to enjoy Brazil next week. Of course, it’s a very special race coming up for many reasons.

“Probably I won’t be in the best state in Vegas, but it’s fine right?!I’m going to enjoy the moment.”

News.title: Photos show elaborate preparations for Thailand’s Royal Barges Procession
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

More than 2,000 oarsmen have spent months preparing for a centuries-old Thai royal tradition that will fill Bangkok’s Chao Phraya River with a fleet of intricately decorated barges on Friday.

The Royal Barge Procession is held in time for the annual Buddhist Kathin ceremony, which takes place after the end of Buddhist Lent. Buddhists offer kathin robes to monks who have remained in their monasteries throughout the three-month retreat in the rainy season.

The fleet, consisting of a total of 52 barges, will take King Maha Vajiralongkorn, Queen Suthida and members of the royal family to the Wat Arun Ratchawararam temple.

The 2,200 oarsmen from the Royal Thai Navy started their training in June, learning how to row the barges in unison at a navy dockyard before rehearsing in the river in late July.

The full dress rehearsals were performed twice in late October, drawing spectators along both sides of the river.

The rowers must master not only the precise movements required to maintain the fleet formation of five columns and three lines, but also the traditional boat songs performed during the procession. The songs help coordinate the rowing while portraying Thailand’s cultural tradition.

Thailand's Fine Arts Department has been restoring the wooden barges while preserving their traditional artistic details. The vessels have also undergone safety inspections and decorative work in preparation for the event.

The fleet includes four principal royal barges distinguished by their elaborate designs and decorations.

One features the head of the golden mythical swan on its prow, while others feature the multi-headed Naga, a mythical serpent, or depict the Hindu deity Narayana riding on a mythical bird-like creature.

The Royal Barge Procession is reserved for special royal occasions. This year's ceremony is being held in an auspicious year for Queen Suthida, who turned 48 in June, marking her fourth 12-year cycle.

The most recent procession took place in 2024 to commemorate King Maha Vajiralongkorn’s 72nd birthday, marking his sixth 12-year cycle.

News.title: The secrets behind Kimi Antonelli’s historic F1 triumph – and how Ferrari missed out on Italian superstar
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

It probably wasn’t quite how Kimi Antonelli envisaged his inaugural top-of-the-step moment. “Congratulations… Kimi Raikkonen!” bellowed long-time Formula 1 podium announcer Bob Constanduros, as the young Italian jumped onto the podium at the Shanghai International Circuit in March. Antonelli, the lad with a ruthless cutting edge intertwined with a feverishly boyish charm, gestured and laughed with his team down below.

While it was a comical blunder, comparisons to his namesake Finnish driver (sadly for this section, Antonelli’s middle name was not in tribute to Raikkonen) seem somewhat appropriate for the 20-year-old Italian who, on Sunday night, became the youngest Formula 1 world champion ever. Raikkonen, Ferrari’s last champion in 2007, was known as “The Iceman”, such was his cold, unflustered demeanour. And in just his second F1 season, Antonelli’s poise and serenity have been his biggest asset.

Antonelli’s third-place finish in Mexico, off the back of his brilliant lights-to-flag victory in Austin last week, rather epitomised the Italian’s near-flawless campaign – and that of his forlorn Mercedes teammate, George Russell. While Antonelli made ground at the start in Mexico City, Russell dropped back and received a 10-second penalty after spinning Isack Hadjar. He finished sixth and did not attend the media pen post-race: it rather summed up the Briton’s year.

open image in gallery Antonelli has not just beaten teammate George Russell this season but wiped the floor with him this year ( Getty )

open image in gallery Twelve world championships: Max Verstappen (four), Lewis Hamilton (seven) and now Kimi Antonelli (one) ( Getty )

A season which had Russell as the clear pre-season favourite – in the quickest car on the grid – has resulted in Toto Wolff’s Italian protege, the teen he trusted with filling Lewis Hamilton’s seismic boots, dominating the 2026 campaign.

And for Antonelli, it is a history-making achievement. At 20 years and 68 days, the Italian becomes the sport’s youngest-ever champion in its 76-year history, beating Sebastian Vettel’s previous record of 23 years of age. In quite the twist of fate, Antonelli was actually born on the same day that Vettel made his F1 race weekend debut in Turkey in August 2006.

Astonishingly, Antonelli also becomes Italy’s first world champion in 73 years, when the great Alberto Ascari won for Ferrari in 1963. Alongside multiple Grand Slam champion Jannik Sinner, he is now Italian sport’s biggest star.

His maturity, a year on from being in tears at Spa-Francorchamps after a disastrous qualifying performance, has been startlingly impressive, witnessed too by journalists up and down the paddock. At the season-opener in Australia, The Independent was present as Mercedes held a press event early on the first media day morning at Albert Park: the ultimate indication that a team is confident in their new car.

Typically with such events, there was a preamble before the driver Q&A: coffees, biscuits, small talk. Antonelli swooped over, shook every reporter’s hand and asked how their journey down under was, such was the Middle East travel chaos that had ensued days before. It’s the small details which stick in the memory of the sport’s travelling circus: Antonelli did similar at F1 75 Live last year in London, greeting members of the press room ahead of his rookie campaign. His affability, despite the no-holds-barred environment of Formula 1, is commendable and a credit to his parents, Marco and Veronica.

It was at three years old when Kimi told Marco that he wanted to try the racing simulator his father, an amateur racer in Italy who ran a team in nearby San Marino, had brought home. So the story goes: Kimi controlled the wheel, Marco the pedals.

Two years later, he started karting at a mini-bike track in Galliano Park in Forli, around an hour from his home in Bologna. At eight years old, he was scouted and signed to Minardi Management; at 12 in 2018 (the same year Russell won Formula 2), he signed onto Mercedes’ young driver programme.

open image in gallery Marco Antonelli has been alongside his son throughout his championship-winning year ( PA Wire )

Now the obvious question that hovers over the Emilia Romagna region: how did Ferrari, Italy’s team based in Maranello, 30 minutes away from Antonelli’s home, miss out on Italian motorsport’s next big thing? Then-team principal Maurizio Arrivabene insisted Antonelli was “too young” to be signed to an F1 team, despite a strong urge from Massimo Rivola, then-director of Ferrari’s Driver Academy. Mercedes did not need any invitation to swoop in themselves.

For a team like Ferrari, notorious for questionable internal decision-making, that really does now look like an all-time fumble.

Yet Ferrari’s pain has proved to be Mercedes’ gain. Antonelli stormed through the junior ranks: from 2018 to 2022, he won an astonishing 18 different karting championships. His inevitable progression up to single-seater open-cockpit cars did not slow his ascent and, when he stormed to Formula Regional titles in the Middle East and Europe in 2023, Mercedes did not waste any time. Instead of the usual progression to Formula 3, Antonelli skipped that series and went straight into Formula 2.

By now, Wolff had a decision to make. Hamilton’s exit had left the Austrian executive on the back foot in the driver market and, when it became apparent that he couldn’t persuade Max Verstappen – the generational driver he always rued missing out on – to jump ship at Red Bull, Wolff ignored seasoned veterans of the sport and plumped for his own in-house generational talent.

It wasn’t a sure-fire thing as it now seems, though. Antonelli did not waltz through his F2 season, ultimately finishing sixth and winning just two races. Most memorably, he also smashed his Mercedes into the wall at Parabolica on his F1 race weekend debut in Monza in 2024, by which time it had already been decided that Antonelli would partner Russell in 2025.

“All good Kimi,” said a stunned Wolff in the garage. “All good.”

open image in gallery Antonelli was earmarked as a generational talent from an early age ( Getty )

open image in gallery Antonelli crashed in his first F1 practice session after just 10 minutes ( Getty )

Yet his on-the-limit driving, despite the costly repair work, was a sign of his killer instinct. And while his rookie F1 campaign ultimately had more downs than ups, this year’s generation of car – away from the ground-effect model which so suited Russell – alongside Mercedes’ newfound competitiveness at the top of the standings has given Antonelli a new lease of life.

Russell, in particular, has found his smoother driving style, breaking earlier with mid-corner speed, hampered this year with a regular overheating of these narrower tyres, leading to lower grip on a handful of tracks. Meanwhile, Antonelli, much like Hamilton this year, has taken to the 50/50 battery-engine combination with aplomb. While the likes of Verstappen and Lando Norris moaned about these questionable new cars, Antonelli kept his head down and worked with it. Throughout it all, he has eeked out every possible millisecond. It’s all about the margins.

And to win a championship, you need consistency. While Antonelli’s advantage in the last few weeks has been seismic, he has not waltzed to endless victories a la Verstappen in 2023. His standout statistic out of 19 rounds this year is not his wins (nine) but his podiums (16). Only twice has Antonelli finished outside the top five. Antonelli’s totting up of points has been relentless – and has not given Russell a sniff.

Of course, there have been standout moments: his win from pole in China (his first in Formula 1) set him on his way to five victories in a row, the last of which came at the sport’s crown jewel event in Monaco. Spa-Francorchamps in July too, perhaps the sport’s most dangerous circuit and where Antonelli toiled last year, saw the Italian absolutely dominate. Last year, the European summer season was a lesson learnt for the then-teen; 12 months on, Antonelli’s growth in stature and maturity was clear as day.

open image in gallery Antonelli was the first Italian to win at Monza since 1966 ( PA Wire )

open image in gallery Toto Wolff never wavered in his belief in Antonelli (David Davies/PA) ( PA Wire )

But when the petrolheads look back on the 2026 campaign, Monza will be the flagship chapter. The Italian, who took an engine penalty, started at the back of the grid in 19th but stormed to the leading contenders by lap 13. Then, he gained 15 seconds over 21 laps on leader Russell and overtook him with a handful of laps remaining. The adoring tifosi, perhaps for the first time ever, celebrated wildly for a driver not decked in Ferrari red. And for Russell, it was a knockout blow.

And when the Briton’s engine failed at the end of the one-off round in Malaysia – it should be noted that Russell has not had any luck this year, with two DNFs costing him 40 points alone – it was virtually game over. Yet the margin extending to three figures in the last few weeks has been damaging for Russell, whose confidence is shot. And after Mexico, he has dropped behind Verstappen and Hamilton to fourth in the championship.

Yet on Halloween weekend in Mexico City, there were no Sunday scaries for Antonelli. With his family watching on proudly in the garage, there were celebrations aplenty in the paddock. Quite surprisingly, the chat is that Mercedes have actually turned down the temptation of a Mexican tequila bar, instead opting to return to base.

But the next generation is now. At the start of the last regulation set, Verstappen stamped his authority and won four in a row. The more pertinent question now looms: how many world championships will Antonelli claim? With this era lasting until 2030, it could well be a very similar story.

News.title: Lewis Hamilton insists ‘serious talks’ needed with Ferrari after Charles Leclerc clash
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Lewis Hamilton insists he needs to have “serious talks” with his Ferrari team after a costly clash with teammate Charles Leclerc at the Mexico City Grand Prix.

Hamilton, starting on pole for the first time in red, defended well from Leclerc at the start before the Monegasque came surging alongside heading into turn four-five.

Leclerc failed to make the corner but took the lead while Hamilton lost second place to Max Verstappen after attempting to stay on the circuit. Leclerc was then given a five-second penalty which, ultimately, handed the win to Verstappen.

In the end, Leclerc finished fourth after losing out on the second restart while Hamilton came home to finish second but – while congratulating Kimi Antonelli on his world title – was notably upset in his post-race interviews.

Prior to the podium, Hamilton told Nico Rosberg: “A tough day. I think we had the pace to win but it wasn't meant to be – we’ll take it offline and wonder what we can do in the battle.

“In the drivers' briefing, we discussed it... as soon as you go off in turn one, you have to give it back. Last year, I got a 10-second [penalty]. Ultimately, that lost us the win today. We have to have some serious talks behind the scenes.

“But the team's worked really hard - good result, good points, shame we didn't get a win but some you win, some you lose.

“I'm hoping next year we have an engine to compete with them [Mercedes] – they were flying past us on the straights. I'm relying on the team, I have 100% faith in them.”

In the race, Hamilton said the team have “big, big problems” and, speaking later to Sky Sports F1, Hamilton insisted that Leclerc’s move was to the detriment of the team.

“In the race, I gave it everything. It was lost in first two corners. We could’ve easily finished first and second in this race.

open image in gallery Hamilton was furious after an early coming together with Leclerc (Bradley Collyer/PA) ( PA Wire )

“We didn’t sit down and talk before. Again, it’s all fair and well racing against your teammate as long as it’s not to the detriment to the team result. The team has to come first. Today, we lost the win, points, lost second in the team championship, it affects so many people. It impacts the people who put in all the hard work in and the tifosi, it’s not good.

“It definitely needs some discussion for sure. We’ll take it offline.”

Leclerc, however, insisted the gap was there to attack on track as he eyed a second victory of the season.

He said: “Turn 1-2 there was a gap… when fighting for a win, I’ll go for it. Turn four-five, we both didn’t make the corner.

open image in gallery Leclerc defended his first lap move ( Getty )

“It was about giving the position back, but then Lewis got overtaken by Max and I thought it was worth it to try and see what happened. I asked on the radio; I kept my position.

“For sure, I’m sure Lewis hated those first few laps; we’ll discuss.”

Pointedly, in his own post-race interview, Ferrari team principal Fred Vasseur seemed to side with seven-time world champion Hamilton.

“It's about respect for the team,” he said. “Working night and day. It’s difficult to digest giving up a win like this; honestly, today I'm a bit down.

“The comments of Lewis we'll discuss with Lewis, comments of Charles we'll discuss with Charles. What I see is the result. We were one-two in Mexico, and you lose the race. We were able to do it.”

Hamilton remains in third in the world championship but now sits behind Verstappen, who occupies second place.

News.title: Burnham unveils £700m million to drive re-industrialisation in latest devolution push
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Andy Burnham has unveiled a £700 million package to help drive reindustrialisation in his latest push for devolution.

Mayors and local leaders are set to help the government identify 10 industrial and commercial sites across the UK in an effort to break down “barriers that hold back investment”.

The Strategic Sites Accelerator will deploy £700 million, alongside expert support including planning, grid connections and access to finance.

The programme aims to attract up to £2 billion in private investment, which according to the government could help to support tens of thousands of jobs over time.

Chancellor John Healey said the scheme will help “break down barriers to local growth”.

“Local leaders know their communities best. Only by trusting them with real power and resources will we see change,” he said.

open image in gallery Andy Burnham has unveiled a £700 million package to help drive reindustrialisation in his latest push for devolution. ( PA Wire )

“This £700 million package is helping break down the barriers to local growth, so people can feel the benefits of a growing economy and love where they live.”

The programme is set to focus on commercially viable sites with strong investor demand, and is already engaging on potential sites in Glasgow, Burgess Hill and Sheffield.

The sites will benefit from access to finance, grid connections, and planning constraints, which would remove the blockers for would-be investors.

Investment opportunities will also be explored in areas such as Greater Manchester, West Yorkshire, West Midlands, South Yorkshire, Liverpool City Region, the North East, Glasgow City Region and Cardiff Capital Region.

No10 North will work alongside the programme and local leaders to support the government’s wider drive to identify investment opportunities across the country, with the programme being open to sites across the UK to support sectors such as advanced manufacturing, digital and tech, defence, and life sciences.

open image in gallery Chancellor John Healey said the scheme will help “break down barriers to local growth”. ( BBC )

Business secretary Jonathan Reynolds said the programme will “get the ball rolling for up to 10 of the UK’s most important potential sites”, helping achieve the government’s promise of “good growth in every postcode”.

“Britain’s potential is everywhere, but we hear the same old arguments all too often – outdated infrastructure, insufficient access to finance, and problems with planning,” he said.

“These are barriers that hold back investment, block new jobs, and shackle our potential, and we need to do more to empower our local leaders and help drive the growth their communities deserve and expect.

“This programme will get the ball rolling for up to 10 of the UK’s most important potential sites, attract billions in investment, unlock tens of thousands of good-quality jobs in the years ahead, and bring good growth to every postcode.”

It marks the prime minister’s latest step in his devolution drive, as ten new devolution agreements are in their final stages.

These will establish new mayoral authorities in: Devon, Plymouth and Torbay; Hertfordshire; Lancashire; Leicester, Leicestershire and Rutland; Stoke and Staffordshire; Surrey; Thames Valley; and Wessex.

Kent and Medway, and Cornwall will set up slightly different devolution models under the proposals.

Delivering the Budget, chancellor John Healey said this would mean: “New powers to the people who know their areas best, not sentimentality but supply-side economics. The biggest wave of devolution in a generation, driving good growth in every postcode delivered to the British people by this Labour government.”

Central to the changes is the plan to give most mayoralties a share of income tax generated in their regions.

From April 2028, authorities with directly elected mayors will receive a uniform rate of local basic-rate income tax. Mayors will not set tax rates or bands, but will retain the revenue to fund local infrastructure, transport, and housing.

News.title: Skilled migrants would boost UK public finances by £115bn under current rules, analysis finds
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

New analysis has found skilled migrants and their dependants would boost the UK’s public finances by £115 billion under current settlement rules, as Shabana Mahmood prepares to unveil her controversial migration reforms.

The home secretary has faced backlash from within her own party over her proposals to double the qualifying period for settlement for most migrants from five to 10 years, and potentially triple it to 15 for care workers.

Ms Mahmood is reportedly expected to announce her final decision on plans - which could apply retrospectively to people already living and working in Britain - to parliament next week, following a public consultation that generated more than 200,000 responses.

The controversial reforms come as new analysis by the Institute for Public Policy Research (IPPR) reveals that skilled migrants and their adult dependants due to settle in the UK under current rules are expected to contribute £115bn more to UK public finances than they cost over their lifetimes.

The analysis uses the same methodology as the government's £10 billion lifetime cost estimate for care workers, highlighting the economic benefits of skilled migration through the taxes they pay.

The home secretary has faced backlash from within her own party over her proposals to double the qualifying period for settlement for most migrants from five to 10 years, and potentially triple it to 15 for care workers ( AFP/Getty )

The influential think tank welcomed signs that care workers could remain on the current five-year route, and proposed finding a “compromise” for other cohorts already in the UK, such as allowing them to stay on a five-year route or introducing an “interim status”.

Marley Morris, associate director for migration, trade and communities at IPPR, said: "Public debate has focused heavily on the costs of recent migration, but this is not the whole story. Our analysis suggests that over their lifetimes skilled migrants are estimated to make a net contribution of billions to the public finances.

“We welcome signs that the government is planning a compromise for its settlement reforms. Ministers should honour the rules people came here under or offer a fair compromise that gives them a secure pathway to settlement and freedom to change jobs after five years.”

Ministers have faced growing demands to curb high levels of migration and reduce pressure on public services, following record net migration figures under the previous Conservative administration.

But the prospect of applying the restrictions retrospectively has triggered internal conflict within the government, with ministers now reportedly poised to scale back the plans, according to the BBC.

There has been a backlash within Labour over the proposals, and tensions in the Cabinet surfaced when Housing Secretary Angela Rayner earlier this year publicly attacked the prospect of backdating the plans.

Last month, amid speculation the proposals could be watered down to avoid a Labour rebellion, prime minister Andy Burnham said he strongly supports that indefinite leave to remain is a “right to be earned”, but stopped short of committing to bringing in all of Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood’s reforms.

Asked if he would commit to sticking to the plans, the PM said: “We’re in a position where we’ve been consulting on those reforms, and we will come forward with our decisions soon.

“But I strongly support the Home Secretary when she says that settlement is a right to be earned through contribution, and that will be the principle that guides our reforms.”

News.title: Tears flow for Antonelli after becoming youngest champion in F1 history
News.content:
Welcome to our coverage for the 2026 Mexico City Grand Prix from the Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez. Today could be the day for Kimi Antonelli, the day he becomes a Formula One world champion. In fact it is very likely. All he needs to confirm the drivers’ championship is to finish ninth or higher. If George Russell or Lewis Hamilton do not claim victory then he is champion whatever happens. Given his season so far, it is difficult to see the title fight going to Brazil next week.

What chance of a decent race here today? The first few laps are often entertaining as the pack bunches up and there are plenty of chances to overtake early on. Generally the top four teams have been close together (last week in Austin excluded) and it is possible to overtake here, though it is not exactly easy.

Qualifying yesterday as an intriguing and close session. Hamilton secured his first grand prix pole for Ferrari, by just 0.009sec from the Mercedes of George Russell, with Charles Leclerc of Ferrari a little behind him in third. Then came Max Verstappen, Antonelli, Norris, Hadjar and Lindblad. Liam Lawson was disqualified on a technicality.

Ferrari have been an up-and-down team this season but have been strong without really delivering on it fully in the last few rounds. Could they secure a third victory of the season today? They do not really need to worry about losing second in the constructors to Red Bull or McLaren and Mercedes are too far out of reach in any case.

In any case, the biggest story is likely to be Antonelli’s coronation in Mexico. Hamilton has won titles here before for Mercedes, will the Italian give the Silver Arrows another fiesta in Mexico City? The race starts at 8pm GMT and we will be here for all the build-up, live updates and reaction from it.

News.title: Mikel Arteta’s smash-and-grab ends Arsenal’s 14-year Anfield hoodoo
News.content:
Arsenal’s version of the Yellow Wall (in their away shirts) was, indeed, hugely impressive – it is now six clean sheets from their nine league games and, despite all their pressure, Liverpool did not have a shot on target. That has never happened in the Premier League since such statistics started to be compiled in 2003 (422 games ago).

“That’s incredible. It did not feel like it on the pitch. Again, it’s the commitment of every single player,” Arteta said. And that was indisputable.

Even the expected second-half momentum, the expected surge of attack after attack as Liverpool faced the Kop, crashed on Arsenal’s backline. The visitors were so well-drilled that they stifled space – they refused to crumble.

Arsenal put their bodies on the line with blocks and tackles and a bit of time-wasting. There were dark arts, especially from both centre-halves with Gabriel going unpunished after claiming he was struck in the face by Isak early on – VAR anyone? – and the otherwise outstanding Ezri Konsa throwing himself to the ground after minimal contact from the Liverpool centre-forward.

In fairness there was also a bit of that from an increasingly frustrated Liverpool with Alexis Mac Allister going down after touching heads with Noni Madueke, having already tried to provoke Martin Odegaard with a hand to the head when the Arsenal captain was on the turf. That was not good from Mac Allister either.

News.title: Lewis Hamilton becomes oldest driver to claim pole position in 44 years
News.content:
Welcome to our live coverage for qualifying for the 2026 Mexico City Grand Prix from the Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez in Mexico City, obviously. The big story this weekend is that Jimi Antonelli is almost certain to become the youngest world champion in Formula One history. To guarantee it he needs just two points, but if George Russell or Lewis Hamilton fail to win here then the title is his whatever he does. It has been a superb, strong and consistent season from the man who began the year as a teenager. He has not quite been faultless, but he has not been far away.

There are other stories floating around the paddock, too. Notably, Esteban Ocon has been dropped by Haas today for final practice, qualifying and the race, to be replaced by reserve driver Ryo Hirakawa for the weekend. Whether Ocon will continue in any other races has yet to be confirmed but you have to say that it seems extremely unlikely. More on that later.

Another line is the ongoing tension between Liam Lawson and Max Verstappen after their crash in FP2 yesterday. It was certainly a strange one in which neither driver backed down, which resulted in contact, debris being strewn across the track and a red flag. Both drivers seemed unrepentant, though admitted it was clumsy. Lawson and Verstappen each receive a one-place grid penalty for the incident, which feels about right given how silly and unnecessary it all was.

But what about the competitive order on track? Since the summer break, and a little before in fairness, things have been unpredictable at the top. Mercedes have still, on average, been the best team but Ferrari, Red Bull and McLaren have all had their moments.

What happened in final practice? It was Lando Norris who topped the timesheets by just 0.001sec ahead of Mercedes’ Antonelli. Charles Leclerc was a further tenth or so back for Ferrari followed by Oscar Piastri in the other McLaren, who was 0.195sec off his team-mate’s pace. Then came Verstappen, Hamilton, Russell, Isack Hadjar, Lawson and Arvid Lindblad. All drivers were within 0.6sec off Norris, which promises a close qualifying session. Let’s hope we get it.

News.title: Suzuki howler costs Aston Villa crucial points
News.content:
Tonight sees a battle between two Spaniards at Villa Park as Aston Villa host Fulham. Both sides are looking to bounce back from disappointing midweeks having been knocked out of the League Cup; Aston Villa lost 3-0 at Bournemouth, while Fulham fell to a 1-0 defeat at home against Crystal Palace.

After a slow start to the season in the league, Aston Villa’s form has picked up, which includes handing Manchester City their first defeat of the season a week ago. After this evening, Aston Villa have games against Barcelona and Manchester United before the international break but Unai Emery has insisted his full focus is on this game.

“If we are thinking after the match against Fulham, then we are making a mistake and we are completely wrong,” Emery said. “We are prioritising the Premier League, and this is the message. To keep our consistency and demands means that each match is a test.”

Having failed to win any of their first six league games, Fulham have now won back-to-back Premier League games, with consecutive 1-0 wins over Hull and Coventry, which has lifted them out of the relegation zone.

“It [managing in England] is a very tough challenge but I am so happy to be here,” Alvaro Arbeloa said. “I am where I want to be and I am really enjoying my days. I want to win games and I think we are performing well but we need to improve.

“They [Aston Villa] are very compact, they defend so well and even with the ball they know what they have to do. And they have top players, and when you have a top coach with top players, normally you have a top team. I think right now he [Unai Emery] is one of the best coaches in the world. He is very, very good, he improves everything every year. It does not matter where he is coaching, he is doing an amazing job, and for me also it is a very good challenge to face him.”

In the two league meetings between these sides last season, it was one win apiece; Aston Villa won this fixture 3-1 just over a year ago before Fulham won 1-0 at Craven Cottage back in April. Team news from Villa Park to follow shortly.

News.title: Alex Mitchell injury blow for England but Northampton dig deep to win
News.content:
England were dealt a fresh blow ahead of their Nations Championship opener with Australia after scrum-half Alex Mitchell was forced off early in Northampton’s victory over Gloucester.

Mitchell left the field gingerly 20 minutes into the action after picking up a suspected hamstring injury following an innocuous coming-together with Gloucester winger Will Joseph.

The Saints scrum-half has suffered a series of hamstring issues this year – this would be a fourth time he has picked up a problem – and he looked visibly disappointed as he limped off.

He suffered a left leg hamstring tear during England’s Six Nations defeat to Ireland which left him sidelined for two months and, in a cruel twist of fate, sustained another on his right leg during an England three-day training camp in Bagshot last May. He suffered the injury for a third time in England’s 73-8 rout of Fiji in July.

With Mitchell’s club-mate, Archie McParland, nursing an unspecified knock that forced him to miss Saints’ high-stakes clash with Gloucester, Jack van Poortvliet is likely to start at nine against the Wallabies next Sunday. McParland was the third-choice scrum-half in England’s Nations Championship squad, but Steve Borthwick may be forced to look elsewhere if Mitchell’s prognosis is serious.

News.title: Spurs win three in row for first time in 616 days to pile pressure on Sage
News.content:
Hello and welcome to our live coverage of this Premier League encounter between Tottenham and Crystal Palace.

Last weekend, Spurs enjoyed a historic result, beating Chelsea 2-0 at Stamford Bridge for only the second time in the league for 36 years thanks to Mike Penders’ own goal and Mathys Tel’s stunning solo strike. This result, coupled with the 3-1 victory over Coventry City in their previous home outing, means that Tottenham have won back-to-back league games and are beginning to gather some momentum under Roberto De Zerbi.

In his pre-match press conference, when asked if he’s felt a change in atmosphere after the triumph at Stamford Bridge, De Zerbi replied: “We have not achieved our goal. We want our fans to be happy, not now, at the end of the season. Now we have to push, we have to stay focused, we have to increase the spirit, the appetite to win games in a row. To do that, we have to show if we are good enough. If we are good enough on the pitch, for sure we are ready. In the head, in the mentality, we have to show, because the step of this club is to win games in a row and to be angry day by day, game by game, win by win. One time or two times are not enough.”

Palace have endured a tricky and inconsistent start to the season under their summer appointment Pierre Sage, accumulating just seven points from their opening seven league matches while shipping 17 goals. The 1-0 League Cup victory over Fulham in midweek has momentarily eased the pressure on the Frenchman, but given their newfound success in recent campaigns, fan expectations have risen, with recent performances prompting some cause for concern.

Tottenham remain without the suspended Rodrigo Bentancur, while Xavi Simons, Wilson Odobert, Lucas Bergvall, Savio, Tosin Adarabioyo and Mykhaylo Mudryk are out injured. James Maddison was substituted early in the second half at Chelsea with an apparent groin strain, but De Zerbi insists he’s available for this one. Destiny Udogie could also be involved after recovering from a knee issue.

News.title: Brighton underline title credentials with impressive win over Man City
News.content:
This Brighton and Hove Albion title challenge – as it must now be classed – flies in the face of the saying that money always talks in football. Manchester City have been found guilty of breaching financial rules and also fielded the most expensive midfield in Premier League history here, yet the match-winners cost a fraction in comparison.

Looking at Brighton’s winning goal, it was created by a cross that flashed across the City goal from Diego Gómez, an £11m signing who was playing in Major League Soccer in the United States not so long ago. Maxim de Cuyper, a £17.5m arrival from Club Brugge, was credited with the assist after Yasin Ayari tapped in.

Ayari cost £3.5m from Swedish club AIK and scored in the 5-0 wins over Coventry and Palace, and now has this winner to add to his collection. The 23-year-old is another example of Brighton polishing these gems and putting them together in a team that can win against any opponent in the Premier League.

News.title: Man Utd the masters of self-destruction as pressure piles on Carrick
News.content:
The strange thing is this could and probably should have been a day when they at least stopped the rot for a few days. But more non-existent defending and brainlessness from Martinez, who was sent off for planting an elbow in Wesley Fofana’s face, put paid to that in a second half in which Carrick admitted United “unravelled”.

Chelsea were cut open on at least five occasions in a see-saw first half and Matheus Cunha also had a goal disallowed for a narrow offside. Xabi Alonso’s side had opportunities of their own – you will always get them against this United team – but they were second best and lucky not to be behind. Everyone talks about United being there for the taking, but the truth is Chelsea, coming off the back of a miserable defeat to Spurs and Carabao Cup exit to Liverpool, were here.

The problem is Carrick’s team could not hit a barn door at the moment. They have scored just three goals in their last six league games and that lack of cutting edge was evident in the way Bruno Fernandes, back in the team as captain, and Amad Diallo (dangerous but with no end product) wasted excellent chances. That wastefulness would put pressure on any back line, let alone one with all the fortitude of wet cardboard. Chelsea were spared and exploited it with the help of the second and most corrosive acts of United’s self-mutilation.

We will come to Martinez’s sending off in a moment, but there had already been a cowardly act of a different kind from the Argentine defender before then in the lead-up to Chelsea’s opening goal soon after the restart.

Take nothing away from Morgan Rogers – his 40yd dash from the edge of the centre circle in United’s half to the six-yard box and the finish that followed were top notch. But where was the challenge? How could not a single player in red have stood in his path? “Come on Morgan, run through us buddy” seemed to be the message.

Sports.title: ‘I don’t forget’ – Piero Hincapie aims dig at Virgil van Dijk after Arsenal’s win at Liverpool as fans hail ‘petty king’
Sports.content:
Next

PIERO HINCAPIE appeared to aim a cheeky dig at Virgil van Dijk after Arsenal beat Liverpool 1-0.

Kai Havertz‘s 13th minute strike was enough to earn the Gunners their first win at Anfield since 2014.

Hincapie, 24, came on as an 84th minute substitute for Christos Tzolis to help see out the victory.



After the match, the Ecuadorian posted pictures from the contest to his Instagram page, captioned: “I don’t forget..”



Initially, the carousel appeared to include a close up image of the gold Premier League badge on his shirt sleeve, denoting Arsenal‘s status as champions.

This appeared to be a jab at Virgil van Dijk, who posted a similar picture of himself after Liverpool’s 0-0 draw at the Emirates in January.

Arsenal fans loved Hincapie’s post, with one calling him a “petty king”.

While a second jibed: “What goes around, comes around.”

A third gushed: “I like how petty we are”.

Although another added: “One is a UCL winner, the other one can’t say”.

The picture of Hincapie’s sleeve mysteriously vanished from the post within a couple of hours.



Declan Rice commented on the post with a smiling emoji.

And Ezri Konsa added two flame emojis and a heart.

Hincapie’s post swiftly received more than 100,000 likes.

Arsenal’s win saw them return to the top of the Premier League table.

The Gunners are three points clear of Manchester City, after Enzo Maresca‘s side lost 1-0 to Brighton on Saturday.

Sports.title: ‘Embarrassing’ – Carragher blasts Mac Allister for ‘joke’ falling theatrics vs Arsenal and demands ‘this has to stop’
Sports.content:
Next

JAMIE CARRAGHER launched a scathing attack on Alexis Mac Allister after trying to get Noni Madueke sent off.

The Argentine, 27, could not stop Liverpool falling to a 1-0 defeat against Premier League table-toppers Arsenal.



And Mac Allister was involved in a major flashpoint after sparking a huge bust-up.

The midfielder screamed at Martin Odegaard and tapped the back of the grounded Arsenal skipper’s head.



Mac Allister, who missed out on a new deal in the summer, then threw himself to the floor when Madueke’s head brushed his.

But Carragher blasted the former Brighton man after attempting to reduce Arsenal to ten men.

The Anfield legend, 48, told Sky Sports: “I want Liverpool to win the game, but I’m delighted he [Madueke] didn’t get sent off.

“We have really got to be calling people out and saying, ‘this is embarrassing’.

“It’s ridiculous and it’s got to stop. I can’t stand it. If someone puts their head back and butts, then it’s a red card.

“But if it’s head-to-head and they touch, the other one goes down and the player gets sent off, as a game, call your own people out on it.

“It’s a joke from Mac Allister and it’s got to stop. People are trying to gain an advantage because they can and red cards are being given for it.

“Whether it’s [ProRef supremo] Howard Webb, the Premier League, the managers getting together, this has got to stop.”

Ex-Liverpool striker Daniel Sturridge, 37, also hit out at Mac Allister’s shock theatrics.

He said: “He doesn’t headbutt him with any force. It’s a coming together and they’re both into it.

“He’s trying to bait him and that is league wide – that’s not just Mac Allister. Every player in world football – that’s the game.



“He knew exactly what he was doing and ultimately it didn’t work out for him. You tried to bait a man into something and he didn’t bite.”

Ian Wright, who joined Carragher and Sturridge on Sky Sports punditry duties, called for changes to be made in an attempt to stop stars trying to get opponents sent off.

“The laws have to do something about this because that [Mac Allister going down] is trying to get someone sent off.”

Sports.title: ‘He doesn’t know how to shoot’ – Heartwarming moment Mbappe comforts young fan struck in face by teammate’s wayward shot
Sports.content:
Next

KYLIAN MBAPPE has shared a heartwarming moment with a child hit by a teammate’s wayward shot.

The Real Madrid star took a moment to comfort the child after being accidentally targeted by a shot from Aurelien Tchouameni, 26, against Racing Santander.



Huge concern was raised for the young Racing fan by supporters after he was hit in the face by the ball during the 51st minute of the match.

Mbappe, 27, had already scored an 11th-minute penalty before further goals from Jude Bellingham and Yan Diomande confirmed the 3-0 away win.



But the France captain was keen to make amends on his teammate’s behalf after the match.

He spent a moment in the tunnel with the youngster, explaining to the child on Real Madrid TV that Tchouameni needs to work on his accuracy.

Mbappe said: “It’s Tchouaméni’s fault.

“He doesn’t know how to shoot.”

The child appeared in good spirits as he shook hands with the Real Madrid striker.

Mbappe then shared a high-five with the child and ruffled his hair before walking away.

It has come just days after the Frenchman fell agonisingly short as Bayern Munich‘s Harry Kane claimed his first Ballon d’Or.

This left Spanish broadcasters stunned as Mbappe missed out on the title by just 41 points.

The Real Madrid star was then slammed for disrespecting Kane at the ceremony, as he appeared to ignore the England captain.

But Mbappe has let his on-pitch form do the talking for him as he helped Real Madrid cruise to a sixth straight win, rising to third in LaLiga.

Sports.title: Kai Havertz makes Premier League HISTORY as Arsenal star nets winning goal at Liverpool to end 14-year Anfield hoodoo
Sports.content:
Next

KAI HAVERTZ became the outright top-scoring German in Premier League history by bagging Arsenal’s winner at Liverpool.

The Gunners forward, 27, swept home Declan Rice‘s pass to hand his side a 1-0 lead on 13 minutes at Anfield.



Havertz’s goal was his 46th in 172 Prem appearances since moving to England in 2020.

It took him above compatriot Ilkay Gundogan‘s tally of 45, which previously was the record for a German player in the Premier League.



Gundogan, 36, achieved his haul in 221 appearances across two spells at Manchester City.

Havertz initially moved to Chelsea in 2020 as more of a midfield player.

The rangy star was eventually moved into a makeshift forward role and performed the role for the Blues as well as Arsenal.

Havertz scored 19 Prem goals in three seasons at Chelsea before signing for the Gunners in a £65million switch in June 2023.

He has since gone to add a further 27 to date for the Gunners.

Havertz’s best tally of Prem goals in a season thus far came during the 2023-24 campaign, when he managed 13 for Arsenal.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

In third place on the leaderboard of German Premier League scorers is Brighton star Pascal Gross.

The creative midfielder has scored 34 goals in 256 appearances in two stints with the Seagulls.

Gross, now 35, initially moved to the Amex in 2017 ahead of their maiden Prem campaign under Chris Hughton.



He signed for Borussia Dortmund in the summer of 2024, only to return to Brighton 18 months later.

Gross’ tally is one above Mesut Ozil’s of 33 – achieved in 184 appearances for Arsenal between 2013 and 2021.

The former Real Madrid star was also a prolific assister, laying on 57 Prem goals for his Gunners team-mates.



Uwe Rosler and Jurgen Klinsmann are next up with 29 apiece.

Klinsmann managed his haul in 56 games across two spells with Tottenham.

The legendary striker bagged 20 during the 1994-95 season after moving to White Hart Lane from Monaco.

After two seasons at Bayern Munich and a short stint with Sampdoria, Klinsmann returned to White Hart Lane on loan in the 1997-98 campaign, scoring nine times in 15 games to help save his beloved Spurs from the drop.



Rosler, meanwhile, scored his 29 goals during three seasons at Manchester City between 1993 and 1996 – including 15 in the 1994-95 campaign.

He would also go on to play 23 times in the Prem for Southampton, but did not score for the Saints.

Leroy Sane bagged 25 times in 90 Premier League outings for Man City.

The winger helped City to league titles in the 2017-18 and 2018-19 campaigns, scoring 10 times in each.



Sane moved to Bayern Munich in 2020 and now, aged 30, plays for Galatasaray in Turkey.

Brentford‘s Kevin Schade has 24 goals in 111 appearances for the Bees since joining from Freiburg in 2023 – and aged 24, seems likely to add many more.

Robert Huth is a surprise name at No9 on the list with 21 goals from 322 Prem outings.



Huth, now 42, won three Premier League titles during his career; two with Chelsea and memorably one with Leicester City.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

His best season tally came in 2010-11, when he managed six for Stoke under Tony Pulis.

Rounding off the list is Lukas Podolski, the left-footed forward scoring 19 times in 60 matches for Arsenal between 2012 and 2015. Podolski, now 41, retired from football earlier this year following a spell in Poland.

Sports.title: Man Utd fans beg former star, 34, to rejoin club and rescue Michael Carrick after signing THREE dud replacements
Sports.content:
Next

MANCHESTER UNITED fans have made a desperate plea for Casemiro to seal a sensational return.

The midfielder, 34, quit Old Trafford when his mega-money deal expired in the summer.



And Casemiro joined MLS side Inter Miami – where he has the likes of Lionel Messi among his team-mates – as a free agent.

But frustrated United supporters are begging for the five-time Champions League winner to make a shock comeback and rescue their season.



The Red Devils extended their winless streak to NINE games as they suffered a 2-0 defeat to Chelsea on Saturday.

United fans flooded the comments section when Casemiro uploaded a snap onto social media promoting Inter Miami’s clash with New England Revolution.

One said: “Please come back to United.”

Another added: “You’re dearly missed.”

A third cheekily asked: “Any chance of a two-month loan to get us to 12-18 points?”

A fourth chimed in: “Casemiro please come back to United. They need you.”

And a fifth claimed: “We really miss you Case. Since you left United, things haven’t been the same again.”

Casemiro played a key role in the Red Devils bagging Champions League qualification last season.

But the Brazilian walked away from Old Trafford, where he got his hands on the FA Cup and Carabao Cup.

United splashed the cash on THREE replacements – with Andrey Santos, Youri Tielemans and £70million Carlos Baleba joining.



The midfield overhaul has not gone to plan and goal difference is all that is separating the Red Devils from the relegation zone.

United chief Michael Carrick is also clinging to his job following the disastrous start to the season.

The former Swansea boss was drafted into the Welsh international backroom staff as an assistant and attacking set-piece coach.

Sheehan told SunSport: “Working with Wales, with Craig and the staff, has given me the bug to really get back into it.

“It’s about trusting your gut and finding true alignment with the owners and sporting directors before you take that next jump.”

He said: “When you step up as interim, you do what’s needed for the club. In the Championship, you have to find a way to win.

Passionate Dragons chief Bellamy has taken international football by storm with his non-negotiable standards and front-foot attacking style.



And Sheehan says the former Liverpool and Manchester City star demands brutal honesty inside his dressing room.

He added: “Craig doesn’t leave any stone unturned. He is the leader — but he is completely secure in himself.

“Craig wants people to give him honest opinions. He doesn’t want yes-men sitting around nodding and agreeing with everything.

Sheehan explained: “I spent time visiting clubs right across the continent to see how different cultures operate.



“I’ve started learning different languages’ just to add another string to my bow.

“Modern changing rooms are so diverse now, and having those languages helps you connect with players on a personal level.”
