Sports.title: Three points from Arsenal’s win at Liverpool, including Saliba’s Konsa issue, Rice’s remedy and tactical dilemma
Sports.content:
Next

ARSENAL secured a huge win against Liverpool on the road to leap to the top of the Premier League table.

Mikel Arteta‘s men took the lead through Kai Havertz in the early stages of the match before weathering a barrage of Reds pressure to protect their three points.



A number of Gunners stars stood out in the thrilling clash at Anfield, but that is not to say there were not signs to learn and improve upon as the season rumbles on.

SunSport’s Simon Collings singled out three things we learned from Arsenal‘s triumph on Merseyside…



KONSA-QUENCES

The defence was at the heart of Arsenal‘s performance as they stole all three points at Anfield for the first time in 14 years.

Ezri Konsa put in a stunning performance alongside Gabriel at the base of the back four as he continues to build on his impressive catalogue of showings since joining from Aston Villa in the summer.

William Saliba is potentially set to make his return to contention in the coming weeks, and could be available for selection as early as after the November international break.

But the Frenchman faces a fight if he wants to reclaim his spot in the starting line-up.

Konsa has built up his relationship with his defensive partner this season, and deciding whether to split them up may prove a real dilemma for Arteta in the near future.

THINK RICE

Declan Rice continued to impress in midfield as he put the ball on a plate for Havertz at the back post to give the Gunners an early lead.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

That made it five assists for the season so far for Rice, who is adding a creative spark to his repertoire of skills this campaign.

But the impactful showing comes on the back of him receiving a rest in the midweek.

The quality of his performance at Anfield is proof that Arteta will have to carefully manage his minutes going forward this season so he can make the difference in the biggest clashes.

RACE FOR PACE

But while the back line and the midfield shone, there was a glaring issue at the other end of the pitch.



Liverpool had the visitors pinned back for large spells in the second half, but Arsenal lacked the pace up front to provide a danger on the counter attack.

The absence was especially stark watching the likes of Bradley Barcola and Alexander Isak bombing down the channels for the hosts when they regained possession.

Arsenal were unable to exploit the space behind Liverpool’s back line when they cranked up the pressure in the defensive third, but a pace injection in the January window could make them a real danger on the counter.

Sports.title: Virgil van Dijk blasts VAR as Liverpool captain goes public after Arsenal penalty denial
Sports.content:
Virgil van Dijk blasts VAR as Liverpool captain goes public after Arsenal penalty denial

After Liverpool were beaten by Arsenal at Anfield, Virgil van Dijk let his feelings about the game's officiating be known

View 3 Images Virgil van Dijk did not hold back in his assessment of the referees (Image: X/Sky Sports Premier League)

Virgil van Dijk hit out at VAR in a prickly post-match interview after Liverpool's defeat to Arsenal. The Premier League champions overcame the Reds 1-0, courtesy of Kai Havertz's first half goal

‌



‌



Andoni Iraola's side were left furious when they saw two first half penalty shouts be waved away by both referee Andy Madley and VAR. The most controversial call came when Jurrien Timber grabbed Alexander Isak by his shirt while the £125m man was trying to get on the end of a dangerous cross from Bradley Barcola.

‌



Gary Neville believed it was a penalty and was left aghast when Isak did not even shout or protest the decision. After the match, Van Dijk blasted the officials operating VAR.

‌



When the incident was put to Van Dijk, he told Sky Sports: "It was a clear penalty on Isak. It’s a penalty but today it wasn’t meant to be.”

The reporter then asked if Isak should have protested the decision to alert the referee about the incident, Van Dijk hit back with some questions of his own, asking: "VAR doesn’t notice it?

"There are 50 cameras. Why does he have to complain when there’s so many cameras? Everyone has seen it. At the end of the day, it wasn’t given so congratulations to Arsenal.”

‌



View 3 Images Isak was pulled back by Timber as he looked to get on the end of a cross (Image: 2026 Getty Images)

Liverpool legend Jamie Carragher was equally furious about the decision, saying VAR did not do what it was brought in to do. He said: "One of the best goalscorers in the league is pulled back seven yards out and it stops him heading the ball - why does he need to make a meal of it? VAR do your job."

‌



Iraola also used his post-match media duties to event about some of the key decisions, saying the striker may have needed to dive to get the call. The Reds boss said: "There is a clear grab [of] the shirt.

"Alex [Isak] was just in front of him, he was going to head in front of the goal but couldn't because he had the shirt. I don't understand why they didn't call it, probably because he has not gone to the floor.

‌



View 3 Images Iraola spent much of the match protesting the decisions which went against his team (Image: 2026 Getty Images)

"I think the Gakpo one was not a penalty but the Alex one he was going to head the ball in front of the goalkeeper.

‌



"He grabbed the shirt. I don't understand why it wasn't called. You have to dive, if you don't dive they won't call it. That's the problem we have with the game. Because he doesn't dive and go to the floor.

"The fact that you are even asking me if he should go to the floor, if he goes to the floor, they call the penalty 100 percent."

Sports.title: Jamie Carragher fumes at Alexis Mac Allister and demands law change over 'embarrassing' act
Sports.content:
Jamie Carragher fumes at Alexis Mac Allister and demands law change over 'embarrassing' act

Alexis Mac Allister's brazen attempt to get Noni Madueke sent off in the closing stages of Arsenal's 1-0 win over Liverpool on Sunday infuriated Jamie Carragher

View 2 Images Alexis Mac Allister went down after going head to head with Noni Madueke (Image: AFP/Getty Images)

Jamie Carragher has slammed Alexis Mac Allister for his "embarrassing" dive to try and get Noni Madeuke sent off - and called for unified action against play-acting.

‌



‌



Mac Allister was at the centre of a flashpoint in the second half of Liverpool's 1-0 defeat by Arsenal on Sunday afternoon. The Liverpool midfielder sparked a melee by slapping Arsenal captain Martin Odegaard on the back of the head while he was on the ground.

‌



Jurrien Timber and Madueke then confronted Mac Allister, who threw himself to the ground dramatically after a minor contact with the latter's forehead. Madueke had already been booked, but the officials weren't fooled, with Mac Allister and Timber given yellow cards by referee Andy Madley.

‌



The VAR Stuart Attwell said: "There is some contact as Madueke and Mac Allister square up. In my opinion, it's not forceful, not violent, not brutal”.

Carragher was furious with Mac Allister's behaviour and called for it to be stamped out of the game. "I'm delighted he didn't get sent off there," he said after the full-time whistle on Sky Sports. "We have really got to be strong and start calling people out and say 'this is embarrassing'. It's got to stop, it's ridiculous. I can't stand it.

"This head to head stuff... if someone puts their head back and butts, of course, red card. But this stuff where they go head to head and if someone touches the other goes down and the player gets sent off... as a game, people in the Premier League, supporters, call your own out for it.

‌



"I'm a Liverpool fan and it's a joke from Mac Allister, it's got to stop. People are trying to gain an advantage because they know they can, because red cards are getting given for it. Whether it's from Howard Webb, the Premier League, the managers get together, stop getting red cards for this c***!"

View 2 Images Noni Madueke went head to head with Alexis Mac Allister before he dived

‌



Make sure you don't miss the best Liverpool coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

Carragher was backed up by Gary Neville on co-commentary. "I don't think Mac Allister needs to go down like that but there's a little nudge with the head. A little inch forward can cost you a lot," he said while watching the incident play out.

‌



"Mac Allister's reaction is a bit over the top, I can tell you that. Get up. Embarrassing. It's Mac Allister's fault because he slaps Odegaard when he's down which is unnecessary.

"It's the little movement forward of Madueke's head they're looking at. I hope they don't go for a red card for it."

‌



Arsenal legend Ian Wright also called for the laws of the game to be changed to clarify these types of situations. "The first thing with Mac Allister is the way he goes over. He's actually slapped Odegaard on the back of the head," he said.

"The laws have to do something about this because that [Mac Allister going down] is trying to get someone sent off. Common sense prevailed because he [Madueke] didn't push his head into him, he just confronted him and Mac Allister tried to take that advantage to go down."

Sports.title: Arsenal star delivers clear message to Mikel Arteta in statement Liverpool victory
Sports.content:
Arsenal made it four Premier League wins in a row as they defeated Liverpool 1-0 at Anfield for the first time in 14 years.

The Gunners dominated possession in the opening period of the game and their fast start paid off after just 16 minutes. Alisson Becker's wayward pass saw the away side pick up the ball in the final third.

The ball made its way to Noni Madueke, who laid it off for an overlapping Declan Rice, and the England star superbly played it across goal to allow Kai Havertz to finish with a close-range tap-in.

Andoni Iraola's side responded exactly how you'd expect a Liverpool team losing at home to do so. The likes of Trey Nyoni and Alexis Mac Allister began getting on the ball in dangerous areas and distributing it to Florian Wirtz and Bradley Barcola, who put the Arsenal defence under pressure.

‌



They failed to test David Raya, but the goalkeeper was beaten by Wirtz's free-kick that was stopped by the crossbar. Liverpool had cause to be annoyed during the first half after a penalty was not awarded when Alexander Isak had his shirt pulled by Jurrien Timber in the box when attempting to get on the end of a cross.

It's the Gunners who end the weekend with all smiles as they move three points ahead of Manchester City to already mark their 10th win of the campaign across all competitions.

‌



ARSENAL STAR DEMONSTRATES IMPORTANCE

Havertz was dropped for the first time this season last week in the Gunners' 2-0 victory over Everton. He did manage a 22-minute cameo against the Toffees, but earned his place back in Arteta's starting XI against Liverpool and what an impact he made.

The 27-year-old was in the perfect position to tap home past Alisson Becker after getting on the end of Rice's accurate pass across the box to give the champions the lead. In what is his third goal this season, Havertz isn't known for his goalscoring prowess, but time and time again, he's come up big for his team.

While his demotion to the bench against Everton may have been partly down to rest and giving Viktor Gyokeres an opportunity to impress, Arteta has been given another reminder of what Havertz provides when he starts.

‌



TRIAL BY CROSSES

Arsenal are usually the team that demonstrates their dominance through incessant crosses, but they've been getting a taste of their own medicine at Anfield. Iraola's side put a staggering 19 crosses in the first half alone as they continually put the Gunners' defence under the cosh.

View 3 Images Alexis Mac Allister couldn't believe he didn't score (Image: Getty Images)

Despite the intense pressure of the ball flying in from the flanks, with Milos Kerkez contributing most of them, the Reds were unable to convert any of the opportunities they created. The best chance came through the Hungarian's pinpoint cross to a free Alexis Mac Allister in the box, but the Argentine failed to get his header on target.

Sports.title: Jamie Carragher fumes over VAR as Liverpool penalty agreement reached - 'Do your job!'
Sports.content:
Jamie Carragher fumes over VAR as Liverpool penalty agreement reached - 'Do your job!'

Liverpool had strong shouts for a penalty waved away during their showdown with Arsenal

View 2 Images Jamie Carragher and the Sky Sports pundits gave their verdict on VAR's role in the Alexander Isak penalty decision (Image: Sky Sports)

Former Liverpool defender Jamie Carragher was left fuming that the video assistant referee missed a penalty shout against Arsenal. Jurrien Timber avoided being penalised for a penalty for an apparent pull on Reds striker Alexander Isak as he looked to head the hosts level.

‌



‌



Bradley Barcola delivered a tantalising cross which narrowly missed the Sweden international, however replays showed the Dutch defender had pulled his shirt. Liverpool fell behind inside 20 minutes after Kai Havertz tapped home with the visitors pouncing on sloppy play out from the back from the Reds backline.

‌



However, after falling behind, Andoni Iraola's side surged back putting the Premier League champions under pressure. Yet, the half-time analysis focused on how Andy Madley missed out on awarding Liverpool a penalty and hand them the chance to level proceedings.

‌



Carragher said: “One of the best goalscorers in the league is pulled back seven yards out and it stops him heading the ball - why does he need to make a meal of it? VAR do your job."

Gary Neville singles out 'embarrassing' Arsenal star minutes into Liverpool clash READ MORE :

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

The former stopper was responding to Daniel Sturridge who felt that Liverpool would have had a stronger shout for a penalty if the Swede made more of a big deal about the tug. He said: “If he [Isak] makes more of it, it's a penalty. I don't think he makes enough of it... It's clear and blatant."

‌



Following the interval, Gary Neville felt the reaction was Isak was "odd". He said: "The guys at half-time said Isak should not have to make more of it [his penalty shout in the first half].

"It's actually unnatural not to make more of it. When you get pulled and you're just about to score, you ordinarily complain like crazy. It's a very odd reaction from Isak."

‌



Ian Wright was among the contingent to represent Arsenal as part of Sky Sports' coverage. But the former Gunners talisman couldn't ignore that the North London club got away with a key moment.

He said: “He shouldn't have to make more of it. We can see it. As an Arsenal man, I'm glad we got away with it.

‌



View 2 Images Andoni Iraola was left angered with the decision not to award Liverpool a penalty against Arsenal. (Image: Photo by Robbie Jay Barratt - AMA/Getty Images)

“Unless I'm pulled back, I'm going to head it as much as I can. When he pulled him, it was just about enough as he would need to go down."

‌



After Brighton & Hove Albion avenged their Carabao Cup exit at the hands of Manchester City in the midweek, the Seagulls dented Enzo Maresca's sides Premier League title hopes with a 1-0 win.

A win for Arsenal would open up the gap in their title defence to three points after City suffered back-to-back defeats in the top-flight, following their 2-1 disappointment at the hands of Aston Villa last week.

Sports.title: Boy, 14, turns himself in to the police after vile Bradley Lowery taunt in Sunderland game
Sports.content:
Boy, 14, turns himself in to the police after vile Bradley Lowery taunt in Sunderland game

West Midlands Police have released a statement to confirm that a 14-year-old boy has turned himself in following a vile incident during Coventry's win over Sunderland

View 3 Images The fan appeared to hold up a photo of Bradley Lowery (Image: x.com/Roker Report)

A 14-year-old boy has turned himself in to the police after footage appeared to show a young Coventry supporter taunting Sunderland fans with a picture of Bradley Lowery.

‌



‌



Footage taken during Coventry's 3-1 Premier League win over Sunderland posted on social media went viral on Saturday. It appeared to show a young supporter showing the away fans a photograph of Lowery, a Sunderland fan who tragically died aged six in 2017 with cancer.

‌



The video sparked outrage, with Bradley's mum Gemma releasing a statement, and West Midlands Police have now given a significant update.

‌



A spokesperson said: “We are aware of a video circulating on social media showing an incident at Coventry City’s Premier League match with Sunderland yesterday afternoon. A thorough investigation has been launched, and a 14-year-old boy has since handed himself in and will be spoken with in due course.

“We understand the upset and outrage this video has caused in the community and to the victim’s family and our officers are keeping them up to date with the progress of our investigation and working closely alongside both football clubs.”

‌



Coventry City said in a statement: "Coventry City FC is aware of footage circulating on social media in connection with an incident during our Premier League fixture against Sunderland. The club does not tolerate offensive behaviour and will liaise with the relevant authorities to determine the appropriate course of action."

Bradley, who had neuroblastoma, touched the hearts of football fans with his bravery and his mum Gemma released an emotional statement on Sunday morning following the disgusting incident.

‌



View 3 Images Bradley Lowery was a passionate Sunderland fan (Image: PA)

She wrote: "My beautiful boy deserves to be remembered with love, not hate. Yesterday, a Coventry fan used a photograph of Bradley to taunt Sunderland supporters. As Bradley’s mam, this is heartbreaking, especially as it’s one of my favourite photographs of him. Just look at that smile.

‌



"I remember that day like it was yesterday. He was so happy, having so much fun. Those moments were precious because they were few and far between. So much of Bradley’s short life was spent battling cancer and enduring treatments no child should ever face. To see such a beautiful memory used in such a cruel way really does make my heart hurt."

She added: "We are a football-loving family who follow Sunderland home and away. I’m all for football banter, but surely mocking a child who died from cancer is not banter? I hope the club takes appropriate action and the young lad’s family help him understand how hurtful his actions were.

‌



View 3 Images Bradley Lowery died in 2017 (Image: PA)

“I don’t want hatred directed towards him, so please please don't, just for him to learn from this. Behind that photograph is a little boy who was loved beyond measure and a family who miss him every day. Thank you to everyone who has defended Bradley and shown us so much love. It means more than you know.

‌



"What some people don’t realise is that Bradley’s story didn’t end when his life did. Because of Bradley, children’s lives are being saved, hundreds of families have received vital support, and children facing unimaginable battles are being given hope.

"Through Super Brad’s Pad, families can escape hospital life, spend precious time together and make memories that last forever. That is Bradley’s legacy. The difference my little boy continues to make in this world. No amount of cruelty will ever take that away.

Article continues below

"So rather than let this photograph be remembered for hatred, I want it remembered for what it truly represents. My beautiful little boy, enjoying one of the happiest days of his life, with the biggest smile on his face. #CancerHasNoColours. That is how I want the world to remember him.”

Sports.title: Ole Gunnar Solskjaer gives Michael Carrick verdict and admits to unfinished business at Man Utd
Sports.content:
Ole Gunnar Solskjaer gives Michael Carrick verdict and admits to unfinished business at Man Utd

Michael Carrick is under huge pressure as Manchester United manager following a nine-match winless run and Ole Gunnar Solskjaer has given his opinion on his former assistant

View 3 Images Carrick is set to be appointed instead of Solskjaer (Image: Getty Images)

Ole Gunnar Solskjaer has thrown his support behind Michael Carrick, despite admitting he would be open to re-joining Manchester United, where he has "something unresolved".

‌



‌



United's 2-0 defeat by Chelsea on Saturday means that Carrick has overseen a nine-match winless streak - the club's worst run since 1988. The team sits 17th in the Premier League, just outside the relegation zone on goal difference.

‌



Carrick kept his job following crisis talks with United chiefs at the start of the week and the 45-year-old is expected to be given the next two matches. But with fixtures against Roma and Aston Villa on the horizon before the international break, his future remains precarious.

‌



Carrick first arrived as interim boss in January following the sacking of Ruben Amorim. That process saw chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox reach out to Solskjaer, who was in charge of the club from 2018 to 2021, as another option.

‌



The Norwegian had Carrick as his assistant during that time and is sure United made the right decision to overlook him. "Michael has what it takes to take that club forward," Solskjaer told told Norwegian outlet TV2. "I think he's the right man. He understands the club, understands the fans and knows what's needed."

Solskjaer's backing of Carrick is hardly surprising given his close friendship with the former midfielder. Carrick revealed recently that he is in regular contact with Solskjaer and Sir Alex Ferguson as he looks to navigate his way through the current malaise.

‌



Despite being supportive of Carrick, Solskjaer admits that he misses managing United and was open to re-joining as interim boss in January.

Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



View 3 Images Ole Gunnar Solskjaer is still open to a Manchester United return (Image: Getty Images)

"Going back to what has been is not always as good," he said. "Yes, I was lined up, but I didn't think it would last longer than the summer. It was probably time for someone else to try. I also feel like I have something unresolved. Of course it would have been nice to have the opportunity again."

‌



Solskjaer is magnanimous after losing out to Carrick, who subsequently led United to third place in the Premier League to secure a return to the Champions League and the job on a permanent basis. He added: "When I spoke to United, I also boasted about Michael. 'If you choose him, you will get a good man,' I said. I think he did the same to me.

"None of us were desperate to get the job. We'd probably be up for the job if they asked. At the time, there was talk of being an interim coach for the rest of the season."

‌



View 3 Images Michael Carrick remains in contact with Ole Gunnar Solskjaer (Image: Clive Brunskill/Getty Images)

While he is firm about his love of the club he represented as a player and manager, Solskjaer did concede that "some of the same problems are still there" from his time in charge.

‌



But, perhaps with one eye on making a return to the hotseat in the future, he is unwilling to spell them out. "No, you see… Those who watch the team see it," he said when asked what the problems are. "Those who work behind the scenes know what the challenges are there."

The possibility of a return is something he is keen to keep on the cards. "If Michael does well for 10 years and decides to quit, and they ask me if I can take them for two months, of course I wouldn't say no," he said. "I've been at that club for 18-19 years, so it's part of the family. But it's not something I'm thinking about."

Sports.title: Barcelona star announces his decision on joining Man Utd in post-match interview
Sports.content:
Barcelona star announces his decision on joining Man Utd in post-match interview

The Barcelona star revealed his stance over a possible move to Manchester United

View 2 Images Fermin Lopez has had a stellar start to the season for Barcelona (Image: Getty Images)

Fermin Lopez announced his desire to retire at Barcelona after rubbishing rumours of a potential transfer to Manchester United. The midfielder delivered the verdict on his future following his starring role in the La Liga champions' 6-1 win over Alaves on Saturday.

‌



‌



The 23-year-old scored and provided two assists in the victory that saw Barca maintain their position at the top of the table. Lopez has enjoyed a productive start to the season with six goals and six assists in 13 games across all competitions and has started eight of their 11 league games thus far.

‌



A move away from his boyhood club is the furthest thing on his mind as he addressed the rumours of a move to Old Trafford. He said after full-time: "Manchester United links? I don’t pay attention to that kind of news.

‌



Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

"I want to stay here at Barcelona as long as possible. I hope to end my football career at this club and retire here."

‌



United are reportedly seeking to add more goals and flair to their midfield, with Lopez emerging as a possible target for next summer. The Spaniard attracted interest from Chelsea and Paris Saint-Germain last year, with the Blues said to have had a £40million bid rejected for the star.

Lopez's dismissal of a move would certainly come as a disappointment to United, given captain Bruno Fernandes is their biggest goal threat and is entering the final year of his contract.

‌



View 2 Images Fermin Lopez has no intention of joining Manchester United (Image: Xavi Urgeles/ZUMA Press Wire/Shutterstock)

The Portuguese star recorded 31 goal involvements last season, just one more than Lopez did in Barca's successful defence of the league title. Hansi Flick's side look on course for a third consecutive championship triumph with 30 points racked up so far.

Lopez's impressive performances have come after a brutal summer where he was ruled out of Spain's World Cup squad due to injury and could only watch as his country went on to win the trophy for a second time.

Sports.title: Erling Haaland's true feelings on Man City future confirmed by dad after guilty verdict
Sports.content:
Erling Haaland's true feelings on Man City future confirmed by dad after guilty verdict

Manchester City are facing serious consequences for systematically breaking the Premier League's financial rules over a nine-year period, leaving players like Erling Haaland in an uncertain position

View 2 Images Alfie Haaland discussed his son's reaction to the guilty verdict (Image: Viaplay)

Erling Haaland is purely focused on playing for Manchester City and is not concerned by the possible punishment the club faces, according to his father Alfie.

‌



‌



City were found guilty of breaching the Premier League's financial rules over a nine-year period and are waiting the outcome of an appeal. An independent commission found the club guilty of 114 of the 115 charges, saying they had used "sham" contracts to disguise funding of more than £830million.

‌



The club have always maintained their innocence and are confident of clearing their name. But the bombshell verdict has cast a shadow of doubt over Enzo Maresca's side, who could be relegated as punishment for the club's past financial cheating.

‌



Haaland has reportedly been calming his teammates down about the potential consequences and his father has given an insight into the striker's mindset. "Erling thinks about playing as much football as he can and concentrates on that. I think it’s more those of us outside the pitch who think a bit more about it," Alfie told ViaPlay.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



"Well, it has been circulating for quite a while, hasn’t it? So finally something came that was concrete, which it is possible to fight against for City as a club.

"Obviously, these are serious allegations, but now there is an appeal case pending to be heard, so I think we have to stay calm, keep our cool, and wait to see how it turns out."

‌



Haaland Snr was then asked whether he felt it would be unfair to punish the current players over financial irregularities which happened between 2009 and 2018. He replied: "Yes, in a way, one might feel that having to potentially take punishment for something done many years ago… yes, I would say so."

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



View 2 Images Erling Haaland could be relegated with Manchester City due to the guilty verdict (Image: Lewis Storey/Getty Images)

Asked if he knew anything more about the appeal, Alfie said: "Nothing more than what’s in the media. And there is an awful lot written there, and very one-sided, I would say, right? Because it's hard for Manchester City to come out right now – with an ongoing appeal – and defend themselves.

‌



"So we hope they get a fair hearing, and then we’ll see if they manage to prove that they are innocent, eventually. Now we just have to wait and see. I think they’ve done more than well to stand tall through this, because of course they have faced plenty of accusations. So I feel the player group has handled it very well.

"We also have to remember that these are things that allegedly happened quite a few years ago. The players today had nothing to do with it. So they’ve played well. They lost their last match, so it’s time to get back to winning ways."

Sports.title: Novak cruises to Mexico Open title for maiden individual PGA Tour triumph
Sports.content:
Andrew Novak bounced back from seeing his six-shot lead halved with three straight birdies to card a two-under 69 and win the Mexico Open by five shots, claiming his first individual PGA Tour title.

Novak staked himself to a big lead with rounds of 61-62 the previous two days, and it was going to take something special to track him down. But with a soft bogey on the 10th hole, his lead was down to three over Steven Fisk and Mexico-born Norwegian Kristoffer Ventura.

And then it was effectively over. Novak hit a greenside bunker shot to four feet on the par-5 12th at Vidanta Vallarta, drove the 13th green to 15 feet for a two-putt birdie, and he ended his decisive run with a 45-foot birdie putt on the 14th.

"That kind of really settled everything," Novak said. "Just happy with how I played today. I thought I grinded it out pretty well."

Fisk and Ventura each closed with a 63, and it was particularly meaningful for Ventura. He was at No. 108 in the FedEx Cup Fall, knowing only the top 100 keep full cards for 2027. The runner-up finish, his best as an individual, moved him to No. 76 and locked up his card.

Mackenzie Hughes of Canada shot 66 and wound up in a tie for fourth when Doug Ghim, playing in the final group, made double bogey on the 18th hole. Hughes moved up to No. 101, a manageable spot with three tournaments remaining.

"Gives me a bit of momentum for the last three," Hughes said. "Obviously, I still know I need more points and I need to keep climbing, but today was a big step in the right direction."

Hughes tied for fourth with Ben Griffin, who was Novak's partner when they won the Zurich Classic of New Orleans last year. Griffin (67) was waiting on the 18th green when Novak finished.

"I loved Zurich and everything about that tournament. That's so fun," Novak said. "But it is nice to have one by myself, too. This is one I've been working for for a while. Obviously not a great season for how I wanted it to go, but this is a nice way to kind of finish."

The outcome was never really in doubt, though Novak must have wondered if anything was going to go his way. On the third hole, the easiest of the par 5s, Novak's second shot plugged into the lip and he could only nudge back into the bunker, leading to par. He missed two other birdie chances from just inside 10 feet on the front nine.

"I played really well on the front and didn't get much out of it," he said.

Novak waited his turn, and three straight birdies was more than enough to send him on his way. He moved from No 89 to No 53 in the FedEx Cup, making him practically a lock to at least be in a pair of $20m (£14m) signature events next year at Pebble Beach and Riviera.

The victory also assures Novak will start the 2028 on the upper Championship Series.

Kihei Akina, the 20-year-old sophomore at Brigham Young University (BYU), closed with a 59 and finished 15th. It was his third top-20 finish on the PGA Tour this year.

Sports.title: Defensive 'masterclass' and elite Rice - how Arsenal ended Anfield torment
Sports.content:
Not since 2012 - when current boss Mikel Arteta was commanding Arsenal's midfield on the pitch - had the Gunners won on Liverpool’s patch. That curse has finally been broken.

Winning at Anfield is a rarity, especially for Arsenal. But Arteta's side were ruthless at both ends of the pitch, a tactical triumph for the boss and one that underlines his side's champion mentality.

"I love when there is something that we haven't done for many years," beamed the Spaniard, who praised his players for a defensive performance he called "remarkable". If Arteta wanted to make a statement, he succeeded.

Despite being pinned back in a first half dominated by Liverpool pressure, the visitors restricted their hosts to zero accurate shots - the first time on record the Reds failed to land at least one attempt on target at home.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player FREE TO WATCH: Highlights from the Premier League match between Liverpool and Arsenal.

"In the end, that defensive line, the way we stick together, that togetherness we have, is undefeated," midfielder Declan Rice reflected. "It's nothing I've ever seen before." Nine games in, Arsenal's title defence is going perfectly to plan.

Jamie Carragher was equally impressed by Arsenal's resilience: "To come to Anfield and be put under that much pressure and not have a shot on target from the opposition, or Liverpool not get a big chance given the money they have spent on their attack, is outstanding.

"When you think about Arsenal winning titles, especially in '89 and '91 with Tony Adams and that famous back four, I think we're getting close to putting this back four in that conversation."

Gary Neville called it a "defensive masterclass", likening Arsenal's nous to that of a side styled on Jose Mourinho's unique compactness.

The Gunners also won 18 fouls, Jurrien Timber, Martin Odegaard and Noni Madueke all responsible for drawing three apiece - a tactic used to stifle Liverpool's momentum. Ezri Konsa won all eight of the duels he contested.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Declan Rice sends a low cross across the box to the far post, where Kai Havertz delivers the finish to put Arsenal ahead against Liverpool.

Such application and exertion is what pleased Arteta most.

Under him, Arsenal have gone on to win 81 per cent of league games in which they have opened the scoring - the masters of preserving a lead.

He added: "Not only for the victory, but for the way we've done it, the spirit that we showed, the way we carried this shirt, this badge. It's a commitment of every single player in every action to deliver those kinds of stats.

"And that's the magical part about this game, that it can take you to really bad places, but four days later you have an incredible opportunity to do something historic, and we've done it."

'World-class Rice the best in Premier League'

Image: Declan Rice won player of the match for a standout performance at Anfield

While Carragher was impressed with the Gunners' collective effort on Super Sunday, he singled out Rice for particular commendation, calling him a "world class" talent.

The midfielder delivered one of his most complete performances of the campaign so far, providing the assist for Kai Havertz's winner and anchoring the middle third in a way that prime Arteta would be proud of.

He was the defensive shield Arsenal needed when Liverpool were generating a headwind and made crucial interceptions in the pressure moments.

His 62 touches were the most of any Arsenal player. "He's one of the best midfield players Arsenal have ever had," Carragher added.

"They've obviously had some great ones. He's right up there with the best of them. He's the best midfield player in the Premier League by a long way. It's not even a debate."

Sports.title: How Antonelli has rewritten Formula 1's record books
Sports.content:
Formula 1 has its 36th world champion after Kimi Antonelli clinched his maiden title by finishing third at the Mexico City Grand Prix.

The Italian youngster has reached the summit of motorsport in just his second season at the top level after a stellar campaign in which he has won nine races for Mercedes.

And while a world championship triumph for any driver is notable, Antonelli's first title carries particularly strong historical significance.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the 2026 Mexico City Grand Prix as Antonelli became the first Italian world champion since 1953

Beating Vettel's 16-year youngest benchmark

Formula 1 has a new youngest world champion in the sport's 76-year history.

After holding the record for 16 years, Sebastian Vettel spell as F1's youngest-ever champion has been beaten - by a full three years.

F1's youngest world champions Driver (season) Age 1) Kimi Antonelli (2026) 20 years and 68 days 2) Sebastian Vettel (2010) 23 years and 134 days 3) Lewis Hamilton (2008) 23 years and 300 days 4) Fernando Alonso (2005) 24 years and 58 days 5) Max Verstappen (2021) 24 years and 73 days

Vettel was aged 23 years and 134 days when he won the first of his four world titles with Red Bull in 2010.

Antonelli clinched his maiden crown aged 20 years and 68 days, a record that may well stand for decades - if not, all time.

In modern times, Antonelli follows Jacques Villeneuve (1997) and Lewis Hamilton (2008) in winning his first F1 title in just his second year competing in the top category of single-seater racing. Juan-Manuel Fangio also won his first of five crowns in the second season of the F1 world championship in 1951, although the Argentine had already been competing in Grand Prix racing before 1950.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sebastian Vettel congratulated Kimi Antonelli on breaking his record as the youngest ever Formula 1 world champion.

Ending Italy's seven-decade wait for another champion

Antonelli has also made history as an Italian driver in F1.

Considering an Italian won three of the first four Drivers' Championships following F1's inception in 1950, and Ferrari is the sport's most successful team, there had been a dearth of individual success in recent decades before Antonelli came along.

Antonelli is Italy's first world champion since 1953, when Alberto Ascari clinched his second and final title.

Italy's F1 world champions Driver Year Giuseppe Farina 1950 Alberto Ascari 1952, 1953 Kimi Antonelli 2026

Antonelli's nine wins this year have already put him second to Ascari (13) in the list of Italian race winners.

One of those wins came on home soil, at Monza in September, which made Antonelli the first Italian winner of the Italian Grand Prix since Ludovico Scarfiotti in 1966.

The other records Antonelli has beaten

While Max Verstappen's win as an 18-year-old at the 2016 Spanish Grand Prix remains the youngest for a driver in F1, Antonelli is the only driver to win multiple races as a teenager.

He won six races before his 20th birthday in August.

He did become the sport's youngest polesitter (China) and the youngest to lead the world championship (Japan) this year, along with the youngest to claim a pole-win-fastest lap hat-trick (China). He is also the youngest to achieve a Grand Slam - which requires a driver to add the lead of every race lap to a hat-trick - in Monaco.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Former World champions Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton lift F1'S newest champion, Kimi Antonelli, onto their shoulders in Mexico.

In addition, he became the first driver to win his first five races in succession thanks to an unbeaten run from China to Monaco.

He was already the youngest driver to lead a race and claim a fastest race lap, feats he achieved as an 18-year-old in 2025.

Formula 1 next heads to Brazil for the final leg of the triple header with the Sao Paulo Grand Prix from November 6-8, live on Sky Sports F1. Stream Sky Sports with NOW, no contract.

Sports.title: Antonelli crowned world champion as Verstappen wins wild Mexico City GP
Sports.content:
Kimi Antonelli became the youngest Formula 1 world champion in history as Max Verstappen held off Lewis Hamilton to win a thrilling Mexico City Grand Prix.

Antonelli finished third to secure the F1 Drivers' Championship with four rounds to spare, becoming the first Italian world champion since Alberto Ascari in 1953.

The 20-year-old avoided all the chaos in one of the most action-packed races of the season and was hugely emotional after the chequered flag.

"We did it, we did it. I wouldn't be here without Mercedes, without my family, so I'm very grateful for this moment and it's one that will live forever," said Antonelli.

"I'm speechless. I'm trying to process what has just happened."

Youngest F1 world champions Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes - 20 years and 68 days (2026)

Sebastian Vettel, Red Bull - 23 years and 134 days (2010)

Lewis Hamilton, McLaren - 23 years and 300 days (2008)

Fernando Alonso,, Renault - 24 years and 58 days (2005)

Max Verstappen, Red Bull - 24 years and 73 days (2021)

Meanwhile, Verstappen took advantage of a big fight between the Ferraris of Hamilton and Charles Leclerc on the opening lap to claim his third win in four races.

Pole-sitter Hamilton went side by side with Leclerc through the tight Turns 1 and 2 before Leclerc attacked again into Turn 4 around the outside.

Both drivers went off the track but Leclerc went across the grass to take the lead, allowing Verstappen to capitalise by overtaking Hamilton.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Relive a dramatic opening lap as Ferrari's Charles Leclerc was given a five-second penalty after overtaking Lewis Hamilton for the lead of the Mexico City Grand Prix

Leclerc was handed a five-second time penalty but a furious Hamilton said "the stewards are basically handling Charles this win" on the radio.

Verstappen crucially stayed within five seconds of Leclerc before the only round of pit stops to take the lead as they pitted together, but appeared to have an inferior car compared to the Ferraris, and was on aging soft tyres.

However, the race was stopped when Cadillac's Valtteri Bottas suffered a huge crash into the barriers as his suspension failed, leaving a standing-start restart with everyone on fresh tyres with 26 laps remaining.

Leclerc got a poor launch from second so Hamilton attacked Verstappen into Turn 1, with the pair making contact as the Red Bull driver came out on top in the exchange.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Valtteri Bottas suffered a suspension failure in his Cadillac as he crashed heavily into the barriers during Sunday's race in Mexico City

Even with a Safety Car for Racing Bulls' Arvid Lindblad crashing after tangling with McLaren's Oscar Piastri, Verstappen did just enough to keep Hamilton at bay with Antonelli, fittingly, just behind the two F1 legends in third.

Leclerc battled his way to fourth with flat-spotted front tyres from a lock up on the restart, while McLaren's Lando Norris finished fifth and Mercedes' George Russell sixth.

Russell had earlier served a 10-second time penalty for colliding with Red Bull's Isack Hadjar on the opening lap, which dropped him out of the podium fight.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Former World champions Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton lift F1's newest champion, Kimi Antonelli, onto their shoulders in Mexico

Piastri had crossed the line in seventh but was given a 10-second time penalty for his collision with Lindblad, so dropped to 15th.

There was more post-race drama as Alpine duo Franco Colapinto and Pierre Gasly both received penalties for failing to slow down under yellow flags and dropped out of the points-paying positions.

Colapinto, who originally finished eighth did not reduce his speed enough under single yellow flags when Lindblad crashed, so was given a 10-second time penalty, while Gasly failed to slow sufficiently under double-waved yellow flags, and was handed a 30-second time penalty.

That means F1 debutant and Haas driver Ryo Hirakawa, who surprisingly replaced Esteban Ocon from Saturday, finished 10th and has scored a point.

Racing Bulls' Liam Lawson moved up to seventh with Audi's Gabriel Bortoleto in eighth and Hadjar in ninth.

Mexico City GP Result: Top 10 1) Max Verstappen, Red Bull



2) Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari



3) Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes



4) Charles Leclerc, Ferrari



5) Lando Norris, McLaren



6) George Russell, Mercedes



7) Liam Lawson, Racing Bulls



8) Gabriel Bortoleto, Audi



9) Isack Hadjar, Red Bull



10) Ryo Hirakawa, Haas

Wolff: THIS is Kimi Antonelli

After a difficult rookie campaign, Antonelli has become just the fourth driver to become world champion in their second Formula 1 season, after Juan Manuel Fangio (1951), Jacques Villeneuve (1997) and Lewis Hamilton (2008).

He has exceeded expectations by winning nine races so far in 2026 and finished just two races outside of the podium places when he has seen the chequered flag.

"[People asked] why do you put this kid in the car? Oh, it's Kimi Antonelli. THIS is Kimi Antonelli!" Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff told Sky Sports F1.

"Incredible. Also today, complete serene. That's what makes him so different."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Kimi Antonelli became the youngest ever Formula 1 world champion after finishing third at the Mexico City Grand Prix

Mexico City race-winner Max Verstappen was unable to challenge Antonelli for the championship this year but says he's "very proud" of the Mercedes driver.

"To do that also at such an age is really, really impressive. It's amazing to see the whole team celebrating with him, his family is here as well," he said. "I'm sure this is a very emotional day for him."

Rosberg: There are going to be many more world titles for Antonelli Sky Sports F1's Nico Rosberg:



"We are all race car drivers, we know at what level he performed all season. It's something we have perhaps never seen in the sport. We have never seen it at the age of 20.



"It feels like there are going to be many more world championships there. I don't know how far he's going to get!"

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lewis Hamilton, Max Verstappen and Kimi Antonelli reflected on Antonelli's maiden world title win in the cooldown room

Antonelli was lifted up by Verstappen and Hamilton on the podium in front of a sold-out crowd at the Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez and says his first world title is "just the beginning".

"It's a day I will remember forever. Thank you so much to my team, my family, my friends and all you guys that support me and the sport. I'm just so grateful and thank you so much," said Antonelli.

"It's starting to get real and I'm going to enjoy every bit."

F1's Italian world champions Giuseppe Farina - 1950

Alberto Ascari - 1952, 1953

Kimi Antonelli - 2026

How Verstappen capitalised on Ferrari drama

The race itself was dramatic from start to finish as Verstappen pounced on an intra-team fight between between Hamilton and Leclerc, which will leave Ferrari with plenty to discuss ahead of next weekend's Sao Paulo Grand Prix.

Ferrari appeared to have the fastest car in Mexico but failed to win the race, largely due to the opening lap squabble between their drivers.

The FIA had warned drivers about corner cutting at Turns 1 and 4, so Hamilton was furious when Leclerc cut Turn 4 to take the lead and only received a five-second time penalty.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lewis Hamilton was left furious after Ferrari team-mate Charles Leclerc overtook him on the opening lap while leaving the track but was only given a five-second penalty for the infringement

"In the drivers' briefing, we discussed as soon as you go off in Turn 1 [and Turn 4], you have to give the position back," said Hamilton.

"Last year I got a 10-second penalty for that same move that he did. But ultimately, it was that that lost us the win today. I think we have to have some serious talks behind the scenes, for sure."

Karun: Ferrari are not going to win with fastest car Sky Sports F1's Karun Chandhok on commentary at the time of the incident:



"It feels like the second weekend in a row when Ferrari had the fastest car and are not going to win the race.



"By not playing the team game properly and not creating a strict structure around the two drivers, they're again not going to win a Grand Prix."

The stewards explained the usual penalty is 10 seconds but there were mitigating circumstances as Hamilton also went off track.

Given overtaking was extremely difficult, Verstappen found himself in second after the first lap thanks to his storming start and Red Bull smartly pitted him on the same lap as Leclerc on Lap 28.

But, Verstappen was now on softs compared to the other front-runners on mediums so needed a tyre masterclass to win the race.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Max Verstappen was full of praise for Kimi Antonelli after he became Formula 1's youngest ever world champion

He never came under threat from Leclerc and was arguably helped by the red flag for Bottas' big crash, although Red Bull have struggled with their starts this year.

Nevertheless, Verstappen got a good enough launch to hold the inside into Turn 1 and aggressively fended off Hamilton, who got a great restart from third on the grid.

That proved to be the final crucial moment as Hamilton was unable to get close to Verstappen to make a serious overtake attempt, even on the Safety Car restart following Lindblad's accident.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Arvid Lindblad suffered his first DNF in Formula 1 after being taken out by McLaren's Oscar Piastri

"The first start already made the race for me. I just had a very good first lap, let's say like that. After that we had a bit of a different strategy," said Verstappen.

"I do think we lacked a little bit of pace, but we just hung in there and made the right calls at the right time.

"Of course, the penalty for Charles then put us in the lead, then you could see they were always staying with me. It was tough. I was sweating at the end to try and keep Lewis behind."

Sports.title: Sale secures Grand Final title and Brown crowned Road to Mallorca No 1
Sports.content:
Julien Sale produced a dominant final round to secure victory at the HotelPlanner Tour’s Grand Final, while Hamish Brown topped the Road to Mallorca rankings.

Frenchman Sale, who was guaranteed promotion to the DP World Tour before the season finale in Mallorca, posted his second 65 of the week to reach 22 under par, four strokes clear of the Brown, who narrowly held onto solo second to capture the season-long title.

Sale ends the year second in the rankings and will now step up to golf's DP World Tour for the first time in his career.

He becomes the fifth player from France to win the Grand Final after Clément Sordet (2017), Benjamin Hebert (2014), Mike Lorenzo-Vera (2007) and Nicolas Joakimides (1997).

Image: Hamish Brown (left) and Julien Sale (right) celebrate successes at the HotelPlanner Tour Grand Final

The 29-year-old started the day with a one-stroke advantage and fired four front-nine birdies to take control at Club de Golf Alcanada.

A gain on the par-five 12th further extended his advantage before he dropped his only shot of the day on the next.

He responded well, however, with three birdies in his final six holes helping him to his second HotelPlanner Tour triumph of 2026, after his win on home soil at the Le Vaudreuil Golf Challenge earlier this year.

He said: "Coming this week, I didn't have much stress because I knew I was inside the top 15 and the goal was to win the tournament and obviously try to finish number one on the ranking.

"I was going to have fun already tonight but now I'm going to enjoy it even more with my family here."

"It means a lot," said Brown. It's been a proper grind again. Ultimately, I couldn't win today thanks to a good Frenchman who played extremely well.

Sports.title: ‘We have to tell them to go down’: Iraola responds to Isak penalty denial for Liverpool
Sports.content:
Andoni Iraola said he will instruct Liverpool players to go down in the box in future after Alexander Isak was denied a penalty during Arsenal’s first win at Anfield for 14 years.

Liverpool were beaten by Kai Havertz’s early strike after a poor clearance from the goalkeeper ­Alisson but had two penalty claims dismissed by the referee, Andy Madley. The first, a shirt-pull by the Arsenal defender Jurriën Timber on Isak, prevented the ­Sweden international reaching Bradley Barcola’s cross. The second, a hold by Christos ­Tzolis on Cody Gakpo, was reviewed by the video assistant referee, Stuart Attwell, but rejected.

Isak stood his ground when held by Timber and Iraola claimed that counted against his team. Asked whether Isak should have collapsed in the area, the Liverpool head coach replied: “It’s a shame you ask me this question but, honestly, yes, we have to tell them to go down because they’re not going to call it otherwise.

“And then referees complain why they go down. Because if you don’t go down, you don’t call it. I think Alex is honest. He tries to go for the ball, everyone can see live straight away there is a clear, clear pull.”

Iraola accepted the reasons for ­dismissing the Gakpo penalty claim but believed they were inconsistent with the explanation for not ­awarding the Isak appeal. “I think there are two situations and they are a bit related,” he said.

“The Isak one is a clear penalty. He is going to head the ball in front of the goal and they grab him where ­everyone sees the shirt. The ball just goes in front of Alex and I don’t see the reason why [it isn’t given]. ­

“Probably because he doesn’t dive or he doesn’t go to the floor. It shouldn’t be a reason not to concede a penalty. The Gakpo one, I think it’s a sustained holding but I understand their argument and I think they are right when they say the ball was too long in the air and Cody wouldn’t have arrived to the ball.

“But then you’re basically ­accepting that the first one is a ­penalty, no? You cannot use the ­argument in both ways differently.”

Iraola’s post-match mood ­contrasted starkly with his childhood friend Mikel Arteta. The Arsenal ­manager, who claimed not to have seen the Isak incident, was elated by his team’s reaction to their Carabao Cup exit at Fleetwood in midweek and his first win at Anfield in charge of the Gunners.

Arteta said: “It feels better as a manager [to win at Anfield] because it has been such a long time without this feeling. I am extremely proud, especially given the conditions we arrived to the game.

“The defeat against Fleetwood looks like the end of the world but then you have to pick yourself up. That is the beautiful part of this game. Four days later you have to come to Anfield, and play against this manager, this team who are in a good moment, and so I am so proud of what my team has done.”

Arsenal have now won at four grounds where they did not win when securing the title last season – Anfield, Villa Park, the Stadium of Light and the City Ground.

“This is a mission we didn’t complete for 14 years,” Arteta said. “There were reasons for that. Some were ­psychological, some were related to the quality we showed on the pitch, and some were decisions. We knew we had to nail all of them. We knew we would have to navigate periods where we had to suffer.”

When informed that his team had denied Liverpool a shot on target in a Premier League game for the first time in 16 years, Arteta said: “I didn’t know about that stat but that is incredible. It didn’t feel like that at the time, they are a team that shoots a lot so you have to be good at denying them space and blocking shots. To do that against this team is remarkable, I would say.”

Sports.title: Hemp strikes back as Manchester City edge out London City Lionesses in thriller
Sports.content:
Goals from Khadija Shaw and Lauren Hemp helped Manchester City to escape from Bromley with three points after a thrilling encounter with London City Lionesses. It was a statement performance from the home team, despite the defeat delivering a blow to any title ambitions they may have been quietly holding on to before kick-off.

The gap between the hosts and the champions is now six points, after Hemp restored City’s lead following Jana Fernández’s equaliser. But that London City had even played their way into conversations about this season’s title contenders in their second season has been impressive.

Andrée Jeglertz, the Manchester City manager, praised the ability of his team to win in different ways as needed, after three games in eight days. “We said afterwards, the players should be so proud of what they put into this game,” he said.

“We’ve learned we’re a great team who can keep the ball for 75% of the game and win that way, or we can win like this. That quality to win in different ways is good to have, but the players also have to adapt to that and feel it’s OK to not have the ball all the time, take pride in defending and only having three or four chances but finishing off those chances.”

Before kick-off, cameras showed London City’s superstar summer signing Alexia Putellas opening the boot of her car and taking out a heavy leather-clad square item, her third Ballon d’Or safely encased inside. The Spain midfielder did not present her trophy to fans in the stands before kick-off, instead choosing to put it on display so supporters could queue to have their photo taken with it.

The only nod to the player’s stunning individual year, in which she won the quadruple with Barcelona before joining London City, was on her feet, the geometric gold on her custom Ballon d’Or-themed boots glinting on their first outing.

There have been jokes aplenty about the unlikelihood of the world’s premier individual award heading to its new Bromley home. To reach the stadium from Hayes Lane, you pass a field of horses on your left. London City Lionesses are not Barcelona, and they have become the home of the Ballon d’Or winner by default rather than being the key component of that individual success.

Except, based on the season London City are having and the ruthless ambitions of the owner, Michelle Kang, the idea that the club could produce a season that delivers them collective success and individual success off the back of it feels less distant than it did just a few short months ago.

Against the champions, London City more than held their own, the opportunity to move level on points with their opponents and league leaders Chelsea an inviting incentive. Their threat was evident within 30 seconds, when the Manchester City defender Rebecca Knaak was forced to turn Lucía Corrales’s cross wide of the far post just ahead of a waiting Isobel Goodwin.

Neither team has impressed defensively this season, each only managing to keep one clean sheet in the Women’s Super League, and it made for a thrilling encounter, the high lines and aggressiveness of both attacks delivering a showstopper.

Making her first WSL start for the home team, with Elene Lete hitherto preferred, Mary Earps made a huge statement with an impressive double save from a Knaak header to keep the game goalless going into the break.

View image in fullscreen Mary Earps dives at the feet of Manchester City’s Khadija Shaw. Photograph: Catherine Ivill/AMA/Getty Images

City broke the deadlock despite London City dominating and it was their most influential player who delivered. Hemp flicked the ball into the run of Shaw and with her first touch, she took it past Earps before she switched the ball on to her right foot and fired in to become just the third player to score in eight consecutive WSL starts.

A deserved equaliser arrived in the 72nd minute, when Fernández was at the near post to meet a corner and her assured header sent the ball looping in at the back post.

The celebrations were emphatic but they were short-lived. This is a new, more resilient Manchester City, one that survived various scares last term to secure a second WSL title, and they re-established their lead two minutes later, when Hemp stretched out a leg to poke in Mary Fowler’s cross from the right to secure the win.

That London City could feel aggrieved at having not taken something from the game was a testament to their performance and how quickly progress is being made. The home team had 23 shots to City’s seven and 52 touches in the opposition box to City’s 13, but critically the visiting team were clinical when it mattered. Converting two of their three efforts on target and showing the edge needed to battle at the top.

Sports.title: WSL roundup: Arsenal stall despite Russo strike; Chelsea’s James suffers injury
Sports.content:
One shot, on target and in the back of the net, was all it took for Aston Villa to reopen the wound that Arsenal had been carefully trying to stitch back up.

Despite almost 65% possession, 28 shots to one, and 56 touches in the opposition box to four, Alessia Russo’s 85th-minute goal meant Arsenal were only able to salvage a point against Villa after back-to-back wins in the league and Champions League had appeared to have kickstarted their season.

The worst possible scenario for a team that has struggled against low blocks arrived in the 25th minute, when Lynn Wilms found Chasity Grant, who fired low into the bottom corner. It was a hammer blow to the home team, with Villa knowing exactly what to do next: stick 11 players behind the ball and frustrate the Gunners.

Russo’s late goal spared Arsenal’s blushes a little, the forward flicking a header in at the far post from a Stina Blackstenius cross, but the reprieve delivered by Arsenal’s victories over Tottenham and Benfica has been rolled back.

The Gunners have an incredibly tricky run of fixtures coming up, with Liverpool away followed by Barcelona, London City and then Lyonnes. And, despite the back-to-back wins, they haven’t been able to resolve the problems in the final third that have plagued every performance.

The pressure will be back on head coach Renée Slegers and there are questions to be asked about some decision making. However, with similar problems present under Joe Montemurro and Jonas Eidevall before her, maybe it’s time to look beyond the head coach.

Elsewhere Lauren James was forced off with an injury in the first half of Chelsea’s 6-0 win at Charlton. The England forward was replaced by Erin Cuthbert in the 35th minute with the away team 4-0 up. There were five different goalscorers with Melvine Malard getting two. The coach, Sonia Bompastor, said: “It is too soon [to know] about Lauren’s injury. I spoke to her at half-time and it seems to be her hamstring so we will have to have a proper assessment tomorrow.”

Tottenham climbed to fourth in the table after a comprehensive 4-1 win at Birmingham City. The Spurs midfielder Drew Spence set a new all-time WSL appearance record with 2017 to move one above the former Chelsea defender Millie Bright. West Ham were also 4-1 winners, over Liverpool, in their third league win of the season, leapfrogging their opponents in the table to move up to 10th.

Annabel Blanchard gave Crystal Palace the lead at Brighton with a glorious long-range effort but the visitors could not hold on and strikes from Caitlin Hayes and Sophie Peskett completed the turnaround 2-1 win for Arturo Ruiz’s side. “I think that these three wins in a row will be key for the rest of the season and we are in a very good moment,” Ruiz told the club website. “And I think that we are showing what we want to do in terms of our energy. The first half was very good even though we conceded a goal.”

Sports.title: European football: Mbappé penalty helps Real Madrid stroll to sixth straight win
Sports.content:
Kylian Mbappé moved on from a tumultuous week by scoring a penalty to help Real Madrid win 3-0 at Racing Santander on Sunday.

The French forward narrowly lost out on the Ballon d’Or to Bayern Munich’s Harry Kane on Monday and then had to apologise after a social media storm following a video in which he joked about the former Chinese leader Mao Zedong.

Real Madrid’s match, along with other Spanish fixtures this weekend, was not broadcast by Chinese state television because of the fallout.

Jude Bellingham and Yan Diomandé were also on target to keep third-placed Madrid within three points of the La Liga leaders, Barcelona, who thrashed Alavés 6-1 on Saturday.

José Mourinho’s side have won six straight games across all competitions and are a point behind Atlético Madrid, who beat Levante 2-0.

Real Sociedad’s four-match winning run came to an end after they lost 2-1 to Athletic Bilbao thanks to first-half goals from Inaki Williams and Alex Berenguer, who scored a penalty.

Gennaro Gattuso’s Lazio consolidated their position at the top of Serie A with a 2-1 victory over Cagliari, nudging ahead of Inter after the two clubs had started the weekend level on points.

Lazio made a poor start as Cagliari took the lead through M’Bala Nzola in the 20th minute before goals in either half from Gustav Isaksen and Andrea Pinamonti gave them a sixth straight Serie A win.

Como moved back into the top four as they eked out a 1-0 victory at home over bottom side Venezia on Sunday for a fifth consecutive victory across all competitions.

The hosts dominated, but needed a penalty to find the back of the net. The Como captain, Lucas Da Cunha, converted in the 43rd minute for the French international’s first goal of the season. “This is the type of match we found hard to win last season,” Da Cunha told DAZN.

Second-half goals from Kerim Alajbegovic and Jeremie Boga ensured Juventus returned to winning ways with a 2-0 victory over 10-man Napoli, who had Luca Marianucci sent off in the second half as they slipped to their fourth defeat of the campaign.

Lyon and Paris FC both won to close in on the defending Ligue 1 champions, Paris Saint-Germain, with the capital team defeating Monaco 3-1.
