View image in fullscreen Lyon’s Corentin Tolisso embraces coach Paulo Fonseca after scoring the second goal against Angers. Photograph: Manon Cruz/Reuters

Lyon won 2-0 at home to Angers with goals in each half from Ernest Nuamah and Corentin Tolisso, as they bounced back from a 2-0 defeat away to PSG last time out.

The seven-time French title winners are third in the table, three points behind PSG and one behind second-placed Lille. Lyon’s win came amid reports that their coach, Paulo Fonseca, is close to leaving the club to return to his native Portugal.

“I know that I will be with the players tomorrow morning but beyond that it is hard to say,” Fonseca, who was in tears as he embraced his backroom staff at the end of the game, told reporters. Fonseca is reportedly a target for Sporting, whose coach Rui Borges is under pressure.

Paris FC are fourth after getting the better of Monaco at the Stade Jean-Bouin. Lassine Sinayoko, the Malian international forward, scored twice late in the first half for Paris FC before Folarin Balogun pulled one back on 65 minutes.

Sports.title: Michael Carrick to stay in charge of Manchester United for Roma game
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick is poised to remain in charge of Manchester United for the Champions League game against Roma at Old Trafford on Tuesday despite the 2-0 defeat at Chelsea on Saturday.

United have not won in nine games and have made their poorest start to a season since 1988, but Carrick’s position is expected to be reviewed again during the international break after the next round of Premier League matches, in which United host Aston Villa next Sunday.

The 45-year-old head coach came close to losing his job last Monday when Jason Wilcox and Omar ­Berrada met at the training ground to discuss his future. The director of football and the chief executive decided ­Carrick should be given a chance to turn form and results around.

Carrick’s side are in 17th with seven points, above the relegation zone only on goal difference.

There remains a view within the hierarchy that Carrick can still transform fortunes, with United’s travelling support still backing him at the end of the defeat at Stamford Bridge on Saturday. After the game the head coach indicated that he expected to still be in position for the Roma match. He said: “We’ve got to move forward and win matches, it’s as simple as that.”

View image in fullscreen Bruno Fernandes, Manchester United’s captain, looks dejected after the 2-0 defeat at Chelsea. Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The Guardian

Eddie Howe is Wilcox’s preferred candidate should Carrick be sacked, with contact between the parties understood to have been made. The former Newcastle manager is open to taking up the position, subject to negotiations. He would cost about £3m in compensation to Newcastle.

Julian Nagelsmann, the ­former Germany and Bayern Munich head coach, is highly regarded by ­Christopher ­Vivell, United’s director of ­recruitment, who is believed to have sounded out his fellow ­German. The pair previously worked together at RB Leipzig.

Sports.title: Scottish roundup: Falkirk shock Celtic; Hibernian beat Hearts in semi-final
Sports.content:
Celtic slumped to a 2-0 defeat at Falkirk on Sunday to ramp up the scrutiny on manager Martin O’Neill after a run of three wins in 10 games. The Scottish champions had the chance to extend their lead at the top of the table to seven points, but never recovered from conceding a third-minute opener to Ethan Ross.

Scott Tanser scored a second before half-time and the Bairns even had a third goal ruled out by a video assistant referee review for handball against Jacob Murrell. The majority of Celtic’s struggles this season have come in European competition as they crashed out of the Champions League qualifiers and have lost all three Europa League group matches.

But sloppy defensive errors and a lack of a clear tactical plan are beginning to cost them domestically as well. Rangers could now close to within one point of their Old Firm rivals should they win a game in hand.

“We’re still in a decent position at this minute,” said a defiant O’Neill. “I keep out the noise at the end of it all. A tough one to take because I know we conceded two goals but we could have scored six or seven dead easily.”

Falkirk had not beaten Celtic since March 2007, but were well worthy of a fourth consecutive victory to move up to fourth in the table. O’Neill recalled Cameron Carter-Vickers to the heart of his defence, but that decision backfired when the American international presented the ball to Ross to slam home the opening goal.

Quick Guide Scottish Premiership roundup: Saints dedicate draw to dismissed Steward Show Simo Valakari dedicated St Johnstone’s battling 2-2 draw at Kilmarnock to the goalkeeper Toby Steward, who was dismissed in the 14th minute (pictured) after misjudging a long ball and handling outside his penalty area. Saints then twice fell behind to Cathal McCarthy and Djenairo Daniels, but equalised both times with goals from Danny Schmidt and Joel Cotterill to capture an unlikely point. The substitute goalkeeper Ross Sinclair, who came on at the expense of Taylor Steven, also made multiple second-half saves to help Saints move up to seventh. Valakari, the St Johnstone manager, said: “Toby has held his hands up and said: ‘I am sorry, boys, for what I did.’ But our team did it for Toby, the boys did it for Taylor, who I needed to take out straight away. “We are all here playing for each other. We have got each other’s backs when things happen. That tells me my players are ready to accept any responsibility. Early red card, with Toby that’s my tactical choice. I ask my keeper to play very high, like a sweeper-keeper for those long balls. In those moments, for a year, Toby has been fantastic in clearing the ball, reading the ball. It’s a thin line, a little outside the box, that can happen.” Alfred Johansson admitted he was left to sweat as Motherwell broke a seven-game winless run with a 1-0 win over St Mirren. Lukas Fadinger rattled home a penalty eight minutes from time to relieve some pressure on the Swede as the Fir Park side climbed into eighth. Johansson was adamant his team were well worthy of a result, which brought welcome relief to both him and his players. He said: “Even more than relief, I felt good, happy, joy, determination. This group has done really well lately and I think it’s very well deserved to get the victory and have at least four points from these last two games. It’s important to build on it, the most important thing today is that we didn’t give away easy goals or big chances at all." Press Association Photograph: Andy Buchanan/Shutterstock Editorial Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

The former Celtic goalkeeper Scott Bain was inspired in the Falkirk goal to deny Haissem Hassan and Camilo Durán, while the Colombian forward also struck a post as the visitors pressed for an equaliser. But Celtic’s leaky defence was exposed once more on 38 minutes when Tanser raced forward from left-back and drilled low into the corner.

O’Neill twice rode to Celtic’s rescue last season to take interim charge, 20 years after his first spell at the club ended. The Northern Irishman then signed a one-year deal in June.

Yet murmurs of discontent among the club’s fanbase have increased in recent weeks with many now calling for a change. “I’ve managed this team now for about a year, give or take a month or two, and I’ve managed before,” said O’Neill. “We’re still top of the league. We came from a mile behind last year to win the league. A mile behind on two or three occasions as well.”

Marink Reedijk secured his first win as Hibernian manager with a memorable 2-1 Premier Sports Cup semi-final victory over Hearts at Hampden.

View image in fullscreen Jamie McGrath wheels away after scoring Hibernian’s second goal. Photograph: Andrew Milligan/PA

A frenetic Edinburgh derby got up and running in the fourth minute when the Hearts attacker Cláudio Braga headed in from a corner, only for Martin Boyle to deservedly level in the 19th minute with a poacher’s goal. A compelling encounter continued and the midfielder Jamie McGrath put the on-top Hibernian ahead three minutes before the interval.

Although Hearts retained a threat in the second half, a stout defensive display by the Leith side means they will meet Rangers in the final at Scotland’s national stadium on Sunday 13 December. Hearts had won the four previous meetings between the teams at Hampden, in 2006, 2012, 2020 and 2022, but this was Hibs’ day.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

On Saturday, Ryan Naderi’s dramatic late strike broke down Aberdeen’s stubborn resistance to earn Rangers a place in the final.

Aberdeen restricted Rangers to one shot on target in a low-quality first half, but Derek McInnes’s side picked up the pace after the break. Aberdeen survived relentless pressure at times but in the 83rd minute Naderi redirected a strike from James Penrice into the net for his eighth goal of the season to seal a 1-0 win at Hampden Park.

The 23-year-old Naderi later tried to share the glory, saying: “It feels amazing. I’m happy, of course, happy to be the one who scores the goals, but happy for the team. I think we deserved it. We believed we could score right up until the very end and we did, and I think it’s a deserved win.”

View image in fullscreen Ryan Naderi: a happy man. Photograph: Jamie Johnston/Focus Images Ltd/Shutterstock

It was another close-range strike from Naderi and he joked about this proficiency from distance. The Germany-born Czechia international said: “I’ve tried to shoot twice today from outside of the box and it didn’t go well. So I went back inside the box. Maybe I should just stick to the easy ones! As I said, I’m just happy how it is right now and I’m going to try to stick to it.”

Sports.title: Should Premier League strugglers stick or twist as pressure on managers mounts?  | Andrew Beasley
Sports.content:
No Premier League manager has yet lost his job this season. In only three of the past 10 campaigns was November reached without a club making a managerial change.

The 2026-27 season commencing with 11 managers who were appointed at some point in 2026 has probably contributed to the early season stability. They have to be given a chance to fashion their side as they see fit. But with roughly a quarter of the season played and only one more round of fixtures before an international break, the first sacking may not be far away.

Michael Carrick remains the favourite to be the next manager to leave his post. He is unsurprisingly followed by the managers of the clubs who occupy the relegation zone: Pierre Sage of Crystal Palace, Sunderland’s Régis Le Bris and Oliver Glasner at Nottingham Forest. It seems almost inevitable that Carrick will leave soon so the more interesting analysis lies among the bottom three.

Sunderland sit 20th and are predicted by Opta to finish there. However, they have had a testing start to the season. Le Bris’s side have faced five of the current top seven clubs, the joint-most along with Liverpool. The manager also has enormous reserves of goodwill after taking the club back to the Premier League and then into Europe.

Despite their tough schedule, Sunderland came into the weekend within one expected point of Chelsea, Manchester United and Tottenham before losing 3-1 at Coventry with the xG count 1.8 to 0.7 in their favour. It was a familiar outcome for a side that has scored 6.2 goals fewer than expected this season.

With Sunderland’s next five league opponents being Chelsea, Aston Villa, Tottenham, Liverpool and Newcastle, the challenge of staying up will not immediately get easier. At least their chance‑converting woes are not as bad as those of Nottingham Forest.

Their shots have been worth 14.7 expected goals, the fourth most in the division after the matches on Saturday. But not once in a game this season have the goals they scored at least equalled their xG, let alone surpassed it. It is a finishing issue, not a question of opposition goalkeepers having super-human performances against them.

The analytical step above standard expected goals is xG on target (xGOT). It measures the likelihood of an on-target shot becoming a goal based on chance quality and shot placement. Forest’s xGOT this season is 7.4, little more than half of their expected goal tally.

This inability to test goalkeepers severely enough explains why Glasner’s men have scored just six times. They are squandering almost one goal per game on average according to their expected goals, a significant shortfall. None of the 96 teams in Europe’s big five leagues were worse than 0.5 goals per match below xG last season, which suggests Forest’s luck should turn for the better.

Is Evangelos Marinakis patient enough for that to happen? Forest’s expected goal data is much stronger for Glasner than it was under any of the four managers their owner fired last season. Whether he pays attention to such numbers is a different issue.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Glasner hinted at a physical deficiency in the squad after defeat at Brentford. “We are outrun by the opposition in every single game. We have to change it,” he said. Distance covered data from Fotmob suggests that is not quite the case, albeit Forest have been outrun in their past five league games. Both the underlying xG data and physical statistics are worse at Glasner’s former club Crystal Palace though.

As expected goals have a far greater bearing on future performance or results than running stats, those numbers are the greater concern. Equally, Palace’s average of 96.9 sprints per match is the fewest in the Premier League (after Saturday’s matches).

The club have been through similar teething troubles with new managers before. Palace’s previous two appointments that occurred between seasons were Frank de Boer and Patrick Vieira. The former was sacked after only five matches in all competitions in 2017, the latter won just one of his first nine league games four years later before recovering to finish 12th.

While Palace are a little wasteful in attack, they have not been as bad as Forest or Sunderland. Their defence is a much bigger problem, which is unusual as Sage’s Lens conceded the fourth fewest expected goals in Ligue 1 last season. Palace are second worst for that metric in the Premier League in 2026‑27, rock bottom if penalties are excluded. Some of that may be down to starting seven combinations of players in the back three because of injuries and Axel Disasi’s three‑match ban, but it is imperative that a manager overcomes such inevitable difficulties.

Palace host Liverpool next weekend. They return after the international break with potentially winnable games against Coventry and Hull. Will those fixtures represent a good opportunity for Sage to kickstart his reign or an excellent chance for his replacement to hit the ground running? Only the chair, Steve Parish, will know the answer but Palace are the strugglers who look most in need of managerial change.

Sports.title: Boy hands himself into police after Bradley Lowery taunt in Sunderland match
Sports.content:
A 14-year-old boy has “handed himself in” to West Midlands police after a video posted on social media appeared to show a Coventry fan taunting Sunderland with a photo of Bradley Lowery during the Premier League match on Saturday.

Sunderland fan Bradley captured the hearts of the football world when he was diagnosed with neuroblastoma, a rare form of childhood cancer. He died aged six in 2017.

Coventry said on Sunday that they were investigating the video footage and Bradley’s mother, Gemma, issued an emotional statement through the Bradley Lowery Foundation, which raises funds and awareness to help and support children.

West Midlands police said: “We are aware of a video circulating on social media showing an incident at Coventry City’s Premier League match with Sunderland [on Saturday] afternoon.

“A thorough investigation has been launched, and a 14-year-old boy has since handed himself in and will be spoken with in due course. We understand the upset and outrage this video has caused in the community and to the victim’s family and our officers are keeping them up to date with the progress of our investigation and working closely alongside both football clubs.”

Coventry said in their earlier statement: “Coventry City FC is aware of footage circulating on social media in connection with an incident during our Premier League fixture against Sunderland. The club does not tolerate offensive behaviour and will liaise with the relevant authorities to determine the appropriate course of action.”

Gemma Lowery said her “beautiful boy deserves to be remembered with love, not hate” in her statement. She posted on Instagram: “Yesterday, a Coventry fan used a photograph of Bradley to taunt Sunderland supporters. As Bradley’s mam, this is heartbreaking, especially as it’s one of my favourite photographs of him. Just look at that smile.

“I remember that day like it was yesterday. He was so happy, having so much fun. Those moments were precious because they were few and far between.

“So much of Bradley’s short life was spent battling cancer and enduring treatments no child should ever face. To see such a beautiful memory used in such a cruel way really does make my heart hurt.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Sport in Focus Our picture editors select their favourite sporting images from the past week, from the spectacular to the powerful, and with a little bit of fun thrown in Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“We are a football-loving family who follow Sunderland home and away. I’m all for football banter, but surely mocking a child who died from cancer is not banter?”

Lowery added: “I hope the club takes appropriate action and the young lad’s family help him understand how hurtful his actions were. I don’t want hatred directed towards him, so please please don’t, just for him to learn from this.

“Behind that photograph is a little boy who was loved beyond measure and a family who miss him every day. Thank you to everyone who has defended Bradley and shown us so much love. It means more than you know.”

Sports.title: Arsenal’s statement win over Liverpool is massive, it’s a one-horse title race
Sports.content:
Arsenal already have one hand on the Premier League title after beating Liverpool at Anfield.

That is according to former Premier League defender Ashley Williams, who believes the champions are effectively in a league of their own.



4 Arsenal have been told they are in a one-horse title race after beating Liverpool Credit: Getty

The Gunners moved three points clear of City after their 1-0 win over Liverpool.

Kai Havertz's first half goal proved to be the winner as they secured their first Premier League victory at Anfield since 2012.

It leaves the Reds nine points adrift of Arsenal, whilst Brighton and Chelsea are both five points off the pace.



Meanwhile, the Seagulls are the only team to take points off of Mikel Arteta's side, who have won eight of their nine matches to date.

Is the title race already over?

Williams does not expect Brighton to be able to keep in touch with the defending champions throughout the campaign, though.



Instead, he believes the title picture can already be considered a 'one-horse race'.

Speaking on The Final Word, he admitted: "We’ve seen other teams win the league like Leicester but I don’t think Brighton can topple Arsenal this season.



"Before the season started I said it was a one-horse race and then I thought maybe it wasn’t but now I’m back to thinking it’s just Arsenal."

Williams continued: "It feels like a bit of a statement win, doesn't it?

"We've become accustomed to this; Arsenal get the job done.

4 The Gunners are three points clear at the top of the Premier League Credit: Getty

"Not to say that they weren't good either, by the way. They were very good. They defended very well.



"They also created more chances but you've got to go there at places like Anfield and dig in. It's hard to play at Anfield.

"I don't care what team you are in the world. You go there, you dig in, you get your points, you get back on the bus happy. So, massive, massive win for Arsenal today."

Arteta verdict on Arsenal win

Prior to Sunday's victory, Arsenal had not won at Anfield in the Premier League since September 2012.

On that occasion, current manager Arteta was in the Gunners' starting line-up as they came away 2-0 winners.



Reflecting on the importance of ending their Merseyside drought after the match, he said: "It's been a long time, it's been too long.

4 Arteta guided Arsenal to their first league win at Anfield since 2012 Credit: Getty

"So everybody attached to the football club should feel very, very proud because of the difficulty of the task that we had today.

"After getting out of the cup in the manner that we did and then being able to come here four days later and perform, compete and earn the right to win the game, tells you the story of of the beautiful game that we are involved in and how crazy and made it can drive you.



"That's why I think it's important to stay emotionally in control, otherwise it's difficult to handle, but I'm extremely proud of what the boys have done."

Arsenal set title pace

Arsenal's latest win sees them earn 24 points after nine matches of the current campaign.

It marks the most by a team at this stage of a Premier League season since the Gunners achieved the same tally in 2022/23.

They have only amassed more points after nine matches on two previous occasions.



4 Arsenal have dropped just three points in their opening nine matches Credit: Getty

Those came during the 2004/05 and 2007/08 seasons, with Arsenal accumulating 25 points under Arsene Wenger on both occasions.

However, neither campaign ended in title glory as the Gunners instead finished second and third, respectively.

Sports.title: Lisandro Martinez red card was ‘mutinous’ as call made for him to never play for Man United again
Sports.content:
Lisandro Martinez red card was ‘mutinous’ as call made for him to never play for Man United again

Lisandro Martinez has been labelled 'pathetic' for his quickfire red card during Manchester United's defeat at Chelsea.

Football writer Henry Winter also described the sending off as 'almost mutinous', as the centre-back picked up two yellow cards in the space of 83 seconds.

3 Martinez didn't take his red card too well and had to be pushed away by Amad Credit: Getty

Martinez's first yellow came as he got into a battle with Morgan Rogers. Rogers turned Martinez, who hauled him to the ground.

From the resulting free-kick, Chelsea were awarded a corner and Martinez was tasked with marking Wesley Fofana.

Martinez lost his man and ended up chasing after him to the back post and elbowing him in the face while not looking at the ball.

VAR recommended an on-field review for the foul and a penalty was awarded with a second yellow card for Martinez then coming.

And speaking with Shaun Custis on The Sunday Edition, he said: "This was just pathetic. 83 seconds, he gets rolled and turned by Morgan Rogers and manages to bring him down at the third time of asking.

"Then, he loses Fofana at the corner and leads with his elbow into him and is sent off. He quite rightly gets blanked by Michael Carrick as he goes down the tunnel, it is almost mutinous a red card like that.

"It is a case of what are you doing? I thought it was absolutely shocking."

And Man United broadcaster Scott Saunders believes that the Argentine shouldn't play for the club again.

Speaking on the talkSPORT Goals Show, he said: "This guy is an idiot. I know he likes to play on the edge, but that is pointless. It is pointless.

"The game is already gone because they are 1-0 down, but that is the icing on the cake.

3 Man United have won just one Premier League game all season Credit: AFP

"There isn't loads of contact, but you are giving the referee a decision to make. I cannot get over this guy. This guy can't play for Man United again.

"He has been my favourite player for years because I talk about intensity and tenacity, and he gave some of that that made me gravitate towards him because it made me feel as if he cares.

"He is meant to be a leader in this team and if that is how leaders act, I dread to think where we are going. I cannot believe he has been that stupid.

"He shouldn't be picked again."

How did Carrick react to the red card?

Man United started the game the better of the two teams and should have scored at least a couple.

Bruno Fernandes and Amad Diallo were the biggest culprits with two sitters.

3 Man United are in a relegation battle at the moment Credit: Getty

Matheus Cunha also had a goal ruled out for offside, meaning the teams headed in at 0-0 only for Rogers to run through the middle of the defence and open the scoring with a deft chip.

Martinez was then sent off and Cole Palmer dispatched the penalty.

And after the match, Carrick was asked about Martinez and if he'd let him down, but he just shook his head.

Sports.title: 14-year-old hands himself into police over sickening Bradley Lowery taunt
Sports.content:
A 14-year-old boy has handed himself into the police after taunting Sunderland fans with a picture of Bradley Lowery.

A video of the incident, taken during Coventry City's 3-1 win over Sunderland on Saturday, was posted to social media and very quickly went viral.



4 An image of the late Bradley Lowery was used by a Coventry City fan to taunt Sunderland fans during the Sky Blues' 3-1 victory on Saturday Credit: Getty

The clip showed the teenage boy taunting the fans in the away end of the Coventry Building Society Arena by pointing to an image of Lowery that he had gotten up on his phone.

Lowery was a young Sunderland supporter who sadly passed away from stage 4 neuroblastoma - a rare and aggressive type of cancer - in 2017 at the age of six.

Prior to his passing, he and his family had forged a close, personal relationship with then-Black Cats striker Jermain Defoe, and also became the club's mascot.



After the Sky Blues learned of this footage that was circulating, they very quickly released a statement which read: “Coventry City FC is aware of footage circulating on social media in connection with an incident during our Premier League fixture against Sunderland.

“The club does not tolerate offensive behaviour and will liaise with the relevant authorities to determine the appropriate course of action.”



Police confirm teenage boy hands himself in

Since then, the West Midlands Police has confirmed that the young fan has turned himself into the police.

“We are aware of a video circulating on social media showing an incident at Coventry City’s Premier League match with Sunderland yesterday afternoon (31 Oct),” their statement read.



“A thorough investigation has been launched, and a 14-year-old boy has since handed himself in and will be spoken with in due course.

“We understand the upset and outrage this video has caused in the community and to the victim’s family and our officers are keeping them up to date with the progress of our investigation and working closely alongside both football clubs.”

In the wake of his passing, Lowery's mother Gemma, helped kickstart The Bradley Lowery Foundation, which raises funds to support families who are fundraising for treatment or equipment that is not covered by the NHS.

4 The Bradley Lowery Foundation was started in August 2017 Credit: Getty



4 Lowery and his family established a close relationship with then-Sunderland striker Jermain Defoe Credit: Getty

This was something the Lowery family had to do in an effort to raise money for Bradley to receive treatment that was only available in the USA - they would raise £1.3 million in their campaign.

The foundation also supports research into neuroblastoma and other childhood cancers.

Lowery's mother pens emotional statement

Gemma also saw the video that circulated during the game, and took to social media through the foundation's page, to issue a statement.



"My beautiful boy deserves to be remembered with love, not hate," she wrote. “Yesterday, a Coventry fan used a photograph of Bradley to taunt Sunderland supporters. As Bradley’s mam, this is heart-breaking, especially as it’s one of my favourite photographs of him.

"Just look at that smile. I remember that day like it was yesterday. He was so happy, having so much fun. Those moments were precious because they were few and far between.

“So much of Bradley’s short life was spent battling cancer and enduring treatments no child should ever face. To see such a beautiful memory used in such a cruel way really does make my heart hurt.

4 Bradley's mother Gemma penned an emotional statement after being made aware of the footage circulating on social media Credit: Getty



“We are a football-loving family who follow Sunderland home and away. I’m all for football banter, but surely mocking a child who died from cancer is not banter?"

But Gemma also recognised that the fan was just a child himself, and urged people not to retaliate with hate.

“I hope the club takes appropriate action and the young lad’s family help him understand how hurtful his actions were," she continued. "I don’t want hatred directed towards him, so please please don’t, just for him to learn from this.

“Behind that photograph is a little boy who was loved beyond measure and a family who miss him every day. Thank you to everyone who has defended Bradley and shown us so much love. It means more than you know.”



After receiving an out-pouring of support, she issued a further statement doubling down on her stance for fans not to direct hate towards the teenager.

"I have spoken to West Midlands Police, who have confirmed that the young lad involved is currently in custody," she wrote. "I have also been informed that he is only 14 years old, same age as Bradley would be now if he was still with us.

"With that in mind, I really want to urge everyone not to take matters into their own hands or direct any hate, threats or harm towards this young boy or his family. As hurtful and upsetting as his actions have been, he is still a child himself.

"The police and Coventry City Football Club will both be speaking with him, and I sincerely hope this is enough to make him understand the seriousness of his actions and the devastating impact that words and actions like these can have on families and friends.



"I don’t want hate to be met with more hate. That is not what Bradley stood for, and it is certainly not what I want in his name. I just hope this young lad learns a very important lesson from all of this and thinks twice before ever doing something so cruel again."

Sports.title: Ole Gunnar Solskjaer coaching at fifth division club after missing out on Man United job
Sports.content:
Ole Gunnar Solskjaer coaching at fifth division club after missing out on Man United job

Ole Gunnar Solskjaer has returned to coaching after missing out on a Manchester United comeback earlier this year.

The 53-year-old is working with the first-team and junior side at fifth-tier Norwegian outfit FCK.

3 Solskjaer has been coaching a fifth-tier club in Norway after missing out on a United return Credit: AFP

It comes after Solskjaer was snubbed for the caretaker role at Old Trafford back in January.

The former Red Devils boss held talks over a return to the club following Ruben Amorim's sacking.

However, Michael Carrick was ultimately appointed before signing a two-year permanent deal in May.

Solskjaer has since started working with local outfit FCK in Kristiansund.

The club are fresh from finishing ninth in the 11-team Norwegian Fourth Division.

Solskjaer eyes managerial return

A return to full-time management remains on the cards for Solskjaer, though.

Speaking to TV2 Sport, he admitted when asked: "Yes, I think I’ll probably take a job."

As for whether he would consider taking the United job again in the future, Solskjaer added: "If Michael does well for ten years and decides to quit, and they ask me if I can take them for two months, of course I wouldn’t say no.

"I’ve been at that club for 18-19 years, so it’s part of the family. But it’s not something I’m thinking about."

Solskjaer at Man United

Solskjaer spent three years in charge of the Red Devils between December 2018 and November 2021.

3 Solskjaer spent three years in charge of United between 2018 and 2021 Credit: Getty Images - Getty

Similarly to Carrick, his tenure began with a spell in caretaker charge after Jose Mourinho's departure.

During his time at the helm, Solskjaer achieved third and second place finishes in the Premier League.

He also guided United to the Europa League final in 2021 before losing on penalties to Villarreal.

His stint as manager followed 11 years at Old Trafford as a player.

Between 1996 and 2007, Solskjaer scored 126 goals in 366 appearances in all competitions.

The forward also won 12 trophies including six Premier League titles and an historic treble in 1999.

3 Solskjaer has been away from the dugout since leaving Besiktas in August 2025 Credit: Sportsfile

Having left United five years ago, Solskjaer's most recent managerial role came at Besiktas.

However, he departed the Turkish giants in August 2025 before returning to his role as a UEFA match analyst in October last year.

Sports.title: Why Noni Madueke wasn’t sent off after headbutt on Alexis Mac Allister
Sports.content:
Why Noni Madueke wasn’t sent off after headbutt on Alexis Mac Allister

Noni Madueke avoided a red card against Liverpool despite appearing to headbutt Alexis Mac Allister.

The Arsenal winger was involved in a flashpoint during the second half at Anfield on Sunday.



3 Madueke avoided a red card despite appearing to headbutt Mac Allister Credit: Getty

Madeuke and Mac Allister clashed after the Liverpool midfielder had fouled Martin Odegaard.

Jurrien Timber also confronted the Argentina international following the foul.

However, it was Madueke who leaned in towards Mac Allister before he fell to the floor.



Madueke avoids red card

Both Mac Allister and Timber were subsequently booked by referee Andy Madley.

Madueke avoided punishment, though, despite moving his head towards his opponent.



The incident was reviewed by VAR, who deemed the contact not to be forceful enough to warrant a red card.

As a result, VAR official Stuart Attwell stuck with the referee's on-field decision not to dismiss Madueke.



The Premier League Match Centre provided an explanation for the decision on social media.

A post on X read: "The referee's call of no violent conduct by Madueke on Mac Allister was checked and confirmed by VAR.

"VAR: 'All of the situations have been checked and cleared. There is some contact as Madueke and Mac Allister square-up. In my opinion, it's not forceful, not violent, not brutal.'"

3 Mac Allister and Madueke clashed as tempers flared at Anfield Credit: AFP



talkSPORT verdict

Meanwhile, Ashley Williams shared his stance on the altercation on The Final Word.

Discussing the incident with Majestic, the talkSPORT co-host said: "No, I'm not having it, I'm not having it.

"Your head has been touched a little bit. If I touch your head now with that much force, you ain't going down like that.

"By the way, he's the one that's going to Odegaard and having a moan about him going down.



"Which was a foul, definitely, and then he's dropping on the floor. What are we doing now?"

Madueke had already been on a yellow card after being cautioned by Madley in the 55th minute.

3 Arsenal picked up their first Premier League win at Anfield for 14 years Credit: Getty

He was booked for a cynical foul on Bradley Barcola early in the second half.



The 24-year-old has never been sent off during his senior club career.

His only red card to date came for PSV's Under-19s against Almere City in 2019.

Arsenal end Anfield wait

The altercation with Mac Allister came with 10 minutes remaining in the match as Arsenal defended their narrow 1-0 lead.

Mikel Arteta's side had opened the scoring through Kai Havertz during the first half.



Arsenal held on to secure victory, moving three points clear at the top of the Premier League in the process.

Meanwhile, they picked up their first Premier League win at Anfield since 2012 with Sunday's triumph.

The defending champions have won eight of their opening nine matches.

Those include four successive victories since their only defeat of the season against Brighton on September 19.

It also marked an ideal response to the Gunners' shock Carabao Cup exit at the hands of Fleetwood Town on Tuesday.

Sports.title: Jude Bellingham eclipses Zinedine Zidane Real Madrid feat in 73 fewer games
Sports.content:
Jude Bellingham scored his 50th Real Madrid goal in their 3-0 win over Racing Santander on Sunday.

Jose Mourinho's side cruised to a dominant away victory after scoring three first half goals at El Sardinero.



3 Bellingham scored his 50th Real Madrid goal on Sunday, doing so much quicker than football icon Zinedine Zidane Credit: Getty

Kylian Mbappe and Yan Diomande were also on the scoresheet either side of Bellingham's 22nd minute strike.

The win leaves Real Madrid third in LaLiga, three points behind leaders Barcelona.

Bellingham makes history

Their victory also saw Bellingham reach an historic milestone in his Los Blancos career.



The England midfielder has now scored 50 goals in 154 matches for the Spanish giants since signing from Borussia Dortmund in 2023.

In doing so, he becomes the 50th player in Real Madrid's history to reach the tally.



Bellingham is also the only player to score 50 goals since his debut season in 2023/24.

His latest effort was already his fourth in 11 LaLiga appearances under Mourinho this season.



Meanwhile, he has overtaken Zinedine Zidane's tally for the club in 73 fewer matches.

The Ballon d'Or winner scored 49 goals altogether in 227 appearances between 2001 and 2006.

Zidane, who also wore the No.5 shirt for Real Madrid, won six trophies during his time at the Santiago Bernabeu.

3 Zidane's incredible volley in the 2002 Champions League goal was surely his best one Credit: Alamy



Those included a LaLiga title and the Champions League, honours which Bellingham won in his debut season in Spain.

The 23-year-old has also won the UEFA Super Cup, FIFA Intercontinental Cup and Spanish Super Cup in the last three years.

LaLiga title race

Real Madrid's latest success has seen them maintain their three-point deficit to bitter rivals Barcelona.

It follows Barca's 6-1 home win over Alaves on Saturday, which temporarily saw them move six points clear of Los Blancos.



Whilst neither side has drawn in LaLiga this season, Real Madrid have suffered two defeats to Barca's one.

The leaders' only setback came in El Clasico last weekend as they were beaten 2-1 at the Camp Nou.

3 Bellingham is the 50th player to score a half century of goals for Real Madrid Credit: AFP

Real Madrid resume their league campaign with a trip to Valencia on Saturday.



It follows a Champions League clash with Greek champions AEK Athens in midweek.

Sports.title: Harry Kane’s former EFL manager details unusual penalty practice technique that saw him refuse help
Sports.content:
Harry Kane’s former EFL manager details unusual penalty practice technique that saw him refuse help

Harry Kane had a unique approach to penalty practice early in his career, a former manager of his has revealed.

The Ballon d'Or winner has built a reputation with his clinical spot-kicks for club and country.

3 Kane missed his second penalty of the season against Borussia Dortmund Credit: Getty

However, Kane's trademark precision deserted him during Bayern Munich's 2-2 draw with Borussia Dortmund on Saturday night.

The England captain struck the crossbar from 12 yards, missing the chance to double his side's lead.

Bayern would go on to be pegged back twice as they were held at the Allianz Arena.

It is already his second miss of the season having hit the woodwork for the Three Lions against Spain in September.

Kane's penalty practice routine

Kane's former Leyton Orient boss Russell Slade has now lifted the lid on the player's penalty routine at the start of his senior career.

The 66-year-old signed a 17-year-old Kane on loan from Tottenham Hotspur back in January 2011.

He went on to score five goals in 18 appearances during his five-month stay at Brisbane Road, having been handed his professional debut by Slade.

None of those strikes were from 12 yards, though, despite Kane often practicing his spot-kicks after training, Slade has revealed.

Speaking to Shaun Custis and Henry Winter on Sunday Edition, he recalled: "He would spend 20 minutes, half an hour, just practicing the run up and exactly where he was placing the ball, time after time.

"I actually remember asking him one day, ‘do you need a keeper?’ He said, ‘no, thank you, it’s ok.’ It was just about his run up and where he was going to plant the ball."

3 Slade has revealed Kane would practice penalties without a goalkeeper Credit: Getty

Slade was also asked if he could see Kane's character straight away when he joined Orient.

He added: "Yes, absolutely. Very calm kid. Very dedicated boy. Would ask maybe the odd question.

"I think it was important that senior players, he quickly got a relationship with them and he wanted knowledge.

"He had a thirst for that knowledge and understanding of the game at a very early age."

The 33-year-old had scored two penalties since the miss against Spain before his wayward effort on Saturday.

It marks the 16th time in his career he has failed to score a penalty during a competitive match.

3 Kane scored five goals in 18 appearances during a loan spell at Orient aged 17 Credit: Getty

Kane has scored 113 penalties from his 129 attempts. The most recent of those converted efforts came against Arsenal in the Champions League last month.

Sports.title: Erik ten Hag takes fresh swipe at Cristiano Ronaldo: ‘It’s simply over’
Sports.content:
Erik ten Hag has had another dig at Cristiano Ronaldo suggesting that his time at the top of football was over years ago.

The former Manchester United manager appeared on ESPN in the Netherlands to talk about Ronaldo in depth.

3 Ten Hag and Ronaldo never saw eye-to-eye Credit: AFP

Ronaldo departed Man United for the second time in November 2022 only a few months after Ten Hag was appointed as the club's manager.

The decision for the Portuguese superstar to leave came after an explosive interview with Piers Morgan in which he claimed he had no respect for Ten Hag.

It's the Dutchman's turn to fight back and he's made some withering claims about Ronaldo.

When asked about his career in the last few years, Ten Hag said: "The players wanted to work for him and looked up to him because he is one of the greats of all time.

"But over the last seven or eight years, he simply can no longer deliver.

"From Juventus, it's simply over."

Ten Hag's Ronaldo claim

The key part of the interview was around Ten Hag talking to Ronaldo about his fitness.

The former Ajax boss claims that the striker simply didn't want to put in the extra work required to be fit enough to lead the line in the Premier League.

Ten Hag said: "When I started at Man United, I explained to him how we were going to play and what his role in that would be.

"But ultimately, you have to deliver. But he could no longer bring himself to push through the pain to give everything every single day and to train at his maximum.

"And if you are not fit to play in the Premier League, you have no chance.

Ten Hag was then asked about Ronaldo having always done that, and he said: "Well, that was the image. But he could no longer bring himself to do that.

"You show him what is required, and he knows it too, and you come to him with arguments that hold up."

3 Ronaldo has now moved to Saudi Arabia and is closing in on 1,000 career goals Credit: Getty

He was asked about Ronaldo's response and if it was to say Ten Hag wasn't good enough.

"No, he doesn't say that because the evidence was so clear. So he had to make a choice.

"At that moment, I have to make a decision that is in the best interests of the club and of the team.

"I know that I did everything I could to persuade him [to be Premier League fit], but the choice is with the individual as to whether he wants to make that investment.

"And if you don't want to, I have to make different choices in the interest of the team, and that's whet we saw."

And that is quite clear in just how little Ronaldo started under Ten Hag.

In the Premier League, he played the full game just three times before his interview with Morgan brought his career at Old Trafford to an unsavoury end.

On the added noise around Ronaldo, the Dutchman said: "No one is bigger than a club or a country not even Messi or Ronaldo.

"In the end, the team always comes first."

3 Ten Hag's time after Ronaldo left saw him pick up two trophies Credit: Getty

What did Ronaldo say?

The interview with Ronaldo by Morgan in 2022 rocked the football world.

And in it, he was brutal about Ten Hag.

At one point, he refused to come on as a substitute for Man United against Tottenham Hotspur, while he also believed he was forced out.

On leaving Man United and the Dutchman, he said: “Don’t tell me that the top players, the guys who want everything, the key players will play three minutes.

"Come on, this is unacceptable after what they keep saying before, that they respect me, that they do this, they do that. For me it was not respect, this is why I take this decision I regret.

"I apologised to my teammates for the situation, I did a post, an Instagram, I regret to left from the stadium. I regret my teammates know what I felt, and I said to them apologised, but in the same way, I’m not regret to take the decisions to not come on.

"The coach didn’t have respect for me. So this is why the relationship, it’s in that way. He keep saying in the press that he come to me, he like me blah, blah, blah but that it’s only for the press. 100%.

“If you don’t have respect for me, I'm never going to have respect for you."

Sports.title: Invincibles beware! Mikel Arteta might just be assembling Arsenal's greatest EVER defence, writes ISAAN KHAN
Sports.content:
Within seconds of the full-time whistle, Gabriel Heinze had lifted an elated Mikel Arteta off the turf. The Argentine knew why this result brought his colleague a certain catharsis, which had eluded him for over a decade. Arteta had previously opened up about the psychological difficulties of playing at Anfield, describing the experience akin to a cyclist suddenly running out of energy. A mental paralysis of sorts. The game in question was in February 2014, having experienced a 5-1 defeat as a Gunners player. Arsenal’s previous victory against Liverpool away dated back to September 2012, a 14-year wait to banish these demons which he was duly reminded of in Friday’s press conference and in the minutes before kick-off. Instead, it’s now getting scary for Arsenal’s Premier League title rivals. The prospect of the Arteta's side opening up a gap from the chasing pack by Christmas is becoming a real possibility — and it’s all because of their defence. A William Saliba-less backline reducing the Reds to zero shots on target at Anfield is a moment worth digesting. Mikel Arteta and Gabriel Heinze jubilantly embrace as the final whistle blows at Anfield Arsenal ended their 14-year wait for a Premier League victory at Anfield with a superb display Winning on opposition territory after an abysmal record lasting over a decade is an achievement in itself. But to ensure a frontline featuring Alexander Isak, Florian Wirtz and Bradley Barcola aren't given so much as a sniff in front of goal is a further statement. For all the focus around the fragilities of their frontline — the weaknesses are still very much in the open, as seen by the shock Carabao Cup defeat to Fleetwood Town — it’s Arsenal’s defence which underpins everything. Since the start of last season, Arsenal have not lost a league game when leading the scoreline at half-time. Just like how Arsenal’s (previously) woeful record at Anfield would be used as a reminder, this statistic is a menacing one for future opponents. It raises the question: how does this backline compare to the best Premier League defences who came before them? If the team carry on in this vein towards a consecutive league title, the Arsenal Invincibles set-up from the historic 2003-04 season of Sol Campbell, Kolo Toure, Ashley Cole and Lauren, with Jens Lehmann in goal, could soon be superseded. The current collection of defenders, backed up by David Raya, create a defensive structure which is proving so hard to break down, even with the lack of a sole regular scorer in the side. Gabriel, despite his embarrassing attempt at pretending Isak struck him in the face yesterday, stayed strong in physical duels and didn’t relent in periods when Liverpool piled the pressure on. By the 42nd minute, the Reds had whipped in 17 crosses, many of which were cleared by Gabriel or Konsa. Riccardo Calafiori is a wonderfully-gifted footballer who finds himself in some unorthodox positions which are difficult to track. The Italian’s menacing runs inverting from the left flank caused Liverpool many a problem. Kai Havertz tapped home from a low cross early on to give Arsenal a crucial lead to defend Even Jurrien Timber, who didn’t have his best game in the final third, helped ensure solidity at right back up against Cody Gakpo. It’s the £55million Ezri Konsa, though, which reflects a shrewdness typifying Arsenal and Arteta. As soon as it emerged that Saliba would be sidelined for months with a back injury, a right-sided centre back became the priority. The 29-year-old has slotted in seamlessly and again shone against the Reds, mirroring the ‘blessed’ tattoo he has in-scripted on his left hand. The versatile defender won 100 per cent of his ground duels, made 14 defensive contributions and completed eight clearances. He ranked No 1 in all these categories yesterday. An Arteta team starts from a rock-solid base with multiple, versatile defenders, often at the cost of fewer frontline options (Arteta struck just two more league goals than third-placed Manchester United last season, for example). It ultimately worked in the previous campaign, their defence propelling Arsenal to a first Premier League title in 22 years. Another title appears to be well on track. And: watch out Campbell and Co. The moniker for Arsenal’s best defence in modern history is at risk. GUNNERS GAINING FROM MIKEL'S RUTHLESS STREAK Arteta’s ruthlessness is well-documented. Just ask Aaron Ramsdale or Jakub Kiwior, who were eased out after being surplus to requirements in recent years. Or the cold treatment of Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang and Mesut Ozil earlier in the Spaniard’s reign over their behaviours. Arteta's ruthlessness with team selection is continuing to pay dividends for the Gunners The current squad is brimming with talent — and spades of uncertainty. Eberechi Eze performed well off the bench against Bayern Munich after Bukayo Saka’s thigh injury on 10 minutes, followed up by a start against Everton — and didn’t get a minute against Liverpool. While Viktor Gyokeres was given his first league start of the season against Everton, where he played well — only to be dropped for this match. As seen by Christos Tzolis’ dash to make yesterday’s squad ahead of schedule, influenced by Max Dowman’s three-match suspension, no one’s place is really secure. That makes for a truly competitive environment. HEINZE IS RAISING THE BAR The final word must rest with Heinze. The fiery serial-winner, drafted in by Arteta in July 2025, was always going to demand high standards and bring a ferocity which can turn some the wrong way. At Argentine side Newell’s Old Boys, for example, he would weigh the players twice a day. Heinze's arrival in July 2025 has added a steeliness to the defence and paid off in spades So the appointment was attached with risks, even if Arteta had grown close to his ex-team-mate from his Paris Saint-Germain. It’s turned out to be a clever addition, which has added a steeliness to the defence and paid off in spades. Sources say that Heinze, who has managed five teams, is well-respected by the players, but is also seen as someone who does not mince his words. They know he’s not here to mess around.

Sports.title: Liverpool's anonymous attackers cost them the chance of beating Arsenal despite dominant display... the gap to the champions is narrowing - but the Reds still aren't close enough, writes LEWIS STEELE
Sports.content:
Liverpool's anonymous attackers cost them the chance of beating Arsenal despite dominant display... the gap to the champions is narrowing - but the Reds still aren't close enough, writes LEWIS STEELE

As disheartened fans spilled out of Anfield, nearly all conversations were about the referee and questions over why he did not point to the penalty spot in the first half when Jurrien Timber pulled back Alexander Isak.

They had a point and this game would have been completely different had Andy Madley – or VAR Stuart Attwell – seen what everyone else saw when Isak was an inch short of connecting with a header and possible goal because he was pulled back by his marker.

It was a similar situation to Liverpool’s only other defeat under new boss Andoni Iraola, where supporters were left aggrieved at the incorrect call to send off Ryan Gravenberch against Manchester City.

In both cases they were unlucky to be on the wrong side of refereeing mistakes and would have cursed the fine margins. But in both cases Reds fans will also realise their team just did not do enough to win too.

Just like against City, Liverpool dominated Arsenal for large parts of this match. It felt as though they were one magic moment or opposition mistake away from scoring and lfiting off the Anfield roof.

But in both cases, that moment never materialised. It felt like the Liverpool attackers were looking around waiting for somebody else to step up and be the man to start the pendulum swinging in Liverpool’s favour.

Alexander Isak and Liverpool's attackers struggled against Arsenal's defence

They had zero shots on target, according to Opta, and that is the only statistic that Iraola will be mulling over in the coming days.

Bradley Barcola, Florian Wirtz and Alexander Isak have all been frighteningly good in recent weeks but in this game, especially the second half, Liverpool’s big-money forwards looked like they had run out of ideas.

Arsenal defended like their lives depended on it and their away fans, who barely saw the ball down their end of the pitch after half-time, celebrated every Gabriel header or David Raya catch like a goal.

The home team, meanwhile, were left throwing long balls forward to Virgil van Dijk – the only player who could aerially compete with Arsenal’s team of giants. It felt like several Hail Mary passes but no one could answer Iraola’s prayers.

Liverpool’s two defeats to City and now Arsenal both demonstrate the gap between Iraola’s outfit and a genuine title contender. There is definitely a small level between Liverpool and Arsenal – but Reds fans can take solace in knowing it is not a chasm like last season.

A referee decision here, a better final ball there and Liverpool may be still unbeaten under Iraola and the whole country would consider them a title contender.

Iraola has closed the gap on the top teams but knows several tweaks are still needed to take that next step. Can they do it this season? It is far from impossible but seems a tall order.

The upcoming fixture list is kinder to them, at least. Of the current top eight, Liverpool have played all of them – two in the Carabao Cup – and won each test apart from City and Arsenal. The next two league games are against teams in 18th and 17th.

Florian Wirtz has improved recently but was unable to provide cutting edge on Sunday

But right now, Liverpool are a team with too many ‘ifs’, ‘buts’ and ‘maybes’. If Alexis Mac Allister did not get under a first-half header that looked like a certain goal… if the referee had given a clear foul on Isak… if the forwards packed their shooting boots.

As it was, for all of the nail-biting moments for Mikel Arteta on the touchline as Liverpool had lots of the ball in the final third, his goalkeeper David Raya could have had a cigar in and read the papers for most of the second half.

That is what will bother Iraola the most.

As for being a complete team able to compete for the league title again, Liverpool seem so close yet so far.

Trey bien

Trey Nyoni made his first Premier League start and it will not be his last after he put in a solid shift.

Though he misplaced some passes and was probably lucky to escape an early yellow card after two late challenges, the 19-year-old presents Iraola with an interesting tactical quirk.

The Englishman always wants the ball and drops into the back line to start attacks, with a maturity beyond his years.

He sits deep which allows Alexis Mac Allister to play as more of a box-to-box midfielder, undoubtedly his best position.

So where does this leave Ryan Gravenberch, who spent the afternoon on the bench? Given the amount of games Liverpool have across competitions, the Dutchman will still play many minutes — but he is currently at risk of falling down the pecking order thanks to the exciting talent of Nyoni.

There is also a conversation to be had about how Liverpool’s balance and control was lost when Nyoni was replaced by Dominik Szoboszlai.

Trey Nyoni excelled for the Reds and helped the home side control the tempo

Another Wirtz no show

Casual football fans who maybe only tune in for the big games have never seen Wirtz play well.

They must wonder what all the fuss is about.

The German has been on fine form in recent weeks but has been like a ghost — no Halloween pun intended — in the two biggest matches against City and Arsenal.

It is all well and good performing against teams like LASK in the Champions League but Wirtz, at £116million, was signed to make a difference in these blockbuster clashes.

Instead, his national team colleague Kai Havertz continued his record of impacting the games that really matter come May. How Wirtz could do with some of that killer instinct.

Sports.title: Kimi Antonelli becomes youngest champion in F1 history! Third-place finish at Mexico Grand Prix secures title triumph for 20-year-old superstar in race won by Max Verstappen
Sports.content:
Kimi Antonelli becomes youngest champion in F1 history! Third-place finish at Mexico Grand Prix secures title triumph for 20-year-old superstar in race won by Max Verstappen

Sobs and wailing, and neither he nor we could fully explain what someone so youthful had done.

‘Champion of the World,’ Kimi Antonelli was told over the Mercedes radio by his race engineer Peter Bonnington. And the crying started.

For once the tension, he admitted, had got to him this weekend. That is how Antonelli felt going into the Mexico City Grand Prix, an incident-laden one, a controversial one, but one from which he emerged emotional as the youngest winner of the Formula One title in history, at 20 years and 68 days.

Nessun Dorma played after he was hailed on the podium, for he was also the first Italian to achieve the feat since Alberto Ascari in 1953, and the operatic master Puccini bowed his knee.

Then, having finished third on the day, behind winner Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton, those pair of giants, with 11 titles between them, lifted the newest member of their exclusive club on to their shoulders.

This was a few minutes before Antonelli had put his gloved hands inside his helmet and all the lad’s emotions poured out after he crossed the line.

Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton lift the new champion Kimi Antonelli on their shoulders after his third-place finish secured the title at the Mexico GP

Antonelli celebrates becoming the youngest world champion in F1 history

Antonelli embraces his team having secured the title with a third-place finish in Mexico

But he was, agonisingly, made to wait here on Sunday after a high-speed crash involving Valtteri Bottas delayed his route in the hot sunshine and thin air of this sprawling city, the honking horns of its roads a contrast to the calm he has exhibited all season – well, until the end and it was all over.

While Ferrari squabbled – more of which later – the details of Antonelli’s coronation being punctuated by 33 minutes: Bottas’ front left wheel was suddenly half torn away from its hinges, still attached yet askew, and his Cadillac was suddenly transporting him as a passenger, a big snap. It looked like a suspension failure. The race was suspended as the Finn received treatment and the fencing was mended. He hobbled away.

So, a red flag was waved and Antonelli prepared to go through a second dose of lights-out torture from fourth place at Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez.

A further delay followed when Racing Bull’s Arvid Lindblad was punted into the air in a tussle with McLaren’s Oscar Piastri. A safety car was deployed.

Even from the original start, long before the Bottas mishap, the drama had been set up in the most intriguing way. Antonelli started on the second row alongside Ferrari’s Charles Leclerc with the only two men who could possibly delay his elevation to champion status in front of him, pole-sitter Hamilton and George Russell.

One of the front-two pair had to win or Antonelli was champion. And even then only if he finished outside the top nine in the case of Russell winning, or outside the top 10 if Hamilton were victorious.

It is a massive 1,000 yards into the first corner and experience suggests that pole here is not always the advantage it usually is. Slipstreaming from pursuers had been key in the past here, and highly dramatic, and it raised the question whether Antonelli would try to impose himself at this early point. Or sit back.

He had, as it were, a three-foot putt to win The Open, but in this case a mighty right-hander waited to test his race-craft and nerve.

Antonelli, pictured during the Mexico GP, did enough on the day with a composed drive

Antonelli's family embraces him after he crossed the finish line to complete his ambition

He looked calm on the grid in the immediate build-up, chatting to his dad Marco under a back umbrella protecting them from the intense heat. He kissed his mother Veronic on the cheek. His little sister Maggie was also in attendance.

The good news for Antonelli is that he was not snared at that opening corner. He held on to fourth position. Verstappen, a past master at that very place and already a five-time winner here, was the big bolter.

Russell fell back to sixth, an emblem of his miserable season. But the real drama was at the front as the two Ferraris tangled at Turn 4, after Leclerc used Russell’s slipstream down the opening straight to press his claims.

They were wheel-to-wheel going into Turn 4. Leclerc went down the outside. The Monegasque could not make the corner and cut across the grass into the lead. They did not quite touch.

Hamilton, who made it around the bend, albeit with a slight wobble, fell back to third. Verstappen cashed in on the internecine squabble to go second. ‘Pushed off by my team-mate,’ complained Hamilton.

The stewards opened their investigation. ‘What is happening about Charles?’ asked Hamilton.

A five-second penalty came Leclerc’s way. Hamilton, who later passed Leclerc at a restart, thought this unfair. He had a point. Leclerc’s questionable lunge had granted him free air at the front. Hamilton asked his pit wall for them to be switched around. This was not so easy because Verstappen was sandwiched between them.

Antonelli is draped in the Italian flag as he takes in the magnitude of his accomplishment

The new world champion receives adulation from the crowd in Mexico City

Join the discussion Is putting such young drivers in top F1 seats helping or harming their development and mental health?

Yes, there was self-interest in Hamilton’s comments but it is hard to argue with his logic. Though, as it turned out, once Leclerc had served his penalty Verstappen just jumped him in the pits for the lead.

Russell, meanwhile, had run into Isack Hadjar on the eventful opening lap and sent the Red Bull No2 to the back of the grid. The stewards’ prosecution workload doubled. He was landed with a 10-second penalty while running fifth. It never rains on George’s side of the garage.

Ha, but meanwhile, the boy prince Kimi was running fourth, and Russell, his bag man, was going to fall further behind once he had sat out his punishment, finishing sixth.

A brittle cocoon of calm was created around the likely-to-be champion.

Though teetotal, Antonelli promised a night with family and friends they would ‘remember for ever’. Who could begrudge it? Four races, or four laps of honour, remain.

From error-prone rookie to history maker: How Antonelli became F1's youngest-ever champion Kimi Antonelli came from the shadows to take the title, having started the year with question marks that arose last season not over his pace, which was never in doubt, but about errors that punctuated his rookie campaign. He had been significantly outgunned by George Russell in the other Mercedes. There was also a feeling that he was overexposed too early in a top seat rather than given time to learn his craft at a less visible team, an accusation that was probably true. The alternative of a year or two at, say, Williams, might have been kinder on his young mind. He was, after all, just 18, and to take up the place vacated by no less than Sir Lewis Hamilton was surely a task for an older head. Would he bounce back from the pounding? Could he rein in the extravagant ebullience that was the extreme edge of his electric speed? In fairness, Toto Wolff was his ever-supportive boss and put an arm around his slender shoulders to emollient effect. Antonelli and Russell have been managed by Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff (left) Wolff, who enlisted Antonelli to Mercedes' young driver programme aged 12, never wavered in his belief that he had unearthed Hamilton's rightful heir. He conveyed this conviction to Kimi both privately and publicly. Still, there were doubts in the paddock. One team principal told me at the start of the season when I asked him for his assessment of Antonelli: 'Undoubtedly quick but prone to too many mistakes.' But he has shown himself to be serene in 2026, and especially so for a driver of 20. Think about that. Only 20. There are only a few examples from the past of this kind of precocious brilliance. Stirling Moss secured his landmark win at Goodwood on his 19th birthday in 1948, announcing his gifts to the world. Max Verstappen won his first F1 race in Spain at 18 in 2016. Well, Antonelli can be satisfied at living in that sort of society. He frankly blew away Russell, who started the season as favourite and full of confidence that his time had come. He duly started in spectacular style in Melbourne with a win there and it looked as if he had only to stay alive to take the title. It was all his for the taking. A pivotal moment, the most significant of all in my estimation, came in China with Antonelli's first victory a week after Russell's Australia. A door opened, just as Russell needed to keep it slammed shut in Antonelli's face, and from there impetus swung the Italian's way. I think Russell, who had won the sprint in China, was psychologically damaged by trailing Antonelli home the next day - five seconds the margin. The usurper had done it from pole, again a first for him. He was to keep his foot to the floor for weeks on end, helped by the good fortune to be driving the grid's dominant car for the early part of the season. Other teams later caught up. Antonelli's first win of the season, in China, may have done the psychological damage to Russell, who trailed him by five seconds Wins in the next four races - Japan, Miami, Canada and Monaco - poleaxed Russell, who was at a loss over how best to drive his machine. Poor George began by talking a good game, but he gradually realised the dream of a lifetime was slipping away from him. Yes, he suffered the bigger slices of bad luck, and perhaps there was a slight bias in the team towards Antonelli, not to the extent of sabotage or ill-intent towards Russell, but a natural inclination towards the star they saw as their future hero. The damage was done by now and Antonelli, skilfully tutored by Lewis Hamilton's old race engineer Peter 'Bono' Bonnington, was always busily aggregating points, there or thereabouts even on his off days. After three races without a win - including Hamilton's maiden victory for Ferrari in Barcelona, something of a false dawn - Antonelli triumphed again in Spa. This represented a big swing. Russell and Hamilton collided on the first lap, with Russell eliminated and Hamilton given a five-second penalty. Antonelli held off Charles Leclerc to stretch his lead over Hamilton to 45 points and over Russell to 50. Antonelli inherited Lewis Hamilton's former race engineer Peter 'Bono' Bonnington when he came in at Mercedes following the seven-time world champion's move to Ferrrari Other highlights? Probably the best was Antonelli's home win in Monza from the back of the grid after taking a penalty for a change of engine. The car was quick, his new power unit strong, and he was favoured by an agreeable strategy, but it was still a fine comeback drive. Most of those in the stands would have preferred a Ferrari victory. Their red tops and their banners signified that. There was barely a Mercedes shirt in sight. But, still, this win helped lift Kimi on to a pedestal in his homeland he had yet to reach. Another milestone in his remarkable championship journey was Russell's engine blowing up in the closing stages of the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia at the start of last month. That sealed it, basically, even though Antonelli finished second to a resurgent Red Bull of Max Verstappen. Still, the points were ticking up all the time. And his victory in Austin last weekend was a remarkably commanding one. Now he has clinched the title with four rounds remaining depending on whether the planned concluding races in the Middle East, in Qatar and Abu Dhabi, survive the vicissitudes of war. If they are off, the planned alternative is a finale in Imola. It would be some party to toast the boy born just 20 miles away in Bologna.
