Sports.title: Hamilton says Leclerc cost Ferrari victory in Mexico and calls for “serious talks” | Formula 1
Sports.content:
A deeply unhappy Lewis Hamilton accused his team mate of costing Ferrari victory in today’s Mexican Grand Prix.

The Ferrari pair went off at turn four when Charles Leclerc tried to take the lead off Hamilton at the start of the race. Leclerc rejoined ahead of his team mate while Hamilton lost a position to Max Verstappen.

The stewards later issued Leclerc a five-second time penalty, which dropped him behind Verstappen but not Hamilton. Although Hamilton managed to pass Leclerc at a later restart he was unable to pass the Red Bull driver and blamed his team mate for costing him the position.

He also suggested the stewards had told drivers to expect stronger penalties for leaving the track at turn four. They issued a statement clarifying the regulations prior to the race.

“In drivers’ briefing we discussed [that] as soon as you go off in turn one you have to give the position back,” said Hamilton. “Obviously last year I got a 10-second penalty for that same move that he did.

“But ultimately it was that that lost us the win today and I think we have to have some serious talks behind the scenes, for sure.”

However Hamilton, who finished less than a second behind Verstappen, said he was pleased with the performance from his car this weekend despite not using the team’s latest power unit.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

“The good thing is the team are working really hard. We’ve really improved our car,” he said. “It’s great to be here.

“We were on the old engine this weekend as well. So [it’s a] good result, good points, shame we didn’t get a win, but some you win, some you lose.”

Leclerc said he chose not to let Hamilton pass him because doing so would also cost him a position to Verstappen.

“The penalty was deserved in a way,” he said. “The thing is that it was a bit confusing because we both didn’t make turn four, then I stayed ahead and then Max got past Lewis. So then I asked what should I do and I kept the position and I took a deserved penalty.

In Leclerc’s view, it was better for Ferrari that he stayed ahead of Verstappen. He also suggested Hamilton squeezed him too much at the first corner.

“I’ll speak with Lewis,” he said. “I think we both didn’t make the corner [at turn four]. I don’t know if Lewis’s point was for me to get P3, but at least having a Red Bull second, I felt it was worth it to kind of keep the position and see what happens. That’s what I did.

“I could be also unhappy with how much he pushed me off the track out of turn one, but I think it’s racing. When you are fighting for a win, It’s the way it should be.”

Sports.title: Beating 40-Year-Old Usyk Won’t Buy David Benavidez Immortality
Sports.content:
David Benavidez might think beating Oleksandr Usyk punches his ticket to the Hall of Fame, but boxing fans will see right through it. Dragging a 40-year-old heavyweight down to 200 pounds gives him a famous scalp on his resume, not an automatic pass to greatness.

“I’m going to get [my respect] one way or another. Once I beat [Usyk], there’s no denying me my spot in the history books,” Benavidez claimed via Fight Hub TV.

That chip on his shoulder is blinding him to reality. Benavidez acts like everyone owes him adulation, but demanding respect while targeting a 40-year-old on a brutal weight drain is the exact definition of taking a shortcut.

Beating Usyk under these conditions proves nothing. Draining an older fighter down 20-plus pounds leaves him vulnerable, sluggish, and dry. When an elite volume puncher swarms a drained legend whose legs are gone by the fifth round, educated fans do not applaud. They write it off as an obvious cash-out mismatch.

History books remember who you conquered at their absolute peak. If Benavidez wants undisputed recognition, he has to run that exact fire line:

– Turn back Jai Opetaia at 200 pounds to settle who actually rules cruiserweight.

– Step into Daniel Dubois’ range and take flush heavyweight heat without blinking.

– Grind out Filip Hrgovic through grueling, foul-filled trench warfare.

– Risk getting sparked out by a vicious young phenom like Moses Itauma.

– Solve the tricky Cuban ring craft of Frank Sanchez without losing discipline.

That five-man run creates an untouchable resume. Beating an aged, depleted Usyk simply adds a famous name with an asterisk next to it. Until Benavidez trades the easy scalps for real danger, that chip on his shoulder is going to stay right where it is.

Before any of that happens, Benavidez has to get past WBC belt-holder Michal Cieslak on December 5 in Glendale with his WBA and WBO straps on the line.

Sports.title: Tim Bradley Says Mbilli Blew Golden Chance Against Canelo
Sports.content:
Tim Bradley believes Christian Mbilli let the threat of Canelo Alvarez’s counters strip away his aggression Saturday night. His harshest criticism was that the pressure fighter stopped fighting like himself once he got in front of the Mexican star.

Rather than setting a grueling pace, Mbilli grew tentative. Bradley noticed a fighter second-guessing his offense out of dread for the incoming counters.

“He was scared to get countered. They came in with an entirely different game plan. He lost his identity last night,” Bradley said on his channel about Mbilli. “He lost his identity last night because Nelo was on a whole another level.”

Bradley praised Canelo’s defense for creating that doubt. He highlighted subtle head movement and shoulder rolls that defused punches, robbing Mbilli of the momentum he needed to let his hands go.

“That slowed down the pace. That discouraged that man even more,” Bradley said. “Mbilli didn’t look ferocious like he usually looks ferocious.”

Bradley even noticed shades of Terence Crawford in Canelo’s tactics. He pointed out the snappy combinations and strategic clinches, suggesting Canelo learned a few practical tricks from their meeting.

“You take something from each fight,” Bradley said. “Crawford tied his ass up when he had to, and Nelo finally tied somebody up. I could not believe it. Turned that pitbull into a poodle,” Bradley said.

Whether Mbilli chose to box off the back foot as a deliberate tactic remains an open question. Nothing from his corner confirmed it after the final bell, but the approach looked calculated rather than fearful.

Mbilli did not look terrified of getting hit. Instead, he looked like a fighter saddled with a flawed strategy, trying to outthink a master counterpuncher at his own game. The decision to abandon his trademark swarm left him stranded in no man’s land.

By the time Mbilli finally realized the mistake and started pressing inside, the fight had already slipped away. Giving up the early and middle rounds in a passive posture dug a hole far too deep to climb out of against someone of Canelo’s caliber.

Mbilli left his mark, connecting with shots whenever he actually let his hands go. The official scorecards did not reflect how competitive those exchanges really were.

More importantly, Mbilli exposed Canelo’s current physical limitations. The Mexican star simply cannot fire sustained combinations or maintain an intense pace anymore. Canelo was fighting in brief spurts, resting frequently, and relying on single power shots.

The real tragedy of the night was Mbilli’s failure to exploit those vulnerabilities. With Canelo showing his age and accumulated ring wear, the blueprint was right there: step on the gas, make him work every second of every round, and drown him in volume. Instead, Mbilli gave an aging veteran the exact thing he needed to survive, which was time to breathe.

Sports.title: Chris Billam-Smith Risks World Title Ambitions On Pointless Clarke Revenge Tour
Sports.content:
Even with a world title on his resume, Chris Billam-Smith cannot completely shake his two amateur losses to Cheavon Clarke. On Saturday, November 7, he gets his shot at redemption, though he risks far more than the man who twice got the better of him in the unpaid ranks.

Their 10-round cruiserweight clash tops Zuffa Boxing 12 at London’s Copper Box Arena, broadcast live on Sky Sports and Paramount+. This marks their first meeting as pros, and Billam-Smith admits those past defeats fuel his fire.

“I’ve got a lot of bitterness inside me which I need to unleash on November 7!” Billam-Smith told Sky Sports in October. Clarke’s wins include the 2016 national amateur championship final, which crushed Billam-Smith’s long-standing tournament dream.

That backstory brings real heat to this matchup, but Billam-Smith must keep his emotions in check. A victory maintains his momentum toward another major title run. Chasing payback for a decade-old loss could easily backfire against a dangerous puncher.

Clarke showcased his resilience along with his defensive flaws against Jack Massey in June. He hit the canvas twice before rallying to halt Massey. Billam-Smith competed on that same Bournemouth card, dispatching Ryan Rozicki in seven rounds. Both enter the ring coming off stoppage wins, yet Clarke’s grit under fire stands out as a crucial factor.

Those knockdowns offer Billam-Smith an incentive to test Clarke’s chin early. Still, they serve as a clear warning to remain composed if Clarke gets hurt. Clarke proved that dropping him does not guarantee the win. Rushing in recklessly could leave Billam-Smith wide open to counterpunches.

As a former WBO champion, Billam-Smith owns the far more accomplished professional resume. That pedigree ought to carry more weight than short-format amateur bouts from years ago. Billam-Smith excels in grueling pro championship rounds where physical strength, inside fighting, and pace control reign supreme.

Clarke is 35, entered the pro ranks late, and his absolute ceiling so far has been British and European contention. If Billam-Smith goes out and dominates him over ten rounds, the immediate reaction will simply be that an experienced former world champion beat a novice pro who started his career late. Nobody is awarding Billam-Smith points in the world cruiserweight rankings for beating a domestic contender.

If things go wrong, the fallout is devastating. Clarke can crack, as Jack Massey found out, and Billam-Smith gets hit cleanly in almost every fight he enters. Getting clipped or outpointed by someone who has not even fought for a world title instantly kills Billam-Smith’s chances of getting back in line for the division leaders or securing another massive payday.

Letting amateur grudges dictate matchmaking at this stage of a pro career is purely emotional thinking. It satisfies a personal itch, but in business terms, it is a massive detour that risks throwing away years of hard-earned status over a couple of short-format bouts from 2016.

Sports.title: Team Haney Overlooking Liam Paro To Chase Ryan Garcia Circus
Sports.content:
Mickey Bey has already mapped out next year, treating Liam Paro like an afterthought. Even with Paro holding the IBF belt, Haney’s trainer cannot stop eyeing a massive repeat encounter with Ryan Garcia.

Bey expects Haney to claim his second 147-pound title in December, hoping Garcia grabs the remaining pair to set up a mega-unification down the line.

“I want Ryan to get the belt from Teofimo and we fighting for the undisputed next year,” Bey said to MillCity Boxing. “That’s the biggest fight in boxing.”

The Ring’s Mike Coppinger reports that Haney and Paro are penciled in for December 19 at Chase Center in San Francisco for unified WBO and IBF honors. The date serves as Haney’s first outing under his fresh DAZN contract, ending a layoff that stretches back to his points win over Brian Norman Jr. last November.

Paro arrives hungry to spoil the party, yet Bey refuses to look at the man right in front of him. Team Haney is banking on Devin doing the business in the Bay Area, then counting on Garcia to snatch the WBA strap away from Teofimo Lopez. It reads like a promoter dream on paper, but counting on two separate fighters to deliver flawless results is asking for trouble.

“But hey, let’s settle the score. Hey, we going to win our fight. We going to have our two on our end. If he get his two, we got it for undisputed,” Bey said.

Collecting four belts looks great on paper, but hardware is not the real motivator here. Avenging the beating against Ryan is about erasing humiliation that titles cannot fix. Garcia planted Haney on the canvas three separate times in April 2024, and while a positive ostarine test officially wiped the defeat into a no-contest, commission paperwork cannot delete the footage. Fans remember Haney wobbling around the ring, and no collection of straps washes that stain away.

Bey keeps harping on Garcia missing weight as the deciding factor in that first beatdown. Complaining about the scale might sell tickets for a rematch, but excuses do not erase a one-sided shellacking. Haney has to get in the ring and physically prove he can handle the smoke himself.

Before any future rematch happens, Liam Paro is standing in the doorway. The Australian won his IBF belt by scraping past Lewis Crocker on tight 115-113 cards in June. That razor-thin margin might make Haney’s team think Paro is ripe for the picking, but the champion is not showing up just to roll over and surrender his hardware.

Between the ropes, Haney brings a frustrating, defensive style built around an active jab and constant retreat. Paro cannot fall into the trap of following him like a tourist. The Australian southpaw has to cut the ring in half, pin Haney against the ropes, and batter the ribs the second Haney dives in to initiate a clinch. If Paro allows Haney to jab, circle away, and reset without taking damage, he will spend the entire night chasing shadows on the scorecards.

Bey talks like December is just a tune-up stop on the road to a mega payday with Garcia. Treating a unified title bout like an afterthought provides Paro with perfect ammunition to derail Team Haney’s master plan before it ever gets off the ground.

An undisputed fight offers both men all four titles to parade around, but everyone knows the hardware is secondary. The actual hook for the public is seeing whether Haney can avoid getting planted on the canvas again, or if Garcia repeats the destruction.

Sports.title: Sheeraz Expects Canelo Payday After Limping Past Zachenhuber
Sports.content:
Hamzah Sheeraz is openly campaigning for an unearned lottery ticket against Canelo Alvarez, and boxing fans are expected to pretend this makes sense.

Fans online already assume Turki Alalshikh will force this matchup. That speaks volumes about the current matchmaking environment. People expect what they think the money wants instead of the fights worth watching. Canelo has genuine options available. A rematch with Terence Crawford makes sense, while Jaron Ennis, Dmitry Bivol, Lester Martinez, or Osleys Iglesias would each offer far more entertainment.

Sheeraz, in contrast, is the ideal safe business fight. He gives the Riyadh Season brass an easy UK marketing angle, brings a recognizable name to British television, and holds zero real threat of upsetting the apple cart. As Simon Zachenhuber showed, Sheeraz is upright, gets uncomfortable when pressed, lacks defensive subtlety, and struggles to impose his height when someone refuses to fold early.

Against Canelo, Sheeraz would stand right in range, get timed coming in, and walk straight into counters without the ringcraft to survive it. Picking him is about protecting the brand and cashing a check, not testing greatness.

“Why not, bro? Why not test myself against the best,” said Sheeraz to DAZN Boxing when asked yesterday why he wants to fight Canelo. “I’m in this game to be the best, and put myself in there with someone with the likes of Canelo. It’s stuff you can dream of. Every day, I wake up, training harder and harder. It’s starting to become more of a reality. So, now it’s like, let me get in there and let me do my thing.”

Sheeraz did himself no favors during his recent majority decision win against Simon Zachenhuber. The German walked through his shots, pressed him constantly, and exposed his discomfort under fire. Nothing in that performance signaled that Sheeraz belongs in the ring with the face of boxing.

His brief title run did not validate him either. Picking up a vacant WBO belt by blowing out Alem Begic in two rounds proved very little. Begic was 39 with a paper record built on obscure opposition. Sheeraz then vacated rather than face Janibek Alimkhanuly, citing low money and an opponent returning from a failed test. He had every right to walk away, but walking away did not prove he is elite.

The refusal to fight Iglesias makes Sheeraz even harder to sell. Canelo openly suggested Hamzah face the dangerous Cuban to earn the shot. Sheeraz rejected the idea, pointing out that Edgar Berlanga and Jaime Munguia never had to pass such an audition. Canelo might have double standards, but whining about Berlanga does not elevate Hamzah’s resume.

Testing yourself against the best is what you do after you run through actual contenders, not after edging Simon Zachenhuber on a majority decision or blasting out Alem Begic.

If Sheeraz genuinely wanted to “test himself against the best” to prepare for Canelo, Osleys Iglesias was standing right there. Canelo offered him the exact blueprint: beat the Cuban southpaw, prove you belong at the elite tier, and bring real credibility to the table.

Saying “It’s stuff you can dream of” gives the game away. It is a dream because it represents the ultimate lottery ticket: a massive purse, global visibility, and zero downside if he loses to an all-time great. Every fringe contender wakes up training hard with that exact dream.

Wanting the biggest purse in the sport is understandable from a business perspective. Pretending that ambition alone makes you a worthy challenger is the part fans are tired of seeing. If everyone who “wakes up dreaming of Canelo” got the call, the sport would be nothing but exhibition paydays. Until Sheeraz takes on a legitimate threat who can punch back, talking about testing himself just sounds like someone angling for a retirement check.

My sources tell me chances are uncomfortably high, easily hovering around 65% to 75% that Canelo fights Hamzah next. Everything coming out of Riyadh points to Hamzah Sheeraz being the preferred target for that spot: Sheeraz sat ringside in Riyadh, gave pre-fight interviews to DAZN building up the matchup, and openly positioned himself as next in line.

That is standard operating procedure when organizers are preparing the public for an announcement. From the promotional side, Sheeraz checks the exact commercial boxes Turki Alalshikh looks for. He provides a British draw to anchor UK pay-per-view buys, brings a Middle Eastern connection based out of Dubai, and comes without the brutal negotiating headaches that accompany figures like Dmitry Bivol or Terence Crawford.

For Canelo, the risk calculus makes Sheeraz almost irresistible. After working through twelve rounds with Christian Mbilli, taking on an upright target who does not use angles or elite lateral footwork is a safe day at the office. Canelo avoids the nightmare styles of Osleys Iglesias or Jaron Ennis while pocketing another massive purse.

The only real hurdles that could derail it are: Crawford agreeing to unretire for the massive bag that a rematch would command. If Crawford says yes, every other fight gets pushed aside immediately. A sudden pivot to a mandatory unification, such as Osleys Iglesias holding the IBF belt or the winner of Janibek Alimkhanuly against Jacob Bank for the vacant WBO strap, if organizers decide they want all the belts consolidated again. Lester Martinez, who holds the WBC interim belt and was also sitting ringside, is being enforced as a mandatory obligation.

As such, unless Crawford signs on the dotted line or public ridicule forces a change in direction, all arrows point toward Sheeraz getting the nod. It is safe matchmaking dressed up as an international event.

Sports.title: Ryan Garcia Talks Mayweather While His Team Pursues Teofimo
Sports.content:
Ryan Garcia says Floyd Mayweather needs to 

“We’ve seen Ryan Garcia say on Twitter that he wants to fight on February 6th, whether it’s against Floyd Mayweather or Teofimo Lopez. I was told that Mayweather wasn’t even in discussion for the next fight,” said Mike Coppinger to DAZN Boxing. “Of course, Mayweather is almost 50 years old now. It’s kind of a pipe dream. It would be a massive event, especially if it was later in the year. First, they’re working on finalizing a fight between Ryan Garcia and Teofimo Lopez, a welterweight title unification. I think it’s one of the biggest fights in all of boxing. Teofimo just regained a title fight in Rolly Romero. I want to see it.”

Teofimo brings plenty of credibility without dragging Mayweather into the promotion. He presents an active, dangerous test with quick hands, explosive pop, elite counter striking. Garcia always carries dynamite in his left hook, though overcommitting against someone as sharp as Lopez creates immediate trouble.

That title bout stands on its own merit. Taking down Lopez proves infinitely more in today’s landscape than defeating an exhibition headliner pushing fifty, regardless of casual fan buzz. As Claudia Trejo noted, Garcia commands attention whenever he speaks. That massive platform works wonders, yet chasing a ghost can drown out the legitimate challenge right in front of him.

Setting a February date proves Garcia wants to compete this winter. It definitely does not prove Mayweather is scrambling to meet a deadline. With Lopez occupying the real negotiating table, Garcia’s final warning sounds like pure noise.

Sports.title: Canelo Alvarez Calls For Terence Crawford Rematch After Win
Sports.content:
Canelo Alvarez made his priority clear right after taking down Christian Mbilli in Riyadh to grab back the WBC super middleweight strap: he wants another shot at Terence Crawford.

In his post-fight interview, Canelo didn’t hide his intentions when asked about coaxing Crawford out of retirement.

“Hopefully, yes. Hopefully, yes. We would honestly love to have that rematch, like I’ve told you. If not, we’ll keep moving forward with our career, but hopefully that fight can happen,” Canelo said.

The desire is there. The evidence of meaningful improvement is harder to find. Beating Mbilli restores Canelo’s position as a champion, but defeating a pressure fighter does not demonstrate that he would fare better against Crawford’s movement, timing, and ability to control distance.

Whether the Mexican star cares about the potential of losing again is unclear. Assuming Turki is on board with financing a second fight, the money Canelo would get would make it worthwhile.

The appetite from fans for a sequel is lukewarm at best, and for good reason. The first bout settled whatever competitive debate existed. Crawford put on a clinic in ring generalship, using distance, a sharp jab, lateral movement, and timely ties inside to neutralize Canelo. While purists could appreciate Crawford’s discipline, it was a pedestrian viewing experience for the casual paying crowd.

Fans remember twelve rounds of Canelo plodding forward, swinging at air, unable to cut off the ring, while Crawford played keep-away and banked rounds on the outside. Rematches of fights like that rarely produce fireworks; they usually produce a carbon copy.

Boxing fans would far rather see matchups that guarantee genuine action and modern divisional relevance: A unification clash with Osleys Iglesias gives hardcore fans an intriguing, high-risk clash against a dangerous, prime southpaw puncher holding the missing IBF strap.

Even a bout against Dmitry Bivol at light heavyweight would hold more competitive curiosity than watching Crawford stick and move his way to another lopsided decision.

The only real driver behind a Crawford rematch is pure business. Turki Alalshikh has the deep pockets to bankroll a massive spectacle, and both fighters stand to collect generational checks. The promotional build would lean on celebrity hype and pageantry, but inside the ring, the paying audience knows exactly what it would look like: twelve more rounds of perimeter defense and frustration.

Sports.title: Alvarez victorious over Mbilli, captures WBC super middleweight title
Sports.content:
Canelo Álvarez (64-3-2, 39 KOs) reclaimed the WBC super middleweight title with a twelve-round unanimous decision over Christian Mbilli (29-1-1, 24 KOs) on Saturday at Kingdom Arena in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. Canelo’s cleaner counters and defensive work earned him scores of 115-112, 116-111 and 117-110 in the DAZN PPV main event.

Returning from a thirteen-month absence following his loss to Terence Crawford, Álvarez landed in bursts while Mbilli pressed forward without consistently connecting cleanly.

Mbilli had success when he sustained his attacks, but too often backed away after throwing, allowing Álvarez time to choose his counters. Canelo’s jab, hooks and uppercuts supplied the more accurate work, although Mbilli’s activity kept several rounds competitive.

In the eighth, referee Hector Afu deducted a point from Mbilli following an illegal punch. Álvarez had repeatedly drawn the referee’s attention to Mbilli’s fouls before the penalty.

Mbilli continued pressing late but could not produce the breakthrough he needed. Álvarez finished effectively in the final two rounds, securing the decision without either fighter scoring a knockdown.

WBA super middleweight champion Jaime Munguía (47-2, 35 KOs) had a much harder evening than the scorecards suggested against Russian southpaw Nikita Zon (12-1-1, 10 KOs). Munguía retained his title by unanimous decision, winning 116-112 and 117-111 twice after twelve competitive rounds.

Their sixth round produced furious action, with both fighters hurt and Munguía in serious danger before recovering. The Mexican’s combinations and greater output helped him through the later rounds, but Zon remained dangerous until the finish.

Munguía’s defensive lapses made this an uncomfortable first defense against an opponent making his first twelve-round appearance.

Rafael Espinoza (29-0, 25 KOs) retained his WBO featherweight title with a third-round TKO over Ricardo Blandón. The ringside doctor stopped the scheduled twelve-round contest at 1:22 because of a severe cut over Blandón’s eye.

Espinoza controlled the action with his jab and pressure. The medical intervention brought an abrupt ending before the challenger’s corner could attempt further treatment between rounds.

Carl Jammes Martin (29-0, 21 KOs) overcame a seventh-round knockdown to take the WBC Silver featherweight title from David Picasso (33-2-1, 18 KOs) by split decision over ten rounds.

Martin bloodied Picasso’s nose with a left hand in the third. Picasso answered in the seventh with a left hook that dropped the Filipino southpaw, who rose quickly and continued.

Martin’s strong final round helped him secure scores of 95-94 and 96-93, while the third judge favored Picasso 95-94.

Super featherweight Reito Tsutsumi (6-0, 5 KOs) stopped Raymundo Rojas García (16-3, 11 KOs) at 2:27 of the second round. The Japanese southpaw scored two knockdowns in the second before a follow-up attack prompted the referee to stop the scheduled ten-round bout.

Bek Nurmaganbet (17-0, 15 KOs) knocked out Marcos Vázquez Rodríguez (21-4-1, 10 KOs) at 2:57 of the opening round in their scheduled ten-round contest. Nurmaganbet scored an initial knockdown with approximately a minute remaining, then finished the Mexican southpaw with a combination that sent him onto his back.

Brayan León (13-0, 9 KOs) earned an eight-round unanimous decision over Hector Aguirre (7-1, 3 KOs) in a lively super middleweight contest. León landed the heavier punches early, but Aguirre rallied and kept the fight competitive.

Both men landed well in the closing rounds before León received scores of 77-75 and 78-74 twice.

Emiliano Rojo (22-0, 9 KOs) stopped Flavius Biea (24-4, 12 KOs) in the fourth round of their scheduled eight-round bout. Rojo’s pressure and body punching wore down the Romanian veteran, bringing the stoppage midway through the fourth.

Sultan Almohammed (6-0, 4 KOs) defeated Erick Jahir Urvina Villegas (5-3-3, 1 KO) by unanimous decision over six rounds. The eighteen-year-old scored a final-round knockdown with a left hand to the chin and won by scores of 60-54 and 59-55 twice.

Ghana News.title: Binance users withdraw $3.6bn after record crypto hack
Ghana News.content:
Binance customers withdrew a net $3.64bn (£2.72bn) of assets from the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange as it reopened on Sunday following a record hack last week.

The firm suspended all transactions after the incident, which affected $6.3bn in digital assets.

Major organisations, including the US Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), have accused North Korea of being responsible for the cyber attack, which is said to be the largest hack in history.

The company said it has covered around 95% of the stolen assets, but the remaining amount may take longer to source. Binance has repeatedly said it would cover all of the losses linked to the attack.

"Between 06:00 and 15:30 [GMT] on November 1, we processed $4.649 billion in withdrawals and $1.01 billion in deposits, resulting in a net outflow of approximately $3.64 billion," Binance posted on X.

There was an "initial spike" in withdrawals, which later declined and "are stabilising as expected", it added.

It also said withdrawals for more than two dozen major cryptocurrencies, including Bitcoin and Ethereum, have resumed, and that more services will resume in phases once security checks are complete.

The attack on Binance has been attributed to TraderTraitor, a North Korean cybercrime group also known as the Lazarus Group, which stole a then-record $1.5bn from crypto exchange Bybit in 2025.

The FBI on Saturday published a list of cryptocurrency wallet addresses linked to the group and urged industry partners to help by blocking transactions involving them.

The hack hit Binance's global centralised exchange, Binance.com, while its US-facing platform said it was not affected.

The exchange scrambled to urge cryptocurrency issuers to freeze affected assets.

Binance said last week that early checks suggest the incident may have started with a compromised engineer's laptop, allowing hackers to make unauthorised transactions.

The withdrawn crypto represents only a fraction of the total value of assets Binance holds.

Binance's exact valuation is unclear because the firm is privately held, though the company said in 2024 that it had more than $160bn in assets in its custody.

The firm said last week it has reserved more than $6.34bn to deal with ​the attack's fallout.

Binance said it replaced customers' assets through a combination of channels, including its corporate treasury and its futures insurance and emergency reserve funds.

"Our commitment remains the same: Binance will fully cover the financial impact of the funds stolen in this incident," the firm said.

Cryptocurrencies are digital assets traded on exchanges such as Binance. Unlike cash, they have no physical form and are managed on computers, smartphones, and other digital devices.

Binance was founded in China and has hundreds of millions of registered users globally.

Ghana News.title: Congo Ebola outbreak kills more than 5,000
Ghana News.content:
The death toll from the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic ​Republic of Congo has surpassed 5,000, government ‌data showed on Friday, as authorities had yet to find a way to control the country's deadliest ​Ebola epidemic on record.

No approved treatments or vaccines can combat the rare Bundibugyo species behind the outbreak in the Central African country.

It has ​infected more than 10,000 people since it was declared in May.

Delayed detection, conflict, and strained health services have helped the virus spread faster than ​in previous outbreaks.

Eight of Congo's 26 provinces have ‌been ⁠affected, with many deaths occurring outside treatment centres.

This year's outbreak is the world's second-largest ever, behind only the 2014-2016 one that infected ​over 28,600 ​people and ⁠killed more than 11,000 across Guinea, Liberia and Sierra Leone.

Last week Nigeria ​became the fourth African country to ​report ⁠an Ebola case, extending the outbreak's geographic spread to West Africa. East African countries Kenya and ⁠Uganda ​have also reported cases.

Ghana News.title: Top Swiss court upholds landmark Liberia war crimes ruling
Ghana News.content:
The top Swiss court on Friday confirmed a ​guilty verdict against a Liberian warlord, ‌upholding his 20-year sentence in the country's first-ever war crimes trial.

Alieu Kosiah, who ​fought in the 1990s against ​then-president Charles Taylor's army during Liberia's ⁠brutal civil war, was originally sentenced to ​20 years in prison in June 2021 ​for rape, murder and cannibalism.

An earlier appeal was rejected in 2023 by the Federal Criminal Court ​and the dismissal of his second ​appeal by Switzerland's highest tribunal the Federal Supreme Court ‌published ⁠on Friday closes the case.

"This is a landmark decision, made possible by the courage of these victims, who have ​written a ​page ⁠of legal history," said Alain Werner, Director of Civitas Maxima, ​an NGO representing victims in ​this ⁠case.

However, the court reversed a parallel conviction for crimes against humanity on the grounds that the 2011 law on this crime cannot be applied retroactively.

Ghana News.title: Police forward Ashie Moore case docket to AG for prosecution over alleged theft
Ghana News.content:
Emmanuel Nii Ashie Moore

By Isaac Yeboah

The Ghana Police Service has forwarded the case docket involving Greater Accra Regional Chairman of the ruling National Democratic Congress (NDC), Emmanuel Nii Ashie Moore, to the Attorney-General's Department for prosecution over allegations of stealing from a Singaporean businessman.

The forwarding of the docket, with a covering letter dated October 28, 2026, marks a new development in a case that has been under police investigation since 2025, and in which the Attorney-General's Department had, as far back as March 16, 2026, advised that Mr Ashie Moore be prosecuted.

Ashie Moore, on the other hand, has vehemently denied any wrongdoing, insisting that the allegations constitute a smear campaign against his political acumen.

The latest police action brings the case a step closer to prosecution, following months of investigations and questions over when the Attorney-General's directive would translate into formal prosecutorial action.

The case stems from a complaint by Singaporean businessman Toh You Kang, who accused Mr Ashie Moore of taking his personal belongings, including his passport, luxury luggage, electronic gadgets and US$10,000 in cash, while he was in police custody in June 2025.

The Attorney-General's Department, after reviewing the police investigation docket, advised that Mr Ashie Moore be charged with stealing, contrary to Section 124 of the Criminal Offences Act, 1960 (Act 29).

The advice, issued by Senior State Attorney Nana Ama A. Prempeh, followed an assessment of statements from the complainant, the suspect and police investigators, as well as CCTV footage and a cybercrime analysis report obtained from Fiesta Residences in Cantonments, Accra.

How the case started

According to the investigation docket, Mr You Kang travelled to Ghana in May 2025 following an invitation from Mr Ashie Moore for a proposed business investment.

The complainant told investigators that he had been introduced to the NDC regional chairman through a business associate and arrived at the Kotoka International Airport on May 28, 2025, accompanied by a second suspect, identified as Luibing Liang, a Chinese national.

He alleged that upon arrival, Mr Ashie Moore took custody of his Singaporean passport under the pretext of facilitating VIP clearance procedures.

The complainant was subsequently accommodated at Fiesta Residences in Cantonments before being taken to a property in Adenta, which he said was presented as Mr Ashie Moore's residence.

There, according to his account, he was accused of fraud and asked to pay US$5.5 million. He alleged that Mr Ashie Moore threatened police involvement and detention if he failed to comply.

Mr You Kang was subsequently arrested on May 28, 2025, following a complaint of defrauding by false pretences lodged by Mr Ashie Moore.

A police investigator, Detective Corporal David Agbeve, told investigators that he led a team to arrest the businessman at a residence in Adenta at about 10 p.m. that day.

The complainant was cautioned and charged on May 29 before being arraigned in court on May 30, 2025, and remanded into custody.

Missing belongings and hotel CCTV footage

The alleged stealing at the centre of the prosecution's advice concerns the complainant's personal belongings at Fiesta Residences while he was in police custody.

Mr You Kang told investigators that he encountered difficulties retrieving his medication and luggage from the hotel during his detention.

A police officer, D/Cpl. Agbeve, said he accompanied the complainant to what they initially believed was Fiesta Royale Hotel in Dzorwulu, but they subsequently established that his accommodation was at Fiesta Residences in Cantonments.

The officer said the complainant's lawyer confirmed the correct location and indicated that hotel management had locked him out of his room over alleged indebtedness.

According to the investigator, Mr Ashie Moore later brought medication the complainant had requested to the Accra Central Police Station cells.

When questioned about how he obtained the medication, Mr Ashie Moore reportedly said he had appealed to the hotel management to retrieve it from the complainant's luggage.

The case was subsequently reassigned to another investigator, who indicated that he would follow up with the hotel management to retrieve the complainant's belongings.

Mr You Kang later alleged that while he was in custody, Mr Ashie Moore and others had checked him out of the hotel and removed his personal effects.

The missing items listed in his statement included a Louis Vuitton duffle bag, a Bugatti luggage bag, four mobile phones, an iPad, credit and debit cards, house keys, two luxury vehicle keys, watches, clothing, perfumes, accessories, medication, his Singaporean passport and US$10,000 in cash.

He told investigators that none of the items had been returned to him.

Police investigation and evidence

The matter was referred to the Special Investigations Unit (SIU) of the Criminal Investigations Department (CID) Headquarters following a petition submitted on behalf of the complainant by Cletus Bayor on June 27, 2025.

Chief Inspector Gabriel Ametame, an investigator with the SIU, told the police that the petition alleged that Mr Ashie Moore had collected the complainant's personal belongings from Fiesta Residences after his arrest and remand.

The police subsequently obtained a court order directing the management of Fiesta Residences to produce CCTV footage covering the relevant period.

According to the statement of Detective Chief Inspector Timothy B. Asamoah of the SIU, who received the docket on July 24, 2025, investigators reviewed the footage alongside a cybercrime analysis report.

The analysis provided a chronological account of activities at the hotel, including the arrival of individuals, the movement of luggage and the handling and retrieval of items considered relevant to the investigation.

Following an examination of the footage and other investigative findings, Mr Ashie Moore was charged with stealing on July 28, 2025.

He, however, denied the allegation in his statement to the police, maintaining that he had not taken the complainant's belongings and did not have any of the items in his possession.

Attorney-General's directive

In her legal advice dated March 16, 2026, Senior State Attorney Nana Ama A. Prempeh said a review of the entire docket, including the statements of the complainant, the suspect and investigating officers, the CCTV footage and the accompanying cybercrime analysis report, provided sufficient evidence to support a charge of stealing against Mr Ashie Moore.

The advice noted that the CCTV footage corroborated the removal of the complainant's luggage from the hotel by Mr Ashie Moore and other unidentified persons.

It also identified what it described as unexplained circumstances surrounding the suspect's possession of the complainant's medication and how the passport eventually came to be deposited at the High Court Registry.

The Attorney-General's Department concluded that the circumstances supported an inference that the complainant's belongings had been dishonestly appropriated without lawful justification.

It consequently directed the police to charge Mr Ashie Moore with stealing under Section 124 of Act 29, obtain a charge statement from him and forward it to the Law Office.

The duplicate SIU docket, with reference number R.O. 204/2025, was retained for prosecution.

The police forwarding of the case docket on October 28 is the latest indication that the process is advancing following the Attorney-General's assessment.

Passport deposited at High Court Registry

The whereabouts of the Singaporean businessman's passport also featured in the investigation.

In a further statement, Mr Ashie Moore told the police that he did not have the passport and believed it had been deposited at the Registry of the High Court's Criminal Division in Accra as part of the complainant's bail conditions.

Investigators subsequently contacted the court registry.

An Assistant Registrar confirmed that the passport had been deposited there but said he could not recall the identity of the person who submitted it.

The case docket also identifies a second suspect, Luibing Liang, who was invited by the police to assist with investigations but reportedly failed to honour the invitation.

The police indicated that she remained at large at the time of the investigation.

The Attorney-General's advice specifically recommended prosecution of Mr Ashie Moore for stealing and did not make a similar prosecution recommendation against Ms Liang.

Ghana News.title: Tilly Akua Nipaa appointed Communications Director of RANA
Ghana News.content:
The Rights Accountability Network Africa (RANA) has appointed Ghanaian media personality and public relations professional Matilda Mensah Marfo, popularly known as Tilly Akua Nipaa, as its Communications Director.

The appointment, announced on Sunday, November 1, 2026, is aimed at strengthening the organisation's institutional communications, expanding public engagement and making human rights advocacy more accessible to citizens across Ghana and the African continent.

Tilly Akua Nipaa has built a career in broadcasting, corporate communications, media relations, brand storytelling and stakeholder engagement.

She has worked as a broadcaster and panellist on platforms under Despite Media and the Multimedia Group.

She currently serves as Head of Public Relations and Marketing at Crux Global, where she leads the company's strategic communications and marketing initiatives.

Her professional experience also includes leading the 2025 Artist of the Year campaign for musician King Promise at the Telecel Ghana Music Awards and contributing to projects associated with the Basketball Africa League (BAL).

Tilly holds a degree in Psychology, English and Theatre Arts from the University of Ghana.

She is also preparing to graduate with a Master's degree in Public Relations and Marketing.

In addition to her professional responsibilities, she serves as the 2026 General Secretary of the Graduate Students' Association of Ghana at the University of Media, Arts and Communication (GRASAG-UNIMAC).

In her new position, she will oversee RANA's communications strategy, media relations, digital engagement and public awareness initiatives.

A key part of her mandate will be to translate the organisation's research, legal interventions and advocacy activities into accessible information to improve public understanding of human rights, encourage civic participation and promote institutional accountability.

RANA said effective communication was an essential part of protecting human rights, noting that citizens needed to understand their rights, recognise threats to them and know how to seek appropriate remedies.

The organisation expressed confidence that her experience and strategic communications expertise would strengthen its advocacy and public engagement efforts.

Ghana News.title: Nigeria reports two suspected Ebola cases in northeast region
Ghana News.content:
Health authorities in Nigeria are investigating two suspected Ebola cases in ​the country's northeast region, the Nigeria Centre for Disease ‌Control and Prevention said on Saturday.

Officials said the two individuals have been isolated while they carry out contact identification, listing, and laboratory testing in a post on X.

The cases remain suspected and confirmation ⁠is subject to laboratory results, the post added.

Nigeria ​confirmed its first Ebola case in more than a ​decade last week in a Swiss woman who had travelled to Uganda and then returned to the capital, Abuja, in ​central Nigeria. She and her husband were evacuated to ​Switzerland on Monday.

The two additional cases, if confirmed, could mean ‌that ⁠the disease has spread within Nigeria, which would be a major public health concern. Authorities did not say whether they believed they were linked to the first case.

The centre ⁠of Africa's Ebola outbreak is in the Democratic Republic of Congo, where more than 5,000 ​people have died since it was ​declared ⁠in May. Kenya and Uganda have also reported cases.

No approved treatments or vaccines exist to combat the rare Bundibugyo species behind ​the Congo outbreak.

Ghana News.title: Russia in talks with four African states on large nuclear power plants, Rosatom says
Ghana News.content:
Russia is ready to supply African countries with nuclear power plants of various sizes and configurations and is ​in talks with four countries on large nuclear projects, ‌the head of the state nuclear corporation Rosatom said on Friday.

Rosatom Chief Executive Alexei Likhachev said the company was discussing building large nuclear power plants with Uganda, Ghana, Ethiopia and Egypt.

"Our partnership ​is based on the principle that Africa is diverse, ⁠and we have a tailored approach for each country that ​goes beyond a single project," Likhachev said.

Nuclear cooperation was among the ​topics discussed at the third Russia-Africa Summit in Moscow this week, attended by representatives from about 50 African countries, including heads of state and government.

Director General of Russia's State Atomic Energy Corporation Rosatom Alexei Likhachev

The forum, ​launched in 2019, is part of Russia's efforts to deepen ​its political and economic ties with Africa.

After the summit, Russian President Vladimir ‌Putin ⁠said African countries had shown strong interest in nuclear power plants, small-scale nuclear technologies and nuclear applications in medicine and agriculture.

Likhachev said nine African countries had expressed "significant interest" in Rosatom's floating nuclear ​power plant technology, ​which the ⁠company has promoted as way for coastal countries to enter the nuclear power sector.

He said detailed negotiations are underway with Egypt, Tanzania, Togo and ​Namibia.

Africa ⁠has only one operating nuclear power plant, South Africa's Koeberg facility, which was built using French technology and entered service in the ⁠mid-1980s.

In Egypt, Rosatom is building the country's first nuclear power plant, the four-reactor El Dabaa project, and is discussing a possible expansion to six reactors.

Ghana News.title: Nigerian families and survivors seek justice over miners’ deaths
Ghana News.content:
Families of 37 artisanal miners who died in custody in Nigeria want ‌swift justice and the return of property seized during their arrest, saying no financial compensation will make up for their loss.

A presidential panel on Tuesday found that the detainees, who were suspected of being illegal miners, had died ​from overcrowding, extreme heat, dehydration and neglect while being held by the Nigeria Security ​and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC) in Niger State last month.

Nigeria's government welcomed the panel's findings, and Interior Minister Olubunmi Tunji-Ojo said it had sent the report to the Attorney General for immediate judicial action. He did not respond to requests for comment on when victims' families ​and survivors would receive compensation.

The deaths, including of teenagers, triggered protests in Nigeria, raising new concerns about conditions in detention facilities and the treatment of suspects awaiting trial.

"What we wanted was for our children to be alive and ​return to us," said Zainab Salihu, whose son was among the dead.

She said the deaths in ​detention had led to the deterioration of the health of her husband, who later died. Reuters was unable to ‌verify ⁠the circumstances of her husband's death.

"No matter how much money they give us, it will never bring our children back," Salihu said.

Dantala Tanko, whose 25-year-old son Suleiman died in detention, is struggling to come to terms with his loss.

"Now he is gone, and this is deeply painful for me. ​I know he will ​never return," he said ⁠after praying at his son's grave.

Some survivors said they appreciated the investigation's findings, but wanted accountability.

"Officers who demonstrate such disregard for human life should ​not remain in positions of authority. They must be held accountable, and ​appropriate disciplinary action ⁠should be taken," said 25-year-old Dauda Shehu.

Abdulsalam Yakubu, 23, said government action had been slow. He said he wanted the government to return motorcycles, phones, mining equipment and gold, which he said had ⁠been ​seized during the victims' arrest.

"We have suffered enough. We are ​asking for justice, the promised support, and the return of our property so that we can begin to rebuild our ​lives," he told Reuters.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.title: Russian authorities detain suspect over St. Petersburg cafe blast
World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”

World.title: Ukraine blames Russia after air alert app sends out false warnings
World.content:
Russian Emergencies Ministry also says its mobile app suffered a ‘massive cyberattack’, leading to ‘false information’.

Share Ukraine blames Russia after air alert app sends out false warnings on social media

Ukraine’s Air Force has said its air raid alert app sent erroneous messages after allegedly being hacked by Russia.

Fake alerts warning of nuclear and chemical threats to areas in and around Kyiv were sent on Sunday, along with warnings of potential street combat. An erroneous message also said Russia’s hypersonic Oreshnik missile had been deployed.

“The air alert app appears to have been subjected to enemy influence,” the Ukrainian Air Force said on Telegram on Sunday. “There is no radiation threat! Stay calm and follow our updates on our channel.”

SPRAVDI, Ukraine’s Centre for Strategic Communications, blamed Russia for the hack in a post on X.

The raid alert app is used across Ukraine to warn people in real time of incoming Russian air attacks. A separate app, specifically for the Ukrainian capital, was working normally, according to Kyiv authorities.

Hours later, early on Monday morning, Russia’s Emergencies Ministry said its mobile app had been hit by a “massive cyberattack”.

The ministry said on Telegram that the attack led to the spread of “false information”.

Russia’s and Ukraine’s announcements follow the end of a truce between the two countries in Kherson.

The localised ceasefire, which began on Tuesday and ended on Sunday, was the longest of the war so far.

World.title: Tens of thousands build 108 Buddhist stupas for Bhutan ‘mindfulness’ city
World.content:
Bhutan is creating a ‘mindfulness’ city aimed at driving economic growth and persuading more young people to stay.

Share Tens of thousands build 108 Buddhist stupas for Bhutan ‘mindfulness’ city on social media

Tens of thousands of volunteers have taken part in building 108 Buddhist stupas in Bhutan’s new “mindfulness” city, as the Himalayan kingdom embarks on an ambitious project to boost economic growth.

The 15-metre-tall (50ft) stupas, sacred Buddhist monuments found across the Himalayas, were installed on Sunday along 12km (7.5 miles) of riverbank near the Indian border, at the site of the future Gelephu Mindfulness City.

More than 40,000 volunteers participated in building the structures as “a physical form of prayer made permanent in stone and earth”, after starting work after midnight, officials said. The number 108 is sacred in Buddhism, widely practised in Bhutan.

About 200,000 people attended the ceremony, or nearly a fourth of the population, officials told the AFP news agency.

“I was worried that raising 108 stupas in a single day might not succeed,” Bhutan’s King Jigme Khesar Namgyel Wangchuck said in a speech at the ceremony.

“But everything went successfully, and for that, I am truly grateful.”

Bhutanese leaders hope that Gelephu Mindfulness City, conceived by the king and designed by Danish architects, will boost the country’s economy and persuade more young people to stay, attracting investment in sustainable business, green technology, education, tourism and financial services.

Bhutan is facing massive economic challenges, from rising unemployment and falling birth rates to the mass migration of skilled workers.

The city, currently a small town with a population of about 10,000, is in southern Bhutan, along the border with India, about 240km (150 miles) south of Thimphu, the nation’s capital.



The king established the special zone by royal charter in 2024, saying its purpose was to “create a vibrant economic hub”.

The landlocked Himalayan nation, with a population of just under 800,000 and wedged between China and India, is known for its policy of prioritising “Gross National Happiness” alongside economic growth.

“This occasion will be recorded in our history for generations to come,” said Nima Gyeltshen, 65, head of the Organisation for Youth Empowerment, which helps young Bhutanese find work.

Cryptocurrency ambitions

Analysts have questioned whether Bhutan can attract sufficient investment to realise its vision for the new city.

But Indian billionaire Gautam Adani, head of the ports-to-power conglomerate, joined the project as a founding member in January.

The site is set to be connected to India’s rail network in neighbouring Assam, with an international airport slated to open in 2029.

The project is also linked to Bhutan’s cryptocurrency ambitions, with the kingdom mining Bitcoin using surplus hydropower and pledging to use digital assets to support the city’s development.

Bishnu Maya Moktang, a resident who attended Sunday’s ceremony, said she was excited about the upcoming mindfulness city.

“I hope to live long enough to see it,” Moktang, 56, told AFP.

“My parents died young, and they would never see the city. I feel fortunate.”

World.title: Nine die in ‘cataclysmic’ Florida business jet crash
World.content:
Florida Governor Ron DeSantis tells reporters there appeared to be no casualties on the ground.

Nine people have died after a business jet crashed into a residential neighbourhood in South Florida, the United States.

All on board were killed in the crash, which US Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy described as a “horrific tragedy” in a post on X on Sunday.

Federal Aviation Administration staff were on their way to the crash site to support a National Transportation Safety Board investigation into the incident, Duffy said.

Disturbing recordings in the plane’s cockpit shortly before the crash, retained by LiveATC.net, captured the pilot talking about “manageable” ice issues, before later saying the plane was rapidly losing altitude.

Shortly after, the panicked crew said, “We’re going to crash into the ground”.

The plane was a Learjet 60 – a popular business jet – heading from Austin, Texas, to the Bahamas. Austin-Bergstrom International airport confirmed that the plane was a private jet, but not who was on board.

Videos of the incident circulating online appear to show the jet striking the ground at high speed and on a sharp angle, followed by a huge explosion.

Footage of the aftermath appears to show flames flickering around debris and chunks of pavement, with people milling around the area.

The plane looked to have fallen just metres from homes and cars, but Florida Governor Ron DeSantis told reporters that there appeared to be no casualties on the ground.

Speaking from the scene, DeSantis described the crash as “cataclysmic” and said the plane “looked like a missile going down, and left a big crater on the side of the road”.

World.title: Israeli officials say results stand as Netanyahu claims election ‘stolen’
World.content:
Election body says deadlocked result won’t be undermined even if foreign interference claims are found to be true.

The head of Israel’s elections commission has said the results of the country’s general election would still stand even if claims of foreign interference were substantiated.

“Our position is that even if the suspicions are substantiated, this would not undermine the integrity of the electoral process or the election results as a whole,” Central Elections Committee head Noam Sohlberg said in a video on Sunday, in which he appeared with the head of the Shin Bet, Israel’s internal security agency, and the attorney general.

Prime Minister Benyamin Netanyahu’s Likud party had questioned the results after saying, without providing evidence, that Arab-led parties, which made significant gains in Tuesday’s elections, “stole” the vote and accepted funding from Qatar to do it.

Qatar has rejected the allegations, calling it a disinformation campaign.

Also on Sunday, Israeli police released two out of three political activists arrested before Tuesday’s polls opened. They were carrying envelopes of cash, allegedly to bribe voters, police said.

One was released on unspecified conditions, while another was ordered to remain on house arrest.

Police said the suspects were connected to the Arab-led Ra’am party, which won eight seats.

Its leader, Mansour Abbas, denounced the arrests as undemocratic and “an attempt to influence the election results”.

‘Orchestrated and organised campaign’

Main opposition leader Eisenkot on Sunday accused Netanyahu of launching an “orchestrated and organised campaign to delegitimise the results”.



Eisenkot has previously ruled out forming a coalition with Arab parties, but a deadlock in Tuesday’s elections means siding with the parties could help him form a government.

Netanyahu’s bloc won 53 seats in Tuesday’s elections, while the opposition bloc, led by Gadi Eisenkot, won 48, meaning neither side can form a government in Israel’s 120-seat parliament alone.

Israel’s three Arab-led parties, including the Ra’am party, won a record 19 seats.

A coalition of Arab parties with Eisenkot would provide a comfortable majority of 67 in parliament. However, for many in Israel, the idea of siding with Arab parties is politically unpalatable.

The results are due to be officially certified this week, after which President Isaac Herzog must nominate a candidate to form a new government.
