“There is room for the pioneer and room for the newcomer; room for the elder and room for the youth; room for those who laid the foundation and room for those who will raise the roof.

“Nobody needs to demolish another person’s mansion to find accommodation, and nobody needs to extinguish another person’s candle for his own light to shine. We may have arrived through different doors, but we must learn to live under one roof,” he added.

Akpabio further urged political leaders and party members to ensure that their political ambitions did not override the welfare and aspirations of the people.

He said political activities should reflect the moral values of the faith professed by the people, stressing that electoral campaigns must respect human dignity and promote peaceful coexistence.

“Therefore, our politics must reflect our faith, our campaigns must honour human dignity, and our ambitions must never become greater than the welfare of our people,” he stated.

The Senate President also described Akwa Ibom as a developing success story, attributing the state’s progress to purposeful leadership, peace and sustained development.

According to him, the state’s achievements should not be measured solely by physical infrastructure but also by its ability to strengthen relationships among its people and restore public confidence in governance.

He said, “Akwa Ibom has become a Nigerian wonder story, a testimony to the possibilities of purposeful leadership, peace and development.

“Our state is demonstrating that progress is not merely about the roads we construct or the buildings we erect, but also about the bridges we build between people and the hope we restore in human hearts.

“We must preserve this progress and ensure that the chapters yet to be written are greater than those already written,” he said.

He also linked the state’s development to the broader national interest, insisting that Akwa Ibom could not achieve sustainable prosperity in isolation from the challenges confronting other parts of the country.

Akpabio said, “Akwa Ibom’s greatness is inseparable from Nigeria’s greatness. We cannot desire peace in Uyo and be indifferent to insecurity elsewhere in our federation, nor celebrate prosperity in our communities while ignoring hardship in other parts of our country.

“Nigeria is not merely the nation to which Akwa Ibom belongs; it is the larger destiny to which Akwa Ibom contributes,” he said.

He urged political stakeholders to demonstrate national solidarity through their actions and strengthen the foundations of democracy.

Earlier, Governor Umo Eno thanked the people of Akwa Ibom for their support during the last election and appealed for even greater backing for Tinubu, Akpabio, himself and other APC candidates in the 2027 general election.

The governor also reaffirmed his commitment to serving the people with the fear of God, expressing the hope that they would give him another mandate to continue his administration’s development agenda.

He urged residents to sustain their support for the APC, describing the forthcoming election as an opportunity to consolidate the party’s political fortunes and development efforts in the state.

World.title: Atiku Accuses APC Presidential Campaign of Obscuring President’s Unfulfilled Promises
World.content:
· ADC council says ruling party’s sustained assault on democracy will fail

Chuks Okocha in Abuja

President candidate of African Democratic Congress (ADC) and former Vice President, Atiku Abubakar, has accused the All Progressives Congress Presidential Campaign Council of seeking to obscure President Bola Tinubu’s unfulfilled electricity promise with a long recital of laws, committees, bonds, and projects.

Atiku made the accusation in a statement by Director of Strategic Communication, ADC Presidential Campaign Council (ADC-PCC), Phrank Shaibu.

Separately, ADC-PCC condemned what it called sustained, coordinated, and state-sponsored assault on democracy, freedom of association, and the constitutional right of Nigerians to political participation under the Tinubu administration. It, however, declared that the assaults would fail and democracy was bound to survive and outlive APC.

Atiku said, in the statement by ADC-PCC, “The APC should spare Nigerians the spectacle of celebrating paperwork while homes and businesses remain in darkness.

“After three and a half years, families still struggle to keep their homes lit. Traders and small business owners spend scarce resources on alternative power, yet struggle to keep their businesses alive.”

ADC campaign council said, “Nigerians are billed for electricity they cannot rely on. President Tinubu promised steady power and an end to estimated billing. That promise has not been kept.

“Across Nigeria, consumers are placed in Bands A, B, C, D and E and charged different rates. In many areas, Band A customers pay about N209.50 per unit before VAT. Rates for the other bands vary by state and electricity provider.

”Yet across every band, the same hardship endures: the power fails, but the bill arrives. No family should have to weigh the cost of electricity against the cost of food. No business should be left to pay more while receiving less.”

ADC added, “The government now says it plans to end electricity subsidies from 2027, even as it insists there will be no immediate tariff increase. Nigerians are entitled to a clear answer: what will happen to their bills when the subsidy ends?”

The ADC presidential candidate promised that if elected, “I will work with state governments and regulators, within the law, to abolish the present band system and replace it with a fair, transparent and affordable framework that protects households and holds power companies accountable for the electricity they deliver.

“Steady power that Nigerians can afford will be a national priority.”

Insisting that Tinubu had no justification for seeking another term, the ADC campaign council stated, “When President Tinubu campaigned in 2022, he made an unmistakable commitment. He said: ‘If I don’t give you constant electricity for four years, when I come back for a second term, don’t vote for me.’

“Nigerians have lived through those four years. They do not need his campaign council to interpret his words for them. They need him to answer for them.

“His administration has not built a single new generation infrastructure of its own to increase Nigeria’s power capacity. Yet it has floated a multitrillion naira bond programme to settle legacy debts owed to generation companies, without showing Nigerians how this financial intervention has produced the steady electricity they were promised.

”Paying old debts is not the same as building new power infrastructure. Bonds cannot be presented as a substitute for power in people’s homes.”

ADC also accused the Tinubu government of worsening the power woes with unjustifiable energy taxes.

It stated, “Meanwhile, Nigerians face VAT on electricity, and the Nigeria Tax Act provides for a five per cent surcharge on certain fossil fuels, including petrol and diesel.

“The government says the surcharge has not been activated and would require a ministerial order. At a time when families already struggle to meet the cost of energy, Nigerians deserve to know why another potential charge has been placed before them.

“Dele Alake’s statement cannot light a home. Signing a law is not electricity. Raising a bond is not electricity. Approving a project is not power delivered. Nigerians cannot cook, study, work or sustain a business on announcements.

”President Tinubu invited Nigerians to judge him by his performance. They have done so. What they seek is simple: reliable electricity they can afford, and a government that keeps its word.”

APC’s Sustained Assault On Democracy Will Fail, Says ADC Presidential Campaign

ADC-PCC condemned what it described as organised assault on democracy and freedom of association and political participation under the administration of Tinubu, declaring that the assaults will fail, as democracy will outlive APC.

The council said the unfolding incidents across the country went beyond ordinary political rivalry. It alleged that the incidents represented a disturbing pattern of intimidation, harassment, and suppression of opposition voices.

The council said the Tinubu government had engaged in calculated atrocious actions skewed to scare Nigerians ahead of the general election.

In a statement signed by its Director of Media and Publicity, Kola Ologbondiyan, ADC-PCC recalled a series of incidents, including attacks on its leaders and members in Kaduna, the reported assault on its Sokoto State governorship candidate, Alhaji Munir Dan Iya, by operatives of the Sokoto Marshals along Airport Road, Sokoto, and alleged attacks on other opposition figures.

It also cited the reported demolition of its governorship campaign office in Kebbi State and the alleged denial of a campaign venue in Enugu State to Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) presidential candidate, Mr Peter Obi.

The council further referenced the reported attacks on the presidential candidate of African Action Congress (AAC), Omoyele Sowore, and other opposition voices, describing the incidents as part of an emerging pattern of political intolerance.

According to ADC-PCC, the attacks, denial of campaign venues, arrests, harassment, and intimidation of opposition figures raised serious concerns about the state of democratic freedoms and political pluralism in Nigeria.

The council maintained that no government, regardless of its political or institutional strength, could successfully suppress the democratic aspirations of Nigerians, recalling that popular resistance contributed to the collapse of former President Olusegun Obasanjo’s third-term agenda.

It also stated that Tinubu and APC enjoyed the benefits of political participation and opposition politics when they were outside government, insisting that those same democratic freedoms must be guaranteed to all political parties and their members.

Sharing Atiku’s thoughts, ADC-PCC also described as an afterthought the attempt by Alake and APC-PCC to rewrite Tinubu’s categorical 2023 electricity pledge through selective quotations and elaborate explanations.

Reacting to comments by Alake, Ologbondiyan maintained that Tinubu was unequivocal when he told Nigerians not to vote for him for a second term if he failed to deliver electricity during his first tenure.

According to ADC-PCC, Nigerians have not forgotten the president’s words. His commitment was clear and unambiguous: “Don’t vote for me for second term if I fail to deliver electricity.”

The council said no amount of selective editing, additional paragraphs, or grammatical gymnastics could erase that commitment from the consciousness of Nigerians.

It said rather than end estimated billing, the Tinubu administration had presided over increased electricity bills, leaving many households struggling to afford power supply.

ADC-PCC further observed that businesses, including hospitality facilities, had been forced to ration electricity by switching off power for guests during daytime hours to contain operating costs.

It also criticised the introduction of discriminatory tariff classifications under Bands A, B, C and others, stating that consumers continue to pay more without receiving reliable electricity supply.

World.title: Tinubu to Nigerian Delegation to Makkah: Our Diversity, A Recipe for Prosperity
World.content:
Deji Elumoye in Abuja

President Bola Ahmed Tinubu prayed Almighty Allah to transform Nigeria’s rich diversity into a source of prosperity, unity, peace and sustainable development for the benefit of all Nigerians.

Tinubu offered the prayer on Sunday in the holy city of Makkah, Saudi Arabia, while hosting members of his delegation for dinner.

The president expressed the hope that Nigeria’s ethnic, religious, and cultural diversity would continue to serve as a source of strength and national advancement rather than division. He stressed the need for citizens to embrace mutual understanding, peaceful coexistence, and a shared commitment to the country’s progress.

He prayed that Almighty Allah would bless Nigeria with enduring peace, harmony, and prosperity, and grant the nation’s leaders the wisdom, courage, and foresight to steer the country towards greater development and improved living conditions for its people.

“May Almighty Allah bless Nigeria, convert our diversity into prosperity as a country,” the president said.

Tinubu also prayed for divine guidance and protection for Nigerians at home and abroad, asking Allah to strengthen the bonds of brotherhood among citizens and inspire a renewed spirit of patriotism, compassion and service to the nation.

The president stated that Nigeria’s abundant human and natural resources, coupled with the talents, creativity and enterprise of its diverse population, provided a strong foundation for building a prosperous and inclusive nation.

The dinner with members of his delegation in Makkah provided an opportunity for fellowship and reflection on Nigerians’ shared aspirations for a peaceful, united and prosperous country.

Tinubu urged Nigerians of all faiths and backgrounds to keep working together in the national interest, expressing confidence that, with faith in Almighty Allah, unity of purpose, and collective determination, Nigeria would overcome its challenges and realise its full potential.

Chairman of BUA, Alhaji Abdulsamad Rabiu, reaffirmed Tinubu’s commitment to peace, unity and prosperity of Nigeria.

Rabiu said, “Today is actually the third dinner we’re having with His Excellency, Mr President, since we came to Makkah on Thursday night or Friday morning when Mr President arrived.

“So, we discussed, and the discussion was, you know, to always continue to pray for Nigeria, for peace, for unity and for Nigeria’s prosperity. To again, you know, thank His Excellency for his passion, for what he’s doing for Nigeria.

“And also for us, it’s quite important because, as I said, it has given us the opportunity to come and pray not only for ourselves and our families, but also for Nigeria.

“We will continue to support His Excellency in whatever capacity we can and, definitely, as you all know, Mr President is very passionate about the country. He’s working very hard, and we’ll continue to support him.”

Kwara State Governor and Chairman of Nigerian Governors’ Forum (NGF), Abdulrahman AbdulRazaq, said the forum was overwhelmed by the president’s passion and commitment to achieving a united and prosperous nation.

AbdulRazaq stated, “Only Allah can reward you; we will continue to pray for you daily and pray for Nigeria that you lead. May Allah continue to strengthen you in making the right decisions, strengthen your wisdom, your boldness, your audacity, your courage. May Allah lead you to the right path.”

Attorney-General of the Federation and Minister of Justice, Mr Lateef Fagbemi (SAN), also prayed for Almighty Allah to continue to strengthen the president in his determination to deliver governance and justice to all Nigerians, irrespective of their religion or ethnic backgrounds.

The dinner was attended by Yobe State Governor Mai Mala Buni; Kaduna State Governor Uba Sani; Jigawa State Governor Mohammed Namadi; Sokoto State Governor Ahmed Aliyu; Borno State Governor Babagana Umara Zulum; Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Professor Mohammed Ali Pate; and National Security Adviser, Mallam Nuhu Ribadu.

Others were Chief Executive Officer of Oando Plc, Mr Wale Tinubu; Special Adviser to the President on Political Matters, Ibrahim Kabiru Masari; and Chief of Staff to the President, Femi Gbajabiamila, among others.

World.title: N70,000 Transport Allowance: Public Service Unions Back NLC as Labour Rift Deepens
World.content:
Onyebuchi Ezigbo in Abuja

The disagreement between the two Labour centres over federal government’s approved N70,000 transportation allowance seemed to be deepening as Joint National Public Service Negotiating Council (JNPSNC) has backed Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC) against Trade Union Congress (TUC) which rejected allowance.

National Secretary of JNPSNC, Comrade Gbenga Olowoyo, said in circular to affiliate unions and state councils that agreement leading to approval was product of constructive engagement and exhaustive negotiation.

He said the meeting was presided over by the Minister of Labour and Employment, Alhaji Mohamed Maigari Dingyadi, and attended by labour team led by NLC President Comrade Joe Ajaero with the participation of leadership of JNPSNC and Joint Health Sector Union (JOHESU).

According to the circular, the meeting was tough and lasted more than six hours before both sides reached terms.

Olowoyo said the N70,000 transportation allowance to be paid for next six months to public servants starting November 2026 is meant to subsidize unbearable transportation cost being experienced by workers.

He expressed hope the state and local governments with humongous allocations will be patriotic enough to concur with the agreement to complement the federal government effort to ameliorate hardship of workers and dependants.

He said agreement also cemented implementation of long overdue 40 per cent peculiar allowance reflecting N70,000 minimum wage, which ought to have started since July 2024 when new minimum wage commenced.

Allowance will be domesticated at sub-national levels from November 2026 while arrears from May 1, 2026 will be paid in three tranches.

Olowoyo noted the federal government agreed to set up tripartite negotiation committee comprising government, labour and NECA representatives with immediate effect, which formed focal request from JNPSNC under Comrade Benjamin Anto Uyanto that necessitated three-day warning strike called on October 2, 2026.

He disabused the notion that NLC is union of junior workers, saying all unions affiliated to NLC have members across Ministries, Departments and Agencies up to Directorate level.

He said clarification became necessary because of position taken by TUC which rejected allowance though it was never part of discussion.

“TUC has explicit right to express opinion on any matter it is directly involved but not on what it was not part of at any stage of engagement or negotiation with the federal government,” he said.

He however said it would be commendable if TUC can secure higher amount above N70,000 already agreed by NLC, JNPSNC and JOHESU.

The circular added that the meeting also resolved other long-standing issues including CONHESS adjustment demand for past 13 years, with National Salaries, Incomes and Wages Commission (NSIWC) given three weeks to finish work and forward to Presidential Committee on Salaries headed by the Minister of Finance for approval.

It approved payment of 19-month arrears of health workers allowances in three installments from December 2026, and resolved issuance of circular for hazard allowance to agricultural professional officers within three weeks.

On tax relief, it was agreed the matter will be presented to National Economic Council as it involves the federal and state governments.

The meeting gave window of one month to reconvene to evaluate implementation level.

Olowoyo said rejection of any item by any trade union is inconsequential to implementation because wider spectrum of workers has applauded decision as right step in right direction.

World.title: NERC: Discos Collected N220.93bn Revenue in August, Billing Efficiency Rose to 75.36%
World.content:
Abuja, Eko lead collection efficiency as Kaduna, Jos struggle



Discos recover 77.63% of allowed revenue per kilowatt-hour



Emmanuel Addeh in Abuja



Nigeria’s electricity Distribution Companies (Discos) collected N220.93 billion from customers in August 2026, representing a 7.49 per cent increase over the previous month, as their revenue collection efficiency rose to 84.62 per cent, according to the Nigerian Electricity Regulatory Commission (NERC).



The commission’s August 2026 factsheet on the commercial performance of the 11 Discos showed that total billings stood at N261.10 billion, leaving N40.17 billion uncollected during the month.

The collection performance, which improved by 2.66 percentage points from July, indicated that the distribution companies collected about 84.62 per cent of the amount billed to customers.

However, the figures also showed significant differences in the ability of the individual Discos to collect revenue, with Abuja, Eko and Ikeja recording relatively strong performances, while Kaduna, Jos and Kano continued to struggle.

Abuja Electricity Distribution Company (AEDC) recorded the highest collection efficiency at 91.91 per cent, collecting N37.57 billion out of N40.88 billion billed to customers. Its performance improved by 10.89 percentage points compared with July.

Despite their strong performances, Eko and Ikeja recorded declines of 5.42 and 9.67 percentage points, respectively, in collection efficiency compared with July.

At the other end of the table, Kaduna Electric recorded the weakest collection performance, collecting N5.57 billion from N10.05 billion billed, representing an efficiency rate of 55.44 per cent.

Jos Disco collected N6.42 billion from N10.35 billion billed, translating to 61.98 per cent, while Kano Electric recorded a collection efficiency of 60.31 per cent after collecting N9.07 billion from N15.04 billion billed.

The figures highlighted the persistent disparity in the commercial performance of the distribution companies, with some collecting nearly all the revenue billed to customers while others recorded substantially lower rates.

On energy billing, the 11 Discos received a total of 346.49 billion naira worth of electricity during the month but billed customers for N261.10 billion, translating to a billing efficiency of 75.36 per cent.

The billing efficiency improved by 0.26 percentage points from July, but the gap between the value of energy received and the amount billed stood at N85.39 billion.

Abuja Disco received energy valued at N54.93 billion but billed customers N40.88 billion, while Ikeja received N54.99 billion and billed N40.45 billion.

Eko recorded the highest billing efficiency at 84.49 per cent, followed by Kano at 82.24 per cent and Port Harcourt at 80.22 per cent. Kaduna recorded the lowest at 60.92 per cent, followed by Yola at 64.04 per cent and Jos at 66.47 per cent.

The NERC data also showed that the distribution companies recovered an average of N101.03 per kilowatt-hour against an allowed average tariff of N130.15 per kilowatt-hour, representing a revenue recovery efficiency of 77.63 per cent.

Although the recovery efficiency improved by 2.71 percentage points from July, the actual average collection remained N29.12 per kilowatt-hour below the allowed average tariff.

Eko Disco recorded the highest recovery efficiency at 96.29 per cent, with an average collection of N135.58 per kilowatt-hour against an allowed tariff of N140.80. Ikeja followed at 84.22 per cent, while Abuja recorded 83.63 per cent.

Kaduna had the lowest recovery efficiency at 41.90 per cent, collecting an average of N51.03 per kilowatt-hour against an allowed tariff of N121.80. Jos followed at 52.80 per cent, while Kano recorded 60.98 per cent.

Enugu and Ibadan also recorded recovery efficiencies below 72 per cent, at 71.49 and 71.22 per cent, respectively.

World.title: Keyamo Unveils Tinubu Aviation Campaign Series Ahead of 2027 Polls
World.content:
30-second television series to broadcast president’s Tinubu administration’s record in aviation

James Emejo in Abuja

Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Mr. Festus Keyamo, has launched a television campaign series to promote President Bola Tinubu’s aviation sector record ahead of the 2027 presidential election.

The move signals an early push to use the administration’s sectoral performance in its re-election campaign.

The 30-second programme, tagged Tinubu Aviation Revolution Series, is scheduled to begin airing on major television stations on November 1, with broadcasts expected to continue until a few days before the presidential election.

The initiative follows Keyamo’s appointment as Director of the Directorate of Air Transport Mobilisation under the All Progressives Congress Presidential Campaign Council (APC PCC), where he is responsible for coordinating air transportation for authorised campaign activities.

A statement issued by the minister’s Special Adviser on Media and Communications, Tunde Moshood, said had mobilised his team to produce the campaign material following his appointment.

The statement added that the television campaign had been fully paid for, although it did not disclose the cost of production or broadcast placement.

The series is designed to present the Tinubu administration’s aviation policies and achievements in a short, accessible format, using the sector’s contribution to economic activity as part of the case for the president’s re-election.

Aviation plays a strategic role in trade, tourism, investment and international connectivity, making developments in the sector a potential component of the administration’s broader economic performance narrative.

The campaign will seek to draw public attention to what the government considers its progress in aviation and link the sector’s development to Tinubu’s Renewed Hope Agenda.

The rollout also marks an early campaign communication initiative by Keyamo in his new role within the APC’s presidential campaign structure, ahead of the 2027 general election.

The television campaign is expected to run until shortly before the presidential poll, placing the administration’s aviation record before voters as political activities gather momentum.

The statement adds, “With aviation serving as a critical driver of economic growth, tourism, trade, investment and international connectivity, the series is intended to draw attention to the sector’s role in advancing the Renewed Hope Agenda and to encourage an informed public assessment of the administration’s performance.

“The launch of the Tinubu Aviation Revolution Series signals the beginning of a focused campaign as the APC prepares for the 2027 general election.”

World.title: Anneline Kriel on Donovan Marx farm attack: ‘Nothing has changed’
World.content:
Former Miss South Africa and Miss World Anneline Kriel has reacted to the news of North West farmer Donovan Marx’s attack, labelling it “cruel suffering”

The beauty queen has been vocal in showing support for farm murders and invasions, including the recent White Cross project display in Washington.

ANNELINE KRIEL REACTS TO DONOVAN MARX FARM ATTACK

On her Facebook page, Anneline Kriel reacted to the attack on North West farmer Donovan Marx.



She shared: “My heart breaks for Donovan Marx and his loved ones. No human should ever have to go through such cruel suffering. I pray with all my heart for Donovan and that God will give his family strength during this heartbreaking time.

“How much more suffering must our farming communities endure? Every life is precious, and no family should have to live in fear. May God protect our farmers and their families”.

Anneline – who won Miss South Africa and Miss World in 1973 – added that “nothing has changed” since her public protest to farm attacks in 2017.



The blonde former beauty queen also reposted a screenshot of a tweet by MK Party MP Andile Mngxitama – whom she has previously clashed with over farm attacks – which claimed Donovan Marx’s attack was “symbolic to denote the refusal of land thieves to listen”.

FARM ATTACK VICTIM TO ADVOCATE

In 2017, Anneline Kriel spoke about being a victim of a farm attack. She claimed that a young woman, who had befriended her stepdaughter, had been murdered on a farm in Stellenbosch.

“I will continue to fight this injustice”, Anneline posted on her platform last year.



Last month, Anneline Kriel shared her support for Erns Roets’s White Cross Project, which was erected in front of the Washington Monument.

“The planting of 3,000 crosses at the Washington Monument is a powerful gesture of remembrance, honouring those who have lost their lives and bringing attention to a cause that deserves to be heard.

She continued: “Thank you for standing up, raising awareness and ensuring that these lives are not forgotten. Every life matters. Every victim deserves to be remembered”.

World.title: ‘Loved-up’ Sacha and Sarah Langa make first couple appearance [video]

Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu and Sarah Langa spotted together. Images via TikTok

SACHA AND SARAH LANGA MAKE GLAM COUPLE APPEARANCE

World.title: Sushi and champers: Sithelo gives birth to baby girl in style
World.content:
Sithelo Shozi has given birth to her fourth child – her third daughter – with her husband, Zim businessman Kudzaishe James Magura.

The DJ and media personality gave the public a look into her delivery room, filled with sushi, champagne and elaborate flower arrangements.

Sithelo has three other children; two daughters, Florence and Coco, with ex, Andile Mpisane, and a firstborn son, Makhosini Maseko, whose father is businessman Phillip Maseko.



SITHELO SHOZI’S LUXURY LABOUR

On her social media platforms, Sithelo Shozi shared a look at the aftermath of the birth of her fourth child.

The 32-year-old had her own private room, adorned with pink balloons and elaborate floral arrangements.

She shared: “Birth plan: A sushi boat and blanc de blanc (champagne) immediately after.



The mother-of-four added that her husband had spoiled her with a luxury push present – a Hermès Birkin!

To top it all, Sithelo’s husband, Kudzaishe James Magura, doted on her hand and foot!

Take a look…



‘DEADBEAT DAD’ EX

Last month, Sithelo Shozi’s ex, Andile Mpisane, clapped back at her comments that he was a “deadbeat dad” to her two daughters, Flo and Coco.

Andile clapped back: “My responsibilities and commitment as a father should not be judged on the basis of speculation, assumptions or one-sided narratives. I have continued to contribute towards my children’s education, including paying their school fees, and I remain committed to their well-being and future.

Andile claimed that his access to his children had been “limited” and that he had recently “reconnected” with them.

World.title: Leon Schuster on Eugène Terre’Blanche prank: ‘I nearly died’ [video]
World.content:
Leon Schuster has claimed his candid camera prank with members of the Afrikaner Weerstandsbeweging (AWB) – whose leader was Eugène Terre’Blanche – was one of his most frightening experiences yet.

The veteran TV actor and comedian reflected on his most memorable movies in an interview with SABC’s Leanne Manas.

The 75-year-old also shared a health update and divulged some of his biggest regrets.



LEON SCHUSTER ON MOST FRIGHTENING TV PRANK

Although he pranked Eugène Terre’Blanche directly, Leon Schuster recalls setting up an elaborate prank in Ventersdorp, the home of the AWB leader.

Schuster told Leanne Manas about his early 90s fake tollgate prank, which fooled and angered many members of the AWB community.

Disguised as a black security guard, Schuster demanded that drivers pay a R50 toll for “reconciliation and development”.

He recalled: “Those okes are far, far right. They drive in their bakkies with their guns on the seat next to them; they will fire! They got so pissed off. I nearly died that day”.

The now 75-year-old said that he was threatened with an AK47, and even assaulted by a few.

The clip made it into his 1997 candid camera, Panic Mechanic.



Take a look…

BRINGING SOUTH AFRICANS TOGETHER

During his interview with Leanne Manas, Leon Schuster added that he had no ill intent behind his candid camera pranks, some of which have courted controversy for its portrayal of “blackface”.

He shared: “I’m a prankster, and I’ll die a prankster. It’s all part of the culture of this land”

“It’s important you know your audience. I try to give the people what they want. I’m so sorry I can’t make one final candid-camera movie. But one more clap and my neck will break”.

He added: “I want to be remembered as that okie from the Free State who stood firmly on the ground, who didnt a swollen head, and who contributed somehow to unify our nation through my movies”.

World.title: Siya Kolisi’s got the sauce! Springbok captain extends business empire
World.content:
Siya Kolisi’s officially got the sauce – after collaborating with Nando’s to create a new condiment. The news comes days after reports that the Springbok captain joined restaurant group Life & Brand Portfolio as a stakeholder.

SIYA KOLISI UNVEILS NANDO’S SAUCE

On social media, several content creators have teased the release of Siya’s Sauce, in collaboration with Nando’s

The sauce – which will reflect the flavours of the Springbok captain – will officially be rolled out in stores on Tuesday, 3 November.



The launch coincided with the opening of the new Nando’s restaurant in Stellenbosch.

EXTENDING HIS BUSINESS INTERESTS

Last month, Siya Kolisi announced that he had acquired a 5% stake in South African restaurant group Life & Brand Portfolio, which owns brands including Tiger’s Milk, La Parada, Harbour House and Old Town Italy.



The Springbok captain is expected to contribute to marketing, business development and the conceptualisation of new restaurant offerings, bringing his ideas and South African cultural influences into the group’s brands.

Siya has also expressed an interest in creating experiences that bring people together through food, sport, music and community events, while using the partnership to support youth and community development.

In a statement, the 35-year-old said of his new role: “It’s a big honour for me. I think I’m at the stage of my life where I’m closer to the end of my career. And it’s daunting to think about what you’re going to do after



He added: “I think the idea is how we can bring more people together. Doing sports, making it more fun, having competitions and all kinds of things. I think we want to bring people together to talk”.

World.title: Da Cruz has a plan for Kaizer Chiefs’ biggest problem
World.content:
Kaizer Chiefs have fallen 12 points behind Mamelodi Sundowns after another inconsistent spell in the league.

A series of draws has proved particularly costly, leaving Amakhosi struggling to keep pace with their title rivals.

FERNANDO DA CRUZ: KAIZER CHIEFS NEED WINNING RUN TO REVIVE TITLE CHALLENGE

Da Cruz admits that the situation has become more complicated following their latest setback. However, the French tactician believes the return of injured players could give his team the consistency they have lacked throughout the campaign.



“It’s more difficult today [Saturday] after this game, but the PSL is a long journey, there are 21 fixtures remaining. When we recover our injured players, where we have been unlucky since the beginning of the season, we will have more consistency in our performances, because we made a lot of draws this season,” Da Cruz said.

The Amakhosi coach believes his team have dropped points in matches where they were capable of collecting maximum points.

However, he also acknowledged that a lack of experience has contributed to their inability to turn promising performances into victories.

For Da Cruz, the immediate priority is getting his injured players back and building the momentum needed to close the gap at the top of the standings.

“Normally, many draws, we deserved to win these games but because of our lack of experience, we didn’t win these games. But we will turn it on our side when we recover our squad and for sure, in one moment we must have some positive dynamic with a few wins in a row to continue this journey. We must keep a positive mindset,” he added.

Chiefs cannot afford many more dropped points if they are serious about challenging for the Betway Premiership title.



With Orlando Pirates and Sundowns setting the pace, Amakhosi need to put together a strong run of results rather than relying on their rivals to slip up.

Da Cruz, however, remains convinced that the campaign is far from over. His message is clear: Chiefs must stay positive, recover their squad and start winning consistently if they are to make a serious challenge for the championship.

World.title: Weather: Brace for a wet and stormy Monday in parts of SA
World.content:
Severe thunderstorms could bring heavy rain, hail and lightning to parts of South Africa on Monday. Image: Supplied

Here is what the weather has in store for KZN, the Free State, and the North West on Monday 2 November 2026.

The South African Weather Service has issued a Yellow Level 4 warning for severe thunderstorms in western and north-eastern KwaZulu-Natal, where heavy downpours, hail and lightning could cause flooding and damage to infrastructure and settlements.

A Yellow Level 2 warning for severe thunderstorms has been issued for the KwaZulu-Natal coast and adjacent interior between Port Edward and Mtubatuba, with heavy downpours, strong gusty winds, hail and lightning.



A Yellow Level 1 warning for severe thunderstorms has been issued for eastern parts of the Free State, with possible localised flooding, property damage and disruptions to power and communications.

KWAZULU-NATAL

Cloudy and cold to cool but warm in places in the north. Scattered showers and thundershowers are expected along the coast and adjacent interior, otherwise widespread.

The wind along the coast will light to moderate south-westerly at first, otherwise southerly to south-easterly, but northerly to north-easterly north of Cape Vidal.



The UVB sunburn is going to be low.

DURBAN

Durban is going to be cloudy with scattered showers and thundershowers.

Light to moderate south-westerly winds will blow at first, before shifting to southerly to south-easterly.



Temperatures will range from 20°C to 22°C.

The UVB sunburn index is going to be low.

FREE STATE

Partly cloudy and warm with isolated showers and thundershowers but scattered in the east, where it will be cloudy



BLOEMFONTEIN

Bloemfontein is going to be partly cloudy with isolated showers and thundershowers.

Temperatures will range from a minimum of 16°C to a maximum of 30°C.

NORTH WEST

North West is going to be partly cloudy and hot with isolated showers and thundershowers but scattered in the east where it will be cloudy



MAHIKENG

Mahikeng is going to be cloudy becoming partly cloudy with isolated afternoon showers and thundershowers.

Temperatures will range from a minimum of 19°C. to a maximum of 31°C.

Weather forecast data provided by the South African Weather Service.

World.title: The Big Metro Face-Off: Battle for control of Joburg
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - With the local government elections just days away, political parties are stepping up efforts to win over voters.

The ANC’s Dada Morero and the DA’s Helen Zille, both mayoral candidates for Johannesburg, went head-to-head in a debate, outlining their plans for the city.

World.title: Mogale claims ANC has reversed eight years of neglect in Tshwane
World.content:
PRETORIA - ANC Tshwane mayoral candidate nominee Tlangi Mogale has defended the party's record in the metro, claiming the ANC has spent the past 24 months reversing years of neglect and prioritising residents' needs.

Speaking during a We The Nation Elections 2026 debate, Mogale said the party had demonstrated its commitment to residents through improved service delivery, infrastructure development and efforts to stabilise the City of Tshwane's finances.

She argued that townships, which she said had been neglected for years while service delivery focused on affluent areas, were now receiving greater attention under the current administration.

“If you check the budget that we have approved through an ANC deployee, we have provided services in the townships, the intergovernmental relations component has also been strengthened,” Mogale said.

Addressing the persistent water challenges in Hammanskraal, Mogale said the City had strengthened its relationship with national government to help deliver projects that were beyond its financial capacity.

She cited the completion of the Klipdrift package plant as one of the developments resulting from these interventions.

“Most importantly, we have undone the injustices that the people of Tshwane were subjected to in the last eight years. Townships were neglected and service delivery only focused in affluent areas,” she said.

Mogale also defended the ANC's handling of the municipality's finances, saying the City was servicing its Eskom debt and maintaining its current account.

She said the administration inherited financial challenges but managed to stabilise the municipality's finances and unlock funding for capital expenditure projects after taking office approximately a year ago.

“Currently, Tshwane is a construction site because of the ANC. I say the ANC because, in as much as we are in a coalition, we enjoy majority seats in the infrastructure structure,” she said.

Tshwane is currently governed by a 10-party coalition comprising the ANC, Economic Freedom Fighters (EFF) and seven smaller parties.

World.title: Brink accuses ANC of planning to use 'puppet' to run Tshwane
World.content:
PRETORIA - Democratic Alliance (DA) Tshwane mayoral candidate Cilliers Brink has accused the ANC of planning to use a political "puppet" to influence the running of the City of Tshwane, rather than fielding its own mayoral candidate.

Brink launched a scathing attack on the ANC, accusing the party of undermining coalition-led governments in Tshwane and other cities since losing its majority.

"Since the ANC has lost its majority in Tshwane and other cities, it has done everything either to bring down the governments that we elected in its place or to sabotage them using a network of cadres and tenderpreneurs," he said.

"That is why they don't have a mayoral candidate. They don't need one. They're going to pick a puppet to do the fronting and they'll make the decisions," he added.

Brink is seeking to reclaim the Tshwane mayoral chain, having previously served as the city's executive mayor from March 2023 until September 2024.

He said the ANC must be "comprehensively defeated", adding that the DA's priorities would include restoring accountability, improving municipal services and tackling corruption.

"Our priority will be to fire corrupt officials and tenderpreneurs and replace them with honest, hardworking people.

"We will also restore law and order using crime-fighting technology, upgrade water, electricity, waste collection and public lighting through private partnerships, and use the assets of the city to draw investment to create jobs," Brink said.

He maintained that restoring Tshwane's administration would require leaders with integrity, claiming that the DA had not been implicated in allegations of corruption or political interference.

"No one from the DA has been mentioned at the Madlanga Commission. None of the DA councillors have been cited as interfering with tenders," he said.

READ MORE | VOTING STATIONS ARE READY SPECIAL VOTES

Brink also vowed to confront what he described as the city's "water tanker mafia", arguing that residents should have reliable access to water through their taps rather than depending on tanker services.

"We have to stand up to the water tanker mafia in this city. We need water in our taps, not via tankers," he said.

World.title: Tshwane's Spies says smaller parties have a place in democracy
World.content:
PRETORIA - With just hours to go before special voting gets underway ahead of the 4 November local government elections, Tshwane FF Plus mayoral candidate Willie Spies has urged voters to choose political parties based on their principles rather than their size.

Spies argues that smaller parties should not be dismissed as offering "wasted votes", saying South Africa's political landscape has changed permanently and that no single party should expect to dominate the political scene.

He criticised parties that campaign on promises to eliminate smaller political players, arguing that such an approach undermines the principles of democracy.

“Up to 10 years ago, there was only one big party in South Africa, and that was the ANC. Every other party was a smaller party. Ten years ago, things changed, and they changed forever. There won't ever be one political party dominating the political scene anymore,” Spies said.

He added that every political party starts an election on an equal footing, with voters ultimately determining how much representation each party receives.

“In an election, every single party starts at zero percent. It is up to the voters to decide what the representation of each and every political party will be after the elections.”

Citing the Democratic Party's performance in the 1994 elections, Spies pointed out that the party secured just 1.7% of the vote before growing into a larger political force.

“Democracy should be allowed to run its course. People should be allowed to vote for principle, not for size. If size is the only thing you can offer, you've got very little to offer.”

The FF Plus is currently the fifth-largest party in the City of Tshwane. Spies believes the municipality urgently needs a change in leadership and management.

“Municipalities are about four things: water, electricity, infrastructure and safety. The past 15 years of municipal management was a dismal failure in all four respects,” Spies said.

READ MORE | PEOPLE STILL BELIEVE THAT SA CAN DO BETTER - HLABISA

He urged voters to look beyond established political power structures and consider parties offering a different approach to governance.

“You cannot keep on doing the same thing and expect any changes. People need to start voting for political parties according to principle.”

Positioning the FF Plus as a potential coalition partner, Spies said the party believes in values-driven governance and wants to see Tshwane succeed.

“The FF Plus is a reliable coalition party. We believe in principle government based on values, and we want to see this city succeed,” he said.

World.title: 2.6 million South Africans set to cast special votes
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - It's all systems go for the 2026 Local Government Elections, with 2.6 million South Africans expected to cast their special votes over the next two days.

Of those approved, 1.9 million will vote at designated voting stations, while the remainder will be visited at their registered addresses by IEC officials.

IEC chief electoral officer Sy Mamabolo said approved home-visit voters must remain available at the addresses provided in their applications on 2 and 3 November.

Voting station-based special voters must cast their ballots at the stations where they are registered.

Gauteng has the highest number of approved voting station-based special votes, at 391,000.

Voting stations will be open from 8am to 5pm on both days.

World.title: We The Nation | Election edition | Tshwane | 1 November 2026
World.content:
PRETORIA - Water. Electricity. Service delivery. These are the issues that matter most to residents of Tshwane.

With the local government elections just days away, the question is simple: who has the plan, the experience and the leadership to turn things around?

The Tshwane mayoral candidates go head-to-head in our final We The Nation Elections 2026 special, live from the University of Pretoria.

We put the tough questions to those hoping to lead the capital city. What have they delivered? What will they change? And, in a city where coalitions are likely to remain part of the political landscape, can they put politics aside and work together in the interests of residents?

With special voting underway and election day approaching on 4 November, the stakes couldn't be higher.

World.title: People still believe that SA can do better - Hlabisa
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - 'If you are tired of empty promises, choose the IFP.'

That's the message from party leader Velenkosini Hlabisa.

Hlabisa closed the IFP election campaign in Ulundi, ahead of Wednesday's elections.

"‘They are tired of failed service deliveries, of dry taps, broken roads, unreliable electricity, uncollected refuse, dark streets and municipal offices that do not respond, tired of seeing the country moving backwards.

"Through our campaign we had something profound and encouraging. Beneath the anger and disappointment, there’s hope. People have not stopped believing that SA can do better, asking for a government that works, leadership that serves and a future that children can look forward to and inherit."

World.title: 'We've heard very clearly' - ANC president tells EC supporters
World.content:
MDANTSANE - ANC President Cyril Ramaphosa said the party has listened to communities’ concerns ahead of the elections.

Speaking at a campaign rally in Mdantsane, he said the ANC heard calls for better working conditions, action against gender-based violence, and greater support for people with disabilities.

Ramaphosa pledged the party’s commitment to addressing these issues.

" We heard very clearly what the aspirations of our people are, but we also heard the enthusiasm as well as the encouragement of our people. We've heard them repeating that they want us to work diligently to advance the lives of our people. We have listened to the workers of our country talking about, yes, the need that they want to see to improve the conditions of employment.

" It is also the ANC's ability to listen and to have deep exchanges with our people. We've also gone around Simamele, Okumkani namakosi ethu, as they too were raising many issues that concern them. We have listened to the women of our country as they too have raised issues that concern gender-based violence. We have listened to people who are disabled, and we have heard too the issues that concern them."

World.title: Gachagua dismisses Uhuru reconciliation calls, says 'we are one team'
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

DCP leader Rigathi Gachagua received at PCEA Kamangu in Kikuyu constituency by former Kiambu governor James Nyoro on November 1, 2026. [George Njunge, Standard]

Former Deputy President Rigathi Gachagua has dismissed calls for mediation between him and former President Uhuru Kenyatta, insisting that the two leaders remain in contact and have no differences requiring reconciliation.

Gachagua said attempts by Mount Kenya elders to broker peace between them were unnecessary, maintaining that he and the former Head of State continue to communicate, meet and share meals despite perceptions of a political fallout.

He challenged elders calling for reconciliation to instead focus on uniting the Mount Kenya community, warning that internal divisions could weaken the region's political voice and influence.

“On unity, as a community we have to remain united. Our unity is strength. Nimeona some elders in the newspaper wakisema tunataka to reconcile Rigathi Gachagua and Uhuru Kenyatta. How do you reconcile two brothers, who love one another and work together?” he posed.

The former Deputy President maintained that he and Uhuru were still on the same team, dismissing claims that their relationship had deteriorated to a point requiring third-party intervention.

“President Uhuru Kenyatta and I are one team. We work together. Please elders don’t reconcile us because there is no need for reconciliation. We are working together. There is no work there, we are one. We talk the same language, we meet, talk, we agree,” he said.

Gachagua further urged Mount Kenya elders to resist attempts to divide the community along political lines and instead promote dialogue and cohesion among its leaders.

“Our unity is our strength as a community. Please help me to unite Mount Kenya elders and tell people not to accept to be divided,” he added.

His remarks come amid growing calls by sections of Mount Kenya elders for reconciliation among influential political figures from the region following political differences that have emerged since the 2022 General Election.

Uhuru, who served as Kenya's fourth president from 2013 to 2022, remains an influential political figure in the region, while Gachagua has continued to position himself as a key voice in Mount Kenya politics.

World.title: Sifuna rallies opposition leaders to unite against Ruto in 2027
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Linda Mwananchi leader Edwin Sifuna adresses a rally at Ukunda in Kwale County on 31st October, 2026. [Omondi Onyango, Standard]

Nairobi Senator Edwin Sifuna’s Linda Mwananchi movement took its grassroots mobilisation tour to Kwale County, a day after unveiling its secretariat and leadership, with leaders urging the opposition to unite behind one candidate to face President William Ruto in 2027.

The unveiling had been marred by disagreement, with Wiper leader Kalonzo Musyoka jeered. Addressing a rally at Masai Grounds in Ukunda town, Sifuna said Kenyans were yearning for a single, strong opposition candidate and asked other leaders not to let them down.

“To send Ruto home, we need a strong team and a strong presidential candidate. I will ask other leaders to listen to the voices of the people politely because this is the voice of God,” he said.

The team made stopovers in Samburu, Kinango, Kwale town and Kombani during the day-long tour. Unlike earlier rallies in Mombasa, the Kwale events drew modest crowds, amid claims that local organisers had failed to mobilise supporters.

The mobilisation tour covered Samburu Town, Kinango Town, Kombani Junction, Lunga Lunga Town, and culminated in a major public rally at the Ukunda Showground.

The movement officially opened its new Kwale County office as part of a push to build county-level structures ahead of the 2027 General Election.

Addressing supporters in the rain, Sifuna declared that he will continue to build consensus among the opposition to ensure that they are united to send Ruto home in 2027. he said that divisions of the opposition leaders will guarantee Ruto a second term.

He warned against schemes to elbow local leaders out of the front lines, stressing that Kwale residents and local aspirants must drive the agenda on regional issues like water shortages and mineral exploitation. The Kwale tour marks the first public rallies after weeks without a large-scale county mobilisation exercise.

It has previously held gatherings in Mombasa and Taita Taveta as part of its plan to reach all 47 counties. The tour took place the same day the Orange Democratic Movement (ODM) was holding a rally at Jacaranda Grounds in Nairobi's Embakasi East constituency.

Embakasi East MP Babu Owino urged Sifuna, Musyoka, DCP leader Rigathi Gachagua and Jubilee leader Fred Matiang’i to agree on one presidential candidate, warning that time was running out.

“We are urging all opposition leaders to sit down and talk. We only have nine months to the General Election, and you should agree on one presidential challenger to President Ruto,” he said. “Sifuna, Kalonzo, Gachagua and Matiang’i should come together now. United we stand, divided we fall.”

isii Senator Richard Onyonka said it was time for opposition leaders to lock themselves in a room and emerge with a single candidate to face Mr Ruto. The call was backed by Linda Mwananchi chairman Godfrey Osotsi and Secretary General Caroli Omondi.

Trans Nzoia Governor George Natembeya, however, said Sifuna was best placed to challenge the President and asked Mr Gachagua and Mr Musyoka to back him.

“I want to urge Gachagua and Kalonzo to back Sifuna for the opposition to secure an easy win against Ruto. I want to assure you that there will be no rigging of the election,” he said.

Meru Governor Kawira Mwangaza said Kenyans would reject Ruto at the ballot for failing to honour pledges, including those on women’s empowerment.

Sifuna accused the President of failing to protect the Constitution and the rights of Kenyans. “He has focused more on building houses and markets and failed to protect lives,” he said.

He also claimed the government had issued title deeds for smaller parcels than residents used to own, while land was stolen. He further alleged that the government was plotting to plunder mineral resources at Mrima Hill in Kwale and demanded that an agreement with American investors be made public.

World.title: Musonye to lead AFCON 2027 preparations
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Sports Cabinet Secretary Salim Mvurya with Local Organising Committee (LOC) Standing Committee chairperson Nicholas Musonye on October 29, 2026. [Jonah Onyango, Standard]

Sports Cabinet Secretary Salim Mvurya has unveiled the Local Organising Committee (LOC) Standing Committee for the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON PAMOJA 2027), with Nicholas Musonye appointed chairman to oversee Kenya’s preparations for the continental football tournament.

Musonye will be deputised by Hussein Mohammed, while Anthony Lung’aho Inzihuli, also known as Antony Emmanuel Inzahuli Lung’aho, will serve as head of the secretariat and chief executive officer.

The committee is tasked with coordinating Kenya’s preparations, including stadium renovations, infrastructure development, operational planning and logistical arrangements ahead of the tournament, which Kenya will co-host with Uganda and Tanzania.

Mvurya said the committee brings together individuals with experience, professional expertise and leadership to help deliver a successful competition that meets the expectations of football fans, participating teams and the Confederation of African Football (CAF).

“I have unveiled the TotalEnergies CAF Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) PAMOJA 2027 LOC Standing Committee, entrusting its members with the national responsibility of coordinating and overseeing Kenya’s preparations towards delivering a world-class, memorable and successful continental football tournament,” Mvurya said.

He challenged members to move from planning to implementation, emphasising operational readiness, coordination, strategic partnerships, financial accountability and adherence to delivery timelines.

“With less than eight months to kick-off, I challenged the committee to move decisively from planning to execution,” he said.

Besides Musonye, Mohammed and Lung’aho Inzihuli, the listed committee members include Football Kenya Federation (FKF) Vice-President McDonald Mariga and FKF National Executive Committee representative Robert Macharia.

Other members named in the roster are Timothy Nabea, a former FKF NEC member; Gabriel Mghendi; Peter Kamau; Kerubo Momanyi; Benard Lagat; Collins Kalee; Caleb Amwayi; Ken Rungu; and Dan Shikanda, the former AFC Leopards chairperson.

The list also includes Charles Njagi, Thomas Karugu, Evelyn Cheluget, Miriam Chepkoech, Rodgers Chimega, Diana Injendi Manyengo and Collins Were.

The 38 committee members also comprises representation across functional areas, including finance, technical matters, refereeing, legal affairs and youth development.

The committee is expected to coordinate the different aspects of tournament preparation and ensure that the relevant agencies and stakeholders work towards agreed targets.

Kenya’s preparations also include the development of Talanta Sports City, officially known as the Raila Odinga International Stadium, which is expected to strengthen the country's capacity to host major international football matches.

Mvurya said the planned high-profile encounter between German giants FC Bayern München and Dutch powerhouse AFC Ajax, scheduled for January 5, 2027, would provide an opportunity to assess the country’s readiness.

The event is expected to test security arrangements, transport and logistics, crowd management, operational systems and the overall fan experience.

The CS also disclosed that representatives of the two European clubs had visited Kenya to assess its capacity to host the proposed fixture.

He said the government was adopting a whole-of-government approach, involving relevant agencies responsible for security, immigration, tourism, travel and hospitality.

AFCON 2027 is expected to attract thousands of supporters, officials and international visitors, creating opportunities for hotels, airlines, tour operators, transport businesses and other service providers.

The government is also positioning the tournament as an opportunity to promote tourism, attract investment, develop sporting infrastructure and inspire young footballers.

Mvurya said the committee carries the responsibility of delivering an event that would bring national pride while creating a lasting legacy for the country.

“I reaffirmed their mandate and reminded them that they carry the hopes and aspirations of over 55 million Kenyans to deliver a tournament that brings pride and joy to the country while securing a lasting legacy in sports development, tourism, investment and economic opportunities,” he said.
