World.title: Malawi: Police Confirm Egyptian Deputy Ambassador Beaten in Lilongwe Attack
World.content:
A senior Egyptian diplomat has been hospitalised after being attacked and beaten in Lilongwe, sparking a police investigation into the shocking assault.

National Police spokesperson Gladys Chiwaula confirmed that Egypt's Deputy Ambassador to Malawi was admitted to a hospital in the capital after the attack.

"Police are following up on the matter and will give more details later," she said.

Chiwaula gave few details.

She did not say where the attack happened, what led to it, or how serious the diplomat's injuries are. Police have also withheld the deputy ambassador's name.

Officers say they are investigating, but the incident is likely to raise alarm over the safety of foreign envoys in the country.

World.title: South Africa: African Horse Sickness Confirmed in Western Cape's Cederberg
World.content:
The Department of Agriculture has confirmed a case of African horse sickness (AHS) in a single horse on a property in the Cederberg Local Municipality in the Western Cape, prompting movement restrictions and intensified surveillance to contain the disease.

Laboratory tests conducted by the University of Pretoria's Veterinary Genetics Laboratory confirmed the presence of AHS virus serotype 7 on the property, which is located within South Africa's established AHS Protection Zone.

Agriculture Minister Willie Aucamp said the case was detected through the country's veterinary surveillance systems, enabling authorities to respond swiftly and implement containment measures.

"The swift detection of this case in the Cederberg Local Municipality is a good example of how South Africa's veterinary surveillance system works. As a result, the authorities were able to move quickly to the affected area and take the required stringent actions as stipulated in the Animal Diseases Act and deploy containment protocols," Aucamp said.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

In accordance with the Animal Diseases Act, 1984 (Act 35 of 1984), and the Western Cape Department of Agriculture's AHS contingency plan, an outbreak containment area has been established and movement controls implemented.

Horse movements within the controlled area ordinarily require a permit issued by the State Veterinarian: Boland. However, the department has advised that no permits will be issued for moving horses out of the affected area, while investigations and surveillance continue.

Veterinary Services, working with authorised veterinarians and industry partners, have also commenced intensive surveillance, tracing and census activities to determine the extent of the outbreak and identify any additional cases.

The department has urged equine owners in the controlled area to cooperate with Veterinary Services and report any animals showing signs consistent with AHS, including unexplained fever, swelling of the head or neck, breathing difficulties or sudden death.

Horse owners are also encouraged to take precautions against Culicoides midges, which transmit the disease. Recommended measures include stabling horses, where possible, from two hours before sunset until two hours after sunrise, avoiding low-lying and wet areas, and appropriately using registered insect repellents and insecticides.

The department has strongly discouraged AHS vaccination at this time, explaining that the currently registered vaccine is live-attenuated and that vaccination during periods of vector activity could result in the vaccine strain being spread by midges, potentially worsening the situation.

Close 

"While there is no proof of large-scale disease activity outside the said property, the department is focused on total vigilance and calls on all horse owners to refrain from AHS vaccination during this period. Veterinary Services will continue to monitor the situation closely and will provide updates as additional information becomes available," Aucamp said.

The department said international trade partners will be notified of the outbreak, with further information on the implications for international trade to be provided in due course.

Updates on containment measures, movement restrictions and permits will be issued by the Western Cape Department of Agriculture. Further information is available from Veterinary Services and at www.myhorse.org.za

World.title: Kenya: No, Kenyan Pastor Victor Kanyari Was Not Killed in a Road Accident
World.content:
No, Kenyan pastor Victor Kanyari was not killed in a road accident

IN SHORT: A fake Citizen Digital news graphic claims Kenyan pastor Victor Kanyari died in a road accident. But the image is fabricated and uses an old photograph of a separate crash.

Social media posts circulating in Kenya feature what appears to be a Citizen Digital breaking news alert, dated 5 October 2026. It claims that pastor Victor Kanyari has died in a road accident along Kangundo Road in the capital, Nairobi.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

The graphic shows Kanyari alongside a badly damaged white vehicle surrounded by onlookers.

Collectively, the posts we sampled received more than 162,000 views and 2,000 likes.

Who is Kanyari?

Kanyari is a Kenyan preacher who heads the Salvation Healing Ministry in Nairobi. He made headlines in 2014 after a KTN investigation exposed staged miracles at his ministry and his controversial KSh310 donation scheme, which he later acknowledged was intended to lift him out of poverty.

Kanyari was previously married to gospel singer Beatrice Wairimu Mbugua, popularly known as Betty Bayo. They had two children. Bayo died of leukaemia on 10 November 2025, prompting a custody dispute between Kanyari and the children's stepfather, Hiram Gitau, popularly known as Tash.

On 26 October 2026, a court awarded Kanyari legal custody but ordered a gradual transition, allowing the children to remain temporarily with Tash.

The dispute, along with his active social media presence, has kept Kanyari in the public eye. He has also announced plans to contest the Kasarani parliamentary seat in Kenya's 2027 general election.

Citizen Digital is the online news platform of Citizen TV, owned by Royal Media Services.

But did the broadcaster report Kanyari's death in a road accident? We checked.

Old accident photo used in fake graphic

We found no credible news reports confirming Kanyari's alleged death or a corresponding report on Citizen Digital or Citizen TV's social media accounts.

In contrast, Kanyari's social media accounts feature recent photos and videos of him going about his usual activities.

A reverse image search revealed that the photo of the wrecked vehicle had been shared on Facebook on 27 June 2024, more than two years before the supposed news alert.

Close 

The earlier post was captioned: "Bad accident on Ngong road joining on to Karen road. Multiple casualties."

The vehicle and onlookers match those in the circulating graphic, confirming the photograph predates the alleged October 2026 crash.

The graphic is fabricated. It uses an old accident photo to support a false claim about Kanyari's death. His recent public activities also contradict the rumour.

World.title: Kenya: 46 Ebola Contacts Set for Discharge From Quarantine On November 3
World.content:
Nairobi — Public Health Principal Secretary May Muthoni says 46 contacts under quarantine are expected to be discharged on November 3 after completing the required monitoring period.

Muthoni has directed health teams to prepare the necessary discharge packages and support for those completing quarantine.

"We must also be able to complete the full 21 days of followup and every person leaving quarantine must receive the agreed discharge package and support... we must also continue to follow up the nine contacts outside Kenya with the countries concerned," she said.



She said every person leaving quarantine must receive the agreed assistance as authorities maintain surveillance to prevent further transmission.

The PS urged response teams to ensure all arrangements are in place ahead of Tuesday's planned discharge.

"Kenya is making progress in containing the Ebola outbreak, with no new cases reported in the last 10 days, following coordinated efforts by the Ministry of Health, County Governments and development partners," Muthoni stated.

So far, the country has recorded nine cases and two deaths;.

Following confirmation of the first Ebola case on 6 October, the health ministry conducted "robust contact tracing of anyone who may have been exposed", the World Health Organization (WHO) says. By 22 October, all contacts had been traced, both in Kenya and internationally, and placed in quarantine, it adds.

The government says that the confirmed cases so far are connected and there is no evidence that the virus has spread to the community.

World.title: Nigeria: Gunmen Kill Four in Plateau Community Despite Curfew
World.content:
The attackers reportedly stormed the community at about 8 p.m. and opened fire on residents, despite the curfew imposed in parts of the state to contain insecurity.

At least four people were killed after gunmen attacked Sabon Angwa community, around Bet/Zat in Barkin Ladi Local Government Area of Plateau State, on Thursday night.

The attackers reportedly stormed the community at about 8 p.m. and opened fire on residents, despite the curfew imposed in parts of the state to contain insecurity.



A resident of Barkin Ladi, Bulus Jok, said the gunmen operated freely for some time, shooting indiscriminately.

"The gunmen struck the community around 8 p.m. despite the curfew in place and started shooting sporadically," Mr Jok said.

He added that the attack threw residents into panic, leaving four people dead.

Mr Jok expressed concern that the incident occurred despite an early warning reportedly sent to relevant authorities a day before the attack.

"It is very sad, especially as there had been an early warning alert sent to the relevant authorities a day before the attack," he said.

The Publicity Secretary of the Berom Youth Moulders-Association, Rwang Tengwong, also confirmed the incident.

Mr Tengwong condemned the killings, describing the attack as unacceptable and expressing concern over the continued assaults on communities despite security measures.

He urged security agencies to intensify surveillance, strengthen their presence in vulnerable communities and respond promptly to intelligence and early warning reports to prevent further attacks.

The latest incident adds to the series of attacks on communities in Plateau State, raising fresh concerns about the effectiveness of security measures, including curfews, in protecting residents.

Efforts to reach security operatives for official confirmation and further details were unsuccessful as of the time of filing this report.

World.title: Ethiopia: U.S. Customs Releases Ethiopia-Made Solar Cell Shipments After Supply Chain Review
World.content:
Addis Abeba — US Customs and Border Protection (CBP) has released shipments of solar cells manufactured at a Japanese company's facility in Ethiopia following a review of its supply chain documentation, SolarQuarter reported.

TOYO Co., Ltd., a Japan-headquartered solar manufacturing company, announced on 29 October that CBP had completed its review after the company submitted documentation demonstrating the traceability of its supply chain, including the origins of polysilicon and wafers used in manufacturing the solar cells.

The company said it cooperated with US authorities throughout the review process and provided detailed documentation on the sourcing of its production materials.

The release of the shipments comes as TOYO seeks to expand its international manufacturing operations and strengthen its presence in the US market. The company operates a manufacturing facility in Humble, Texas, and is pursuing certification under CBP's Customs Trade Partnership Against Terrorism (CTPAT) programme, which is designed to strengthen supply chain security and import compliance.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

TOYO Chief Executive Officer Takahiko Onozuka welcomed the completion of the review, expressing appreciation for what he described as CBP's professional approach. He said the company remained committed to transparency and regulatory compliance as it expands its US operations.

Onozuka also stressed the importance of providing customers with confidence in the origins of solar products through greater supply chain traceability.

The development highlights the importance of supply chain documentation and regulatory compliance for solar manufacturers operating across multiple countries, particularly as scrutiny of the origins of imported products increases.

The release of the shipments follows an ongoing US investigation into whether solar cell manufacturers operating in Ethiopia are circumventing existing American trade duties on Chinese solar products.

In July 2026, Addis Standard reported that the US Department of Commerce had launched a country-wide investigation into imports of silicon solar cells from Ethiopia to determine whether they were circumventing longstanding antidumping and countervailing duty (AD/CVD) orders on Chinese solar products.

The investigation followed a petition filed in May 2026 by eight US solar manufacturers -- DYCM Power, First Solar, Qcells, Silfab, Solx, Suniva, Swift Solar and Talon PV -- alleging that two manufacturers operating in Ethiopia, TOYO and Origin Solar, were using Chinese-origin wafers to produce solar cells in Ethiopia before assembling them into solar modules locally or in Vietnam for export to the US.

According to the petition, nearly 70% of finished solar modules exported from Ethiopia contained Chinese components and underwent processing allegedly covered by existing US trade restrictions. Solar Power World reported that imports of Ethiopia-origin solar cells and modules, which were virtually nonexistent before July 2025, reached an estimated $277 million in the second half of that year, with shipments continuing to increase in 2026.

The petitioners argued that the surge in exports coincided with increased shipments of key solar manufacturing inputs from China to Ethiopia. Both TOYO and Origin Solar subsequently submitted factual information to the Department of Commerce in response to the allegations.

The investigation is expected to reach a preliminary determination by 10 December 2026, with a final decision anticipated around 10 May 2027. In the meantime, US Customs and Border Protection was instructed to suspend liquidation of relevant imports and apply cash deposit requirements pending the outcome. Any duties imposed could be applied retroactively to the investigation's initiation date.

Close 

The dispute first emerged publicly in May 2026, when Addis Standard, citing Reuters, reported that a coalition of US solar manufacturers had petitioned the Department of Commerce to investigate imports from Ethiopia over alleged tariff circumvention.

The petition came weeks after Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed inaugurated solar manufacturing facilities at Hawassa Industrial Park on 25 April 2026. According to state media, the facilities included TOYO Phase 2, Origin and Lumintech, which were expected to have a combined annual production capacity of 11.3 gigawatts.

At the inauguration, Abiy said the projects reflected Ethiopia's ambition to expand its industrial base and renewable energy sector.

World.title: Ethiopia: 'Ethiopia's Return to a Sea Port Is Inevitable': Navy Commander Calls for Regional Maritime Cooperation
World.content:
Addis Abeba — Ethiopian Navy Commander Vice Admiral Kindu Gezu has called for closer regional cooperation and dialogue on maritime security, saying Ethiopia's return to a seaport is inevitable and requires stronger engagement with neighboring countries.

"Since Ethiopia's return to a sea port is inevitable, working closely and through dialogue with regional countries is essential," Kindu said on Friday, a day after the conclusion of a regional maritime security forum organized by the Ethiopian Navy Headquarters, according to the army.

The forum brought together naval commanders and representatives from Yemen, Oman, Djibouti, Somaliland, and Puntland to exchange experiences and explore joint approaches to maritime search and rescue operations and regional security challenges. ENDF said the forum was organized with the support of the European Union.

Kindu described the gathering as "the first of its kind in Ethiopia" to discuss regional maritime search and rescue plans, saying it demonstrated the Ethiopian Navy's growing capabilities and readiness to engage in regional and continental maritime affairs.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

He also highlighted growing security challenges around the Strait of Hormuz, warning that threats in the area could increasingly affect the wider region. No country, regardless of its strength, could independently ensure maritime security or resolve emerging challenges, he said, emphasizing the need for countries of different sizes to pool their capabilities.

"The participating countries of the forum must work together to solve the problems observed in the region," Kindu said, adding that regional cooperation was essential to addressing maritime threats and ensuring safe maritime movement.

Ethiopian Navy Deputy Commander for Operations Commodore Jemal Tufisa said the forum had helped establish practical foundations for regional cooperation through cross-border information sharing, identifying areas of concern, and conducting joint operational exercises.

"We trust that upon returning to your respective countries, you will translate the lessons gained from the workshop into action, working effectively on regional maritime security and performing tasks with international acceptance," Jemal said.

Rear Admiral Kenneth Nyagah, a search and rescue project expert, and Master Kuraja Mishini, manager of the Djibouti Code of Conduct, commended the Ethiopian Navy's initiative in creating communication channels for information sharing, coordinated decision-making, and joint responses to regional threats. Both expressed their commitment to continued cooperation.

Close 

The forum concluded on Thursday with discussions on "existing maritime security conditions and potential future scenarios", including the actions participating countries should take in responding to specific emergencies and threats.

World.title: Liberia: Congo Town Overpasses Spark Political Storm
World.content:
The ongoing construction of two overpass bridges along Tubman Boulevard in Congo Town has sparked a political dispute between supporters of former President George Manneh Weah's Congress for Democratic Change (CDC) and President Joseph Nyuma Boakai's ruling Unity Party (UP), with both sides claiming credit for the Chinese-funded infrastructure project.

While CDC supporters insist that the project was initiated and negotiated under the Weah administration, supporters of the ruling Unity Party point to the Boakai government's role in overseeing its implementation and advancing construction.

The controversy has revived debate over which administration deserves recognition for major infrastructure projects initiated under previous governments but implemented or completed by their successors.

Official records indicate that the Congo Town overpass project originated during the Weah administration, following diplomatic engagements between Liberia and China.



On September 1, 2018, former President Weah met Chinese President Xi Jinping in Beijing, where discussions centered on strengthening bilateral relations and supporting infrastructure development in Liberia.

According to an Executive Mansion statement issued at the time, the discussions included plans to construct two overpasses at SKD Boulevard and near the Ministerial Complex in Congo Town.

The initiative gained momentum on September 9, 2019, when Liberia and China signed an agreement for the construction of the two overhead bridges, according to records from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

Another significant milestone came on June 8, 2021, when the two countries signed an implementation agreement for the project along Tubman Boulevard.

The Ministry of Public Works subsequently identified the overpasses as part of China's infrastructure assistance to Liberia.

CDC supporters argue that these diplomatic engagements and agreements establish that the project was conceived and negotiated under the Weah administration, contrary to suggestions that it originated under President Boakai.

However, supporters of the ruling Unity Party maintain that the current administration deserves recognition for advancing the project through the construction phase.

The disagreement underscores the distinction between initiating and securing financing for infrastructure projects and supervising their implementation and eventual completion.

Close 

The controversy also comes amid a broader political exchange between officials of the current and former administrations over the ownership of ongoing development projects.

Finance and Development Planning Minister Augustine K. Ngafuan recently challenged claims by former Finance Minister Samuel Tweah that several projects being implemented by the Boakai administration were inherited from the CDC government.

Ngafuan argued that completing unfinished projects inherited from previous administrations does not prevent the government from pursuing new development initiatives.

"If you had completed the old projects, we would have been doing only the new projects. But we now have to complete the old projects while doing the new ones simultaneously," Ngafuan said.

His remarks reflect the administration's position that completing inherited infrastructure projects forms part of its responsibility to ensure continuity in national development.

Meanwhile, construction of the two Congo Town overpasses remained underway as of October 28, 2026.

The bridges are expected to ease traffic congestion, improve road safety and reduce travel times along Tubman Boulevard, a major transportation corridor connecting Monrovia and Paynesville.

The project, estimated at approximately US$36.6 million, is being financed by the Chinese government through an assistance grant.

Although the political debate over credit continues, the project's documented history spans successive administrations, from diplomatic negotiations and agreements under Weah to ongoing construction under Boakai. -Editing by The New Dawn

World.title: Chris Pratt went from living in a van to Hollywood stardom after chance encounter changed everything
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

Chris Pratt's journey to becoming one of Hollywood's go-to action stars started with him living in a van in Hawaii.

In a recent post on X, the 47-year-old actor reflected on his beginnings: "Before Hollywood, I was living in a van in Hawaii and waiting tables at Bubba Gump Shrimp Company," revealing that a chance encounter working one night changed his life.

"One day, the incredible Rae Dawn Chong walked into the restaurant, and naturally, I went up to her table and said, 'Hey, you’re a movie star! What are you doing here?'" he recalled. "She asked if I could act, and I said, 'F- - - yeah, put me in your movie!'"

Since he didn't have a phone, he gave Chong his friend Mike's number, who told him a few days later that someone had called for him.

NICKI MINAJ, ANNA NICOLE SMITH AND MORE STARS WHO GOT THEIR START WAITING TABLES AT RED LOBSTER

"I called her back, and sure enough, she was serious," he wrote. "I drove over to pick up the script, went back to Mike’s house, and read all 120 pages three times in a row. First script I’d ever read. My character's name was Devon, and I remember thinking, 'Sweet! I could totally play a Devon!'

After the audition, he recalled Chung telling him he "could act and offered me the part."

While he lived in Hawaii, the movie was filming in Los Angeles, which made Pratt a little nervous, as he had "about $60 to my name, a bag of clothes, and some rollerblades." He then found out that Chung would fly him out to Los Angeles for production.

"I remember thinking right then and there, my life just changed forever. I'm going to be an actor," he wrote. "That little movie was 'Cursed Part 3,' a low-budget horror comedy that opened the door to Hollywood for me. I'll forever be grateful to Rae for taking a chance on a kid working at a shrimp restaurant. Everybody starts somewhere, and this is where it all began for me."

Pratt's role in "Cursed Part 3" led to bigger projects, including his breakout role playing Andy Dwyer in the hit NBC show, "Parks and Recreation."

He then landed the role of Peter Quill, or Star-Lord, in the Marvel movie, "Guardians of the Galaxy," playing the character in the film's two sequels, as well as in "Avengers: Infinity War" and "Avengers: Endgame."

When speaking to Moviefone in May 2023, Pratt shared he is "grateful" for "Guardians of the Galaxy" director James Gunn for casting him as the lead in the movie, saying, "He's changed my life" and the life of his children.

"He found a working actor who had already at that point done way better than most people who come out to town. I wasn't a waiter any longer, I was a series regular on a show. I was getting recognition," he said. "He brought me to a whole new level that ultimately changed the entire way the industry saw me. I no longer was auditioning. That was the last audition I ever had. So he changed my life."

Since becoming a Marvel superhero, Pratt has starred in the "Jurassic World" franchise, voiced characters in "The Lego Movie" and its sequel, "The Super Mario Bros. Movie" and its sequel and "Onward," and has starred in the TV series "The Terminal List" since 2022.

He has also starred in a number of standalone blockbusters, including "Passengers," "The Magnificent Seven," "The Tomorrow War" and many others.

Pratt was married to actress Anna Faris from July 2009 to August 2017, when they announced their separation. They share one child together, a son named Jack, 14.

He then married Katherine Schwarzenegger in June 2019, and they share three children together; Lyla, 6, Eloise, 4, and Ford, 1.

"It's an incredible blessing to be a father. It's also a lot of hard work. And so I think I just want to teach them that ... I don't know, I want to do my best," he told Fox News Digital in October. "I basically want to get right everything my dad got right and get right everything my dad got wrong. And I'm sure I'll screw up both, you know?"

Ukraine officials said the country’s official air-raid alert app was likely hacked after emergency alerts warned on Sunday that there was a "radiation hazard" and a "chemical attack alert" in Kyiv.

RUSSIA LAUNCHES BALLISTIC MISSILE ATTACK ON KYIV HOURS AFTER ZELENSKYY WARNS OF MAJOR STRIKE

The public air alert online map also displayed Kyiv and other areas as under a nuclear alert. The app also issued false warnings about Russia’s hypersonic Oreshnik missile and alleged street fighting in Kyiv.

But Ukraine’s Air Force said its air alert app was hacked and that there was no radiation hazard to be concerned about.

World.title: Big 12 Conference admits officials got call wrong that benefited BYU Cougars in win over Arizona State
World.content:
Maybe the BYU Cougars being a religious school can pay some dividends.

The Cougars have benefited from a very fortunate run of officiating in recent weeks. At home against the then-No. 2 ranked Notre Dame Fighting Irish, BYU pulled off a stunning upset. Thanks in small part to yet another controversial literal last second clock call this college football season.

This page may contain affiliate links to legal sports betting partners. If you sign up or place a wager, FOX News may be compensated. This content was created by a team that works independently from the FOX newsroom.

Quarterback Bear Bachmeier found tight end Walker Lyons with 1:47 remaining in the fourth quarter to give the Cougars a 28-24 lead, putting Notre Dame's winning streak in jeopardy. The Irish drove down the field, converting a six-yard pass on fourth-and-5 to give themselves one last shot at the end zone from the 8-yard line with four seconds left. C.J. Carr's pass fell incomplete, and fans stormed the field.

BIG 12 CONFERENCE ADDRESSES OFFENSIVE CHANTS FROM UCF FANS DIRECTED AT BYU DURING UPSET WIN

Except, eagle-eyed viewers noticed that the stadium game clock clearly read 0:01 as the ball hit the turf. And the Big 12 Conference acknowledged they were right, and that Notre Dame should have had time for one last play.

"Following the Big 12's review of the final play of Saturday's Notre Dame-BYU game, it was determined that time remained on the clock when the ball hit the ground and the play was incorrectly cleared by the replay officiating crew," they explained in a statement. "The Conference will conduct a complete review of its end-of-game officiating process in advance of next week's games."

Yes, BYU may still have stopped the Irish and won the game anyway, but it was a clear officiating mistake that benefited the Cougars. It happened again the next week.

On the road at UCF, BYU found themselves locked in a tight game late in the fourth quarter against what should have been an overmatched opponent. With the game tied 24-24 and 11 seconds left, the Knights set up for a field goal attempt on third down. Kicker Will Stone's attempted was blocked without crossing the line of scrimmage, and Stone recovered it himself.



As he was tackled, his helmet came off, with the officials throwing a flag for a BYU facemask. Which they promptly picked up. Not only that, they then incorrectly applied a 10-second runoff for the helmet coming off. As rules analysts explained, that runoff is only required when the helmet coming off is the reason for the clock stoppage. But the clock also stopped because of a "legal kick down," per Terry McAulay, meaning that the runoff should not have been applied.

Instead of UCF having another opportunity at a game-winning field goal, the game went to overtime. That said, the Cougars did wind up losing in double overtime anyway, thanks in part to some less-than-beneficial officiating. As Stone made a field goal to go up 34-31, BYU's Kendall Wall was flagged for roughing the kicker. Instead of the Cougars needing just a field goal to tie the score, UCF converted the ensuing first-and-goal for a touchdown, making the two-point conversion as well.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

BYU had four tries from the four-yard-line, but came up empty, and the Knights pulled off the upset. Still, there's a case to be made that the game may never have reached overtime in the first place, had the rules been correctly applied.

Well, fast-forward to BYU-Arizona State on Halloween, and it happened again. Though at least this mistake wasn't in the closing seconds of the game.

In the first quarter in Provo, Bachmeier tried to run the ball in for a touchdown from the one-yard line, but fumbled immediately after the snap. Sione Moa jumped on it, advancing it into the end zone for a touchdown. Replay review confirmed that Bachmeier had indeed fumbled, and separately confirmed that Moa had scored.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

But the review team should never have allowed the touchdown to stand, because the whistle blew on the play to signal that Bachmeier had been ruled down. Once that happened, the ball could not be advanced after a fumble. Inexplicably though, they awarded the Cougars a TD anyway.

And now the Big 12 Conference has been forced to issue yet another statement that the officiating crew had made a mistake.

"Replay was incorrect in awarding a score," the statement read. "The correct ruling should have been BYU ball for a third-and-goal from the 2-yard line."

Sure, the Cougars may have punched it in from the two, but you never know in college football, and the call handed them a touchdown that should not have happened. Understandably, ASU head coach Kenny Dillingham was furious with the officiating crew at the time, and after the game.

OUTKICK IS NOW AVAILABLE ON THE FOX NEWS APP: CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD

"I was trying to argue that he does have the right to recover it post-whistle, but that's not a clear advancement, which means the ball should be at the three," he said. "Obviously, that wasn't what happened. It's not the officials' fault. Those officials don't have say in that. That's all back home."

There's little doubt that these mistakes are simply that, mistakes, and not some grand conspiracy by the Big 12 Conference to help get BYU to the College Football Playoff. But it's a sign of the seemingly growing officiating problem in college football, and yet another example of the fact that referees can, and often do, impact a game negatively. Some Cougars fans will also be quick to point out any number of calls they believe went against their team.

Normally, over the course of a season, these things even out. It's just unfortunate when there are several high-profile mistakes all happening around the same program.

BYU has yet another massive game this Saturday, as they travel up the road to play their heated rivals, the Utah Utes, in Salt Lake City. The No. 3 Utah Utes and No. 7 BYU Cougars. Just as everyone expected. And given the tight Big 12 race, with Utah 5-0, BYU 4-1 and Texas Tech 4-1, it could have tremendous implications in determining which teams will play in the conference championship game, as well as a spot in the playoff.

Hopefully we're not talking about the refs after this one.

World.title: Josh Jacobs' lawyers call police release of previously unreported abuse allegations 'character assassination'
World.content:
The attorneys representing Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs admitted that the recently released police case file that includes new allegations of domestic abuse from years ago are threatening the running back's career, but also see it as a case of "character assassination" that is easily disproven.

That is the underlying point of a statement released Sunday afternoon by attorneys David Z. Chesnoff, Richard A. Schonfeld and Clarence F. Duchac III to the media, including OutKick and Fox News Digital.

"The three accounts are old, are hearsay, and easily disproven, yet released to the media by police without any investigation to determine whether they were accurate or contradicted by evidence," the statement reads. "Josh is answering them in detail because of the character assassination that is occurring, unfairly threatening his career."

NFL LIFTS ABUSE SUSPENSIONS ON GREEN BAY'S JOSH JACOBS AND DENVER'S JONATHON COOPER AS INVESTIGATIONS CONTINUE

The NFL said in a statement Saturday that it is reviewing the previously unreported allegations that Jacobs physically abused multiple women whose existence came to light amid the investigation into the May 23 incident that was well-chronicled.

The NFL was already investigating Jacobs for that May 23 incident in which Jacobs pleaded no contest to misdemeanor battery and misdemeanor criminal damage to property connected to a domestic incident with an ex-girlfriend in Green Bay.

Jacobs was convicted of the battery charge in September and spent six games on the commissioner’s exempt list this season. He has returned to the Packers, but the team has been among those keeping in contact with the Indianapolis Colts about trading for running back Jonathan Taylor.

The Packers would not be interested in Taylor if they expected to keep Jacobs.

PACKERS' INTEREST IN JONATHAN TAYLOR SHOWS DESIRE TO MOVE ON FROM JOSH JACOBS AND HIS DOMESTIC ABUSE ISSUES

Understanding this, the statement takes aim at the Hobart-Lawrence Police Department's case file release to the media.

"The file includes summaries of three telephone interviews describing events in 2021 and 2022," the statement from Jacobs' attorneys said. "Josh Jacobs denies all three accounts and has a substantial body of tangible evidence to back up his assertions.

"The police department’s released file contains only phone interviews, taken years after the fact, with no additional investigation, save for an acknowledgment that Josh did nothing wrong. Josh was not given an opportunity to present evidence to Hobart-Lawrence in response to the uncorroborated report, primarily because Hobart-Lawrence took no action related to the unsupported and stale allegations."

And then the details, according to the Jacobs side:

"One of these three women made a claim to the NFL, which reviewed it and decided no action was warranted. Josh has kept evidence that supports his accounts and the NFL’s decision. Nothing in the released file indicates that any such evidence was used or even sought. Indeed, the police report did not even present any of this information.

"Another woman made a claim in 2021, but only after Josh called the Las Vegas police to his home to report the woman for misconduct. A police report was written that day, which effectively undermined her claims. No further action was taken by any authority after she was removed from Josh’s home."

The police file, per NBC26 in Wisconsin, claims a third woman told the police that Jacobs slapped her in the face, threw her onto a bed, threw her to the floor, spit on her and grabbed her throat in January 2022.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

"Josh denies any physical altercation with the third woman," the statement from Jacobs' attorneys said. "She first contacted Josh and asked to visit. She came to Las Vegas and stayed at his home. Another person was present in the house during part of her stay. She stayed there overnight and left the following evening — on her own, in a car she ordered herself. The receipt for that ride is in the police file the department released, and it is consistent with Josh’s account of how the visit ended, not hers."

It's clear the Jacobs camp understands the stakes: Their client's enduring status in the NFL.

And they want to remind everyone that charges that resulted in a trial are the only history that should matter.

"Josh took responsibility for what happened in May," the attorneys said. "He entered into an agreement with prosecutors for two misdemeanors, and he is meeting the court’s requirements."

In his two games since returning to the 5–3 Packers, Jacobs has rushed 32 times for 75 yards and a touchdown, averaging just 2.3 yards per carry. The three-time Pro Bowler has been more productive as a receiver, catching 11 passes for 68 yards and two touchdowns.

After scoring one of his touchdowns in the Packers' 27-19 win over the Carolina Panthers on Thursday, Jacobs had a controversial touchdown celebration. He insisted he wasn't making light of his recent arrest and that the celebration was instead inspired by a gospel song.

World.title: Iranian ‘ghost fleet’ filmed evading US blockade en route to China, UANI says
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

Small Iranian "ghost fleet" tankers are slipping past the U.S. naval blockade and smuggling sanctioned liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) to China through a shadowy maritime hub off Malaysia, according to U.S. investigators who covertly filmed one of the vessels en route in September.

United Against Nuclear Iran (UANI), which conducted the months-long probe, said at least nine similar tankers carrying Iranian oil or LPG have also evaded U.S. restrictions in the Strait of Hormuz since Washington reinstated the Iranian port blockade in July.

UANI identified one of the sanctioned tankers as the SOGL. It allegedly escaped the blockade on Sept. 1 carrying approximately 500,000 barrels of Iranian LPG after collecting it at an Iranian port in August.

The vessel then traveled thousands of miles to a Malaysian offshore anchorage, where UANI filmed the vessel receiving fuel and other services offshore. The ship then traveled on to China, where the organization said it discharged its Iranian cargo.

IRAN’S $800M OIL SMUGGLING SCHEME USES TANKERS POSING AS IRAQI SHIPS TO DODGE BLOCKADE

"This tanker had loaded its Iranian LPG from Assaluyeh Port, Iran, in late August. It then breached the U.S. blockade and made its way to a Malaysian anchorage," Jemima Shelley, a senior analyst at UANI, explained.

"What this shows us is that some vessels are managing to breach the U.S. maritime blockade," Shelley said of the footage shared exclusively with Fox News Digital.

"Most vessels aren't, but since the reinstatement in mid-July, we have seen only nine small tankers being successful in their breach of the U.S. blockade and departing the Gulf of Oman laden with oil or LPG."

At the center of the operation is the Malaysian Eastern Outer Port Limits Anchorage, known as the EOPL, an offshore shipping area approximately 70 kilometers from Malaysia’s coastline.

The anchorage has become a critical staging ground for Iran’s sanctioned energy trade with China, Shelley said.

The area allows vessels to wait offshore, receive supplies and transfer cargo between tankers, providing a logistical lifeline for Iranian energy exports as American naval forces patrol waters closer to Iran.

UANI had been monitoring the SOGL before its arrival in Malaysian waters, Shelley explained.

US TARGETS CHINESE REFINERY IN SWEEPING IRAN OIL CRACKDOWN, SANCTIONS ‘SHADOW FLEET’ TANKERS

"On September 16th, United Against Nuclear Iran chartered a supply vessel and transited 100 nautical miles into the Malaysian Eastern Outer Port Limits Anchorage," Shelley said.

"Here we witnessed firsthand the illicit activities of ghost fleet tankers, as well as some Iran-flagged cargo ships that were located in this anchorage, one of them being the SOGL."

She described the SOGL as "a Handymax small tanker that was laden with 500,000 barrels of Iranian LPG."

The U.S. maritime blockade was first imposed April 13, temporarily lifted in mid-June and reinstated July 14 after diplomatic negotiations collapsed. The operation has largely stopped Iran from exporting crude oil, depriving Tehran of a major source of revenue as the country faces intense economic pressure.

"The U.S. blockade is an overwhelming success at preventing vessels laden with Iranian oil and petrochemicals from leaving the Gulf of Oman," Shelley said.

She added that since the blockade was reinstated, "no Iranian crude oil has managed to depart and be a successful export for Iran, which is a huge economic pressure for the Iranian regime."

"It's just that there are some opportunistic small tankers that are just managing to breach the blockade."

The United States, she said, is primarily prioritizing Iranian crude and very large tankers, which often carry "two million barrels of Iranian crude."

MORNING GLORY: PRESIDENT TRUMP AND THE AMERICAN MILITARY HAVE BEATEN IRAN

LPG is a flammable mixture of hydrocarbons, primarily propane and butane, used for heating, cooking, transportation and industrial production.

"LPG carries a lot of risks," Shelley said. "The U.S. blockade's first course of action is to try to attempt to turn around these vessels, which is their main technique for enforcing the U.S. blockade."

"However, sometimes they do have to use military force and this would be incredibly high risk on far more volatile cargo such as LPG."

According to Shelley, the smaller vessels exploit those challenges while using tactics commonly associated with Iran’s ghost fleet.

"So what they'll do is they will turn off their AIS. They will often fly a false flag so they're completely stateless vessels," she added.

Automatic Identification System, or AIS, transponders broadcast a vessel’s identity, position and movements to other ships and maritime authorities. Switching them off can make a vessel more difficult to track.

"Often they will load, and then they will transit the Persian Gulf, the Strait of Hormuz, and then in the Gulf of Oman, they will conduct a ship-to-ship transfer there," Shelley said, describing it as a "very high-risk ship-to-ship transfer because it's LPG, not crude oil."

"And then the other tanker that's receiving the LPG will then transit and attempt to breach the blockade."

The overall scale remains relatively small compared with Iran’s historical energy exports.

US ECONOMIC CHOKEHOLD ON IRAN REACHES PEAK LEVERAGE AS COLLAPSE RISKS EMERGE

The SOGL, identified by IMO number 9208227, was added to the U.S. Treasury Department’s Office of Foreign Assets Control sanctions list Oct. 8 over its alleged involvement in transporting Iranian petroleum products since 2025.

The vessel has operated under multiple flags, including the Comoros and Zimbabwe, and has been linked in sanctions records to Gravion Maritime Co.

"Most of these tankers are very emblematic of what ghost fleet tankers do and so are flying false flags, which means they're completely stateless and will have very complicated front companies running them," Shelley said.

Meanwhile, the EOPL anchorage in Malaysia — roughly a 10-day-to-two-week journey from Iran — has become an important logistical center for Iranian vessels traveling toward Chinese buyers and a "key node in Iran's oil trade to China," Shelley said.

"It is used by ghost fleet tankers, Iran-flagged tankers that will load Iranian crude and then transit eastwards from Iran all the way to this anchorage where they will often conduct ship-to-ship transfers with the final tanker bound for China."

"Often this anchorage is also used for floating storage, which is how Iran managed to survive for so long with the U.S. blockade being reinstated in July," Shelley said.

She also clarified that since the blockade has been enforced, Iranian floating storage has fallen to "zero to seven million barrels."

"So you can see how they have survived from having this offshore anchorage where illicit ghost fleet tankers have been able to wait laden with Iranian products."

IRAN’S OIL LIFELINE IS DRYING UP. THE BIGGEST PAIN MAY FALL ON ORDINARY CITIZENS

UANI’s video also shows the SOGL sitting low in the water and receiving bunkering services from a smaller tanker off Malaysia, where Shelley said authorities appear to be "looking the other way."

"This is a common thing that you will see in this anchorage, because not only is this anchorage used for ship-to-ship transfers, but also these ghost fleet tankers, as well as some cargo ships in this anchorage, require various services, whether that is food, logistics or bunker fuel."

China is the dominant destination for Iranian oil and LPG, providing Tehran with a critical economic outlet despite U.S. sanctions and the naval blockade.

"For years, China has made up 80% of Iran's liquid cargo exports, and we have seen that only grow since the beginning of the Iran War. Now China is importing almost 100% of Iran's oil and LPG exports."

"It has created a system and trade that has allowed Iran to avoid sanctions, U.S. and OPEC sanctions, whilst China is able to buy highly discounted Iranian oil and LPG."

IRAN SEIZES SHIPS IN HORMUZ AS US TALKS FALTER AFTER CEASEFIRE EXTENSION

"After United Against Nuclear Iran's trip to the EOPL, interestingly, this small LPG tanker SOGL did not conduct a ship-to-ship transfer," Shelley said.

"Instead, it transited northbound into the South China Sea, where it finally discharged its Iranian LPG at Xinzhou Port in China."

The G Summer, a U.S.-sanctioned LPG carrier with a capacity of approximately 7,000 cubic meters, was also separately tracked transmitting signals from the Arabian Sea beyond the American blockade line in April, according to Bloomberg.

The vessel broadcast a message indicating it had an "all Chinese crew" aboard, while shipping analytics identified Iran as its last cargo country and Galle, Sri Lanka, as its reported destination.

World.title: 'SNL' co-host Michael Che turns Israel voter turnout into 'genocide' punchline on 'Weekend Update'

On NBC's "Saturday Night Live," "Weekend Update" co-host Michael Che joked about genocide while discussing voter turnout in Israel's elections, referencing voters on the right and left of the country's political spectrum.

"This week, a record number of people voted in Israel’s election, which is great to see regardless of if you’re on the right side, or the left side, or the genocide," Che said.

A spokesperson for the Campaign Against Antisemitism acknowledged that the comment was a joke but challenged its premise.

"There's always a lot of latitude with comedy, and this joke is hardly an exception," the spokesperson told Fox News Digital. The problem is that it's playing on what has become a widespread but baseless belief that Israel has committed genocide in Gaza."

NETANYAHU ALLEGES FRAUD AS ARAB PARTIES SCORE RECORD GAINS — EMERGE AS POTENTIAL KINGMAKERS

The organization argued that allegations of genocide against Israel portray Jews as perpetrators of the same crime committed against them during the Holocaust and are "motivated in no small part by a desperation to assuage global guilt for a real genocide against the Jews by casting the Jews as perpetrators of this grave crime themselves."

"It has fueled abuse and violence against Jews worldwide — including terrorism and murder," the spokesperson added.

NewsBusters managing editor Curtis Houck also criticized the joke, questioning whether viewers understood the meaning of genocide and criticizing the use of the term in discussions about Israel.

"We're now at the point where it's a punchline to refer to Israel as a genocidal state," Houck told Fox News Digital. "SNL's ill-informed viewers are unlikely to know the actual meaning of the word, and that it's more applicable to how many Arabs view whether Israel should be allowed to exist."

World.title: Democrats in key battlegrounds throw Joe Biden under the bus on the border
World.content:
WASHINGTON — Democratic candidates in 2026 battleground races are directly criticizing Joe Biden’s handling of border security when he was president, seeking to neutralize a political vulnerability and signaling a new path for the party on the thorny issue.

Candidates are throwing the ex-president under the bus on border policy in key states that will decide control of the Senate and some battleground House races across the country.

“I called out Joe Biden for failing us on the border,” Texas’ Democratic Senate nominee James Talarico says in a recent ad airing in the closing stretch of his neck-and-neck race against Republican Ken Paxton. He also criticized Biden in July for having “failed us on our southern border” as he rolled out his own border security plan.

He’s not alone.

In Kansas, a longtime Republican stronghold, Democrat Adam Hamilton criticized Biden in a recent debate with Republican Sen. Roger Marshall.

“I want to be crystal clear, first of all: Immigration at the border under Biden was a disaster. That is how we ended up where we are today,” he said. “Second, what we did in response to that has been a disaster for people across the state of Kansas.”

Hamilton, like other Democrats in areas that voted for Trump in 2024, paired his critique of Biden with criticism that the current president has gone too far on enforcement. Polls show many Americans have soured on Trump’s handling of the issue in the wake of immigration officers fatally shooting two Americans in Minnesota and one in Maine this year.

Still, the comments reflect a recognition that the issue of border security remains a vulnerability for Democrats as Republicans continue to accuse them of promoting “open borders” in a bid to mobilize their base and win swing voters. Biden’s ratings on the issue tanked amid a surge in migrant crossings during his presidency, which Trump successfully weaponized in 2024.

Entering office in 2021, Biden inherited a Covid-era migration surge that intensified in the United States after he made good on his pledge to roll back Trump-era policies and restrictions, allowing more asylum-seekers to stay in the country as their cases were being considered. The collective result was a huge spike in border crossings that became associated with the Biden presidency and brought down his approval ratings.

Even as Trump’s approval rating has fallen to 38%, polls show border security continues to be one of his highest-polling issues, although that number has fallen from the highs of his early second term.

“The Biden administration failed at the border,” Democratic House candidate Paige Cognetti said at a debate Thursday night.

Cognetti, who is vying to unseat Rep. Rob Bresnahan, R-Pa., in a highly competitive Scranton-area working-class district, later added: “The Biden administration did fail. We need to make sure that the border is secure. It’s a good thing that it is. We do need to make sure that the pathways to citizenship are there.”

In South Carolina, Democratic Senate candidate Annie Andrews said in a debate, “Democrats have failed on the border.”

Democratic pollster Celinda Lake said it’s “very smart” for candidates to distance themselves from Biden and that “there’s nobody contesting that interpretation” that he blundered on the border.

In the 2024 election, “immigration was playing a major, major role, and it was energizing Republicans. And it was the best issue among swing voters for Republicans,” she said. “ICE has gone too far, and that has backfired now.”

She added that the “best messaging” on immigration is “some control for the border plus a humanitarian process for immigration.”

Iowa’s Democratic Senate candidate Josh Turek traveled more than 800 miles to Laredo, Texas, to film an ad at the border touting his support for tougher enforcement.

“I came to the border to meet firsthand with the people who work to keep it secure. What happens down here affects us up in Iowa, so we’ve got to address it,” Turek says in the ad. “I voted with Republicans to allow law enforcement to arrest and deport criminals.”

Weeks earlier, he released another ad speaking to Iowans and vowing that he would “work with anyone” to fix immigration — “including President Trump, to secure the border.”

Closer to the border, Democrat Johnny Garcia is trying to win Texas’ redrawn and Republican-friendly 35th Congressional District against GOP nominee Carlos De La Cruz.

Garcia criticized Trump’s ICE raids as detrimental to the economy. But at a recent forum, he also blamed Biden’s policies for failures at the border and referred to a fatal smuggling conspiracy in 2022 that led to the deaths of dozens of people.

“We’ve also gotten to see, unfortunately, how Biden got it wrong on the border,” Garcia said. “I’ll admit that every single day. We got to see one of the largest migrant fatalities in this district in south San Antonio, with 53 migrants that were locked in a trailer.”

“So we can’t afford to just turn a blind eye to our border,” he added. “But at the same time, we can’t turn a blind eye to what we’re seeing happening on our streets.”

World.title: Sen. Tim Scott dodges on whether he would accept the results of the Alaska Senate race
World.content:
Sen. Tim Scott, R-S.C., declined to say whether he would accept the results of the Alaska Senate race if Democrat Mary Peltola wins following a bombshell report from The New York Times about Democrats’ alleged efforts to recruit a candidate with the same name as the Republican incumbent.

Asked on NBC News’ “Meet the Press” whether he would accept the election results if Peltola is certified to have won the Senate seat, Scott did not directly answer the question.

“Dan Sullivan is going to win, Kristen,” he told moderator Kristen Welker. “You know that, and that’s the only thing I’m going to tell you because it’s the truth.”

Scott went on to criticize Democrats for allegedly working to recruit a candidate with the same name as Republican Sen. Dan S. Sullivan, a controversy that exploded last week following a report from The New York Times.

“What I can tell you about the truth is you can’t trust Mary Peltola’s campaign and the collusion between her campaign and the DSCC,” said Scott, who also serves as the chairman of the National Republican Senatorial Committee, the GOP counterpart to the DSCC.

The New York Times reported Wednesday that Democrats allegedly sought to recruit a candidate named Dan J. Sullivan. The report said the efforts allegedly involved members of the Peltola campaign and the Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee, which works to elect Democrats to the Senate.

Following the report, the DSCC said in a statement that it “is not involved with Dan J. Sullivan.” Peltola, too, said she “knew nothing about any other candidates on the ballot except for me and the incumbent.”

Asked a second time whether he would accept the election results, Scott dodged the question.

“Number one, Dan Sullivan, the real Dan Sullivan, will win,” said Scott. “And number two, it actually is a federal offense to confuse voters.”

NBC News has previously reported that people who worked to recruit the challenger Dan J. Sullivan did not necessarily violate the law.

Elisa Rios, Peltola’s former campaign manager who was fired in August, participated in interviews with The New York Times, but later said she retracted “all statements made regarding the 2026 Alaska Senate race.”

Before The New York Times report was published, the Justice Department filed a lawsuit in Alaska seeking to block the certification of the results of the Senate election if Dan S. Sullivan loses. The DOJ cited potential voter confusion over having another candidate named Dan Sullivan on the ballot.

In the aftermath of the Times’ report, President Donald Trump has said that both Peltola and the challenger Sullivan should be removed from the ballot and prosecuted.

On Thursday, Alaska Gov. Mike Dunleavy, a Republican, said he was ordering a state investigation to determine whether the alleged “scheme violated Alaska’s laws and whether criminal charges or civil action are warranted.”

Poll: Voters demand change and a check on Trump, fueling steep Democratic advantage

Democrats have a sizable advantage in the battle for control of Congress days ahead of the midterm elections, a new national NBC News poll finds, with voters clamoring for change and voicing all-time high disapproval of President Donald Trump.

Registered voters prefer a Democratic-controlled Congress by a 7-point margin, with Democrats leading Republicans 52%-45% — 2 points more than in last month’s poll. That includes a 21-point lead among independents.

The president’s disapproval rating has climbed to 60%, a new high mark across his two terms in the NBC News poll. And for the first time in 30 years of NBC News polling, more voters say they are dissatisfied with their financial situation (51%) than satisfied (49%).

But it’s not all good news for Democrats: The poll contains fresh signs that a number of voters are pushing back on the GOP, as opposed to falling in love with the Democratic Party.

Federal judge dismisses Trump attempt to interfere in Alaska Senate race

Alaska's U.S. Senate candidates: Mary Peltola; Dan J. Sullivan; Sen. Dan S. Sullivan. Bloomberg; AP; Getty

A federal judge in Alaska on Sunday dismissed the Trump administration’s lawsuit seeking to separate and preserve certain ballots in the state’s upcoming Senate election, where GOP Sen. Dan Sullivan faces Democrat Mary Peltola.

In the last week, Peltola’s campaign has faced scrutiny after The New York Times reported the campaign and other Democrats recruited a candidate — Dan J. Sullivan — to run for the Senate with the same name as the incumbent senator.

Citing potential voter confusion, the Trump administration sought to separate and preserve ballots with votes for Dan J. Sullivan, arguing that if the incumbent loses, it may be because people voted for the other Sullivan by mistake.

In her ruling, U.S. District Judge Sharon Gleason voiced concerns about voters’ right to a secret ballot.

Sen. Tim Scott, R-S.C., declined to say whether he would accept the results of the Alaska Senate race if Peltola wins.

Asked on NBC News’ “Meet the Press” whether he would accept the results if Peltola is certified to have won the Senate seat, Scott did not directly answer the question.

“Dan Sullivan is going to win, Kristen,” he told moderator Kristen Welker. “You know that, and that’s the only thing I’m going to tell you, because it’s the truth.”

Murphy hospitalized: Sen. Chris Murphy, D-Conn., was hospitalized Saturday for a stroke after he “started experiencing numbness in his arm while at his son’s hockey game,” his chief of staff said in a statement.

Called out: Democratic candidates in battleground races are throwing Joe Biden under the bus on the border.

Democratic candidates in battleground races are on the border. Signed, sealed, delivered: A federal judge tossed a revised version of Trump’s $10 billion defamation suit against The Wall Street Journal over a story about a birthday card he allegedly sent Jeffrey Epstein.

Stores looted in German riots as Gen Z activists protest living costs, military service

A fire burns in Frankfurt's city center Saturday. Andreas Arnold / dpa/picture alliance

Rioters looted stores and set fire to barricades in Frankfurt on Saturday as demonstrations across Germany called for lower living costs and better education.

Tens of thousands of people took to the streets in more than 30 cities, including Berlin and Frankfurt, in protests organized by the campaign group Gen Z Regelt, or Gen Z Takes Charge.

France, Italy, Serbia and Spain have seen protests against the cost of living, among other causes. As the demonstrations began Saturday afternoon in Paris, protesters were pictured holding a banner that read: “We do not need tear gas for our future to be blurry.”

Martha Stewart responds to backlash over ‘hungry’ homeless Halloween costume

Martha Stewart in New York City on May 12. John Lamparski / Getty

Martha Stewart on Sunday responded to backlash about her Halloween costume, saying she was “distressed” to learn that her outfit, which depicted a “hungry” homeless person, had caused offense.

Stewart shared a photo of herself in tattered clothing, holding a clipboard that read, “I AM HUNGRY HELP ME!!” She posed with a tired expression and makeup meant to look like dirt on her face.

The photo was the third slide in an Instagram carousel promoting her candle collection on QVC.

Many interpreted the costume as mocking the poor, and some called it “out of touch” and “dystopian.”

Golden State Valkyries defeat Atlanta Dream for first WNBA title

Golden State Valkyries players lift the WNBA championship trophy after defeating the Atlanta Dream in Game 7 of the Finals at the Chase Center in San Francisco on Saturday. Getty

In only their second season in existence, the Golden State Valkyries are WNBA champions.

The Valkyries won their first title on Saturday, defeating the Atlanta Dream 68-63 in the first Game 7 in WNBA Finals history. Forward Gabby Williams led with 30 points and was named MVP.

Williams scored just two points in the first half, but rallied with 28 in the second, a record for the most points scored in a half in the WNBA postseason. Teammate Kiah Stokes led rebounds at 13.

“This is just incredible,” Stokes said of her fourth championship title. “But just my teammates, they’re amazing. The love that we feel is just incredible. I mean, this one just might be as good as my first.”

Extreme heat and drought, intensified by a “super” El Niño weather pattern, have made this Indonesia’s worst fire season in more than a decade.

The persistent haze has affected millions across the region since the fires began in July, forcing school closures in several countries and fueling disputes over who is to blame. Protesters in Indonesia have accused their government of failing to act, while neighboring countries are threatening legal action.

World.title: Golden State wins first WNBA title in franchise history
World.content:
The Golden State Valkyries brought to a conclusion a WNBA season that shattered viewership and attendance records with their first WNBA championship Saturday in a thrilling 68-63 victory over the Atlanta Dream in Game 7.

Golden State star Gabby Williams paced the Valkyries with 30 points, 4 blocks and 3 steals in 38 minutes.

The Golden State Valkyries huddle after defeating the Atlanta Dream in Game 7 of the WNBA Finals at Chase Center on Oct. 31, 2026, in San Francisco, California. Thearon W. Henderson / Getty Images

"All we heard last year: We don't have no stars, we don't have no talent," Williams said after the game. "Yeah right. We got good people. We got winners."

Jordin Canada led the Atlanta Dream in scoring with 18 points, adding 5 assists and 4 rebounds. Atlanta superstar Angel Reese struggled throughout the game, finishing with 8 points on 3-of-7 shooting in 33 minutes.

The victory was the first for a team in a Game 7. The league transitioned from a five-game series to a seven-game series starting last year.

This is the first title for the Valkyries in just their second season as a team. And the Dream are now winless in four WNBA Finals appearances.

The 2026 season was an unqualified success for the WNBA. The league set a new attendance record with 3.8 million fans attending 330 regular season games, according to the WNBA. The league said average attendance was up 21% from last year's record high.

ESPN, ABC and CBS all delivered their most-watched seasons in history, according to the WNBA. The league had three times as many games averaging at least 1 million viewers as the previous record set last year.

Gabby Williams of the Golden State Valkyries attempts a 3-pointer in front of Angel Reese of the Atlanta Dream Game 7 of the WNBA Finals at Chase Center on Oct. 31, 2026, in San Francisco, California. Ezra Shaw / Getty Images

How they got here

The Valkyries, despite having just one All-Star, took a major leap in just their second year in the league.

The team is owned by Joe Lacob and Peter Guber, who also own the Golden State Warriors. The team quickly became relevant, going 23-21 in their first year in existence before losing in the first round of the playoffs.

The signing of Gabby Williams in the offseason propelled the team to even greater success. The Valkyries went 32-12 in the regular season and beat the Paige Bueckers-led Dallas Wings and A'ja Wilson-led Las Vegas Aces to advance to the title series.

The Dream didn't lose a game on its path to the title series, defeating the Kiki Iriafen-led Washington Mystics and the Breanna Stewart-led New York Liberty in sweeps.

The Valkyries won Game 1 at home, 68-64, behind 26 points from Williams. Atlanta dominated the next two games behind all-time great performances from star Angel Reese. The Dream star posted 30 points and 16 rebounds in Game 2 and 21 points and 12 rebounds in Game 3.

Reese struggled to score in Games 4 and 5, shooting just 4-of-20 with 15 points combined, as the Valkyries wrestled control of the series away from the Dream.

Game 6 controversy

Game 6 started at 12:30 p.m. since the Atlanta Hawks were scheduled to play at the State Farm Arena on Thursday night. The Dream plays its regular season games at Gateway Center Arena, but its capacity is just 3,500 compared to about 17,000 at State Farm Arena.

"This incredible run by our players has also made something else abundantly clear: the Atlanta Dream has earned the right to be taken seriously," the team's ownership, husband and wife Larry Gottesdiener and Robyn Gottesdiener, Suzanne Abair and Renee Montgomery, said in a statement.

"Two months ago, when the WNBA finalized playoff dates and times, we raised concerns that the W Finals schedule conflicted with NBA games at State Farm Arena," the statement continued. "As we moved through the playoffs, we reiterated those concerns. Our concerns did not receive the attention, nor the urgency that they deserved."

Despite the early start time, the Dream still sold out the arena.

In a statement, WNBA Commissioner Cathy Engelbert said the league preferred to play the game at State Farm Arena.

"The sellout crowds and extraordinary atmosphere at State Farm Arena for Games 3 and 4 were a tremendous success, and we're excited to give thousands more fans the opportunity to experience Game 6 with a championship on the line," said Engelbert. "We thank the NBA, Dream, Valkyries, Hawks, State Farm Arena and USA Network for the collaboration and flexibility that made this move possible. We look forward to delivering another unforgettable Finals experience in Atlanta."

World.title: Sen. Chris Murphy hospitalized following stroke

Washington — Democratic Sen. Chris Murphy of Connecticut was hospitalized on Saturday after experiencing a stroke, his office said.

"Yesterday afternoon, Senator Murphy started experiencing numbness in his arm while at his son's hockey game. He was taken to a local hospital, where it was discovered he had experienced a stroke," Murphy's chief of staff Allison Herwitt said in a statement on Sunday.
