Subsequent to completion of assessment, the investigation unit conducted enquiries into the value of the shares of Pawan Impex (P) Ltd and SVIIT Software (P) Ltd and prepared a report.

The report concluded, prima facie, that the shares were overvalued when compared with the cost of their land and building, which was much lower than the transaction amounts of Rs 195 crore and Rs 60 crore, respectively.

The enquiries revealed the appellants purchased one-half share of the property at Sikandara Road, Delhi, in April 2010 through a court auction, and that the major source of this investment was the sale proceeds of the shares of the companies. On perusal of the investigation report and after a gap of four years, the department issued a notice under Section 148 of the act for reassessment.

World.title: Introspect on need to improve judiciary responsiveness: CJI
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Flagging the importance of timely intervention by courts in crucial matters, CJI Surya Kant said the difference between justice and injustice was not in the final judgement but in whether the court intervened when "intervention was most needed".

He underlined the need for the judiciary, particularly constitutional courts, to introspect to further improve their working and to make listing of cases "more transparent and predictable".

Speaking at the platinum jubilee celebration of Kerala HC, CJI Kant said constitutional justice in India did not begin and end in New Delhi and its strength lay in the robust network of 25 HCs spread across the country, each entrusted with the duty of protecting rights and upholding the rule of law.

He said HCs were better placed to deal with citizens' problems as they were closely connected with the everyday realities of people.

"It is in this context that I wish to emphasise the extraordinary constitutional significance of Article 226. Its breadth is one of the greatest strengths of our judicial architecture. While Article 32 guarantees access to SC for enforcement of fundamental rights, Article 226 empowers HCs to issue appropriate writs and directions not only for fundamental rights but also for other legal rights.





This wide constitutional canvas allows HCs to fashion meaningful remedies across diverse legal, statutory, administrative and contractual disputes.

Equally important is their power to grant timely interim protection," the CJI said.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

He said there has been a growing tendency of litigants to approach SC requesting directions for urgent listing or early hearing of matters pending before HCs and asked whether the present process could be improved, including listing of cases.

"SC has consistently respected the institutional autonomy of HCs, including their authority to regulate their own rosters. That position is rooted in respect for the constitutional status of these institutions. Yet, the frequency of such requests invites us to consider whether there is room to improve the responsiveness of our processes. We must ask ourselves: Can urgent matters be identified more effectively? Can listing procedures be made more transparent and predictable? Can technology assist in prioritising cases where delay may cause irreversible prejudice?.

.." he said.

"These are not questions of institutional criticism but of collective responsibility," the CJI added.

World.title: Poverty removal not just slogan: PM Modi on World Bank data
World.content:
PM Narendra Modi cites World Bank data showing India's extreme poverty rate fell 90% to 2.6% between 2011 and 2023, with nearly 50 crore people lifted out of extreme poverty.

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: India has recorded one of the fastest poverty declines in the world, with the extreme poverty rate in the country "collapsing" by 90% between 2011 and 2023 to a low of 2.6%, Prime Minister Narendra Modi said on Saturday, while asserting that elimination of poverty is a commitment for his govt."A historic fall in poverty. A generational rise in opportunity... Gareebi hatao was never a slogan for us. It is our commitment. From more than 1 in 4 Indians to roughly 1 in 38 (in extreme poverty)," the PM posted on Instagram Saturday, citing the World Bank's latest numbers. He highlighted that nearly 50 crore people had moved out of poverty during these 12 years.Besides, Modi added, employment had grown by 13.4 crore between 2017 and 2023, which was nearly twice the increase in India's working age population. "Inequality has fallen sharply. India's Gini index has dropped by over 20% from 29 in 2011 to 23 in 2023," the Prime Minister said in the Instagram post. The Gini index reflects how equitable is the distribution of income or wealth across a population, with a lower number indicating greater equality.World Bank's latest Poverty and Equity brief, released last week, said that poverty rate in India, defined at $4.2 a day, will decline to 12.1% in 2028 from 57.7% in 2011, having fallen to 16.1% in 2023.Meanwhile, extreme poverty, defined as spending $3 a day, declined from 27.1% in 2011 to 2.6% in 2023."This progress was mainly driven by strong consumption growth; rising employment, especially among women; and expanded social transfers, including food subsidies. As poverty declined, it became increasingly concentrated among households with lower education, fewer assets, limited access to stable employment and higher dependency ratios. Wage disparities, however, remain pronounced, as median earnings among the top 10% of workers were about 13 times those of the bottom 10% in 2023," the World Bank had said.

World.title: 1984 survivors, Sikh groups question timing of INDIA bloc rally on Nov 1, seek apology
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Survivors of the 1984 anti-Sikh killings and Sikh organisations Sunday questioned Congress's decision to hold the INDIA bloc rally on Nov 1, the 42nd anniversary of the massacre.

With Punjab assembly elections due in 2027, the rally's timing also gave BJP political ammunition against Congress.

The day saw a BJP-organised protest march in West Delhi, objections from victims' groups and renewed demands for justice.

In West Delhi, Sikh community members and survivors joined a march from Hari Nagar towards Tilak Nagar, demanding an apology from Congress and Rahul Gandhi. Union minister Hardeep Singh Puri, Delhi CM Rekha Gupta, minister Manjinder Singh Sirsa and senior advocate HS Phoolka, who has represented riot victims for decades, participated.

"Nov 1 is not only a black day for the Sikhs but the entire country. They (Congress) should also observe it as a black day and hang their heads in shame," Phoolka had said ahead of the rally.

The 1984 Riot Victims Welfare Society also objected to the timing of the rally. Its representatives, who had met Punjab governor Gulab Chand Kataria on Friday, said Nov 1 was a day of mourning, not political mobilisation. They also raised pending demands for housing, employment and rehabilitation.

Society president Surjit Singh sought dignified rehabilitation, while women's wing president Bibi Gurdeep Kaur recalled losing eight family members in the violence.

Rajya Sabha MP Vikramjit Singh Sahney, who met survivors in Delhi, recalled losing four family members and alleged that the killings were systematically planned.

Separately, SGPC president Harjinder Singh Dhami described the massacre as "a stain on the forehead of the world's largest democracy". "Until those responsible are punished for their actions, the hearts of the victim families will not find peace," he said.

World.title: Gyanesh has to go, PM & Shah next, says Rahul Gandhi at anti-CEC rally
World.content:
NEW DELHI: In a Ramlila Maidan packed with protesters and ringing with anti-BJP and anti-CEC slogans Sunday, Congress MP

said the opposition will confront the top

duo of Narendra Modi and Amit Shah after Gyanesh Kumar's removal as chief election commissioner.

The trio was losing sleep over the agitation, he claimed, and said the CEC's exit would be the first step in putting the country back on track.

With opposition biggies Congress chief Mallikarjun Kharge, Sonia Gandhi, Akhilesh Yadav, Mamata Banerjee, Tejashwi Yadav, Dipankar Bhattacharya, MA Baby, Farooq Abdullah and Mehbooba Mufti on the dais, leader of opposition in Lok Sabha said the "voice of the people of India" is greater to him than religion, and he will brook no assault on it.

Mocking BJP's catchphrase - "Modi kahin nahin jayega" - which was coined in response to Kharge's comment, Rahul said the PM won't be allowed to go anywhere. "You cannot flee... You will stay here and face action."

2024 polls illegal, says Rahul; Modi picking voters: Kharge

With a âvote bachao, desh bachaoâ banner forming the backdrop of the dais, the speakers focused on âvote choriâ, repeating allegations about SIR and deletion of around 14 crore voters. Rahul accused the CEC, PM and Shah of suppressing the voice of people through âvote choriâ.





While Mamata and Akhilesh said the West Bengal mandate to BJP was âstolenâ, Rahul mentioned the Maharashtra, Haryana, Chhattisgarh, MP and 2024 Lok Sabha polls.

He said the 2024 polls were illegal, arguing the difference between NDA and opposition was merely 3%, while 15% of the 2024 voters have been deleted under SIR. âModi is selecting the voters,â Congress chief Kharge said.

Led by Kharge, most INDIA bloc members stressed ejecting BJP from office was a must to save democracy, even leading the crowd in âBJP hatao, desh bachaoâ chants.

Some reminded the crowd that Ramlila Maidan has been the harbinger of history and change in the past. SP chief Akhilesh called the historic venue the âHaldighati of democracyâ, referring to the battlefield in Rajasthan where Maharana Pratap faced off with the Mughals in 1576, remembered as a symbol of defiant resistance to a powerful empire.

Addressing the crowd that had been growing since 9am and remained eager even as main INDIA bloc members came on the dais only by 3pm, Akhilesh, who occupied a key spot with UP polls looming, hit out at Modi, saying, âJo UP se aaye the, woh UP se hi jaayenge (those who came from UP, will go from UP)â.

âThe UP poll results will see off BJP from office in Lucknow and Delhi,â he said, also raising âchanda choriâ in Ayodhya in his speech. Akhilesh warned BJP was constantly trying to steal elections, even blaming SPâs 2022 assembly defeat on voter list manipulation. The SP chief said UP BJP has stated that 1.27 crore votes of Hindus have been deleted in UP. He said the statement seems designed to âput the blame for their upcoming defeat on someone elseâ â touching upon the much-talked about âDelhi vs Lucknowâ faultlines in BJP.

Indulging the sloganeering crowd, Rahul said his predictions always come true, and he was now forecasting that CEC Kumar would go to jail.

âVote choriâ is no smalltime shoplifting but a ârarest of rare caseâ which qualifies as âtreasonâ, Rahul said. âWithout Gyanesh, Modi would not be PM and Shah would not be HM. He also accused RSS of capturing all institutions, including judiciary and bureaucracy, while âtwo or three people like Ambani and Adani have cornered all the wealthâ.

World.title: Fake claims, evasion of Rs 5.3 crore land, techie couple in I-T net
World.content:
IT professional and wife face Rs 5.3 crore taxevasion allegations over fabricated donation and loan claims, including forged documents and receipts. (Representative image)

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: In a stern message to those making false income tax claims, authorities have carried out a rare search action on an IT professional and his wife, estimating alleged bogus claims and tax evasion of Rs 5.3 crore over five years, according to the department. The couple also face charges of forging documents.Tax officials found that deduction claims involved fake political donations, interest on home and education loans, while rental income was not disclosed. They had purchased half-a-dozen properties using some of these funds.It all started with the wife's tax return claiming a deduction of over Rs 40 lakh for a donation to a political party. While her Form 16 showed deductions of around Rs 1.2 lakh, the return claimed an additional deduction. When the claim was verified with the party, officials found that the taxpayer had actually donated Rs 50, for which a receipt had been issued. Investigators found that the receipt had been digitally modified and several fabricated receipts generated to support the claim of a donation exceeding Rs 40 lakh.But the couple, who live in Delhi-NCR, did not give in easily. When summoned during the investigation, the husband, who filed the returns, not only presented the "modified" receipts but also submitted bank statements to support the claim.Officials sought to verify the statements with the bank, as the transactions did not tally.Loan payments, credit card payments and bank transfers, including transfers to their own account, had been forged to show them as political donations.The couple had claimed nearly Rs 3 crore in education loan interest for studies at Yale University. An interest certificate was submitted. During probe, officials discovered that no family member of the couple under scrutiny had ever studied at Yale and that the certificate had been prepared using ChatGPT.The couple also made a bogus housing loan claim, with both spouses describing themselves as the sole owner of the same property, although they have now admitted that it was jointly owned. Contrary to their claims, the property was always rented out and was not self-occupied.In their returns, one spouse had claimed nil rental income and interest payment of Rs 2 lakh, while the other had claimed up to Rs 5 lakh as interest income. Since tax returns now require individuals to disclose loan account number and the bank, the name of the bank was changed in one case and the loan amount increased to Rs 6 crore, with interest claimed at Rs 8 lakh. The probe revealed that the loan had been repaid in 2015, while the claims under scrutiny related to the period beginning FY2021-22. The property was earning rent of Rs 10-16 lakh during this period.Dealing with the couple has not been easy. When their case was first picked up, the husband shifted the deduction claim for political donations under Section 80GGC to donations to charities under Section 80G, without surrendering the claim.The couple now face penalties and other legal action.

World.title: Odisha CM announces special package for families affected by Cyclone Arnab
World.content:
Odisha Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi on Sunday (November 2, 2026) announced a special package of 50kg of rice and ₹2,500 for every family affected by the recent rain and flood in the southern districts, besides damages for losses to crops and property due to Cyclone Arnab.

Also Read: Odisha short of equipment, may use explosives to rescue landslide victims

With another cyclonic storm expected to hit the coasts of Andhra Pradesh, the Chief Minister said the relief package will be reviewed again upon assessing damage after the weather system passes.

After reviewing the prevailing flood situation in the State in the evening, CM Majhi said people in several districts, especially Ganjam, Gajapati and Kandhamal, were affected by cyclone Arnab and its aftermath of heavy rainfall.

“Thousands of acres of crops and several houses have been damaged,” he told reporters and pointed out that assessment of damage was underway while the primary task was relief distribution and restoration.

Also Read: Search underway for 12 people missing in landslide-hit southern Odisha village

"I am hopeful that normalcy will return in affected areas in the next one or two days as the administration is taking all necessary measures," he said.

The Chief Minister announced that all affected families will get 50kg of rice and ₹2,500 in cash.

Small and marginal farmers, who sustained crop loss of 33% and above, will receive an agricultural input subsidy of ₹8,500 per hectare of land in rain-fed and non-irrigated areas, while ₹17,000 per hectare of land will be provided for areas under assured irrigation, he said.

Similarly, assistance for perennial crops like mango and cashew will be ₹22,500 per hectare, the Chief Minister said, adding that a minimum agricultural input subsidy of ₹2500 will be given to any affected farmer for perennial crops and ₹1000 for non-irrigated areas.

"The government will provide ₹18,000 to each affected farmer to remove sand and silt from the fields. The State will also provide 1.75 lakh mini kits to farmers for free," he added.

Under the housing sector, he said assistance of ₹1.20 lakh will be given for fully damaged houses in the plains, ₹1.30 lakh in hilly areas, while ₹6,500 and ₹4,000 will be given for partially damaged pucca and kutcha houses, respectively.

CM Majhi said his government has decided to provide compensation of ₹10,000 for affected small shops, street vendors and kiosks and ₹25,000 for affected big shops and commercial establishments.

For fisherfolk, he announced assistance of ₹22,500 for boat purchase and ₹15,000 for fishing nets. Besides, financial assistance of up to 75% at a rate of ₹1.12 lakh per hectare will be distributed to affected fish farmers, CM Majhi added.

For the handicrafts and handloom sector, assistance of ₹5000 will be distributed per artisan for replacement of equipment and ₹5,000 per artisan for loss of raw material/goods in process/finished goods.

World.title: Jet crash in Florida: All nine people aboard killed, says Transportation Secretary
World.content:
All nine people died aboard a business jet that crashed into a Florida neighborhood, U.S. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said Sunday (November 1, 2026).

The aircraft departed from Austin, Texas, and was headed to the Bahamas. Duffy said the Federal Aviation Administration is sending a team to support the National Transportation Safety Board's investigation into the cause.

The Learjet 60 carrying nine people nose-dived into a South Florida neighborhood on Sunday (November 1, 2026) and erupted into a giant fireball that appeared to just miss homes before crashing near a busy roadway, creating a giant fiery crater in the pavement.

The aircraft had departed Austin-Bergstrom International Airport in Texas and was headed to the Bahamas, according to the Federal Aviation Administration. Authorities did not immediately say what caused the jet to go down or who was on it.

Jim Reynolds, a spokesperson for Austin-Bergstrom International Airport, said it was a private aircraft. He could not immediately provide details about who was on the flight.

“This is definitely a tragedy,” he said.

He said the tail number for the flight was N722BD.

Video shot from people inside their cars captured the terrifying moment the aircraft plunged from the sky, before striking near the roadway and exploding. Flames flickered around chunks of pavement lining the crater as people milled about, expressing shock it landed only feet from homes and only inches from passing vehicles. Thick black smoke engulfed the crash site.

It was unclear if the crash caused any damage to homes.

The crash occurred near Military Trail and 10th Avenue North. The Palm Beach County Sheriff's Office closed roads in both directions and urged motorists to avoid the area. Firefighters and other emergency personnel rushed to the scene.

A woman working nearby said electricity in the area had been out for approximately two hours following the crash.

World.title: Four crew members eject safely after two Navy jets crash during air show in Idaho
World.content:
All four crew members ejected safely after two Navy jets collided and crashed on Sunday (May 17, 2026) during an air show at the Mountain Home Air Force Base in western Idaho, officials said.

The collision involved two U.S. Navy EA18-G Growlers from the Electronic Attack Squadron 129 in Whidbey Island, Washington, said Cmdr Amelia Umayam, spokesperson for Naval Air Forces, U.S. Pacific Fleet.

Jet crash in Florida: All nine people aboard killed, says Transportation Secretary

The aircraft were performing an aerial demonstration when the crash occurred, Cmdr Umayam said in a statement. The four crew members from both jets safely ejected, and the crash was under investigation, she said.

The crew members were in stable condition, base officials said.

Nobody at the military base was hurt, said Kim Sykes, marketing director with Silver Wings of Idaho, which helped to plan the air show.

“Everyone is safe, and I think that's the most important thing,” Sykes said.

Planes fell to the ground together

The base said in a social media post that it was locked down immediately following the crash. The remainder of the air show was cancelled.

Videos posted online by spectators showed four parachutes opening in the sky as the aircraft plummeted to the ground near the base about 50 miles (80 kilometres) south of Boise.

The EA-18G Growler is a variant of the F/A-18 Super Hornet fighter jet with sophisticated electronic warfare systems.

Shane Ogden said he was filming the two jets as they came close together. A video he captured shows the two aircraft appear to make contact and then spin in tandem as the crew members eject and their parachutes open. The planes then fall together, exploding into a fireball upon impact as the crew members drift to the ground nearby.

“I was just filming thinking they were going to split apart, and that happened, and I filmed the rest,” Ogden said in a text message. He said he left soon after the crash because he did not want to get in the way of emergency responders.

Also read: IAF’s Tejas fighter jet crashes at Dubai Air Show; pilot killed

Organisers said the popular air show that includes flying demonstrations and parachute jumps is a celebration of aviation history and a look at modern military capabilities. The U.S. Air Force Thunderbirds demonstration squadron headlined the show both days.

The National Weather Service reported good visibility and winds gusting up to 29 mph (47 kph) around the time of the crash.

Little room for error

It was remarkable that both crews were able to eject from their planes, and aviation safety expert Jeff Guzzetti said that may have been possible because of the way the planes collided and appeared to remain stuck together in midair before falling to Earth. Crews usually don't have a chance to eject in a midair collision, he said.

“It's really striking to see,” Guzzetti said. “It looks like they struck each other in a very unique fashion to cause them to remain intact and kind of stick to each other, and that very well could have saved them.” “It appears to be a pilot issue to me. It doesn't look like it was a mechanical malfunction,” he added. “Rendezvousing with another aeroplane in formation flight is challenging, and it has to be done just right to prevent exactly this kind of thing.”

Aviation safety expert John Cox, who is CEO of Safety Operating Systems, said the pilots who perform at air shows are among the best, but there is little room for error.

“Air show flying is demanding. It has very little tolerance,” Cox said. “The people who do it are very good, and it's a small margin for error. I'm glad everybody was able to get out.”

This year's Gunfighter Skies event was the first at the base since 2018, when a hang glider pilot died in a crash during an air show performance.

In 2003, a Thunderbirds aircraft crashed while attempting a manoeuvre. The pilot, who was not hurt, was able to steer the plane away from the crowd and eject less than a second before it hit the ground.

The air show industry has been working to improve safety for years at the roughly 200 events held each year in the U.S. The last fatal crash at an air show came in 2022 when two vintage military planes collided at an event in Dallas and killed six people.

An average of 3.8 deaths a year occurred at U.S. air shows from 1991 to 2006, said John Cudahy, president and CEO of the International Council of Air Shows. That fatality rate has been improving, and since 2017, there have been an average of 1.1 deaths per year, even including the 2022 crash. There were no U.S. air show deaths in 2023 or 2025, and a spectator hasn't been killed at an air show in the U.S. since 1952.

“Safety-wise, we've enjoyed really an unprecedented term of few accidents,” Cudahy said.

Investigators may be able to quickly get an idea of what happened in Sunday's crash because the crews of both planes survived and will be able to tell investigators what they saw and experienced before the collision. The Navy will lead the investigation, so there won't be as much information shared publicly as in civilian crashes.

The Iran war has led to the cancellation of some air shows this year at bases where military units are flying missions related to the conflict.

World.title: Kimi Antonelli becomes youngest F1 champion; Max Verstappen wins in Mexico
World.content:
Kimi Antonelli was crowned the youngest-ever Formula 1 world champion on Sunday after the Italian star finished third behind Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton at the ​Mexico City Grand Prix.

That podium told the story of Formula 1’s recent past, present ‌and future: Hamilton, the greatest driver of his generation with a ​record-tying seven drivers’ championships; Verstappen, who dominated the start of this ⁠decade with four consecutive titles from 2021-24; and Antonelli, who wrote his name in the record books thanks to nine wins and 16 podiums this year.

Antonelli has risen to 380 ‌points with four races remaining. Verstappen (261) snuck past Hamilton (259) in the standings, but they will be racing for second the rest of the way.

Antonelli ‌celebrated his first F1 world championship at 20 years and 68 ‌days old, ⁠more than three years younger than Germany’s Sebastian Vettel when ⁠he set the previous record in 2010.

“It’s a day I will remember forever,” Antonelli said. “Thank you to my team, my family and everyone who supports me. It’s starting to feel real now, I’m going ​to enjoy every bit.

“We had ‌such a strong car, and we were so consistent, I knew we had a chance. Just so glad we could finish it off.”

Verstappen crossed the finish line in 2:20:28.772, edging Hamilton by 0.799 seconds. The Red Bull Racing ‌star has won three of the past four Grand Prix.

“I had ​a very good first lap,” Verstappen said. “We had a good strategy, I do think we lacked a little bit of pace but ⁠we hung in there.

“It was tough. I was sweating at the end to keep Lewis behind.”

The Dutchman was also among those who took time to ‌congratulate Antonelli, who also became the first Italian world champion in 73 years.

“It is incredible, what a season (Antonelli) has had, and to do this at such an age ... I’m sure this is a very emotional day for him, and I am very proud of him,” Verstappen said.

Antonelli started the race in fourth and needed to finish ninth or better to secure the championship on Sunday no matter ‌what his peers did. He had a relatively drama-free run, though the race was interrupted by ​a red flag around Lap 45 when Valtteri Bottas crashed.

Antonelli managed to pass Charles Leclerc for third around Lap 48, and the Mercedes ⁠driver was in fine shape the rest of the day.

“Without them I wouldn’t ⁠be here, without Mercedes and my family,” Antonelli said. “It’s a special moment and one that will live forever. I’m speechless, I’m trying to process ‌what just happened.

“It’s been an incredible season, to share this podium with Max and Lewis is really incredible. I’m looking forward to more battles in ​the future.”

Mercedes now sits at 630 points in the constructors’ championship standings, a healthy 126-point lead over Ferrari.

World.title: Cyber attacks hit Russia, Ukraine after truce ends
World.content:
Russia said its emergency warnings app came under a “massive cyberattack” on Monday (November 2, 2026), hours after Ukraine reported a hack in an apparent exchange of blows between the foes, as their longest truce came to an end.

Moscow’s emergencies ministry said hackers posted “false information” on the app, which is designed to warn the public of incoming drone attacks and other threats.

Hours earlier, Ukraine said it suspected its air raid alert system had been compromised, after baseless alerts of a radiation threat appeared on the app.

The cyber attacks came as the longest truce of the war, limited to Ukraine’s eastern Kherson region, ended on Sunday (November 1, 2026) after Russia refused the offer of an extension, according to Kyiv.

Moscow did not immediately say who was behind the attack on its app, while Ukraine’s Center for Strategic Communications SPRAVDI blamed the hack it suffered on Russia.

The rare pause in fighting, brokered by US First Lady Melania Trump and which began early Tuesday, had enabled a humanitarian mission to the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky as the war grinds through its fifth year.

“The ceasefire, which was in effect from October 27 to November 1, has ended,” Ukraine’s Parliament Commissioner for Human Rights, Dmytro Lubinets, said.

He called the temporary truce “an important step in our joint humanitarian efforts” with Russia.

U.S.-mediated talks between Russia and Ukraine are set to resume this month, having been effectively frozen since the United States and Israel launched joint strikes on Iran in February.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said on Sunday his country would stop hitting Russian oil refineries — as U.S. counterpart Donald Trump has demanded — if Washington provided Kyiv with powerful Patriot interceptor missiles.

Raid alert app hack

Kherson regional governor Oleksandr Prokudin warned local people to be particularly vigilant when the ceasefire ended and to “respond immediately to warnings about Russian attacks”.

“The Air Alarm application has probably been subjected to hostile interference,” Ukraine’s air force said in a message. “There is no radiation threat.”

Air force spokesman Yuriy Ignat confirmed to AFP that the app had been hacked.

Hours later, Russia’s emergencies ministry said its teams were working to fix a “massive cyberattack” which was “enabling attackers to send false information to the public”.

‘Worse than before’

Russia’s full-scale invasion in February 2022 has destroyed parts of eastern and southern Ukraine, left hundreds of thousands of soldiers and civilians dead and forced millions to flee their homes.

AFP spoke to several Kherson residents, one of whom said the ceasefire had been a “breath of fresh air”.

“We have to use this time to get things done,” said Volodymyr Omeltchenko, a 38-year-old gardener, before the truce ended.

“We’re pruning the rose bushes for winter.”

Pope Leo, who had pressed Russia for a truce in Oleshky, had said he hoped the temporary pause would “strengthen the desire for dialogue and lead to new concrete peace initiatives”.

A Ukrainian military officer, speaking on condition of anonymity, expressed concern that the fighting would be “worse than before” when it resumed.

Russian forces on the other side of the Dnipro river had taken advantage of the calm of the past few days to amass new troops, transport ammunition stocks and collect intelligence on Ukrainian positions using surveillance drones, the officer said.

Oil attacks

Russia and Ukraine exchanged strikes elsewhere on Sunday.

Russia said a drone had struck an “industrial enterprise” east of Moscow overnight, with Ukrainian media reporting that Kyiv had attacked the Kstovo oil refinery.

Kyiv has repeatedly struck Russian oil and gas sites, in what it says is fair retaliation for Russian attacks on Ukrainian energy infrastructure.

Mr. Trump has been pressing Kyiv to stop the attacks, blaming them for rising diesel costs that analysts attribute to the Iran war.

Mr. Zelenskyy said on Fox News on Sunday that he told Mr. Trump and his team: “If you want us not to attack Russia’s refineries, they have not to attack our energy system.”

“Another alternative, give us Patriot missiles,” he said.

Ukraine’s Energy Ministry reported fresh power outages across the country Sunday, including in Kyiv, following Russian strikes on Ukrainian energy infrastructure.

World.title: How are tropical cyclones named?
World.content:
Cyclone 'Murasu' has intensified into a Severe Cyclonic Storm over the West Central and Southwest Bay of Bengal on November 2, 2026.

The IMD, or India Meteorological Department, says that the system may continue to move northwestwards and cross the south Andhra Pradesh coast, near Ongole, as a Severe Cyclonic Storm, with wind speeds expected to be between 100 to 110 kmph, gusting 120 kmph.

Cyclone Murasu comes days after Cyclone Arnab hit the coast of Andhra Pradesh

The Cyclonic Storm "Murasu" [Pronunciation: Murasu]" over Westcentral & adjoining Southwest Bay of Bengal moved nearly northwestwards with speed of 20 kmph during past 06 hours, intensified into severe cyclonic storm and lay centered at 0230 hours IST of today, the 02nd November, 2026 over the same region near Latitude 13.6°N and Longitude 82.5°E, about 260 km east-northeast of Chennai (Tamil Nadu), 290 km east-southeast of Nellore (Andhra Pradesh), 320 km south-southeast of Machilipatnam (Andhra Pradesh), 310 km east-southeast of Kavali (Andhra Pradesh), 330 km southeast of Ongole (Andhra Pradesh) and 470 km south of Vishakhapatnam (Andhra Pradesh). It is very likely to continue to move northwestwards and cross south Andhra Pradesh coast as a Severe Cyclonic Storm with wind speed of 100 to 110 kmph gusting 120 kmph between Nellore and Narsapur close to Ongole during midnight (2330 Hrs IST) of 2nd to early hours (0400 Hrs IST) of 3rd November, 2026. — India Meteorological Department (@Indiametdept) November 2, 2026

Chennai and Tiruvallur District Collectors have announced that schools and colleges in the districts will be closed on Monday (November 2, 2026) due to heavy rains. An orange alert was announced in six Telangana districts and a yellow alert in five districts in Telangana for Monday.

Cyclone Murasu live updates

What are tropical cyclones?

A tropical cyclone is a rapidly rotating storm that begins over a tropical ocean and can vary in speed, size, and intensity. They are also called hurricanes or typhoons, depending on the region.

Tropical cyclones are the second-most dangerous natural hazards, after earthquakes, according to the World Meteorological Organisation.

How are cyclones named?

The WMO elaborates that the process of determining names for tropical cyclones is conducted by the relevant tropical cyclone regional body at its annual or biennial session.

There are five tropical cyclone regional bodies, which are:

WMO Typhoon Committee WMO Panel on Tropical Cyclones Regional Association I Tropical Cyclone Committee Regional Association IV Hurricane Committee Regional Association V Tropical Cyclone Committee

These bodies establish pre-designated lists of names, the procedures for which can vary, with some regions using alphabetical order and others using the alphabetical order of country names. No tropical cyclone is named after an individual.

Factors that are considered while selecting a new name:

Short in character length for ease of use in communication. Easy to pronounce Appropriate significance in different languages Uniqueness- same names cannot be used in other regions.

The WMO adds that the Regional Specialised Meteorological Centre (RSMC) New Delhi Tropical Cyclone Centre is responsible for naming the tropical cyclones that have formed over the Bay of Bengal and the Arabian Sea when they have reached the relevant intensity.

Cyclones that form in the Northern Indian Ocean are named in a cyclical fashion by thirteen countries — Bangladesh, India, Iran, Maldives, Myanmar, Oman, Pakistan, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, Sri Lanka, Thailand, United Arab Emirates, and Yemen.

How are tropical cyclones classified?

The classification of a tropical cyclone depends on its maximum sustained wind speed. They are designated as follows:

1. Tropical depression is when the maximum sustained windspeed is less than 63 km/hour.

2.Tropical storm is when the maximum sustained wind speed is more than 63 km/hour. It is then also given a name.

3. Hurricane, typhoon, tropical cyclone, very severe cyclonic storm, depending on the basin, when the maximum sustained wind speed exceeds 116 km/hour.

Names of next ten cyclones after Cyclone Murasu

Name of cyclone Country which gave the name Cyclone Akvan Iran Cyclone Kaani Maldives Cyclone Ngamann Myanmar Cyclone Sail Oman Cyclone Sahab Pakistan Cyclone Lulu Qatar Cyclone Ghazeer Saudi Arabia Cyclone Gigum Sri Lanka Cyclone Thianyot Thailand Cyclone Afoor United Arab Emirates

*All information has been taken by the World Meteorological Organisation’s website

World.title: US-backed consortium proposes $4.4bn LNG project
World.content:
• Proposal envisages four tanks holding 560,000 cubic metres at Port Qasim in first phase of the $4.4bn plan that also includes a 1,100km upcountry gas pipeline

• Project would charge $4.93 per mmBtu for terminal and storage, $1.91 for transmission over first decade

ISLAMABAD: A private consortium of US companies, backed by the Trump administration, is pushing for an investment of up to $4.4 billion in an integrated liquefied natural gas (LNG) project in Pakistan, covering imports, storage, re-gasification, gas transmission and sales to large consumers on a ‘merchant basis’.

The development comes after Energas, an earlier frontrunner consisting of the Lucky Group and QatarEnergy, abandoned a similar project citing fundamental changes in Pakistan’s energy policy and requirements, as well as longstanding unresolved policy and fiscal issues.

The US consortium comprises Global Vision Energy Partners (GVEP) and Khanjee Holdings, both related firms, along with strategic co-investors from other countries and General Mediterranean Holding, a Luxem­bo­urg-based US financial conglomerate.

The sponsors have reportedly sec­ured consent from the Port Qasim Aut­hority for the proposed project site. An application has also been filed with the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) for a provisional licence.

A special purpose vehicle (SPV), a separate legal entity established to hold specific assets and liabilities and isolate financial risks, has been incorporated. Government facilitation has also been conveyed through the Mini­stry of Maritime Affairs and the Mini­stry of Energy’s Petroleum Divi­sion, according to documents seen by Dawn.

The project has been approved for consideration under the US Trade and Development Agency’s (USTDA) project preparation programme. It may also receive partial financing from the US Development Finance Corporation, backed by export credit guarantees from the US Export-Import Bank for technology, equipment and services.

Pakistan currently has no LNG storage facilities, leaving its domestic re-gasified LNG supplies entirely dependent on import supply chains and international energy prices.

The sponsors plan to develop the project in two phases. The first phase will comprise an LNG terminal and storage facility with four tanks and an estimated annual throughput of 35 billion cubic feet (BCF), at a cost of $1.7bn.

The second phase will involve the construction of a 1,100km, 42-48-inch pipeline to transport gas upcountry, with a capacity of around 1.2 billion cubic feet per day (BCFD). This will take the total project cost to $4.4bn.

The government had previously pursued a similar North-South gas pipeline project with Russia.

The proposed venture is being structured as a merchant infrastructure platform to meet domestic regasification requirements while establishing a physical LNG storage and trading hub in South Asia for US and Middle Eastern suppliers.

The consortium is engaging local inve­stors for up to 10 per cent equity participation, with indicative investments starting at $50 million per investor.

The sponsors also expect to attract strategic co-investors, including global energy and infrastructure funds and institutional investors such as Grey Rock Investment Partners, Kohlberg Kravis Roberts & Co, Blackstone Inc., Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund and the Kuwait Investment Authority.

Their participation remains subject to due diligence, investment approvals and definitive agreements. No binding equity commitments have been confirmed so far.

The SPV will develop, own and operate the project as a regional LNG storage, regasification and trading hub, serving Pakistan’s domestic gas market alongside US and Middle Eastern LNG suppliers. The model will not depend on a single government-backed offtake arrangement.

Re-gasification tariffs for the domestic market will be submitted to Ogra for approval, while other commercial services, including storage, tolling and transshipment, will be priced on market-based terms.

The US sponsors consider Port Qasim strategically important because of its existing port infrastructure and marine access for LNG carriers. Its location outside the Strait of Hormuz, one of the world’s most significant energy shipping chokepoints, is another key consideration.

Under the proposed financing structure, the project will have a 70:30 debt-to-equity ratio. GVEP will hold a 26pc stake, followed by General Mediterranean Holding with 24pc, and Khanjee Holdings and strategic co-investors with 20pc each. Local investors will hold the remaining 10pc in the first phase, which is estimated to cost $1.32bn (70pc of the $1.7bn cost).

The final project cost will be determined after the execution of engineering, procurement and construction (EPC) contracts and other construction and supply agreements.

The commercial model is expected to combine long-term tolling and storage agreements, transshipment arrangements and take-or-pay commitments where appropriate, with the remaining capacity reserved for merchant activities.

The proposed tolling tariff for the terminal and storage facility is $4.93 per million British thermal units (mmBtu), while the separate transmission tariff is estimated at $1.91 per mmBtu for the first 10 years. These rates are projected to decline to $2.20 and $0.92 per mmBtu, respectively, thereafter.

The LNG terminal and storage facility will have four tanks, each with a capacity of 140,000 cubic metres, providing total static storage capacity of 560,000 cubic metres.

Based on three inventory turnover cycles annually, the facility is expected to handle approximately 35.6BCF of LNG a year, with storage capacity of around 11.9BCF per cycle.

Published in Dawn, November 2nd, 2026

World.title: Kabul warned of ‘unbearable punishment’ as clashes persist along border
World.content:
• Torkham stays shut for five hours following firefight over disputed check post

• Military spox says Afghan Taliban ‘won’t be able to bear cost’ of harbouring terrorists

• Names India as ‘prime contractor’ behind terrorism in Pakistan

• Rubio says US shares Pakistan’s concerns over attacks from Afghan soil, open to role in easing tensions

KHYBER/LOWER SOUTH WAZIRISTAN: Pakistani and Afghan border forces exchanged fire at several points along their border on Sunday, as the military warned that the Afghan Taliban would not be able to withstand the “punishment” Islamabad could inflict if Kabul failed to rein in terrorists.

The fresh clashes temporarily shut down the busy Torkham border crossing over a disputed check post and killed one civilian in mortar shelling near the Angoor Adda crossing.

The situation unfolded as Washington validated Pakistan’s concerns regarding cross-border terrorist attacks originating from Afghanistan and signalled openness to playing a productive role in easing tensions.

The situation at the Torkham cro­ssing stabilised after a nearly five-hour closure caused by an hou­rlong exchange of light-arms fire.

It reopened only after border officials from both countries agreed through intermediaries to halt all construction near the border. However, tensions remained high in the Angoor Adda area of Lower South Waziristan.

According to the deputy commissioner of Lower South Wazir­istan, Taliban fighters continued to target Pakistani border checkpoints with unprovoked firing.

Pakistani security forces responded immediately and effectively, targeting “multiple Afghan border posts, mortar positions, and defensive checkpoints”, the official wrote on X, adding that no reports of any casualties have emerged from the border areas on the Pakistani side.

Border clashes

According to locals, gunfire erupted at Torkham on Sunday when Afghan authorities once again started construction on a disputed check post.

Authorities at Torkham said the Afghan side began work on the controversial Zangali check post, situated within a 100-metre radius of the Afghan side of the border, despite Pakistan’s strong objections.

The firing continued for nearly an hour with no casualties on the Pakistani side. The two nations had previously agreed to refrain from building security structures within a 100-metre radius of the border.

The intense firing caused the immediate closure of the border and panic among returning Afghans and local residents.

During the standoff, resident Siraj Khan told Dawn that he saw about 20 vehicles carrying unregistered Afghan families hastily returning from the border at Zero Point amid the crossfire.

The repatriation of unregistered Afghans was suspended, and government offices were closed.

Meanwhile, tensions escalated in the Angoor Adda area after two mortar shells were reportedly fired from the Afghan side.

Military’s warning

The flare-ups underscored a stark warning delivered by Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) chief, Lt Gen Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry.

In an interview with a news agency earlier this week, portions of which were broadcast by state media on Sunday, the military’s spokesperson said Pakistan has the operational readiness and a clear strategy to impose a heavy cost on the interim Afghan leadership if terrorism continues originating from Afghan soil.

“Whatever they want to send, they can, they may try. We have the capability to take them out,” Lt Gen Chaudhry said. “They don’t have, I think, the capability to then absorb the punishment that we can [inflict].”

He noted that Pakistan has no desire to interfere in Afghanistan’s internal governance. “We only ask that you don’t support terrorism inside Pakistan. Stop harbouring the terrorist leaders,” he added.

The ISPR chief asserted that while foreign military forces have physically withdrawn from Afghanistan, the Afghan Taliban front continues to operate as a proxy for multiple external parties, singling out India as the primary sponsor of anti-Pakistan terrorism.

“In the case of Pakistan, the prime contractor is India, and the proxies are TTP and the BLA,” he said, describing New Delhi as “the biggest terror sponsor here” and stating that “as far as terrorism in Pakistan is concerned, they [the Afghan Taliban] are a proxy of the Indians”.

Addressing whether Pakistan fears a cross-border drone dynamic similar to Houthi attacks against Saudi Arabia, Lt Gen Chaudhry noted Afghanistan has no domestic drone industry and relies entirely on external sponsors.

“The capability of Afghans, whatever they have, firstly it’s not their own. There’s no drone industry, there is no technology of that sort in Afghanistan. So it’s been provided by the sponsors, the terror sponsors, because the biggest terror sponsor here is India,” he said.

The ISPR chief emphasised that the Pakistan Army is systematically adapting to the changing character of modern warfare across contact and non-contact domains, cyber operations, drones and long-range munitions.

US shares Pakistan’s concerns

The security concerns were echoed in Washington’s diplomatic messaging, as Secretary of State Marco Rubio affirmed that the US shares Pakistan’s concerns regarding cross-border terrorist attacks originating from Afghanistan and signalled openness to playing a productive role in easing tensions.

“We don’t want Pakistan to be targeted for terrorism,” he told reporters at the G20 foreign ministers meeting in Atlanta, Georgia.

“Pakistan is concerned about terrorist attacks that are being sponsored from the territory of Afghanistan. They think that the Taliban has not done enough to constrain those attacks,” Mr Rubio said, noting that Pakistan had taken action in response to the threat.

He added that Washington did not have close relations with the Taliban authorities in Afghanistan and the US opposed terrorism regardless of where it originated or whom it targeted.

“We’ve heard the concerns that Pakistan has raised, and we’ve seen some of those attacks that they point to,” Rubio said. “We’re against terrorism no matter where it emanates from and who it targets.”

With input from APP

World.title: JUI-F asks its workers to ‘be prepared’
World.content:
QUETTA: The Jamiat Ulema-i-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F) Balochistan chapter has directed party workers across the province to prepare for any political developments and complete organisational and protest preparations in line with the directives of party chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman.

The directives were issued at a meeting of the party’s provincial executive committee and parliamentary members, chaired by provincial chief Senator Maulana Abdul Wasey on Sunday.

The meeting endorsed Maulana Fazlur Rehman’s stance and the decisions of the party’s central executive council, urging workers to remain ready to respond to any call from the leadership. It also decided to immediately activate party organisations at the provincial, district, tehsil and union council levels.

Expressing serious concern over the political, economic and law and order situation in Balochistan, the meeting said business activity had come to a standstill, unemployment was rising and incidents of targeted killings and violence had become increasingly common. It also noted that national highways had become unsafe for commuters.

Expresses concern over worsening security, unemployment, business conditions

The participants accused the provincial government of failing to ensure public safety, employment opportunities and basic facilities, saying its administrative control appeared to be weakening.

The meeting demanded that the government immediately introduce a bill in the Balochistan Assembly on the registration, administration and legal affairs of religious seminaries.

It also called for the draft Mines and Minerals legislation to be presented in the assembly for review, urging the government to honour its commitments.

Addressing the meeting, Maulana Abdul Wasey said the JUI-F and its chief remained committed to public rights, constitutional supremacy, democratic values and religious identity, while other political parties were largely pursuing personal interests and political expediency.

He warned against attempts to drag Pakistan into conflicts at the behest of foreign powers, particularly the United States and Israel, saying such moves were against the interests of the country and its people.

Provincial General Secretary Agha Mahmood Shah said the party’s visits to different districts would strengthen its organisational structure and expand public outreach.

The meeting reaffirmed its commitment to continuing a constitutional, democratic and peaceful political struggle und­er Maulana Fazlur Rehman’s leadership.
